Cardinals vs Cowboys Final Injury Report: Who's In, Who's Out?
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Dallas Cowboys are set to shortly meet at AT&T Stadium for Week 8 NFL action.
Per NFL rules, both teams have made their final rulings on inactive players, trimming their game day rosters down to 48 players each.
Final inactives for both sides ahead of today's 11:00 AM MST kickoff:
Inactives : Carson Beck, Starling Thomas. Evan Hull, Eku Leota, Jon Gaines II, Albert Reese, Walter Nolen III
Our inactives for today's game pic.twitter.com/4N0GMmtQX1
This means that all three questionable players for Arizona in Hjalte Froholdt, Andrew Wingard and Max Melton are active for the Cardinals today. That's a big boost for a Cardinals team looking for a major upset over Dallas.
Speaking of the Cowboys, they also got some good news ahead of Week 8:
Inactives : KaVontae Turpin, Shavon Revel Jr., Dee Winters, Tyrus Wheat, Drew Shelton, Luke Schoonmaker
Dallas Cowboys inactives against Arizona today: KaVontae Turpin (WR) Shavon Revel Jr. (CB) Dee Winters (LB) Tyrus Wheat (OLB) Drew Shelton (T) Luke Schoonmaker (TE)
This means the Cowboys will have George Pickens and Kenny Clark active today against Arizona. Both were listed as questionable on Friday.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur On what he learned about adversity during his time as the Offensive Coordinator at Davidson University during the 2013 season and how that experience shaped his career:
“I learned that it was a cool place to live and they love their basketball. It was cool. I still have relationships back there. It was an interesting situation. I think there was a five-year span where there were four wins or something like that, but whoever came in turned it around and showed that they can actually do it. You’re always learning from those types of experiences.
"The Davidson one, sure. I’m not going to really reflect on that too much. Shoot, in Atlanta, we started 5-0 in that first year with (Commanders Head Coach) Dan Quinn  — or 4-1, something like that. We had a stretch where we lost seven in a row and it was tough sledding (and) then the next year ended up going to the Super Bowl. Then (49ers Head Coach) Kyle (Shanahan) gets the head job in San Francisco — we’re all fired up and ready to install this thing and get it going. We were 0-9 and it was tough.
"There are a lot of different experiences you lean on in those times. Where I always try to put my focus is that this is a week-to-week league. I want these guys to be where their feet are. The highs that they felt last week (and) the lows that they felt after this last game — once you reset, you learn from it on those Mondays, you get right back to work, and you work to be 1-0. Good, bad, or anything in between, I don’t try to look past that. (I) try to lean on those experiences that I’m talking about and that you’re alluding to and then just try to grow.”

title: Cardinals Reshuffle Roster Before Cowboys Game
full_text:
ARIZONA — There's no sugarcoating how important of a game the Arizona Cardinals have ahead.
Week 8's clash with the Dallas Cowboys could potentially decide the direction of the Cardinals' season. A win against Dallas would push Arizona to 3-5 and keep just the slightest flame of hope alive for a turnaround while a 2-6 start would all but officially cement the Cardinals' fate of the 2026 season.
Eying a potential upset, the Cardinals made two roster moves today:
On Saturday, Arizona elevated DL Jared Harrison-Hunte and TE Kenny Yeboah for tomorrow's game vs. Dallas. The Cardinals used both of their standard practice squad elevations.
Arizona previously ruled out DL Walter Nolen III and OL Jon Gaines on Friday. Harrison-Hunte will supply the Cardinals numbers along the defensive line while this could signal Arizona is confident in the questionable Hjalte Froholdt to play center on Sunday.
The same could be said for other questionable players in CB Max Melton and S Andrew Wingard.
The decision to elevate Yeboah is an interesting one, as all of Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano were healthy this week. Perhaps Arizona wanted an extra body in their room, as they do utilize 13 (one running back, three tight end) personnel more than almost any other team in the NFL.
The Cardinals have won their last eight of nine matchups against the Cowboys, as Dallas' last win against Arizona came back in 2017.
That's an odd stat, as the Cardinals have continally ranked near the bottom of the basement of NFL standings while the Cowboys are consistently viewed as playoff contenders on a yearly basis.
"Yeah, it's just crazy," Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb told reporters on never beating Arizona since he came into the league (h/t Cowboys' Official Team Site ). "[We were] being very, very relaxed, and they punched us in the mouth every single time. They've always had more energy They were more excited, regardless of if it was a 12 o'clock, Sunday night or Monday night.
"We've played them in prime time, they beat us there. So, we need to treat them as if they are a Super Bowl contending team, which they may be, you know what I'm saying? Hats off to them in their prep, and we just got to go match them. If not overpowered that."
We'll see if the Cardinals can continue their success in AT&T Stadium.

title: NFL Fines Cardinals' Trey McBride Almost $24,000
full_text:
Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride has been a favorite of league officials in terms of paying fines.
In Week 4, McBride was assessed a $17,911 fine for a leg-whip block.
After reviewing all plays in Week 7, McBride was hit for two more fines against the Denver Broncos — one for a facemask and another for taunting. Both fines were $11,941, totaling nearly $24,000 off just two plays alone.
#AZCardinals TE Trey McBride was fined just under $24,000 total for two plays in Week 7. Play 1: facemask Play 2: taunting McBride was also fined $17,911 for leg whip block back in Week 4. pic.twitter.com/h4lEaR7HNG
Even though he drew a pass interference on the taunting play, McBride told reporters he should have made a play on the ball.
"Honestly I should've made that play on the pass interference and it eats me up," McBride said . "That's a play I can make. I'm capable of making that through contact through the pass interference, whatever that is. I've got to come down with those plays.
"If I make that play, onside kick, we're still in that game. That's what kind of frustrates me the most. I had a good game, but I didn't finish the job."
McBride has now been fined nearly $42,000 on the season. We've not even reached Week 8.
McBride's pocketbooks probably aren't hurting too egregiously after inking a record-setting deal to make him the NFL's highest-paid tight end ahead of the 2025 season. However, the bulk of his extension begins kicking in next season.
The Cardinals have seen several players fined already this season. Inside linebacker Karson Sharar was fined $5,372 for a late hit in Week 2, tight end Elijah Higgins was hit for $20,411 for illegal use of helmet in Week 5. To continue things, outside linebacker Eku Leota was fined over $6,000 for a blindside block during a punt return while tight end Teagan Quitoriano was also fined nearly $7,000 for a leg-whip block.
This season, McBride has 59 receptions for 472 yards and four touchdowns. He leads all NFL players in catches.
"I think you guys all know what (TE) Trey (McBride) can do," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said this season.
"You have different skill sets that these guys can provide for us, not just in the run game but in the pass game as well. To be able to present some of those formations or some of that 13-personnel — not just old school (style with) all (of the) guys hands in the dirt but spread it out a little bit and give the defense a few wrinkles.”

title: What Budda Baker Said as Cardinals Trade Rumors Intensify
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals dealt Marvin Harrison Jr. weeks ago, and as the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline approaches, they might not be done dealing some of their biggest names.
Budda Baker is no stranger to seeing his name involved in trade discussions, as we've now approached yearly tradition for content creators and other outlets to include Arizona's defensive leader and longest-tenured Cardinal in theoretical trades.
2026 is no different, as the Cardinals are off to a rocky start and Baker again finds himself in trade rumors. After another failed season looks to be shaping up in the desert, many are curious to see if the Pro Bowl safety is moved.
The player himself isn't paying any mind to the chatter.
“Just living in the present. Like today, having a great time with you guys, and going to have a great Friday practice. Just focus on playing against the Dallas Cowboys and trying to get a W at their stadium," Baker told reporters this week.
Baker's in his tenth season and has played in just one playoff game with the Cardinals. Since arriving, Arizona hasn't won the NFC West once. The Cardinals are just 2-5 this season under new head coach Mike LaFleur.
The losing has certainly piled in the desert, reaching a point where if Baker requested a trade to pursue a Super Bowl push elsewhere, Arizona would do right by their face of the franchise.
"My approach is I'm here," Baker told ESPN's Josh Weinfuss in an interview earlier this week.
"I'm here. I want to win. I want to be here. And I'm just controlling what I can control, just taking it one week at a time, and hopefully when the deadline ends, I'll still be here. If not, I mean, it's a business. I understand at the end of the day and that's it."
Baker has earned the right to dictate his future. What exactly that holds remains to be seen, though either possibility of him staying or leaving appears to be on the table.

title: Cardinals-Cowboys Injury Report: Who's Officially Out, Questionable?
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Dallas Cowboys have revealed their final injury reports of their practice week ahead of Sunday's clash.
The Cardinals have ruled out Walter Nolen III (ankle) and Jon Gaines II (ankle) entering the weekend.
Three faces in Hjalte Froholdt (knee), Max Melton (knee) and Andrew Wingard (knee) are questionable. Prominent names such as Budda Baker, Jeremiyah Love , Josh Sweat, Michael Wilson and Mack Wilson Sr. were removed off the injury report and are good to go.
Dallas, meanwhile, ruled out Ka'Vontae Turpin (ribs) and Dee Winters (calf). The Cowboys have a laundry list of players questionable entering the weekend, which includes: Jonathan Bullard (calf), Kenny Clark (back), Marist Liufau (forearm), P.J. Locke (foot), George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring), and Luke Schoonmaker (groin).
The Cardinals and Cowboys will both have the opportunity to make up to two standard practice squad elevations on Saturday. These moves, based on the positions, could be key in determining who the respective teams believe will be in or out.
Sunday, the two sides will make final active or inactive decisions on injured players, which are due by the NFL 90 minutes prior to kickoff. With kickoff at 11:00 AM MST on Sunday, this report will be due at 9:30 AM MST.
Teams are only allowed to dress 48 players on a game day.
Despite the Cowboys being under .500 entering Week 8, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur knows exactly what's in store with Dallas:
“They have a lot of talent, I know that. I’ve always had a lot of respect for Dak. I’ve had a lot of respect for ‘Schotty’ (Cowboys Head Coach Brian Schottenheimer) — he’s as good a human in this league as there is," LaFleur told reporters.
"You know they’re always going to be a talent-filled team. It’s always fun to go into that stadium (AT&T Stadium) and play those guys for obvious reasons. We have our hands full like you do every week but yes, these guys are talented.”
Star Cowboys wideout CeeDee Lamb had some thoughts on Arizona winning their last eight-of-nine matchups against Dallas.
"They've always had more energy. They were more excited, regardless of if it was a 12 o'clock, Sunday night or Monday night," Lamb told the Cowboys' official team site.
“I've never beat the Cardinals since I've been in the league, so that's kind of fair to say,” Lamb said. “I wouldn't say heightened focus, but it's definitely another take.”
The Cardinals haven't lost to Dallas since 2017.

title: Cardinals Rule 2 Starters Out vs Cowboys
full_text:
ARIZONA – The Arizona Cardinals are ruling two starters out against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Friday morning that defensive lineman Walter Nolen III and offensive lineman Jon Gaines II are out this weekend.
Arizona Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur says DL Walter Nolen III & G Jon Gaines II are both OUT against the Cowboys. pic.twitter.com/xyHjpv2zUD
Nolen and Gaines are both set to miss their second matchup in a row and did not practice at all this week due to ankle injuries.
Arizona is set to get running back Jeremiyah Love in the mix — you can read about that here .
Both are respectively big pieces to the Cardinals' trenches, as Nolen (a former first-round pick) has been dealing with injuries since entering the league while Gaines was recently thrust into a starting role.
Arizona now enters Sunday's contest in Dallas with even more depleted play on both sides of the line of scrimmage, which doesn't bode well for their chances to control the game.
The Cardinals are expecting right tackle Elijah Wilkinson to play this week while Hjalte Froholdt was missing from Friday's practice.
Both Arizona and Dallas will reveal their respective injury reports later today, though things don't look good for the Cardinals.
The Cowboys have one of the NFL's worst defensive units, though LaFleur says there's talent across the board on their team.
“I just said the talent. There is talent on all their levels, but their defensive line is real. I’ve been with (Cowboys DT) Quinnen (Williams) in New York. It starts with him. He can wreck a game quickly. I remember that when he was a young guy, I remember that being with him and it certainly hasn’t changed," LaFleur said.
"Sometimes, particularly early (in the scouting process) as you’re trying to learn some things and stuff like that — you just look at the tape and what your eyes tell you more than the numbers.”

title: Jeremiyah Love Gets Green Light For Cardinals-Cowboys
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are set to get Jeremiyah Love back from injury.
Ahead of the team's Week 8 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, head coach Mike LaFleur confirmed the Cardinals would have Love available this Sunday after missing the last two games with an ankle injury .
"Yeah, he'll be good," LaFleur said of Love.
"Even though he's been out for two weeks, none of these guys by November 1 are truly at 100%. But he's feeling as good as he can feel."
Love, the third overall pick, has been plagued by injuries during his rookie season but has impressed when taking the field. Arizona's hoping to improve their 2-5 record against a Cowboys team that statistically has the worst run defense in the league.
"We're never going to put a guy out there that we don't think can obviously benefit the team, benefit in this case the offense. So I'll keep it at that. But I mean, he's out there for a reason, and we expect him to go," LaFleur continued on Love.
"... Especially the guys that you're giving the ball to. Like if they're not dynamic within their own ability, I mean, let's let's get the next guy up. We feel good. He feels good enough to go out there and produce, and look forward to having him back out there."
Tyler Allgeier has been listed on this week's report with a toe injury while Bam Knight has steadied the ship for Arizona since Love departed the lineup.
The Cardinals are desperately trying to revamp their rushing attack, one that ranks in the bottom ten of the league at 96 yards per game. Injuries have battered Arizona's offensive line and running back room, though LaFleur highlighted continuity as a major piece the Cardinals have to have.
"I think it's improved, but still a long way to go. Run game is a mindset and it's continuity. I know our guys have the mindset, there's no doubt, but just continue to build that continuity with the mixture of guys we got going," LaFleur said.
Love has 245 yards on 67 carries (3.7 yards per carry) and one touchdown on the ground to pair with 11 receptions for 36 yards and one touchdown through the air.

title: Walter Nolen III's Outlook For Cardinals-Cowboys is Concerning
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals , for a second straight day, did not see defensive lineman Walter Nolen III practice.
Nolen missed Arizona's Week 7 matchup against the Denver Broncos with an ankle injury and is now on track to suffer a similar fate for Week 8's road test against the Dallas Cowboys barring a strong turnaround in the next 48 hours.
The Cardinals' defense is much different when Nolen is healthy and in the lineup, as his ability to disrupt both the run and pass is crucial for Arizona to control the line of scrimmage. The former first-round pick, unfortunately, continues to deal with injuries early in his career.
With a loaded Cowboys offense playing host to Arizona on Sunday, the Cardinals' chances of slowing them down could take a turn.
“They have a lot of talent, I know that," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of Dallas' offense.
"I’ve always had a lot of respect for Dak. I’ve had a lot of respect for ‘Schotty’ (Cowboys Head Coach Brian Schottenheimer) — he’s as good a human in this league as there is. You know they’re always going to be a talent-filled team. It’s always fun to go into that stadium (AT&T Stadium) and play those guys for obvious reasons. We have our hands full like you do every week but yes, these guys are talented.”
The Cardinals will rely on Roy Lopez and Darius Robinson to step up if Nolen can't go. Both players have had respectively nice 2026 campaigns. Dante Stills likely gets the nod inside while Andrew Billings could find himself active.

title: Where Cardinals, Josh Sweat Trade Stands After NFL Blockbusters
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are expected to make Josh Sweat readily available for trade ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline.
We've already seen two defensive front players dealt for picks in DeForest Bucker (49ers) and Jeffery Simmons (Bears) with more moves potentially on the way.
What the recent deals mean for Sweat and the Cardinals:
Giving up two future first-round picks for a player essentially pushes you out of the running for any other major moves, and that's what stamped Chicago's deal for Simmons this morning. The Bears were also interested in Buckner and reportedly offered a better package than the 49ers for Buckner before the player himself reportedly only wanted the 49ers.
Chicago appeared to be serious on acquiring some sort of pass rush help. That's what they're getting in Simmons, and barring a "forget those picks" mentality from the Bears, they're out of the running for Sweat.
Even after getting Buckner, ESPN 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner says another move is still on the table for San Francisco:
"An addition such as Mack -- or other potentially available edge rushers like the Jets' Will McDonald IV, Cardinals' Josh Sweat or Bucs' Yaya Diaby -- would make sense to round out San Francisco's rotation for a reasonable cost in terms of what they need to give up," he wrote .
However, it would have to cost the 49ers.
Trading Sweat inside the NFC West would only happen if the receiving team would add a sweetener to the deal, as the Cardinals wouldn't be in the business of helping out a rival get a Super Bowl ring now without it paying dividends in the future.
The Cardinals' reported asking price of a second-round pick should remain the same, even after other deals on the defensive front market in recent days. One could make an argument Sweat's value for interested teams goes up due to other top names now off the market.
While Arizona should stay firm on their asking price of a high Day 2 pick, there also may be a sense of urgency to strike a deal now as opposed to waiting next offseason, where Sweat will be 30 and demanding a new contract with zero money guaranteed on the final two years of his deal.
If there was ever a time for the Cardinals to trade Sweat, it would be in the coming days.
The Cowboys are naturally a team that has been connected to Sweat in recent weeks. With a Dallas defense that needs another pass rusher on a team that conceivably wants to win now, Sweat's name makes sense.
However, Dallas doesn't quite have ample 2027 draft capital to make some moves — owning Green Bay's first-round pick, their own second and Pittsburgh's fourth to begin festivities next offseason.
That's not quite exciting if you're the Cardinals, and if you're Dallas, are you really looking to empty the clip on a guy who you'll have to pay more in the coming years?

title: Jeremiyah Love Headlines Loaded Cardinals-Cowboys Injury Report
full_text:
Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love headlines a loaded injury report ahead of the team's Week 8 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.
Love, who has missed the last two weeks with an ankle injury, returned to the practice field in limited fashion today.
Out of the 15 total Cardinals listed on Wednesday's report, nine did not participate.
Full reports for both sides:

It appears the Cardinals could get Love back into the mix, though head coach Mike LaFleur says impressive backup running back Bam Knight could still have a role.

You have to pick and choose our spots when we’re not going to get as many up and we’re going to help out with some of the ribs and licks and stuff like that — our chip mechanisms.
"Again, it’s all-encompassing but I know collectively as a group, we can all do better (at) coaching and playing.”

title: How Falcons Safety Jessie Bates III Perfected the NFL’s 'Peanut Punch'
full_text:
The “Peanut Punch,” made famous by former All-Pro cornerback Charles Tillman, is surging across the NFL.
Defenders are increasingly targeting the football with a closed fist, trying to punch it out of the ball carriers’ hands. The technique is making an impact across the NFL, with forced fumbles up 39% compared to the 2025 season, according to Jomboy Media.
In Atlanta, there is someone who’s perfected the “Peanut Punch,” in safety Jessie Bates III . It was on full display last Sunday, Oct. 25, when he punched the ball out of tight end George Kittle’s hands to preserve a 29-20 Falcons win to knock off the undefeated San Francisco 49ers .
🚨 ¡La D de Atlanta con el fumble! 😱 Jessie Bates III le sacó el balón a George Kittle y ¡Terminó con el invicto de los San Francisco 49ers! 🤯 #NFLMX 📺💻 @somos_FOX pic.twitter.com/u4kNujehak
“There are people doing it around the league,” Bates told reporters Monday. “It’s not like I’m reinventing the wheel.”
Bates also caught a toe-tap interception from Niners quarterback Brock Purdy. The pick and forced fumble moved his total to six games with both, only behind Rod Woodson (seven), a fellow Fort Wayne, Indiana native and Snider High School alumnus.
The ninth-year NFL veteran Bates says the talent comes from his time, when he starred as a three-sport letterman athlete on Snider’s football, basketball, and baseball teams before starring on the gridiron at Wake Forest.
“You go back to my high school tapes. I’m punching at the ball, I’m picking the ball off,” Bates said.
“I definitely encourage guys to play multiple sports because it does translate. The same way I pick a pocket in basketball is the same way I can punch the ball out on a football play. Baseball, coming off a bat, is the same thing as a quarterback throwing the ball.”
Since arriving in Atlanta in 2023, Bates’ forced fumbles are almost on par with his interception total. Through 58 games with the franchise, he has 10 forced fumbles compared to 14 interceptions.
His season-high forced fumbles are four, set in 2024. He’s already halfway towards that total through the Falcons’ first seven games, at two.
Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich called Bates “the best in football” at the “Peanut Punch.”
“It’s no surprise to us,” Ulbrich said. “If you just watch any one of our practices, you see how intentional Jessie is about hitting the ball. And it’s not just the random haymakers on the ball. It’s really the precision, trying to find the leather, and then ultimately trying to find the air behind the ball. He’s got an amazing feel for that. We’ve always got to keep the ball at the forefront of our minds, and having a guy like Jessie leading the charge, I feel fortunate in that way.”
Bates’ mastery of “Peanut Punch” has spread to the entire team – even on offense. It forces a heightened sense of ball security for players like running back Bijan Robinson , who’s known not to fumble often.
“Those things don’t just happen on Sunday,” Bates explained. “Our whole defense does a good job of doing that in practice. When you’re punching at the ball on Bijan, it makes him better as well. Makes our football team better.”
Bates returns to action when Atlanta (3-4) heads to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5) for a Week 8 NFC South clash . Kickoff is at 1 p.m. from Raymond James Stadium and will be televised on FOX.

title: Atlanta Falcons vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers Weather Update: It Could Get Ugly
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. is headed back to play in his hometown of Tampa, Fla. for the first time since as a professional, but the conditions could be less than ideal.
Playing in a dome for home games and three road games in the NFC South, the weather isn't something the Falcons typically have to worry too much about, except for the random trip to Buffalo or anywhere in the AFC East late in the season.
However, that's not the case in Tampa today.
The Falcons are scheduled to kick off against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at 1:00 p.m. on Sunday afternoon, and the weather conditions could play a huge role in the game and the viewing experience, even for the television audience.
The Weather Channel predicts scattered thunderstorms beginning at 10:00 a.m. in Tampa, and then it gets ugly.
They predict a 100% chance of heavy thunderstorms starting at Noon and lasting until 3:00 p.m., when they start to dissipate. Even then, they predict scattered thunderstorms until 5:00 p.m. EST.
Raymond James Stadium doesn't allow umbrellas , so if you made the trip to Tampa, leave those in the car. There's no doubt that fans at the game are going to get wet. The biggest concern in the heavy thunderstorms will be the lightning.
The NFL will play through a downpour, but they'll clear the stadium in the event of lightning in close proximity, and that appears to be inevitable this afternoon. We'll keep you updated on delays if they occur through the afternoon.
The Buccaneers and Falcons are both good running teams, and they're both good at stopping the run. Tampa has the NFL's No. 3 rushing offense at 146.4 yards per game, and the Falcons come in at No. 6 at 139.9.
The Buccaneers also edge Atlanta on run defense with the league's No. 2 rush defense, allowing just 77.3 yards per game, and the Falcons are No. 4 at 88.9 yards per game.
Tampa holds a slight edge in both categories and would welcome a sloppy game that helps negate the Falcons' advantage in the air.
Both teams have had their struggles at quarterback at various times this season. But despite starting two games with Cooper Rush under center, Atlanta still has the No. 4 passing offense at 255.6 yards per game.
Tampa was without Baker Mayfield for three games this season, and even when he came back last week, he needed just 64 yards in the Buccaneers' blowout of Carolina. Tampa is averaging 217.4 yards per game through the air, 19th in the NFL.
Adding to their desire to keep this a battle in the trenches, star wide receiver Emeka Egbuka has been ruled out with a concussion.
The kicking game will also be affected. Falcons kicker Nick Folk has struggled beyond 50 yards so far this season, and Atlanta may scrap the idea of kicking from distance all together today.
We'll hope for no lightning delays. There's little hope that fans will stay dry. A sloppy game in the elements favors the home team. Will it be enough? We'll find out on Sunday afternoon.

title: Falcons Coach Makes Feelings Clear on Struggling Kicker Nick Folk
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are standing behind veteran kicker Nick Folk despite some difficulties this season.
Folk entered the season coming off one of the most accurate campaigns of his career. Folk led the NFL in field goal percentage with the New York Jets in 2025 and with the Titans the two years prior. He'd only missed three field goals in the last three seasons combined, all three from over 50 yards.
However, the 41-year-old has experienced a noticeable decline in accuracy during his first season in Atlanta.
Through seven games, Folk had converted 12 of 15 field goal attempts, an 80% success rate. That represents a significant drop from his production last season, when he made 28 of 29 attempts for a league-leading 96.6% conversion rate. He also converted all 22 extra point attempts in 2025, and he didn't miss in 2024 either, compared with 15 of 16 this season.
Despite this, special teams coach Craig Aukerman is not concerned about Folk's ability to recover.
"We have all the confidence in the world with him," Aukerman said.
Folk's experience is one reason the Falcons remain confident in their kicker. The veteran has spent nearly two decades in the NFL, and Aukerman understands that his role is not necessarily to overhaul Folk's technique after every missed kick.
Instead, the special teams coordinator wants to help the kicker maintain his confidence.
"My biggest thing is I just want to support him," Aukerman said. "If there are things that I can tell him along the way, whether it's a plant foot or whether it's his angle, or whether I see a few things here and there."
Aukerman also emphasized the importance of moving forward rather than allowing one missed kick to affect the next opportunity.
"I want to be out there and let him know that, hey, we're moving on to the next one. And the next one is the most important kick that you have."
That approach was evident after Folk missed an extra point.
"That's the greatest thing, again, about Nick. He can self-correct himself at any point in time," Aukerman said.
Folk subsequently converted all three of his field goal attempts against the San Francisco 49ers, providing a positive response after the missed extra point.
Atlanta signed Folk in March after cycling through three kickers during the 2025 season. His recent track record made him an appealing option for a team seeking stability at the position.
Before joining Atlanta, Folk had made at least 95% of his field goal attempts in each of the previous three seasons. He converted 29 of 30 attempts with Tennessee in 2023, 21 of 22 in 2024, and 28 of 29 with New York in 2025. To be fair, two of his three misses this year have been beyond 50 yards.
Those numbers explain why the Falcons are willing to be patient. Folk has demonstrated that he can deliver consistent results over an extended period, even if his early production in Atlanta has fallen short of that standard.
For now, the Falcons are relying on Folk, and a few mistakes will not change the team's belief in its veteran kicker.

title: Falcons Lose Former Draft Pick to Career-Ending Medical Condition
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have received heartbreaking news regarding rookie defensive tackle Anterio Thompson, who revealed that he has been told he will never play football again because of a genetic mutation affecting his spinal cord.
Thompson, who has been on the non-football injury list since the beginning of training camp, recently shared the news in an emotional social media post. He was informed that his medical condition would prevent him from continuing his football career, Thompson revealed on his Instagram story .
The sixth-round selection in the 2026 NFL Draft reflected on the difficult situation, explaining how challenging it has been to process the unexpected news after reaching the highest level of professional football.
“Mentally, I’ve been better than anyone would be in my situation,” Thompson wrote. “As a football player, you know one day you’ll have to hang up your cleats, but you just hope it’s on your own terms. It’s hard to explain what it feels like to go through the highest of highs to the lowest of lows in the matter of seconds.”
For Thompson, reaching the NFL was supposed to be the beginning of a new chapter. Instead, the young defensive lineman now faces the reality of a football career ending before he could make his professional debut.
Thompson’s announcement also came shortly after Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski was asked about the rookie during his Friday media availability. Coincidentally, Stefanski addressed Thompson before the player’s Instagram post began circulating publicly.
The Falcons selected Thompson in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft after he played college football at Washington in 2025. Although he entered the organization with an opportunity to compete for a spot on Atlanta’s defensive line, his medical situation kept him from participating in training camp.
Thompson’s placement on the non-football injury list had kept him away from the field throughout the offseason and preseason. His latest revelation now provides additional context surrounding his absence and the challenges he has been facing behind the scenes.
For any NFL prospect, hearing his name called during the draft represents years of hard work coming together. Thompson experienced that moment in 2026, but the opportunity to turn that achievement into an NFL career has been cut short by circumstances beyond his control.
While his playing career has come to an unexpected end, Thompson’s emotional message highlights the personal difficulty of losing something he spent years working to achieve.
The Falcons rookie now faces an uncertain future outside of football, with the support of those around him as he navigates this difficult transition.

title: 3 Keys to Victory: How the Falcons Can Beat the Buccaneers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have an opportunity to pick up an NFC South victory when they travel to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers on Sunday.
With both teams looking to gain ground in the division, Atlanta will need to execute in several key areas to come away with a win. If Atlanta wins, they'll take sole possession of first place in the division, and all but end Tampa's chances by sending them to 2-6.
If the Buccaneers win, they're right back in the thick of things at 3-5, tied with the Falcons and just half a game behind the Panthers. This is a big one in the NFC South.
Here are three keys to victory for the Falcons.
Tampa Bay has been aggressive defensively this season, blitzing on 40.9% of its charted dropbacks, the fifth-highest rate in the NFL.
That presents a significant challenge for Michael Penix Jr. and Atlanta’s offensive line. The Falcons cannot afford to allow the Buccaneers to consistently pressure their quarterback and disrupt the timing of the offense.
Penix has demonstrated the ability to take advantage of aggressive defenses, but he will need to make quick decisions against Tampa Bay. Atlanta should utilize short passes, screens and pre-snap motion to help identify defensive coverage and create opportunities for Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson.
Against Chicago in Week 6, Penix completed 10 of 18 passes for 121 yards and three touchdowns against the blitz, but he was also sacked five times.
The Falcons need to find a better balance between attacking downfield and getting the football out quickly.
The weather could play a significant role in Sunday’s matchup, making Atlanta’s rushing attack even more important.
The Falcons average 149.5 rushing yards per game, fourth-best in the NFL. Bijan Robinson has been a major reason for that success, recording 704 rushing yards and five touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry.
Tampa Bay, however, has allowed just 77.3 rushing yards per game, ranking second in the league.
That makes this one of Atlanta’s toughest challenges, but Robinson’s involvement will be critical. With rain potentially impacting passing conditions and footing, the Falcons should look to establish their ground game early.
Robinson is coming off a 122-yard performance from scrimmage against San Francisco. Atlanta needs another productive afternoon from its star running back to control the clock, keep Penix out of obvious passing situations, and wear down Tampa Bay’s defense.
Atlanta cannot afford another slow start, especially against a Buccaneers team coming off a 43-13 victory over Carolina.
The Falcons have allowed 6.3 points per game in the first quarter, tied for the third-worst mark in the NFL. They also possess the football for just 38.5% of the opening quarter, the second-lowest percentage in the league.
Those numbers highlight the importance of establishing momentum early.
Atlanta has averaged 31 points per game over its last five contests, showing the potential of its offense when everything clicks.
The Falcons need to carry that production into the opening quarter. Whether through Robinson establishing the run or Penix connecting with his receivers, Atlanta must put points on the board early.
Falling behind could force the Falcons into predictable passing situations against an aggressive Tampa Bay defense.
A fast start, combined with a productive running game and an effective plan against the blitz, could put Atlanta in position to earn a much-needed division victory.

title: Bears Jeffery Simmons Trade Makes Prior Falcons Trade Look Like Robbery
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans and Chicago Bears executed a blockbuster trade on Thursday, but Atlanta Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham came out a winner.
In late August, the Falcons sent cornerback Clark Phillips III and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Bears for interior defensive lineman Gervon Dexter . The Bears then turned around and made this lucrative deal for Jeffery Simmons (two first-rounders and a fourth-rounder to the Tennessee Titans for Simmons and a fifth-rounder) just a few months later.
Simmons is an elite player who deserves this sort of capital, but that is an expensive deal for a player whose output has been eerily similar to the one they just sent away.
Dexter, 6-foot-6 and 326 pounds, has been a force for the Falcons since coming to Atlanta ahead of the regular season. He boasts a pass-rush win rate of 15.8, with 18 hurries, four quarterback hits, two sacks, and 24 pressures – which is right in line with Simmons’ pass-rush win rate of 14.3, with 14 hurries, six quarterback hits, four sacks, and 24 pressures.
Dexter's numbers match Simmons, despite the former Titan playing nearly twice the snaps (425-279). Dexter's run defense, a sore spot in Chicago, also matches up well against Simmons.
Not that far apart in dbl team rate. pic.twitter.com/sRab1khSMW
The Bears’ new interior piece is an elite player and has been for several years (three-time All-Pro), but the Falcons might have found a similar player in Dexter, who's four years younger,  for considerably less. It’s why they felt compelled to extend him just a month after making that deal.
“He repped our style at the highest level: strain, effort, toughness, violence, awareness, instinct, all of that,” Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said after Dexter signed that deal. “He proved a lot before he got here, and then he's just validated it, because you never know until you get your hands on a guy and you're really around him on a day-to-day capacity, what his makeup is – and his makeup is elite.”
Atlanta needed to get bigger and stronger in the trenches, and Cunningham made that a priority this offseason. The process, which included adding Dexter from the Bears, has paid off in a big way. The Falcons have been one of the NFL’s best defensive lines this season, generating pressure at a high clip without sending added blitzers and stuffing the run.
This isn't the first time in the recent past the Bears and Falcons have been linked at the position. Prior to the 2025 season, the Falcons waived stalwart Grady Jarrett for salary cap reasons. The Bears quickly pounced on Jarrett and gave him a three-year, $43 million contract.
The 33-year-old Jarrett started just four games for the Bears last year and has 12 tackles in seven starts this season.
The Falcons' four-man rotation at defensive tackle costs less than Jarrett's $18.9 million cap hit combined. And they have been one of the most productive units in the NFL.
Falcons have 4 guys in the top right. It gives me another opportunity to say that ranking them the 32nd DL was ignorant. https://t.co/mrOWz5zD6O
Does all this mean that Dexter is as good a player as Simmons? Maybe not, but he is four years younger, matches his production, and it didn’t cost the Falcons a pair of first-rounders to get him. You be the judge.

title: Ravens Week 8 Inactives, With Lamar Jackson Returning
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens may be a few more AFC losses from being out of contending more and into player-development mode with another season in the balance, but they are leaning into their experience Sunday at Buffalo.
With the return of Lamar Jackson from a three-week absence with a high-ankle sprain, Baltimore badly needs to beat the Bills to turn the tide after blowing double-digit leads in the second half two straight weeks in losses to the division rival Bengals and Browns. With that in mind, general manager Eric DeCosta is leaning into his highest-paid players at Buffalo – despite their historic struggles – and the inactives for this game speak to that dynamic.
The Ravens also knew their top pick, guard Vega Ioane (14th overall and the best center on the team as well) was out with a knee injury. Perhaps he can get back for Thursday’s game bit this is obviously a short week. Rookie receiver Elijah Sarratt (fourth round) was also inactive and the Baltimore native has yet to find his way in this offense.
Rookie slot corner Chandler Rivers (fifth-round) has strong instincts attack the ball on screens in front of him but has been picked on badly in coverage – Baltimore’s slot defense has been atrocious - and has plenty to do with them getting DeCosta-ed week after week – and he is not playing in this game, either.
Young guard Emery Jones has been battling injury which means a sixth new offensive line combination in eight games, with struggling Andrew Vorhees likely thrust back into that role. Aeneas Peebles – the only defensive tackle DeCosta took in a historically significant 2025 DT draft despite it being a big need – still cannot see the field and he was scratched again. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is again the emergency third QB.
Starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins was ruled out with injury on Friday.
Jackson’s return gives this team a chance to reverse the course of its season, but it carries almost identical warts and serious personnel concerns as the pathetic product DeCosta fielded in 2025, when he won a power struggle with potential Hall of Fame head coach John Harbaugh, gutting that staff that included offensive coordinator Todd Monken, now head coach of the Browns and a top midseason candidate for NFL Coach of the Year, along with Harbaugh (Giants).
DeCosta and team president Sashi Brown branded this a Super Bowl contender when they hired novice head coach Jesse Minter and built one of only two staffs in the entire NFL without a former NFL head coach on the roster . Yet about 20 percent of the Week 1 roster was compromised of players without an NFL snap, while at the same time the bulk of the team-record $370M payroll was going to veterans decidedly on the decline with ridiculously bloated contracts (Roquan Smith, Marlon Humphrey, Mark Andrews, John Simpson).
The coming weeks will be critical to determining how much longer they can afford to prop up some of them, as we discussed recently with longtime NFL GM Marty Hurney on "The Daily Flock."
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Predicting What Lamar Jackson Will Do Vs. Bills In First Game Back From Injury
full_text:
It’s been a month since we were able to forecast what Lamar Jackson was about to do to an NFL defense.
Man, have we missed doing the research and, especially, watching him play. We were quite on point about what to expect from him in each of the first four games, and unfortunately Jackson suffered a high-ankle sprain at the end of the first half in Week 4 and the Ravens spiraled without him (7-14 all time when he can’t start). He covers up the repeated failures of general manager Eric DeCosta , and he is the genius – not rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle who has been getting exposed lately – and he has carved up the Bills in the regular season throughout his career and this Bills defense is particularly vulnerable.
So what do we expect on Sunday afternoon with Jackson just back from injury? Well, after being able to practice fully all week, and given the magnitude of this game (it’s must-win for Baltimore, one could argue), and given the Ravens’ proclivity for getting DeCosta-ed every week without him ( blowing a double-digit lead in the second half and losing ), I believe we are going to see the two-time MVP in do-it-all mode from the onset, whether that’s how Doyle is calling the game or not.
Jackson knows best. And the Ravens best operate accordingly
The Ravens should get over their projected team total here and 30 points feels right (of course, that’s unlikely to be enough to win given the state of Baltimore’s defense, which needs changes before the trade deadline) . Jackson has faced Buffalo five times in the regular season, and they average 33.2 points/game when he does. Buffalo will likely move the ball at will , so pressure will be on to score.
The Bills rely on a few pass rushers to get them off the field, but the secondary is among the worst in the NFL and we doubt they figured out how to overcome their talent limitations in the bye week. Doyle’s early-game scripts have been remarkable, Zay Flowers has been featured in those looks, and that won’t change against these defensive backs.
Flowers, despite missing time to injury and despite Jackson missing half the season, leads the NFL in receptions per game in the first half (27 in 6 games), and first-half receiving yards (486) at an astounding 18 yards/reception. Doyle will go after this group – Buffalo has allowed 26 passes of 20 yards or more (third in NFL despite already having their bye) and 15 of 25 yards or more (fifth-most) and they don’t have anyone who can handle Flowers with a two-way go in the slot.
Buffalo’s slot defense is even worse than Jesse Minter’s – which is saying something – ranking 28th in allowing a 122.2 rating and 9.2 yards/attempt (26th). We anticipate explosives with YAC and air yards and could see Jackson having a 50-yard pass and 25-yard run.
Jackson tends to prove a point when people doubt his physical ability and playing against Josh Allen, the rare running QB who can rival him, tends to get Jackson’s wheels going, too. He’s never had a 20 yard run against Buffalo in the regular season but he tends to extend drives repeatedly with his legs.
Jackson averages 8 runs for 55 yards against these guys and he has at least six carries in every meeting with them in the regular season and this defense, while 15th in Defensive Expected Points Added vs QB runs, is allowing 5.5 yards/carry to them but has not really been tested in ways that Jackson’s can challenge them.
Doyle’s run scheme is failing with Derrick Henry starting to show his age at 32 – and leading the NFL in carries, while averaging just 3.9 yards/rush (gulp) – and this offensive line is not good. Jackson is going to have to scoot and make things happen himself outside the pocket to revive a dormant attack. We believe he will do just that and believe he has to run for 3-5 first downs and 65 or more yards if he’s going to keep pace with what Baltimore’s defense is going to yield to Allen (Ravens are 30th in EPA vs QB runs despite not facing anyone who really wants to run this season).
Jackson was a top five QB in the redzone before his injury. Doyle has defaulted to the failing run game without him – as he should with Snoop Huntley in charge – but that’s over now. And handing it off to Henry in short-yardage situations has been a disaster. Jackson will finish multiple drives with redzone TD passes and we suspect rookie tight ends Josh Cuevas and Matthew Hibner to get chances to hit pay dirt.
The Ravens need Jackson's genius most in the RZ, and there is no reason to doubt it.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Red Zone Report: What’s Working And Failing And What Must Change in Week 8
full_text:
There is so much going on with the Ravens at a macro level right now between coaches and general managers getting exposed and all the second-half collapses and blaming fans for not being loud enough and with team legends excoriating this current edition on social media, it’s easy to gloss over specific micro issues.
And, with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson coming back from a three-week absence due to a high-ankle sprain, it’s also easy to fall into the trap that he’s going to just solve everything. Indeed, he is the ultimate deodorant that covers up Eric DeCosta’s nasty work as an evaluator and negotiator and “steward” of the franchise, and they need him desperately. They need him to save the offense and therefore provide an even greater safety net to a defense that’s on fraud alert.
The Ravens especially need him to find ways to finish drives in the second half of games after Baltimore has failed to score after the half in two straight games with “genius” offensive coordinator Declan Doyle at the helm, stalling out in the redzone when they manage to get there. Jackson can’t do much to help the Ravens defensive redzone woes, but the more points the better ahead of what could be a shootout with the Bills in Buffalo on Sunday.
The Ravens rank 20th in the NFL in redzone TD% differential (-4.2%) and 25th in redzone scoring differential (-8.3%) and no one in the media is even bringing it up because of all the other chaos and noise. But if they don’t fix it soon, this season will spiral into the abyss like last year’s and they’ll keep getting Decosta-ed (blowing second-half, double-digit leads to lose) week after week.
RedZone TD Efficiency : 62.5% (13th) 3rd-and-1/4th-and-1 Rush Conv : 25% (27th)
Total Pass EPA/Game : 0.50 (14th) Total Run EPA/G : -.27 (21st)
The issues with the offensive line are getting compounded as the field compresses and the play book constricts, and as the rookie play caller gets into clutch situations in the second half of games. Doyle spoke about wanting to script even more of the game as he explained his self-scout this week; um, yeah I am not sure thinking you can have even more of the game called a day before it starts is the answer, but whatever.
“I would say I probably haven't stuck to that second-half script enough,”’ Doyle offered this week, “and I probably have to stick with my guns a little more at times, and that would be kind of my own self-evaluation of that.”
I would say Jackson is the only thing keeping this from being a bottom-eight offense, and you’d best defer to his true genius in the redzone and let him do what he wants and follow what he sees. Stay out of the way. And lean into him doing what he wants at the line of scrimmage.
The best offensive lineman on the team – rookie Vega Ioane – is out with a knee injury it will be yet another new offensive line combination (the sixth unique one to start a game). Doyle also needs to change his play calling trends now that Snoop Huntley is making way for Jackson. The Ravens are throwing the ball just 39% of the time in the RZ – 30th in the NFL – and with tight end Mark Andrews fully cooked and this team’s only big-play threat quite small to go real damage in the redzone (Zay Flowers) Doyle better start flooding this area with his rookie tight ends.
The short-yardage game with Derrick Henry (who looks like a 32-year old back and needs help in the backfield by the deadline ) hasn’t been good for over a year now, this line stinks inside (paying a ridiculous ransom of a struggling offensive lineman will go down as another DeCosta FAIL , and Doyle better lean into the option game and RPOs in this part of the field.
RedZone TD Efficiency: 66.7% (T-20th) Opposing Passer Rating : 111.7 (25th)
Pressure Rate: 30% (20th) Third Down Conv: 46.3% (T-20th)
Total Pass D EPA: -1.61 (23rd)                                 T otal Rush D EPA : -0.84 (29th)
Rookie head coach in Jesse Minter, no former head coaches on staff ( just the way DeCosta designed it ), trying to manage a defense through an entire game and run a sideline and coach an entire team for the first time on an alleged Super Bowl contender, was a big ask. Of course it’s manifesting more profoundly in the second half of games as injuries mount and adjustments are demanded in all three phases. And of course that nativity shows up most in special situations: RZ is everything in this modern game (with defensive coordinator often willing to bleed out yards between the 20s playing soft zone – and that’s all Minter does).
His defensive backs are a tragedy right now, they don’t seem connected or comfortable with his zone assignments and longtime head coach Marvin Lewis pointed out on “The Daily Flock” the obvious communication issues and bad fits in key moments. Minter best get that fixed first.
“It just starts with us putting them in a better position,” Minter said Monday. “Always starts with the coaching, in my opinion, and I'll leave it at that."
As always, we have suggestions (and they read everything, trust me).
Start with what Wink Martindale, the guy who created this defense with some help from Minter and Seahawks Super Bowl winning coach Mike McDonald, who agreed with me that Minter “needs to blitz more.” Let’s start there. DeCosta’s secondary lacks anything close to a play maker on the back end (Kyle Hamilton is a linebacker).
He also needs to get Marlon Humphrey into the slot in these tight-field situations, he should have him blitzing more from the slot and getting Roquan Smith off the field in some of these dime looks – yeah I get it he wears the green dot – is something I called for way back in the summer when defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver guaranteed an impact season.
This chart would say otherwise .
The sooner DeCosta’s made men start seeing more of the bench , the better the chances of actually keeping this from being another total disaster.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Four Storylines For Ravens' Matchup vs. Bills
full_text:
After a massively disappointing performance at home last week, the Baltimore Ravens will be back on the road in Week 8 for their third straight game against an AFC opponent with a winning record when they take on the Buffalo Bills on Sunday afternoon at Highmark Stadium.
Coming off an embarrassing loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 7, in which they blew another double-digit lead after a first-half shutout, the Ravens currently have the worst record in the AFC North at 4-3 and are deservedly alone in last place.
There are several intriguing storylines surrounding this matchup between these two teams with first-year head coaches and Super Bowl aspirations. Here are the top four.
Following his first full week of practice in a month since he suffered a high ankle sprain that caused him to miss the last three games, the two-time MVP will be making his long-awaited return to the starting lineup just in time for arguably the Ravens' toughest test to date. He was a full participant all three days and was removed from the final injury report without a game designation .
"I'm always excited when I'm able to be back on the field with my guys, man," Jackson said. "[I want to] put us in the win column [and] help us get another dub. That's what I'm ready to do."
In Jackson's absence, the offense fell into a godawful rut, failing to score a single point in the second half of three of the team's last four games. The deep passing game was essentially nonexistent without him, and the ground game suffered as well, since opposing defenses didn't respect their ability to push the ball downfield and consistently loaded the box as a result.
"The sense of urgency is extremely high," Jackson said. "The divisional game didn't go the way we wanted to last week, [but] guys [have] just been hitting the ground running. [We are] just trying to get back to where we should be [in] all phases; special teams, defense and offense."
Having Jackson back, who is unquestionably the heart and soul of the team, will give them a much-needed jolt and a sorely missed confidence boost that their odds of winning are high because he's available. Nevertheless, they can't continue to be a team that only plays well in all three phases when things are going their way and can't pick themselves back up or find a way to stop the bleeding when adversity strikes.
After their other highly compensated core leaders on both sides of the ball failed miserably in their duties when it came to uplifting the team with their words and play on the field last week as the Bengals stormed back, they'll be under a microscope in this game. They need to show that they can bring their own energy and retake momentum if they get punched in the mouth instead of laying back and getting pummeled into submission over and over again, as was the case a week ago.
"We can't let the things dictate how we're going to play," left tackle Ronnie Stanley said. "We can't let things that we can't control affect us and not being a momentum-based team. We have to be able to rise above all that and play to our own standards and as if we just do this because this is what we believe, more than because people are watching or worried about the perception."
The Ravens have been held to under 100 rushing yards in back-to-back games for the first time in two seasons. Having their star dual-threat signal caller back under center will help lighten the box because of his ability to attack opposing defenses through the air with his arm and present another dangerous running element with his legs.
However, just not having their No. 1 quarterback wasn't the only reason they've struggled mightily to move the ball on the ground with any consistency or explosiveness over the past two weeks. If they want to get five-time Pro Bowl running back Derrick Henry rolling again going up against a Bills run defense that he has averaged 146.3 yards and scored four touchdowns against since joining the Ravens, they'll need to block better along the offensive line and on the perimeter for him to get to the second and third levels.
Henry has been getting contacted in the backfield and at the line of scrimmage for negative plays and minimal gains far too often. With first-round starting right guard Vega Ioane out with a knee injury in this game, they'll need their struggling remaining guards to stop up and stop blowing so many blocks, as well as better blocking execution from their tight ends.
"There are too many times where we have unblocked players that are unaccounted for that should be accounted for in the scheme," offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said. "We have to clean that up as a staff, as players, to be able to go out and execute really what looks good on paper, but we don't play the game on paper. So, as things change, pressures show up and things like that, we have to be able to echo the calls that handle those problems."
Last week, the Ravens went from making Cincinnati's Joe Burrow look rattled and playing at a less-than-pedestrian level in the first half to having a near-flawless performance over the final two quarters. He led five straight touchdown-scoring drives and threw for more touchdowns than he had incompletions, with a 4-2 ratio. Keeping Buffalo's bulldozing behemoth, that is, Josh Allen, will be an even taller task this week because of how dangerous a threat he presents with his strong arm as well as his legs on scrambles and designed runs.
The Bills don't have an advantage when it comes to talent at the skill positions, and if the Ravens' interior defensive line plays up to its potential, the two teams are pretty much equally matched in the trenches. This means this game may ultimately come down to how well they can limit Allen as a runner and improvisational passer on extended and broken plays because he's especially lethal on plays where he buys time for his running backs to leak out of the backfield and pass catchers to uncover deep downfield.
"[It] takes all 11," defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said. "We've got to stop the run, first and foremost, [and] try not to give them [any] 50/50 run [or] pass situations. We know any time it is a pass that can turn into a run too with Josh [Allen]. [It's a] tremendous challenge [with a] tremendous quarterback. We know he's an elite [player], so it's going to take all of us."
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On SI focusing primarily on original content and reporting. He provides analysis, breakdowns, profiles, and reports on important news and transactions from and about the Ravens. His professional resume as a sports reporter includes covering local events, teams, and athletes in his hometown of Anchorage, Alaska for Anchorage Daily News. His coverage on the Ravens and other NFL teams has been featured on Heavy.com/sports, Maryland Sports Blog and most recently Baltimore Beatdown from 2021 until 2025.

title: Ravens Need To Do Some Soul Searching Ahead Of Critical Make-Or-Break Slate
full_text:
There's no denying that Lamar Jackson is the heart and soul of the Baltimore Ravens' offense and team as a whole, and fellow future Hall of Famer, Derrick Henry, admitted to as much when he spoke to the media on Wednesday.
The two-time league MVP has missed the Ravens' last three games since suffering what he later personally revealed was a high ankle sprain in Week 4.
"He's the leader of this offense, so anytime he's out there, it's always great," Henry said. "I know he wants to be out there with us and to put us in the best position to win. He wants the guys to play great as well. So, I'll be excited whenever he's back out there, and I look forward to it."
After rallying to notch a come-from-behind victory over the Atlanta Falcons in primetime in their first game without him, they went from sitting atop the AFC North standings to falling all the way to the bottom after dropping back-to-back games to the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals over the past two weeks.
Despite being without arguably the best player in the league when healthy, they built early double-digit leads and shut out both of their rivals, only to get shut out and get outscored by 10-plus points in the second half of each deflating loss.
This past Sunday's lopsided 35-13 loss to the Bengals was equally discouraging and infuriating because of how well they played on both sides of the ball in the first half compared to the second. The lack of leadership and juice without Jackson was on full display as they put up little-to-no resistance as Joe Burrow and Co. came storming from behind to beat them on their own home turf.
It marked the second year in a row that they allowed this particular opponent to come into M&T Bank Stadium and notch a statement win by multiple scores instead of getting sent home packing.
All signs are pointing towards Jackson being available for the Ravens ' massive AFC showdown coming up this Sunday on the road against the Buffalo Bills after he's been a full participant in practice for the first time in nearly a month.
However, they are a setback away (normally a 4-6 week injury), a wrong plant or big hit away from being right back where they've been the past three weeks, looking to avoid letting history repeat itself and keep their hopes of returning to the playoffs alive without their best player.
Every team with a franchise quarterback, especially one as generationally gifted as Jackson, should be able to rely on him to give them a chance to emerge victorious whenever he's out on the field, but they shouldn't be so overdependent on him that they can't find ways to close out games without him.
The Ravens' offense has sputtered in Jackson's absence outside of promising and potent opening scripts. That shouldn't have any bearing on how the defense performs from one half to the next when it comes to maintaining focus, communication and executing proper technique, all of which waned far too many high-leverage moments in the second half over the past two weeks.
Some of these epic collapses would by no means be excusable. Still, they could be somewhat understandable for a team littered with and heavily relying on a young core of ascending playmakers who lack a plethora of big-game experience. That isn't and hasn't been the case for the Ravens since Jackson was still on his rookie deal.
The majority of the players who are responsible for the recurring mistakes that blow leads and make them a hard watch without him are his fellow established starters with years of experience and a number of impressive accolades under their belt.
"I think there's a level of accountability, especially when you're creating your own standard and culture and things like that, you have to be able to hold those guys accountable," head coach Jesse Minter said Monday.
"At the same time, normally the really good ones are the first ones coming in and saying, 'That's my fault. This was me. How do I do this better?' And so, we have a bunch of guys that take accountability when they mess something up, just like we have a coaching staff that does the same thing."
With Jackson set to be back in action against the Bills, there's no refuting that his return will provide them with a "big boost," but they can't continue to be a momentum team that constantly needs to be energized by a singular player or a turning of the tide in a game.
"We all know how good of a player he is, but we also don't want to rely on him having to carry us as a team," left tackle Ronnie Stanley said. Whoever's in there, we're confident that they're going to be able to perform, and we still feel like we had enough to win all the games that we had without him, but without a doubt, him being back would definitely be a boost."
The Ravens will face a pair of AFC powerhouses who are both currently leading their respective divisions and are legit Super Bowl contenders in back-to-back games in less than five days. After traveling to upstate New York to take on Josh Allen the Bills on Sunday afternoon, they'll turn around and host Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars in primetime on Thursday night.
This team remains strong on paper and appears to be getting healthier at the right time , but they have to look inward at the kind of team they want to be and what kind of product they want to put on the field moving forward. Their fragile mental fortitude, as a result of past trauma, has continued to be the root cause of their downfall, and that needs to change.
"It's okay for players to have scars and coaches to have scars," Minter said. "I have my own scars from other places that I've been, and things like that. But it's also us collectively together, let's look at what we've been through together. Let's keep chasing how we fix ourselves in those moments.
"We've proven a couple times that we can do well in those moments, and we've proven a couple times that we haven't had what it took to close out those really tight games. Let's keep attacking it together. Let's keep adjusting our process and finding a better way for us to play well in those big moments. That's what we'll constantly be searching for."
A huge talking point around the Ravens' building in both the locker room and in meeting rooms has been the leadership, or rather, lack thereof, from prominent players aside from Jackson, especially with how lifeless the team looked on the sidelines during the second half of the Bengals' losses as their rivals rallied past them.
"I can speak for myself. I pride myself in being one of the leaders on this team," Henry said. "I am one of the vets, and I haven't been doing a good enough job as far as leading.
"When I talked about it being flat on the sidelines, when we don't have energy or things are not going the way they're supposed to, somebody has to bring that spark, whether it's speaking or out there on the field making a play that turns everything around. That's what I need to do. The leaders have to lead, have to have accountability and have to bring the juice."
Stanley shared that some of the leaders met after the game without Minter suggesting or even having to tell them to address how they can improve in that vital aspect of the game.
"Just seeing the energy that we had on the sideline when things aren't going our way is something that needs to change," Stanley said. "A lot of people have different ways they lead and different leadership styles, but I think being more vocal is something that I can get better at personally."
Following Thursday's practice, three-time All Pro safety Kyle Hamilton, one of the Ravens' most outspoken leaders, admitted that the players and coaches come together to have some "grown-man conversations" and feels confident they can get things turnaround.
"This season can go one of two different directions, and there's obviously the direction that we want to go in, so I think everybody took steps this week to give us our best chance to do that," Hamilton said.
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On…

title: Top 3 Reasons The Bills Could Expose The Ravens In Week 8
full_text:
The Ravens are getting back their franchise savior for Sunday’s game, with Lamar Jackson back from nearly a month out with a high-ankle sprain.
Jackson says the pain is “bearable” and rookie head coach Jesse Minter – who claimed for nearly three weeks this was a day-to-day-situation – is pushing the idea, hard, that Jackson will be all-systems-go and able to run as much as ever. We’ll see about all of that, but with Baltimore’s season on the brink, and it’s roster and leadership and failing general manager all in question, and with the Bills coming off the bye, this will be quite the challenge.
In situations like these, teams that do have a backbone and accountability tend to rise up and play their best ball of the season and make a statement. And that’s what will be required for the Ravens’ stumbling defense, which has not been any good for years and which is where a bulk of GM’s Eric DeCosta’s nastiest work has left even Minter – hailed as a schematic genius – utterly clueless and unmasked in the second half of games.
Getting DeCosta-ed 17 times since 2019 is no joke, and they’re managed to do it (blow double-digit leads to lose) two weeks in a row in critical AFC games. They’ve done it under two head coaches and seven coordinators but just one front office. Hmm. So maybe we get the best of what Baltimore will ever have to offer, and that had best be the case.
Even 75% of Lamar should be enough to put up points on a Buffalo secondary that is among the worst in football and has massive holes everywhere. But can the Ravens do enough to keep Josh Allen from putting up a point or two more than Jackson? I have my reservations and in particular about these four key matchup elements :
The Ravens have yet to be tested on the ground, at all. They haven’t faced an opponent that even feigns to run the ball at all; the only one that could, the Colts in Week 1, didn’t because they had a stupid game plan and they fell desperately behind early. The Saints, Bengals, Cowboys, Titans, don’t threaten anyone, and so the Ravens being 12th in success rate (22nd in EPA) probably flatters them.
The Bills are arguably the best rushing team in the NFL with a multi-faceted attack James Cook is tops in rushing yards since the start of last season and Josh Allen is a historically significant running QB who is a TD machine on the ground. When they run from middle to the left it’s six yards a carry; $30M “closer”’ Trey Hendrickson always lines up over left tackle; good luck with that.
Longtime Ravens defensive coordinator Wink Martindale said it best on “The Daily Flock” this week – Hendrickson can’t stop the run enough to get on the field on early downs for him and is a “designated pass rusher,” no matter how much DeCosta paid him . Oh, and the Ravens most complete edge defender, Tavius Robinson, is out for the season.
Suggestion : They’d better be willing to play second-round pick Zion Young way more than they have been in this one. If Minter uses a LB like Trenton Simpson to spy Allen, I suspect it comes back to bite him in the pass game.
We have been chronicling this deficiency on a weekly basis and it could be acute Sunday. Joe Burrow has so much success shredding Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey on the outside racking up 35-unanswered points Sunday he didn’t need to ping tight end Mike Gesicki in the slot much. Allen is top 5 in the NFL with a 117 rating throwing to the slow since the start of last season (18 TDs – 6 INTs) and his emerging TE Dalton Kincaid is going to be a handful for this group.
The Ravens have seen the second-fewest targets to TEs in the NFL, but allow a 132.5 rating when they are thrown to, and Kincaid is catching everything he sees this season. Khalil Shakir will tear up the Ravens smaller dime defenders if they get that match up and DJ Moore (questionable) is a two-way go is a problem and he could be back for this one too.
The free yards in the slot have been a blight on Minter’s defense and if he keeps up the same dime looks with the same personnel he will get cooked again.
Suggestion : Hamilton probably needs to do the job on the tight end and Marlon Humphrey needs to be in the slot and TJ Tampa needs to get a run on the outside. Minter better be willing to get into more man looks and blitz Allen, because he will shred this defense in the quick game just like Burrow did if he isn’t in duress. (Oh and dump Humphrey's salary by the deadline)
The Ravens have doomed themselves with their character flaws week after week. If they start slowly, and have to chase the game, with a QB who was out nearly a month, that’s not great. And even if they build a nice early lead, well, we know how that goes.
The lack of experience on this coaching staff and the lack of intensity from the highest-paid veterans on the defense is a toxic combination. Minter and defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver were falling all over themselves to talk around some of their issues – blaming the crowd was quite a touch – but there better be some tough love going on in those meeting rooms.
Getting John Harbagh run out of town for these kinds of losses and then walking all over the new guy is an ugly look. Things always seem too comfortable when the GM is buddies with certain guys and plays favorites but its time for Minter to step up and shake things up. (Martindale explains the impact it has on a coaching staff and locker room here)
Suggestion : Better be ready to bench people. Needs to get real. Their paychecks are guaranteed, but DeCosta isn’t a coach as much as he preens and pretends he is on the sidelines. Trenton Simpson for Roquan Smith, Hendrickson on a pitch count, Humphrey on his way to the bench have to be on the table, and fast, if this garbage continues. If Mark Andrews plays ahead of rookies Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas on offense it’s a sign of what an unserious, totally political operation they are running. Wake up.
