title: What To Expect From Lamar Jackson in Week 8: Ravens MVP QB Updates Ankle Injury
full_text:
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed on Friday that the team expects Lamar Jackson to start Sunday in Buffalo after a third-straight full day of practice and sounded hopeful that the two-time MVP will be able to utilize his legs as much as possible.
Jackson, who said the pain has subsided to a large degree, returned to practice on Wednesday, able to put in a full day of work for the first time since suffering the ankle injury.  And he has continued to do more since. Snoop Huntley had served as the backup in that stretch during which the Ravens fell to 4-3 after losing consecutive games to AFC North teams in which they blew a double-digit lead. The team’s hope is that the rest and recovery have put Jackson in a position in which he will not be compromised by the ankle injury; given how bad the offensive line has been much of this season, that’s hugely important.
“I think he’ll look like Lamar Jackson,” Minter said after Friday’s practice. “He’s just done such a good job dealing with the injury … Now he’ll be in a position to play Lamar Jackson football.”
Jackson said the pain in his ankle is “bearable” and thus he can play: “I feel like I’m no longer a statue. I’m able to move around a little better. It’s time to give it a shot.”
Jackson said swelling in the ankle last weekend, after limited practices, precluded him from playing in Week 7.
Jackson suffered the ankle injury at the end of the first half in Week 4, trying to escape a sack, when he was caught from behind and his left ankle twisted in an extreme manner. Jackson made it clear he was told it was a high-ankle sprain which he called “very, very painful” when he met the media for the first time since the injury last Friday.
The Ravens insisted on having the rookie head coach refer to it as “day-to-day,” relentlessly, even through two straight weeks of Jackson doing nothing or next-to-nothing on the practice field. That only heightened the scrutiny around the situation, leading to some suggesting perhaps he could have returned sooner (and several prominent national reporters were pushing that narrative, leaving one to wonder who they were getting that directive from, because it clearly wasn’t Jackson).
“Why would you second guess me?” Jackson said Friday. “Why would you second guess me.”
Then again not much with Jackson is normal, especially in regards to general manager Eric DeCosta. Having him on a non-exclusive franchise tag at the end of his rookie deal and making him play out that first contract; opining after Buffalo’s Josh Allen got a new deal in March of 2025 that he didn’t have much contract work of his own to tend to do. And now Jackson has reached a point with this failing front office where he will be able to act as a de-facto free agent as soon as this season ends.
It’s always weird with this sophomoric GM and the greatest thing that has happened to this franchise, arguably, ever, from a personnel standpoint (a QB this transformational at the end of the first round?). Now they need Jackson to prop up a roster with massive warts and major holes – same as ever, especially a secondary that DeCosta likes to pretend is his strength . Now Jackson has to try to right another season spiraling amid pleas from an overmatched coaching staff for someone to be a leader .
Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, who now sounds like he wants to script the entire game beforehand (how long before he’s back on the sidelines calling plays?), had better be willing to activate Jackson’s legs more than he has to this point; the traditional run game with Derrick Henry is a joke behind another DeCosta offensive line, and they need to attack the perimeter with speed as much as possible.
A third straight loss, with a quick turnaround against Jacksonville on Thursday, could send a season teetering on the brink right over the ledge.
“The sense of urgency is extremely high,” Jackson said of a critical game with the Bills.
“I think we’ll see a great version of Lamar,” Minter said.
He’d better. He’ll need it.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Case For The Ravens Being NFL Trade Deadline Sellers. And Who Should Go ASAP
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens might be three weeks away from truly pivoting to playing their youngsters and embracing the fact that the alleged Super Bowl contender carried 20 percent of its roster with rookies to open the season in the first place.
If they lose to the Bills and Jaguars in the span of a few days, and if their second-half defense continues to be historically suspect, and if their novice coaches continue to looks horribly overmatched after halftime ( they should have hired them help ), and if Jesse Minter keeps wondering why his $370M roster can’t display any heart and leadership, then it just might be that this team is a mere extension of last year's disaster, and that general manager Eric DeCosta is one of the biggest frauds in the NFL, and that Baltimore is doomed again.
This might just be a bloated, complacent roster that is the handiwork of an entitled, stubborn, egomaniacal fake smart guy (just like Mike Elias), who skirts accountability and blames others and curries favor with checked-out billionaires. Meantime John Harbaugh and Todd Monken – the men allegedly holding back DeCosta’s treasure trove of talent – compete for NFL Coach of the Year honors elsewhere.
DeCosta tends to put own self-interest ahead of the team, wanting “his guys” to make him look good for rewarding them with unnecessarily rich extensions while primo young talent leaves the building (which is why the baby-faced coach is forced to start guys, who are replacement-level talent, at best, making top-10 money at their positions).
But imagine if the Ravens had an honest broker running the team. Someone clear-eyed – not a politician obsessed with his media clippings who is constantly working to hone that image – who could see this Frankenstein roster for what it is. What would they do? Well, as longtime NFL GM Marty Hurney suggested on “The Daily Flock” several times this year and again this week, this was always going to be the final year in Baltimore for a legion of starters and key reserves, and this organization might need to shift into player-development mode soon.
“At some point if things still have not gotten right, I do think you have to make that switch and start playing more of the young guys,” Hurney told me, “and try to make that transition. Because I think that every team hits it and the Ravens do a really good job, as good as anybody of really turning it over and not having the ‘window; philosophy, because they've always drafted well and had a lot of draft choices. But right now, you kind of feel like this is a time where the young guys need to step up and it feels like there's a little bit of a transition taking place in Baltimore."
Indeed, so, wouldn’t it make sense to load up on draft picks – even very low draft picks because these are more salary dumps than football trades (again, blame DeCosta and blame a half-interested owner for not rebuilding his decaying front office when he fired Harbaugh). Getting DeCosta-ed 17 times since this guy was handed the reigns from Ozzie Newsome is a sign that even Lamar Jackson can’t overcome this mess, isn’t it?
There are some moves they could make to buy on the fringes ... but DeCosta may have created more problems already with a desperate deal for Cam Jurgens . Not sure he should be trusted to add more.
DeCosta is beyond a failure when it comes to extending his QBs contract like any half-assed GM would. So Jackson can decide if he wants to go to Miami, or whatever, and DeCosta knows it, which explains why he acted like a fool at his pre-season press conference when pressed on this topic.
But if Jackson doesn’t want to take their money, he doesn’t have to, and with an $85M cap hit the Ravens would have to move him. So there’s that. Then consider that it’s painfully obvious that Ronnie Stanley, Mark Andrews, Derrick Henry, Roquan Smith, Marlon Humphrey, Rashod Bateman and Calais Campbell are at the end here (and would be if this team had a real GM in charge). And that of their young players on rookie deals, only Tavius Robinson (on season-ending IR) and Trent Simpson would be making a case for an extension.
That’s bleak folks. But that’s DeCosta, who would rather give Humphrey the 10th most money of any corner in the NFL, than admit he did another stupid contract structure and acknowledge his obvious decline  just pay him $4M to leave.
And in terms of blue chip players on a contract extension, there’s Kyle Hamilton and Zay Flowers and Nnamdi Madubuike and that’s it. Not much.
But their culture is clearly warped - DeCosta is at the core of that - and it’s not getting better and I’d be perfectly fine with taking whatever you can get for Smith and Andrews and Bateman and Humphrey right now and embracing a future without them. Move Simpson to Smith’s spot, or Teddye Buchanan, give TJ Tampa a run for Humphrey, and they drafted two tight ends who are already better than Andrews.
Now, let's be real - no one wants those veterans. No one would give DeCosta anything for Andrews after the 2024 season and he insisted in paying him again, anyway. Oh, and the real problem is his drafts have stunk too, so the next man up at these positions could be perilous.
Sending a message to the locker room and starting to position for the future isn’t crazy. If those guys can’t lead – and Minter says he’s desperately searching for leaders – then empower your youth. I don’t think the drop-off would be significant in most cases (maybe not even going from Stanley to Carson Vinson)
They're going to need to convince Jackson why he should stay, and almost none of those veterans will be back here in 2027, whether the QB is or not.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Thursday Injury Report Includes Major News For Lamar Jackson
full_text:
The Ravens have been coy in their handling of Lamar Jackson’s ankle injury for a month now.
Since the two-time MVP suffered the injury on a sack from behind at the end of the first half in Week 4, Baltimore’s offense has fallen onto a major funk, and rookie head coach Jesse Minter has walked a verbal minefield about conveying some semblance of the extent of the injury to his paying customers – through the media – but also needing to respect the player’s reputation and make it clear this is a significant setback for him to navigate that.
Ravens public relations has a poor reputation in such matters, throwing a novice head coach into the mix has only exacerbated the messaging issues, and Minter would barely saying anything on Wednesday about his quarterback other than the team would be issuing an injury report – as mandated by the NFL – and Jackson would be listed on it in some capacity. Lesson learned, it seems (be careful who you take counsel from in The Castle, rook; they’ll hide and cower and let you take the fall).
Turns out Jackson practiced in full on Wednesday , the first time he did so since before facing the Titans on Oct. 4, and he did the same on Thursday. The longer this situation played out – it was obvious he was going to miss at least two games from the onset – it became clear that Jackson was going to have to get through a full week of full practices before being activated to return to play. He is checking those boxes now.
Kyle Hamilton, the Ravens best defensive player, returned to practice Thursday as did rookie guard Vega Ioane, who just suffered a knee inury that some reported would be multiple weeks (Minter did not close the door on him playing Sunday) and middle linebcker Roquan Smith was back on the field, too, as all did not take part in any capacity Wednesday.
Should Jackson practice fully on Friday – it’s a limited workday and barring some totally unforeseen circumstance that will be the case – it’s fair to expect he will have no injury designation on Friday’s injury report. He was ruled out on Friday on each of the first two weeks after his injury – which Jackson has described as a “very, very painful” high-ankle sprain. Last week he was listed as questionable and then the team announced on Saturday afternoon that he had been downgraded to out (which raised anew questions about their public handling of this situation all along).
While Ravens rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle was being hailed as a “genius” all summer, he was quick to point out himself on Thursday he is only seven games into calling plays and is trying to adjust his processes with one of the worst second-half offenses in the NFL. Jackson is the genius, he covers up the warts on a roster that is 7-14 without him, while wins 70% of the regular-season games he starts. And if this offense rebounds, it’s because the best player in the league returned (and if it doesn’t out late-summer prediction that Doyle is going to end up calling plays from the sidelines and trying to connect better with his players is going to look sage ).
How much Doyle is willing to lean into Jackson’s legs to boost a moribund run game will be telling; he’s already riding Derrick Henry at an historic rate for any age 32 RB in NFL history , with diminishing returns. The ability to generate explosive plays will be back – Jackson leads the NFL at 10.1 yards/attempts (no one else is above 8.8) – as backup Snoop Huntley doesn’t average even six yards per pass in his NFL career.
Henry has averaged just 3.4 yards per rush the last four weeks (35th in the NFL). Getting rookie “Joker” Adam Randall (a hybrid RB/TE/H-Back/WR ), off Injured Reserve could add wrinkled for Doyle, too. Something has to change in a major way for Baltimore in the second half and this young staff better figure it out quickly. Consider that without Jackson the Ravens have fallen to 31st in second-half scoring, dead-last in third-down conversions in that half and 29th in three-and-out percentage.
Also consider how it came to pass again that Ravens struggling general manager Eric DeCosta (better do something at the deadline, hoss )  let Jackson enter a potential walk season without a contract extension after the QB had to dangle on a non-exclusive franchise tag and demand a trade to get a fair-market deal after his rookie deal expired, which Baltimore made him play out.
The Miami Dolphins badly need a quarterback and a superstar to market the team around and an identity and they are loaded with draft capital. I’m just sayin .
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Is Ravens GM Eric DeCosta At The Core Of Their Losing Ways? Longtime Coordinator Wink Martindale Thinks So
full_text:
There’s a reason so many Ravens defensive stars from the past took to social media in the aftermath of Baltimore’s pathetic second half Sunday, allowing 35 unanswered points to the Bengals and looking like quitters in the process.
Guys like Ed Reed and Terrell Suggs seemed appalled by it all , the franchise DeCosta-ed for the 17th time since 2019 (blowing a double-digit lead in the second half in a loss), and the one constant during this entire uninspired brand of Ravens football is the general manager, Eric DeCosta, who curries favor with the billionaire boss and divides the organization and plays favorites in the locker room and creates a culture that continually produces spineless results.
Yet that billionaire chose to empower him even more than ever before when he fired John Harbaugh (needed to fire them both ), and with an overmatched novice head coach on board they keep hitting new lows. Rookie coach Jesse Minter is stuck with a legion of bad contracts DeCosta handed out all over that defense, and while there are some schematic changes he is going to have to make (as we discussed with longtime head coach Marvin Lewis here ), he’s also going have a hard time altering the psyche and heart of a football team poisoned by the guy who controls the salaries.
Longtime former Ravens defensive coordinator Wink Martindale, who has known Minter forever and was invited to Ravens practices this offseason and whom Minter helped create the defensive packages that make the hub of this 2026 Ravens defense, is aghast at what’s going on in Baltimore. He knows the role that DeCosta has played in this mess better than most, and kept it real with me on “The Daily Flock” this week.
“This isn't good enough,” Martindale said. “This is not the standard. This is not Baltimore defense.  And you know, I was there first, you know, in 2012 when we won the Super Bowl with Ray Lewis. You think Ray Lewis would put up with that [crap]? You think Ed Reed would put up with that [crap)? You think (Terrell) Suggs would put up with that [crap]? You think Haloti Ngata would put up with that [crap]? …
“You can still hold people accountable and you can still say, ‘This guy's better than this guy because of this this and this. And this guy's got to play, not because of what they get paid, you know, (but because they deserve it). They got a left tackle that's been paid a [crap] ton of money who needs to step up and be a leader, you know, with Ronnie (Stanley). And I love Ronnie, and these guys I’m talking about.
“They’re good people, but God damn it, we want to win in Baltimore. And that's where I was at the longest in my career ever in coaching. I was there for 10 years. So, like my kids who were born in Ohio think they're from Maryland because that's the longest we were in place …  And I just think that they need to step up and say, ‘Here's who we're going to be."’ Yeah. And if they don't, they're going to continue to do the [crap] they're doing.”
Martindale believes $19M corner Marlon Humphrey probably needs to move to safety or just play considerably less, though the team is short of corners despite it being one of DeCosta’s primary fetishes. He wouldn’t play overpaid $30M pass rusher Trey Hendrickson on early downs as much as Baltimore is (but DeCosta demands it with that salary!). Wink believes Minter needs to start blitzing more even though it runs counter to some of his core philosophies. (DeCosta better explore some of these cheap trade deadline options , ASAP)
He gives deep explanations for such on the show. The biggest reason for the organizations falloff, he believes is the move from longtime general manager Ozzie Newsome to DeCosta. And like so many around the NFL know, DeCosta built a reputation and career off of Newsome’s accomplishments, used it to get promoted repeatedly and ingratiated himself incredibly well with Steve Bisciotti back when he was still a minority owner in the team.
“I think the biggest impact was when it went from Ozzie to Eric,” Martindale said, noting DeCosta likes to hang on the sidelines and in the locker room and fraternize with certain players in a way Newsome never considered. And I know what (Owner) Mr. Steve Bisciotti wanted to do with Eric, but I also think it's time to for Eric to step up and win a Super Bowl because, you know, Ozzie’s last draft class (2018, when he selected Lamar Jackson) you can look at his last pick – it was (defensive lineman) Zach Sieler, who’s had three contracts down at Miami now.
“And I know their (scouting and evaluation) system and I would do the same system that they have there. But there's also times where you’ve got to come to dinner and say here's what it is, and not just keep patting yourself on the back because you get an A++ in every draft (from the media).”
Truthbombs. The show is loaded with them. Not everybody can stomach frauds.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Buffalo Bills Week 8 Inactives: DJ Moore, Dalton Kincaid Will be in Action
full_text:

title: Will Dalton Kincaid Play for Bills Today? TE Fantasy Advice
full_text:
Dalton Kincaid started the season on fire for the Buffalo Bills, but has since slowed down some. Still, he remains one of the more intriguing fantasy options, especially in a high-octane offense.
Even during their Week 7 outing against the Las Vegas Raiders , Kincaid managed double-digit points, hauling in seven passes for 38 yards. His day could have been even better as he had a touchdown called back due to penalty.
Not everything was great for Kincaid, even though that game was on his birthday. The tight end had to leave briefly when he suffered a chest injury. He was able to return and had the week to rest up with the Bills off in Week 7.
Now as the Bills prepare to play the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8 , the question is whether he will suit up. Kincaid was limited during the week, but said he felt good entering the weekend.
“Feeling good. Just how football goes. Some weeks will be worse than others, and then some weeks will feel great. But lucky and grateful enough to be able to go out there and practice," said Kincaid after Wednesday's practice (via WGR's Sal Capaccio ).
Entering the weekend, Kincaid is one of the Bills listed as questionable , but the belief is that he will be able to play. The next question, is how much of an impact can he make against Baltimore. He's been hopeful, although the team will make the determination after warmups.
From @SportsCenter over weekend on Bills: -Dalton Kincaid optimistic about playing. Bills to determine but he’s been hopeful -D.J. Moore could be back for the first time in about a month pic.twitter.com/t00nd6ApGo
Overall, the Ravens have been strong against tight ends this season, although they did surrender two touchdowns last weekend as Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample of the Cincinnati Bengals both found their way to the end zone.
That said, Kincaid hasn't been ultra reliable. He had 130 yards in Week 1 followed by 95 yards in Week 2. Since then, he has yet to record more than 38 yards in a game. Oddly enough, he hit that number twice and has just seven yards in his two other appearances since his breakout.
As for the last time he faced the Ravens, he did finish with four receptions for 48 yards and a touchdown. That's a solid fantasy performance, but at this point, Kincaid is a touchdown-reliant player. Until he proves he's back to running routes the way he did to start the season, fantasy owners should exercise caution.

title: Will DJ Moore Play Today? Injury Update, Fantasy Advice for Bills' WR in Week 8
full_text:
UPDATE: Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore is officially active for Week 8 .
Here we are once again with uncertainty surrounding Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore ahead of the Week 8 game against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday afternoon.
Moore has unfortunately been dealing with a shoulder injury for much of the 2026 season and hasn't played in what seems like forever.
After his impressive debut in Week 1, Moore suffered an AC joint sprain in Week 2 and then re-aggravated the injury in Week 4 and has not appeared in a game since then.

title: NFL Prediction Panel's Consensus Pick for Bills' Return to Action vs. Ravens
full_text:
There are multiple intangibles that favor the Buffalo Bills in their Week 8 home game against the Baltimore Ravens, but the same can be said from the other side.
Yes, the Bills have home-field advantage along with the benefit of extra rest and recovery from the Week 7 bye .
"Extra week's great. Great for everybody, honestly. Just mental, physical reset," said tight end Dalton Kincaid, who is questionable to play due to a rib issue.
The Bills can move one step closer to NFL history by winning again immediately following their bye week. Buffalo is 11-0 over its last 11 games after a bye. The Philadelphia Eagles set the record with 13 consecutive wins from 1999 through 2011.
In addition to the historical trend ebeing in the Bills' side, there's  the fact that Buffalo leads the NFL in scoring offense while Baltimore was forced for 35 points last time out.
It seems as if that is enough to convince Sports Illustrated's weekly prediction panel to back the Bills over the Ravens on November 1.
All eight experts, including senior reporter Albert Breer, picked Buffalo to take care of business in Orchard Park and move to 6-1 overall. As always, SI's selections are straight up. When it comes to the official wagering line, the Bills are a 3.0-point home favorite ( per DraftKings ).
There is, however, reason for caution amongst Bills' backers. On the other sideline, the heavily-criticized Ravens should be a hungry, desperate bunch having lost their last two games.
Furthermore, they should receive a noticeable boost from quarterback Lamar Jackson's return to the lineup after missing three consecutive contests.
"I'm excited. I'm always excited when I'm able to be back on the field with my guys. Put us in the win column, help us get another dub," said Jackson on Friday.
Buffalo not only has to account for the explosive dual threat that Jackson presents. Ravens' primary running back Derrick Henry is on the back end of a Hall-of-Fame career.
"They're two dimensional in everything that can do. It's gonna be a huge task for our defense, but it's a great opportunity for us as well," said Brady.
In his last two regular season games against the Bills, Henry has rushed for a remarkable 368 yards on a combined 42 carries.
Making for an even greater challenge, Buffalo is shorthanded in the defensive secondary. Safety CJ Gardner-Johnson is suspended for the game while slot cornerback Dee Alford will likely be unavailable due to an ankle injury.
Veteran Damar Hamlin will start in Gardner-Johnson's place, and Buffalo added three reinforcements to the defensive backfield on Saturday.
On the plus side, the Bills are expected to welcome back defensive tackle Ed Oliver to the front for the first time since Week 4.

title: Analyzing Three Trade Deadline Targets Linked to Bills
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills need help on defense.
That's probably why NFL analyst Bucky Brooks linked the team to three defenders potentially on the trade block when analyzing the best fits for them at the deadline.
But are any of these players actually realistic options for Brandon Beane?
How he could help: Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams have not been playing their best football this season. The former has surrendered 22 receptions for 233 yards and a 98.8 passer rating when targeted (per PFF), and has missed five tackles in six games. The latter has given up 17 receptions for 146 yards and three TDs, along with a 116.3 passer rating against (per PFF).
Brooks writes, "His instincts, awareness and disruptiveness make him a perfect addition for any roster that lacks an alpha dog in the middle."
Why it won't happen: Aside from the Dolphins likely avoiding trading one of their best players to another AFC East team, Brooks recently signed an extension keeping him in Miami until 2029 as one of the highest paid linebackers in the NFL. The Bills would need to prepare to take on his $17 million cap hit next season, with the two seasons after costing even more.
How he could help: The Bills need help on the back end too. CJ Gardner-Johnson has been wildly inconsistent and is now serving a one-game suspension , and Cole Bishop likely needs more stability in a safety partner in order to take the next step as an emerging player.
Why it might work: Arizona likely won't be a serious contender this year, and already traded away Marvin Harrison Jr. Baker has just one year remaining on his deal, with $0 guaranteed after this season. The Bills would need to take on roughly $8 million of Baker's contract this season, meaning Brandon Beane would need to pull some levers or negotiate salary retention for Arizona to help the Bills stay under the cap.
How he could help: Despite playing in his age-35 season, Mack is still a viable edge rusher. Per PFF, his 10.1% win rate is nearly identical to TJ Watt and ahead of players like Josh Hines-Allen and Brian Burns. In fact, Greg Rousseau is the only Bill with a higher win rate.
Why it shouldn't happen: I would love to see Mack return to Buffalo, but the Bills have already poured too many assets into the edge rusher position and need to spread the wealth. Beane signed Bradley Chubb to a three-year $43.5 million contract and drafted TJ Parker with their first selection in the 2026 NFL Draft. That was with Greg Rousseau and Michael Hoecht already on the roster. The Bills would need to give up a draft pick and roughly $4.5 million in cap space in order to obtain Mack, who would crowd an edge rusher room full of capable bodies already.

title: Buffalo Bills vs. Baltimore Ravens Week 8 Expert Pick Roundup
full_text:

title: Bills Make Three Roster Moves to Bolster Beleaguered Secondary for Sunday vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' defensive secondary needs a boost on multiple fronts.
In addition to being the nervous system of the NFL's next-to-last ranked pass defense (285.8), the unit is shorthanded heading into the November 1 home game against the Baltimore Ravens.
As a result, the Bills (5-1) made three roster moves to bolster their defensive backfield on the eve of their critical AFC battle against the Ravens (4-3) in Week 8.
Not to mention, Buffalo's secondary is likely to be tested early and often on Sunday as Baltimore welcomes quarterback Lamar Jackson back to the lineup after missing three games due to an ankle injury.
First, Buffalo signed versatile defensive back Te'Cory Couch to the active 53-man roster. It allowed the Bills to fill a temporary vacancy created by safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson's one-game suspension for spitting at an opponent in Week 6.
Furthermore, the Bills used both of their weekly allotted practice squad elevations for the defensive backfield. Buffalo called up veteran safety Geno Stone and cornerback AJ Woods for Sunday's game day roster.
In addition to Gardner-Johnson's suspension, the Bills must guard against the possibility that starting slot cornerback Dee Alford is inactive. Alford is officially questionable to play due to an ankle injury. Meanwhile, backup nickel cornerback Jordan Hancock remains on Injured Reserve.
The Couch signing and Woods elevation are ominous signs for Alford's availability. Both Couch and Woods have the ability to play in the slot.
Alford initially injured his ankle in Week 4 against the New England Patriots. After missing the Week 5 game in Los Angeles, the slot cornerback returned to play 43 defensive snaps in Week 6 against Las Vegas.
Following limited participation at Wednesday's practice, Alford missed back-to-back days . That pattern suggests he could have reaggravated the injury during practice.
Couch, who is in his third season as a Bills' practice squad player, will seemingly be the next man up provided Alford can't go. He's already made two appearances as a practice squad elevation this season, totaling 21 special teams reps in Weeks 3 and 4.
Woods has been with five different NFL organizations since 2024, but he has yet to appear in a regular season game. He spent this past summer with the Atlanta Falcons before joining the Bills on October 6.
With veteran Damar Hamlin stepping up to start in Gardner-Johnson's absence, the Bills have no proven depth on the bench.
While fifth-round rookie safety Jalon Kilgore may have a promising future, he has little time on task on this stage. Hence, it makes perfect sense for the Bills to elevate Stone, who made 34 consecutive starts for the Cincinnati Bengals prior to landing in Buffalo this past offseason .
Fittingly, Stone will make his Bills' debut against the team that drafted him at No. 219 overall in 2020. Stone led all NFL safeties with seven interceptions in 2023. By comparison, teammate Kyle Hamilton was second on the Ravens with four picks that season.
The Bills welcome the Ravens to Highmark Stadium for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on CBS. Here's the full injury outlook for Buffalo.

title: Buffalo Bills Connected to Eagles, Cardinals in Pair of Trade Projections
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills need to add help on the defensive side of the ball and an analyst has proposed a pair of trades for general manager Brandon Beane to accomplish that task.
The Athletic's Ted Nguyen came up with 10 different hypothetical trades for NFL teams and the Bills were involved in two of them.
One saw the Bills matched up with the Philadelphia Eagles in a trade for defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. The proposed deal saw Buffalo give up a third-round pick.
"Ojomo, who could be a game-changer for the Bills as a run stuffer and interior pass rusher. He also fits into Buffalo’s 3-4 scheme," he said. "Pairing Ojomo with budding star Deone Walker would be a move for this season and the future."
After that, Nguyen then had the Bills acquiring Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker for a fourth-round pick.
"They need defensive help badly. Ojomo would help the front, and Baker would give Leonhard his playmaking safety on the back end," Nguyen said. "While Leonhard was with the Broncos, he saw first-hand the impact that Talanoa Hufanga had. Baker has been out of the limelight in Arizona, but with the Bills, the world could see how special he is on the big stage."
While it remains to be seen if the Bills would be open to acquiring either player, we could see both getting moved at the deadline.
Ojomo is in the final year of his deal and the Eagles already have a lot invested upfront with Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, so they could look to unload Ojomo during a season in which Philly isn't going anywhere.
Baker is a logical trade candidate because Arizona needs more draft capital for the rebuild and it doesn't make much sense to hold on to a 30-year-old safety who could decline before the Cardinals are competitive again.
The interior of the defensive line is one of the most stable spots on the Bills' defense, so they don't necessarily need a D-tackle.
That said, it certainly wouldn't hurt to upgrade the position and Ojomo would amount to a better option than T.J. Sanders and DeWayne Carter.
Ojomo doesn't have any sacks this season, but he does have 16 pressures and he did post six sacks in 2025. As far as his run defense is concerned, he's comparable to Sanders and Carter.
Ojomo is a good, up-and-coming young player and he would be a welcomed addition in Buffalo. However, if it really costs a third-rounder, the Bills should pass.
Baker is a different story. The Cardinals safety has been one of the better players at his position in the NFL for a decade now, as evidenced by his eight Pro Bowls and four All-Pro nods.
Baker doesn't offer much in coverage, but he is an excellent box safety who plays the run at an elite level and can get after the quarterback when sent to blitz.
At the very least, the Bills need more depth at safety , but they can really use a starting-caliber player, as the duo of C.J. Gardner-Johnson and Cole Bishop has left a lot to be desired in 2026.
If all it takes is a fourth-round pick, acquiring Baker is a no-brainer for Buffalo.

title: New Bills 2027 NFL Mock Draft Lands Instinctive Safety Who Surprisingly Drops in  Round 1
full_text:
Entering Week 8 of the 2026 season, the Buffalo Bills clearly have one major weakness. The Bills are 31st in the league in pass defense, already surrendering 1,715 through the air in seven games.
They recently brought back veteran Tre'Davious White , which could help shore up their concerns at cornerback, but that's just a Band-Aid approach. There's still a lot of rebuilding that needs to be done in the secondary, especially at safety where they've been a mess in coverage.
That's why CBS Sports' Josh Edwards has Buffalo targeting a safety in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft. With the Bills' first selection in Round 1, he has them taking Notre Dame's Tae Johnson at No. 29 overall.
Asd Edwards states, Johnson is an instinctive safety who will give their secondary some "accountability." He also said that Jim Leonhard's arrival on its own was not the cure-all for their defense, which is why a rebuild in the secondary is neccessary.
"A change in defensive coordinator was not the cure-all for Buffalo's defensive woes. Tae Johnson is an instinctual safety who should bring some accountability back to the Bills' secondary," Edwards wrote.
Johnson was a multi-sport star in high school, playing football and basketball. He's incredibly athletic, and previously played wide receiver. That was evident during his breakout season in 2025 when Johnson recorded four interceptions for the Fighting Irish.
Unfortunately, Johnson has not been able to play much this season after suffering a foot injury in the opener against Wisconsin. He is expected to return sometime in November, but since he had a foot injury in the past, the coaching staff is proceeding with caution.
Buffalo has had more than its fair share of injuries in the secondary. Maxwell Hairston missed plenty of time as a rookie in 2025 and they have seen players such as Dee Alford, C.J. Gardner-Johnson , Jordan Hancock, and Christian Benford all battle injuries this season. The Bills also already have concerns about durability with safety Cole Bishop, who missed time during each of his first two seasons, which slowed his development.
Johnson has the makings of a centerfielder with excellent coverage skills and a nose for the ball. That will be intriguing for the Bills, but they need to do their homework with medical checks since they can't afford to add another player who might not always be available.

title: Four Key Bills-Ravens Matchups in Critical AFC Battle
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have had a busy few days since returning from their bye in Week 7 to prepare to take on the Baltimore Ravens at Highmark Stadium Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET.
The Bills will be looking to continue their winning ways, but coming away with a victory against the 4-3 Baltimore Ravens, who are in last place in the AFC North, will be easier said than done.
With starting franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson expected to be back in the lineup after missing several weeks with a high ankle sprain, the Ravens will undoubtedly be rejuvenated, despite losing two straight.
And, given that Buffalo will be without starting nickel cornerback Dee Alford and possibly a few others on both sides of the ball , it’ll only make matters more difficult.
There are some matchups that the Bills must either look to exploit or keep under wraps. Here are four areas to watch out for.
Probably unbeknownst to many casual fans around the NFL, Ravens’ fourth-year wideout Zay Flowers currently leads the AFC in receiving yards with 608 yards on 40 catches, and he’s done so while only playing in six of Baltimore’s seven games.
The former Boston College speedster is having a phenomenal season with or without franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson in the lineup, too, and it should frighten Bills Mafia considering that Bills’ defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s unit is allowing the second most yards in the league right now at 285.8 yards per game.
If Leonhard and Co. can’t come up with a plan to at least slow down Flowers, then it’s going to be a long afternoon for Buffalo’s defense . . . and it could get scary.
Rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun and veteran Christian Benford will be tasked with covering him on the outside at times, but Flowers also plays in the slot.
So, whomever Leonhard decides to replace the previously mentioned Alford with in the slot will also have a huge job on their hands.
A key to victory on Sunday will be how the Bills’ offensive line performs against a Ravens’ pass rush that is currently tied for the seventh most sacks in the NFL with 16 quarterback sacks, equating to 2.3 sacks per contest.
For comparison, the Bills' group of Rousseau (6 sacks) and Co. have just 11 combined sacks through six games as a unit.
With starting right tackle Bills’ Spencer Brown listed as questionable after only practicing on Friday—due to ongoing back issues—there is concern regarding how Buffalo can manage to protect quarterback Josh Allen on Sunday, especially if Brown can’t go.
Brown left early against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5, but was able to return to play against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. For that reason, this is definitely an area to watch, especially if third-year tackle Tylan Grable has to make the start in Brown's absence.
As Bills ON SI already covered earlier this week, sixth-year veteran outside linebacker Gregory Rousseau has gone missing on the stat sheet recently, and it’s left a lot to be desired for Buffalo’s pass rush.
Much like Buffalo, Baltimore is also dealing with some unfortunate injury issues up front as rookie first-round right guard Olaivavega Ioane was ruled out with a sprained MCL.  The injury will force the Ravens to trot out their sixth different offensive line combination of the 2026 season on Sunday.
The Bills’ interior defensive linemen, specifically veteran Ed Oliver and second-year Deone Walker, need to take advantage of the Ravens rotating o-line.
If the Bills allow quarterback Lamar Jackson to easily stand in the pocket or give him easy escape lanes, then it could be a day to forget in Western New York. They can't allow running back Derrick Henry to get loose at the second level of the defense, either.
It’ll be imperative that Oliver, Walker, and the rest of the defensive front win their one-on-one matchups on a regular basis in this pivotal AFC meeting.
As it stands right now, it appears that the Ravens’ pass defense ( 16th, 220.9 YPG ) might be lagging slightly behind its run defense ( 9th, 96.6 YPG ).
However, that doesn’t mean that the Bills’ should just look to air it out on Sunday. Instead, they should look to strategically attack Baltimore’s defensive front with James Cook and the running game , and somehow find ways to make things slightly easier on quarterback Josh Allen and the passing offense.
Doing so will be easier said than done, but there’s a reason that Cook is still third in the NFL in yards gained on the ground through Week 7 in 2026 after earning the rushing title in 2025.
The former Georgia Bulldog is also doing so while having carried the ball less than every other running back in the top-six of that category  this year heading into the first Sunday of November.
If Cook can get into a groove in the ground game against the Ravens’ stout run defense, then it’ll do wonders for Allen and the rest of the offensive operation.

title: The Panthers Aren't Playing Sunday, But There's One Team They Need to Win
full_text:
I'm not used to the Panthers already being done for the week when Sunday gets here. After watching them lose to Green Bay on Thursday night , I guess the good part is I can sit back today and watch everybody else.
There is one game I'll be paying attention to more than the others.
Atlanta plays Tampa Bay, and as much as I hate to say it, I'm pulling for the Falcons.
I probably wouldn't care much about this game if Tampa hadn't just embarrassed Carolina. The Bucs came into Charlotte with one win and left with a 43-13 win . I didn't see that coming at all.
What bothers me now is Tampa is sitting at 2-5 and still isn't buried. That's crazy when you think about it. Carolina and Atlanta only have one more win, and New Orleans is sitting there with two as well .
So I'm looking at Tampa a little differently than I was a week ago. I thought the Panthers would beat them. Instead, Tampa beat Carolina by 30 and now gets another NFC South game at home.
Let Atlanta handle them today.
I'm not thrilled about the Falcons getting to four wins either. I just don't care about that as much today.
Carolina gets Atlanta again later this season . If that game matters when we get there, the Panthers can do something about it themselves. Right now I'd rather see Tampa take another loss.
Maybe I'm putting too much into what happened last week. A 30-point loss will do that to you. I just watched Tampa look a whole lot better than its record against Carolina, and I'm not interested in seeing whether it can start putting a few wins together.
The Panthers can't do anything about their 3-4 record today. They already played their game this week and lost it. All they can do now is watch the rest of the division play out.
If Tampa loses, I'll take it. The Bucs stay at two wins, Carolina gets a few extra days to get itself together and we move on to next week.
It might feel strange pulling for Atlanta for three hours.

title: Panthers Given Mandate to Make 1 Crucial Trade to Salvage Season
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have to make a trade. After another debacle , this time on national television, Thursday night, the Panthers clearly don't have the guns to keep up with actual NFC contenders. They may not have the guns to keep up with NFC South contenders.
Injuries are probably the main reason why. It is hard to say this team wouldn't be pretty good if at least some of Xavier Legette, Taylor Moton, Damien Lewis, Ikem Ekwonu, Will Lee III, Nic Scourton, Chris Brazzell, Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Jaelan Phillips were out on the field.
The Panthers have to do something if they really want to try to contend this year, and their offseason spending spree suggests that they do. And if that's the case, FOX Sports' Greg Auman has a clear target in mind.
The last two weeks (or five days) have been absolutely brutal to the Panthers. Not only did more injuries pop up, but every facet of this team came crashing back down to earth as the Panthers slipped from 3-2 to 3-4. It has been ugly.
Bad performance has played a part, but a complete lack of healthy players has, too. And that is nowhere felt more than at cornerback. It's been weeks since Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went on IR, and Dan Morgan has sat idly by. The injuries at corner haven't gotten better.
Akayleb Evans, who was outmatched as a starting corner, is on IR now. Will Lee III went down on Thursday, and it doesn't look good. They're trotting practice squad players out and running out of options at the same time.
A trade just has to happen, and according to Greg Auman of FOX Sports, it needs to be Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen.
"There’s so much of a Seattle presence in Carolina between head coach Dave Canales and general manager Dan Morgan, both longtime Seahawks guys and where Tariq Woolen began his career," he wrote, highlighting the obvious connection.
"Backups aren’t likely going to get them a repeat division title, so upgrading the secondary would be a priority if they were to be active at the trade deadline," Auman concluded.
The Panthers can't survive with the corner situation as it is. They also can't survive the offensive line situation, but Woolen is available, and starting-caliber offensive linemen just aren't. Cornerbacks are also cheaper.
The Panthers may or may not make a move, but this is one that has to be on the radar. We simply cannot go on like this unless Carolina is content struggling all year.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: Ejiro Evero's Firing Just Put More Pressure on Dave Canales
full_text:
I wasn't surprised when the Panthers fired Ejiro Evero on Friday. I probably would've been more surprised if they kept him after what we've watched the last couple of weeks. My first thought when I saw it wasn't really about Evero though. It was about Dave Canales.
Evero is gone now. Jonathan Cooley is gone too. Todd Wash gets the defense, and we'll find out soon enough if any of that makes a difference. I went back and forth on Evero for a while this season, but after the last two games I understood why Carolina finally did it.
The Tampa Bay game was probably where I had enough. I watched the Buccaneers come into Charlotte and score 43 points, then Green Bay put up another 30 four days later. It's hard to defend a defensive coordinator after giving up 73 points in five days.
Here's the thing I kept thinking about after Evero was fired. Carolina scored 13 against Tampa Bay and 19 against Green Bay. I actually went back and added it up because it didn't seem like they had scored that much. Thirty-two points in two games isn't exactly helping anybody.
I've had questions about the offense for a while anyway. Some weeks I like what Carolina is doing and then the next week I'm wondering where it went. I've wondered why Chuba Hubbard wasn't getting the ball more, and there have been play calls where I've just sat there trying to figure out what Canales saw that I didn't.
That's the stuff I'm watching now. Evero can't take the blame for any of it.
I had forgotten Evero was already in Carolina when Canales got the job until I started thinking about all of this. Canales kept him, which made sense to me at the time. Evero was getting head-coaching interviews and there were years when I wondered why somebody hadn't hired him yet.
Funny how quickly that changed.
Now Wash gets his shot. I don't know if he's going to make the defense any better, and I'm definitely not expecting everything to suddenly look different because one coach is gone. I mostly want to see if there are things I notice right away.
I'm going to be doing the same thing with the offense. Canales came to Carolina with an offensive background, and that's the side of the ball where I expected him to make the biggest difference. Lately I haven't seen enough of it.
I'm not there. I don't think that's where this conversation needs to go seven games into the season.
But I do think Friday changed things for him. One of his coordinators is already gone, Carolina has lost two straight and the Panthers are sitting at 3-4. Canales has a few extra days now to look at all of it.
I'm curious what he changes.

title: Rookie Defender Has Been Bright Spot in Panthers' Latest Rollercoaster Season
full_text:
On Thursday night at Lambeau Field, the Carolina Panthers fell below the .500 mark with a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Dave Canales’s club couldn’t slow down Matt LaFleur’s one-dimensional offense. While the worst ground game in the league was held under 100 yards for the eighth time in as many games, the Panthers had no answers for Packers’ quarterback Jordan Love.
Green Bay’s signal-caller hit on 30-of 41 throws for 288 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception. Carolina’s pass rush finished with zero sacks and zero quarterback hits, and defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero was fired by the team on Friday.
Intercepted by Zakee Wheatley ‼️ CARvsGB on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vOUDlt94xC
As for that one interception, it was the first of his NFL career for Panthers’ rookie safety Zakee Wheatley. Per Pro Football Focus, only Green Bay’s Evan Williams (90.6) has a higher grade at the position than Carolina’s second pick (89.8) in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL draft. The former Nittany Lion has excelled in pass coverage and is PFF’s No. 3 safety in this facet with an 83.4 grade, behind only Williams (90.1) and Seattle’s Julian Love (85.4).
Although Wheatley was inactive for the season-opener against the Bears, he has played in each of the past six games and made four starts. He ranks sixth on the club with 25 defensive stops (18 solo), one forced fumble, Thursday night’s interception of Jordan Love, and four passes defensed. He also recorded a solo tackle on special teams.
In the loss to the Packers, the five starting members of Carolina’s secondary were cornerbacks Marco Wilson (his first game with the team) and rookie Will Lee III, as well as safeties Wheatley, Nick Scott, and Tre’von Moehrig.
Wilson led the club with eight tackles, while Wheatley and linebacker Devin Lloyd were tied for second with seven stops. It marked the fifth time in six games that the 24-year-old rookie totaled at least four defensive stops in a contest.
There are certain aspects of Carolina’s defense that have improved from a year ago. Of course, the back end of this unit has certainly been hamstrung by the absences of veteran cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. And with pass-rusher Jaelan Phillips out the last two games, the Panthers failed to come up with a sack in each of those contests.
Still, Wheatley has stood out this season and looks like a Day 3 steal, which may not be a total surprise considering some post-draft evaluations of Dan Morgan’s 2026 draft class.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Ikem Ekwonu's Value Keeps Rising While Panthers Wait for Return
full_text:
Ikem Ekwonu hasn't played a snap for the Panthers this season, and I think I've appreciated him a little more every week he's been out. I definitely did after watching Carolina's offensive line against Tampa Bay and Green Bay.
Ekwonu is still working his way back from the torn patellar tendon he suffered against the Los Angeles Rams in January. Carolina signed Rasheed Walker after four seasons in Green Bay and put him at left tackle while Ekwonu recovered. So far, that hasn't gone very well.
Tampa Bay was probably the worst of it. Walker gave up three sacks and seven pressures, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Young didn't have much time to get comfortable that afternoon, and the Panthers ended up losing 43-13.
Four days later, Young was running around again. Green Bay pressured him on 48.9% of his dropbacks and sacked him six times. Walker was out there for all 73 offensive snaps against his old team.
Through seven games, Walker has allowed 30 pressures and four sacks, according to Core Football Labs. He's also been called for six penalties. I've seen enough to know Carolina needs better play at left tackle.
I'm not putting all of the problems up front on Walker. Taylor Moton is out for the season, Damien Lewis didn't play Thursday and Corey Bullock hurt his quad during the game. This line looks a lot different from the one Carolina expected to have, but Walker hasn't helped much either.
Dave Canales gave an update this week and said Ekwonu is “trending in the right direction.” He's doing more individual work now, which is good to hear considering the injury he's coming back from.
Canales isn't ready to have somebody go at him full speed yet, and I'm fine with that. A torn patellar tendon isn't something I'd mess around with just because the offensive line has struggled for a couple of weeks. The Panthers have already gone this long without Ekwonu.
Carolina also has some extra time before Denver comes to Charlotte on Nov. 8. Maybe Ekwonu is ready by then and maybe he isn't. I sure wouldn't mind seeing No. 79 again soon, but there's no reason to put him out there before he's ready.
Ekwonu has frustrated me plenty since Carolina took him sixth overall in 2022. His pass protection hasn't always been where it needs to be, and I've wondered at times whether the Panthers had their long-term answer at left tackle. I haven't wondered nearly as much lately.
Young has been under pressure on half of his dropbacks over the last two games. That number was 39.4% before this stretch, and his yards per attempt under pressure has fallen from 6.2 to 3.2. Watching Young deal with that much pressure has made Ekwonu's absence pretty noticeable.
Putting Ekwonu back at left tackle isn't going to fix the entire offensive line. Moton isn't walking back through the door this season, and we don't know what the group will look like by the time Denver gets here. I just know I'd rather have Ekwonu protecting Young's blind side right now.
Seven games without him have changed my mind quite a bit.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Overreaction? The Panthers' Season May Already Be Over
full_text:
Five days ago, the Panthers were 3-2 and had Tampa Bay coming to Charlotte. The Buccaneers had won one game, and I thought Carolina had a pretty good chance to get to 4-2 before heading to Green Bay four days later.
Well, that went about as bad as it could've gone. Tampa Bay beat Carolina 43-13, and the Panthers followed that with a 27-19 loss at Green Bay. They're 3-4 now, and I'll admit I'm looking at the rest of this season a lot differently than I was a week ago.
The Green Bay loss isn't the one that gets me. Carolina was on the road four days after getting beat up by Tampa Bay, and the Packers are a good football team. The Panthers actually did some things I liked in that game.
They held Josh Jacobs to 39 yards on 21 carries. That was nice to see after Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards Sunday. Chuba Hubbard had another good night with 119 yards from scrimmage, and Carolina took the ball away three times.
Getting three points off those turnovers is what hurts. Carolina had the ball three extra times and couldn't turn any of them into a touchdown. Young also took six sacks, and Green Bay eventually put the game away.
Tampa Bay is harder for me to explain. The Panthers were at home against a 1-5 team and got beat by 30. If Carolina ends up a game short of winning the division or getting into the playoffs, I have a feeling we're going to remember that one.
I've watched Young throw for 329 yards against Detroit this season. He had 287 against Atlanta, and a few weeks later he threw for 281 against Philadelphia. We haven't seen much of that lately.
Thursday was rough. Young threw for 209 yards and took plenty of hits while trying to get the ball out. Six of those plays ended with him on the ground.
Carolina doesn't have its normal offensive line out there right now. Taylor Moton is on injured reserve. Damien Lewis wasn't available against Green Bay, and then Corey Bullock hurt his quad during the game.
I had the offensive line on my list after Thursday's loss . The Panthers have more than a week before Denver, so we'll see who they can get back by then.
Hubbard hasn't been the problem. He ran for 81 yards and a touchdown Thursday and added 38 more through the air. I'd keep throwing it to him too, especially if Young is going to have defenders in his face that often.
Denver is up first on Nov. 8. Carolina gets New Orleans after that before Baltimore comes to Charlotte. The Panthers will see Tampa Bay again at the end of November.
December isn't exactly empty either. Minnesota and Pittsburgh are both on there, and Seattle comes to Charlotte a few days before Christmas.
Maybe I'm putting too much into two bad games. Carolina has played well this season, and I've seen enough from this team to know Thursday night isn't necessarily what we're going to get every week.
But 3-4 doesn't leave much room to keep finding out.
The Panthers still have their division games, which is probably the best thing they have going for them right now. They'll get another shot at Tampa Bay, and they haven't played New Orleans yet. Atlanta comes at the end of the season.
I'm looking at Denver first. Get that one and you're 4-4 with New Orleans coming up. Lose it and you're sitting at 3-5.
I'm not ready to call the season over.

title: Panthers Stock Report: Chuba Hubbard Rises, Bryce Young Falls After Packers Loss
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers didn't have much time to figure out what went wrong against Tampa Bay before turning around and playing Green Bay four days later. There were some things I liked Thursday night, but not enough of them as Carolina left Green Bay with a 27-19 loss.
The run defense was much better, and Chuba Hubbard had another good game. Bryce Young and the passing game struggled for the second straight week, and the offensive line had a hard time keeping Green Bay out of the backfield. The Panthers also forced three turnovers and somehow got only three points out of them.
Here's where I have the Panthers' stock after Thursday night.
Hubbard was good again Thursday night. He carried it 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown and caught seven passes for another 38 yards. That's 119 yards from scrimmage on 29 touches.
The seven catches are what caught my attention. Young was under pressure for much of the night, and there wasn't much happening downfield, so Hubbard gave him another option. I wrote about Carolina using Hubbard more as a receiver during the game , and I hope we see more of it.
I was a little worried about this matchup after Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards against Carolina on Sunday. Going from that to facing Josh Jacobs four days later didn't exactly look like a great situation for the Panthers.
Jacobs ended up with only 39 yards on 21 carries, and Green Bay had 66 rushing yards as a team. He scored twice, including once as a receiver, but Carolina didn't let him beat them on the ground.
Green Bay had plenty of success throwing the ball, especially to Christian Watson. I'm not giving the entire defense a pass here. But considering what Bucky Irving and Tampa Bay did four days earlier, I'll take what Carolina did against Jacobs.
I've liked what we've seen from Wheatley, and Thursday gave us another reason. He picked off Jordan Love in the fourth quarter for the first interception of his NFL career and gave Carolina another possession with a chance to get back into the game.
According to the Panthers' postgame numbers , Wheatley is one of five rookies in franchise history with an interception and a forced fumble through his first six games. With all the injuries in Carolina's secondary, we're probably going to see a lot more of him.
Young finished 23-of-41 for 209 yards, one touchdown and one interception. He made a nice throw to Jalen Coker for a 26-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, but before that there wasn't much happening in the passing game.
The protection wasn't good, so I'm not putting everything on Young. There were still throws he missed, and on a few of the sacks he held onto the football too long. I gave him a C- in my postgame report card , and I'm still right around there.
We've seen Young play a lot better than this. He threw for 329 yards against Detroit, 287 against Atlanta and 281 against Philadelphia. I expected something closer to that after the Tampa Bay game, and we didn't get it.
Six sacks and nine quarterback hits aren't going to work. Green Bay pressured Young on 48.9% of his dropbacks, and there were several plays where he didn't have much time to do anything.
Carolina is pretty beat up up front right now. Taylor Moton is on injured reserve, Damien Lewis missed the Green Bay game and Corey Bullock left with a quad injury. Jake Curhan ended up playing left guard after being elevated from the practice squad.
The Panthers have some time before Denver, and hopefully that helps get a couple of guys back. I already had the offensive line on my list of things Carolina needed to work on . Watching Young get sacked six times didn't change anything for me.
This is the one that bothers me.
Carolina forced three Green Bay turnovers and got three points out of them. Jackson Kuwatch forced a fumble on the opening kickoff, Nick Scott forced another one in the second quarter and Wheatley picked off Love in the fourth.
The Panthers lost by eight. I'm not saying Carolina scores a touchdown every time Green Bay turns it over, but getting three extra possessions and coming away with three points isn't good enough. One touchdown on any of those possessions could have made the fourth quarter a lot more interesting.
Carolina is 3-4 and doesn't play again until Nov. 8 against Denver. After playing twice in five days, the Panthers have some time to get healthy and figure out what they want to change before then.

title: Dan Orlovsky Disagrees With Panthers Firing Ejiro Evero, But He's Wrong
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers made the surprising decision to fire defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero on Friday, hours after the Panthers fell to the Green Bay Packers. It is surprising not because it wasn't warranted, but because the Panthers had previously not shown that they cared enough to do something.
Firing Evero was warranted. Too many times, his players didn't look ready to play . Too many times, his decision-making boggled the mind and led to success for the opposing offense. And far too many times, some aspect of his defense completely fell off.
Dan Orlovsky couldn't believe the news, but we could.
Dan Orlovsky, former NFL quarterback turned analyst for ESPN, was in shock when he learned that the Panthers had fired Ejiro Evero. Perhaps he was a little surprised by the timing after a decent defensive outing, but this was coming after Sunday's loss to Tampa Bay.
Really surprised by this. Injuries were a huge issue—good coach https://t.co/0Ik0oGPfAK
He captioned his tweet with a claim that Evero is a "really good coach," and on ESPN, he said, "That's a good coach, man. Ejiro is a very good coach, very good coach. They're beat up in the secondary, he's a very good coach." This was after a mouth-agape stare in shock for a few seconds.
Evero is well-respected across the NFL, but there are no tangible results one can point to to back Orlovsky's point up. Evero was a good coach in Denver, which is why the Panthers poached him, and he was decent in 2023, which is why Dave Canales kept him around.
The production just wasn't there. In 2024, they set a record for the most points allowed in NFL history. In 2025, they were middle-of-the-pack in yards and points, but they had bad success rates and other advanced analytics.
This year, after bringing in Devin Lloyd, Jaelan Phillips, Bobby Okereke, Lee Hunter, Zakee Wheatley, and Will Lee, production was both too inconsistent and not good enough on the better days.
Injuries have played a role, but injuries aren't why Evero couldn't time a blitz right or get home with any amount of rushers. Injuries aren't why the defense forgot how to tackle or where to play every other week.
This was supposed to be a top-10 unit. If you'd told someone before Week 1 that the Panthers would be tied for first on October 30, they would've believed that hyped defense had delivered. It hasn't.
The defense is bottom-10 in yards per game, third-worst in rushing yards per game (bolstered by the Green Bay Packers' 32nd-ranked rushing attack), and sixth-worst in points per game.
And at some point, injuries or not, someone has to be accountable for the miscues on defense. That is, more often than not, the coordinator.

title: Todd Wash is Interim DC. Here are 3 Other Options Panthers Should Consider This Offseason
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are making changes after a 3-4 start to the season, firing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero along with pass game coordinator Jonathon Cooley.
This comes less than 12 hours after Carolina lost its second straight game , showing lapses in defensive coverage and poor playcalling on that side of the ball. This move had to be made; the Panthers' defense has been a complete letdown when it was supposed to be the team's strength.
Even when fully healthy, Carolina was embarrassed against the Chicago Bears in Week 1, and only performed well against Deshaun Watson, and backup QBs Tanner McKee and Cooper Rush.
Now that Evero is gone, Carolina has an interim defensive coordinator. The Panthers hired Todd Wash in 2023 under former head coach Frank Reich. Wash has 20 years of coaching experience in the NFL, and 31 years of coaching experience total.
Before coming to Carolina, Wash spent time with the Detroit Lions and previously had a long stint with the Jacksonville Jaguars before that. He's coached elite players such as Aidan Hutchinson and Calais Campbell.
With a long resume to his name already, Wash will have a shot at earning the official defensive coordinator job. However, if he doesn't, then here are three names to watch in the offseason.
Scott is the defensive backs coach and defensive pass game coordinator for the Seattle Seahawks. Seattle has been one of, if not the best, defenses in the NFL for the last two seasons, and the elite secondary has been a huge piece of that.
Scott joined Seattle in 2022, which was Dave Canales' final season with the franchise before heading to Tampa Bay, so there is some familiarity.
Edwards has experience as a defensive coordinator, having served as the DC for the Minnesota Vikings, Washington Redskins, and Buffalo Bills.
Edwards is in his fourth season with the Buccaneers, currently serving as the pass game coordinator. Like Karl Scott, Edwards spent a single season with Canales. In Canales' lone season with Tampa Bay, Edwards coached the outside linebackers, so he's versatile in where he can coach on defense, and Carolina's pass rush right now looks awful based on Thursday night.
Another pass game coordinator, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores, would be the dream candidate, but he'll be interviewing for head coaching jobs, not coordinator jobs.
That said, the Vikings' defense is rolling on all cylinders, and Gerald Alexander is a focal point of that staff. Minnesota currently ranks second in the NFL in pass defense, surrendering just 155 yards per game.
Alexander also has a connection to the Panthers, and it's not with Dave Canales. Alexander played for Carolina for less than a full season in 2010. As a player, he had a journeyman career, but as a coach, he's one of the league's more intriguing young options.

title: 4 Players Who Will Feel the Impact of Ejiro Evero's Absence, Both Good and Bad
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers fired Ejiro Evero from his role as defensive coordinator . Pass game coordinator Jonathan Cooley went with him. The change was a long time coming , and Evero did not do anything to justify more time.
However, whenever someone is fired, there are ramifications, both good and bad. Some players will benefit from a new coordinator. Others will not.
Both Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are excellent cornerbacks, but Horn in particular is elite at press man coverage. He is supremely physical, so not having a coordinator who wants him to play off in a zone is going to be a huge change, and probably a really good one.
Of course, there is the caveat that Horn is on IR right now, but when he comes back, we expect he will do a little better (he was already good) with a different coordinator who might be willing to adjust to the strength of his players more often.
Ejiro Evero's 3-4 scheme was good for Devin Lloyd, who was thriving under the coordinator. The former All-Pro can succeed with anyone, but Evero was able to help bring out the best in Lloyd both in coverage and as a run defender.
We will still see him all over the field, but the importance of inside linebackers will be diluted a bit with a new coordinator. Lloyd and Bobby Okereke might not have as much production, though that doesn't mean they're worse players now.
Whether or not the Panthers will adopt a 4-3 under Todd Wash remains to be seen, but regardless, Derrick Brown is in line to perform better with Wash being elevated and taking over for Ejiro Evero. Wash was the defensive line coach, and last night, the line was actually really good in run defense, and Brown had a breakout game.
Brown has always been good, but he hasn't always thrived in Evero's system. He did make a Pro Bowl under Evero, but he had a few really excellent seasons before Evero arrived in 2023. Look for Brown to return to form soon.
When Jaelan Phillips comes back, he might be in for a very different role. Obviously, he's still going to rush the passer and set the edge, but a 3-4 system like the one Evero used is often much more favorable for edge rushers. They get more creative ways to get into the backfield.
Phillips was playing just fine under Evero, although the bar for him after a $120 million contract is much higher than that. Still, if the system changes at all, we could be looking at an even more frustrating pass rush from Phillips.

title: Bears Trade Rumor Details Deadline Focus, Latest on Possible Khalil Mack Deal
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have already pulled off one blockbuster trade before the Nov. 10 trade deadline and one NFL insider says they might not be done.
The Bears pulled off the trade with the Tennessee Titans for star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons on Thursday, but they could still use an edge rusher to really fortify their defense.
Well, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports that the Bears are indeed still looking around for an edge rusher ahead of the deadline next month.
He also added that he "wouldn't be surprised" if the Bears come away with Khalil Mack in a trade with the Los Angeles Chargers.
"Meanwhile, the Bears may not actually be done," Rapoport said on Sunday morning. "I'm told they are still calling around, still looking on the edges of their defense."
"Wouldn't be surprised if a Khalil Mack trade was in (cards) here. A possible reunion for Mack and the Bears," Rapoport added.
The fact that the Bears are looking around for edge rusher help and continue to be linked to Mack by NFL insiders only adds credibility to a possible Mack trade.
We also know, according to FOX's Jay Glazer , that the Bears have put in a call to the Chargers for Mack, so they are clearly interested in a reunion with their former edge rusher.
The biggest roadblock for a Mack trade currently appears to be the Chargers themselves, as The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported on Saturday morning.
"The Chargers have confounded teams by not engaging in trade talks," Jones stated. "The Bolts are 0-6 but are telling teams Khalil Mack isn’t available. It’s hard to envision that remaining the case over the next 10 days."
We tend to believe this is just posturing from the Chargers in a quest to get the best return possible. After all, if teams know the Chargers are hellbent on selling, that will hurt the offers Los Angeles will receive.
It just makes sense for the 0-6 Chargers to sell at least the players who are set to be free agents in 2027, and Mack is included in that group. There's also the possibility that Mack could retire after he considered doing so after the 2024 campaign .
Of course, Mack doesn't have a no-trade clause, but chances are the Chargers would work with him to send him where he wants to go out of respect for the future Hall of Famer.
And, based on how fondly he viewed his time in Chicago and the opportunity the Bears will give him to make a deep playoff run, it's absolutely conceivable Mack could request to be traded to back to his old team.
At this point, it just feels like all the stars are aligning for a Bears-Chargers trade to go down. Our prediction is it ultimately does happen and Mack returns to the Bears.

title: Ben Johnson's Ideas on Jeffery Simmons' Workload Against Seattle
full_text:
Just about everyone at Halas Hall short of George McCaskey himself has weighed in on the Bears' acquisition of Jeffery Simmons at this point, except for someone else rather important.
Actually, it's the guy who has to coach the team.
Ben Johnson said something through canned quote issued by the team but on Saturday he said not only what he thinks of the effect Simmons can have , but discussed how much the All-Pro might be playing against Seattle on Monday night after only two practices.
"He’s a guy that forces an offense to know where he is and affects their protection, affects the run game, all those things," Johnson said. "We look forward to seeing the impact he can have, not just on dictating some terms to the offense but also elevating those around him as well through his play and through his leadership because those have been kind of the constants throughout his career so far.
"Only been a few days. Getting to know the person as much as we already know the player. He’s got a lot of film out there and a heck of a resume. Right now it’s just trying to connect him to all of our guys and indoctrinate him to a degree."
What Johnson had to say was in line with what defensive coordinator Dennis Allen suggested on Thursday and that was how the whole defense benefits.
"You get a guy like this and it frees up a lot of things. It takes a lot of issues that you might have seen as shortcomings and can mask those to a degree because when you've got a defensive player that's as dominant as this guy is, it just takes him making a play to cover up some things across the board," Johnson said. "Like I said before, I really believe he's going to elevate the play of everybody around him as well.
"Just having him out there is going to be a shot in the arm for us, to a degree.”
No matter what Vegas says, Bears are now the favorite. Super Bowl-or-bust stakes for Ben Johnson & Caleb Williams. Target on their backs & just like my #Seahawks s/o re: Quenton Nelson + not shying away from the price of chasing greatness, I bleeping love it. After watching…
Johnson was well aware of the situation involving the grade even though GM Ryan Poles said Thursday the entire thing had been accomplished late at night.

It's not the easiest thing to get a player ready to play in a new scheme after only two practices but this is what they're doing. It's probably no more difficult than the assignment facing the player who will square off against Simmons much of the time, new Seahawks guard Quenton Nelson. Seattle has to get Nelson up to speed on actually blocking plays in a full offense on only about four practices.

"They’ve been coaching. He’s a smart guy and we’ve been encouraged with what we’ve seen so far."
Told Simmons' normal workload is 87% of plays in a game, Johnson wasn't quite sure they'd be stretching playing time that much.
"Yeah, he might not be quite that high Week 1 for us, but he certainly has shown to be able to carry a load," Johnson said.
New Chicago Bears defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons is the only iDL to clear the 95th percentile in pressures, sacks, run stops, tackles for a loss, and QB hits over the last 3 seasons, per @SumerSports : pic.twitter.com/6Wz2LXUOH5
The 87% is only during this season to date. While Simmons has played a lot in the past he was at 81% each of the last three seasons before 2026 and his high for a full season per Pro Football Reference is 85%. Simmons hasn't played a full season since 2021, the only year out of eight before now that he played every game. He has the chance to hit 17 this year. He has missed 18 games in eight seasons.
The Bears haven't been asking reps of this type from their defensive tackles. They use a rotation. For instance, starter Grady Jarrett has been getting 72% of reps this year after 68% last year. Starter Kentavius Street is at 43% and backup Neville Gallimore 34%. Then again, none of these players have been at Simmons' level of play.
There's no sense letting talent go to waste but you don't want a 29-year-old player in his prime wearing out.
