Considering the importance Simmons has to the future of the team, there's no sense forcing the issue in his very first game. Putting players into risk by playing too many downs when they don't even know the full defense yet can not only hurt the team's chances but leave the player trying to do things he isn't prepared to do. That can mean injuries.
It's a situation the Bears need to monitor closely Monday night at Seattle.
However, in the long term Simmons will definitely get his reps. And in the NFL there could be no better position on defense where a team can invest in players 29 to 33 years old than at defensive tackle.

title: Ben Johnson Suggests Caleb Williams Lost Cleat Dispute After Second Fine
full_text:
The Caleb Williams-Caddix cleats controversy hasn't ended just because the Bears QB says he's wearing those cleats and will deal with the fine.
The problem with the NFL uniform policy, just like with fines for other violations, is it can keep players from taking the field.
According to ESPN's Courtney Cronin , Williams was fined $23,882 more on Friday for wearing the cleats against New England after he had been fined initially last week for the Atlanta game. He has now been fined a total of $35,823.
The process for a uniform fine and discipline is somewhat different than it is for being fined and suspended by the league for penalties in a game. After multi-week fined, the NFL can have equipment staff and game officials simply prevent the player from coming on the field until they alter their uniform. In this case, it would mean Williams would be forced to change them or sit out.
For players penalized as a result of on-field play, the league policy is three fines for the same thing before a player can be suspended but they also have to have a meeting with league officials first before the playing time penalty comes down. This doesn't work the same way with the equipment situation.
Coach Ben Johnson on Saturday said he's well aware of the shoe situation with Williams and it doesn't sound like his QB is winning this one.
Asked about it, Johnson said of Williams: "He's all about the team and I know he's not going to hurt the team," Johnson said.
Unboxing cleats from the brand behind Caleb Williams’ $36,000 in NFL fines. Don’t worry, the brand’s got him covered. 👀 pic.twitter.com/Lv6upOTOpR
From that end, it sounds as if Williams is going to have to cover up the logo on his cleats, the way other players have done who wear them. It's either that or he'll be wearing different cleats or he'll sit.  At least covering up the logo is a compromise.
It doesn't matter that Joe Flacco also wears those cleats and said he'd pick up the fine for Williams wearing them, or that the people from Caddix reportedly say they will pay Williams' fine. Neither Flacco nor the shoe people are going to be able to make up the lost playing time Williams would get for wearing the shoes, or make up for the losses the Bears could absorb without Williams playing.
The entire rule is far too stringent when it comes to dress code for the league but the rule is in effect and there is nothing one quarterback is going to do to change it for this season.
Williams might feel more comfortable in these particular cleats but he's simply going to need be comfortable enough wearing NIKE, Under Armor or adidas brand shoes. Either that or his compromise must be covering up the logo. Those other three brands are approved by the NFL. Perhaps in the next offseason the shoe manufacturer and proponents like Flacco and Williams can do something about getting the NFL to accept its equipment as standard issue.
Don't bet on it.  The league gets set in its ways and the dollars are rolling in, which means more than all of the complaining to Roger Goodell and owners combined.

title: Bears' Jeffery Simmons Explains Taking New Jersey Number Despite Opportunity to Get 98
full_text:
One of the first steps after Jeffery Simmons joined the Chicago Bears in a trade on Thursday was choosing a jersey number.
Simmons has since done that, taking No. 99 , which is not the No. 98 he wore with the Tennessee Titans. We figured Simmons simply took 99 because Montez Sweat, his former college teammate, already had No. 98 and wasn't willing to give it up.
However, that turned out not to be the case. Sweat actually did offer up his No. 98 to Simmons, but the four-time Pro Bowler decided to decline.
Why did he do that, you ask? Well, Simmons thought it would be good to get a new number amid his fresh start in Chicago.
"I was actually on the plane when I was headed out here yesterday, and I was just thinking, this is something new for me. This is a new beginning. I feel like this is just a new chapter in my life," he said.
"I knew Sweat didn't mind giving me 98, but I also said I didn't want to get the number from him, one," Simmons added. "But two, it was more I wanted something new. I wanted this to be a new chapter, a new reason behind everything I do. I just said it's only right to go with a new number and that was 99. And 98 +1 = 99."
It isn't clear if Sweat had any dollar amount attached to giving up his No. 98 to Simmons, but Simmons definitely could've afford it with his $105 million deal.
It makes total sense for Simmons to want a completely fresh start. Not only is he going to a new team, he is completely flipping the script by going from a rebuilding squad to one that looks like it could compete for a Super Bowl in 2026.
The closest Simmons has come to a Super Bowl was his rookie season, when the Titans made an improbable playoff run to the AFC Championship Game where they fell victim to the eventual Super Bowl champions, the Kansas City Chiefs.
Since then, the Titans put together two more winning seasons in 2020 and 2021, but they failed to win a playoff game in those campaigns.
Since 2022, the Titans have been a mess, with the team posting a 20-55 record in that span. Simmons also played under three head coaches, Mike Vrabel, Brian Callahan and Robert Saleh.
There was also significant turnover at the quarterback position, with the Titans going from Ryan Tannehill, to Will Levis, to Cam Ward, with Ward looking like he won't pan out.
Barring something unforeseen, the Bears should not see that kind of turnover at head coach or quarterback. Both Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams look well entrenched in their roles , and as long as they're doing their thing, the Bears should be in great shape.
Now, Simmons will look to be one of the pieces that puts the Bears over the top to a Super Bowl that has alluded Simmons since 2019, and Chicago since 1985.

title: What to Expect From Bears' Jeffery Simmons Against the Seattle Seahawks
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' decision to trade for four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons measured on seismographs.
It was a blockbuster in the same vein as the Rams' trade for Myles Garrett and the Bears' 2018 trade for Khalil Mack ( although that move included much different circumstances ).
Simmons is one of the league's premier players on either side of the ball. Through the first seven games, he has four sacks and leads all defensive tackles in pressures.
He'll have a massive impact on a Bears defensive line that has struggled to collapse the pocket this season. Kentavius Street is the only true DT with a sack this season ( although two of Dayo Odeyingbo's three sacks came on the interior ).
Ryan Poles and Co. saw the Seahawks trade for future Hall of Famer Quenton Nelson ahead of their Week 8 clash and said, 'hold my beer.' Now the question is whether Simmons can play a full complement of snaps on Monday night.
If you want a trade acquisition to play immediately, then landing a defensive lineman would probably be your best bet. Simmons won't have a firm grasp of the Bears' defensive scheme four days after landing at O'Hare.
However, he won't need to. He won't be tasked with dropping into coverage anytime soon, but Dennis Allen won't get cute with him at any point regardless of his comfort level. Simmons will be tasked with hunting opposing QBs and shoring up their run defense, and he shouldn't have any issues doing that against Seattle.
Simmons might be on a snap count, but he's an ultimate competitor. It's safe to assume he'll welcome the opportunity to make his mark against the defending Super Bowl champions, especially with his former nemesis (Quenton Nelson) on the other side .
Simmons played 87% of the Titans' defensive snaps this season. He'll probably exceed the 75% threshold against Seattle.
Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen is the obvious biggest winner of the trade. He's put together a few rock-solid gameplans this season, but they've largely been built on sending extra rushers from the secondary to counteract their lack of consistent impact up front.
That won't be the case anymore (if he can help it after Kyler Gordon's hyper-efficient start to the season , anyway). He all but confirmed that Simmons will play a key role on Monday, although he wouldn't commit to a specific snap count for the new defensive star.
"We'll see what he can digest, and how much he can take in in a short period of time," Allen said. "Again, the fact that he is such a professional, and really studies the game allows him to catch up pretty quickly, but we'll see how that goes throughout the course of the next few days.
"The more he can digest, the more opportunities there are for him to be on the field. I think anytime you have a guy that can be as destructive as he can be on the interior of your defense, it frees some other guys up too."

title: Bears Defensive Coordinator Dennis Allen Has Huge Problem to Solve Even After Trade
full_text:
Oh yeah, there's a football game this week for the Bears.
After their major trade , the fact they're playing the defending Super Bowl champions can't be forgotten. Neither can one play in particular from their last game, the win over the other Super Bowl LX participant. This was, of course, the 48-yard touchdown pass to Rhamondre Stevenson to end the first half.
A missed tackle by Jaylon Johnson on that play horrified Bears fans, who have noted the team-high seven missed tackles already by the veteran cornerback. And now the Bears are facing Seattle receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who is fifth in the NFL in yards after the catch.
In days gone by, the Bears could simply put their lockdown cornerback on an opponent's top receiver but that was Johnson. This version of Johnson doesn't allow for this.
Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen isn't worried about Johnson's tackling, or at least says this.
Not glossed over! He's playing like a loaf.
“I think everybody at times has some up and down moments," Allen said. "And so, we try to focus on where do we need to improve and how do we need to improve? And I said this a couple of weeks ago, there's 11 guys out there on the football field that affect the game on every single play. And I think sometimes it's easy to try to point out a particular individual.
"And yet I know Jaylon would say himself that there's some things that he has to improve on. So we all have to do that. And that's our focus is. Our focus is not on, 'OK, who can we find out here where we can start placing some blame on some things?' All right, let's work as all 11. And how do we improve as a collective group? And that's what we're trying to do.”
Jaylon Johnson is a massive problem, and that’s an understatement. The missed tackle % is enough to make you vomit. pic.twitter.com/ycvFoFizaH
Johnson wasn't the only one who played the pass poorly. It seemed Stevenson ran past virtually everyone from the linebackers through the safeties. It was the Hail Mary play flipped upside down and the Bears couldn't handle it.
"Yeah, look that's always been a focus and I think all those things start, No. 1, with execution and doing everything right," Allen said. "And when you do everything right you eliminate the space and therefore not a lot of open field space for guys to run in. So I think that's where it starts."
It's at least good Allen has a concept of how to halt this issue. Despite the Stevenson play and several others this year, and the fact the Bears had given up the most yards per pass in the NFL this year heading into Week 8, they haven't been the worst team at limiting yards after catch. They ranked 17th in yards allowed after the catch, so close to the middle or right at it.
RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️ 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW
Allen has one other tool now for keeping teams from piling up YAC or even making catches downfield, and that's interior pass rusher Jeffery Simmons. One of the ways teams get yards after catch is completing quick, timing passes. The only type of rush capable of getting to passers on such plays is the interior. The Bears haven't had a good interior rusher like Simmons since Akiem Hicks in 2018-19, and even Hicks wasn't close to being as quick off the ball as Simmons.
"I think it will help in terms of pass coverage," Allen said. "You know, if we're able to affect the interior of the pocket a little bit more, get a little bit more quick pressure on the quarterback, maybe some quick wins, I think that speeds up the process for the quarterback.
"It makes it easier for us to do some things on the back end."
Jeffery Simmons 10 Fastest Sacks since 2024: pic.twitter.com/WSpz3hnfHE
It's still not going to be easy to stop Njigba. The Chargers were the only team to hold Njigba to less than 100 receiving yards this year. He torched everyone. At least the 49ers held him to five receptions, like the Chargers. The other five Seattle opponents couldn't keep him to less than eight receptions. Last week he went for nine receptions and 150 yards against the Chiefs, and has eight TD receptions.
For all of his defense of Johnson, of the impact he thinks Simmons can make, Allen readily admitted they're up against it this week stopping JSN.
"Listen, I think he does a really good job of creating access on the line of scrimmage," Allen said. "I think he does a really good job of creating separation at the top of the route. I think what makes him exceptional is his ability with run after catch. He can take a short throw and it's 40 or 50 yards later before somebody is finally getting him down on the ground.
Tom Brady explains what makes Jaxon Smith-Njigba so special. pic.twitter.com/Oc3gAykDyc
"There's several examples of that. One the opening game of the season they throw a little quick hitch on a spot route on a short-yardage plays and he makes somebody miss and the next thing you know the game's tied."
Allen went on to list great hands and ability to work one-on-one matchups in the red zone as other Njigba strengths. The bottom line for the Bears is pretty simple this week.
They need to come ready to defend the pass because their own offense is going to find itself tested to the extreme by what looks like the best all-around defense in the league. They won't get away with tactical wins by holding the ball on offense and keeping their defense off the field when the opponent has so effective of a weapon available.
Yet, the Seahawks are only one game over .500 and three losses show one key to beating them. That's getting Sam Darnold to cough up the football in the air or with their pass rush. Seattle committed 10 turnovers in its three losses and three in its four wins.
It's going to need to be rush and cover, and they appear to have the rush taken care of going forward thanks to a trade. The cover is their question.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba is going to be a really, really big problem for the Bears when they visit the Seahawks. "They're not going to stop him," @BigAntHerron says. "What they have to do is hope they can force Sam Darnold into a mistake — or mistakes, plural." pic.twitter.com/VPu7XID579

title: Colston Loveland, Kyle Monangai & More Injury Updates From Bears' Final Practice Report
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' final Week 8 injury report is out and the Bears have a total of one player ruled out and another two questionable ahead of the game against the Seattle Seahawks.
All week long we've been monitoring the status of running back Kyle Monangai, who hasn't suited up since Week 4 because of a turf toe injury.
We've also been closely monitoring the statuses of cornerback Malik Muhammad, linebacker D'Marco Jackson and tight end Colston Loveland, with Loveland being a mid-week addition because of a neck injury.
Here's the latest updates on those four players and everyone else who was listed on the team's injury report this week.
Loveland popped up on the injury report on Friday, which was obviously concerning. However, head coach Ben Johnson told reporters on Saturday that the injury was believed to be minor .
Clearly that is indeed the case, as Loveland turned in a full session and was removed from the injury report. He's now good to go.
That's a huge development because the Bears could ill-afford to lose another tight end after Cole Kmet was ruled out for the season due to his knee injury suffered in Week 7.
Monangai has been ruled out for a fourth consecutive contest, something Johnson revealed before practice.
We're a bit surprised Monangai is going to miss a fourth game after the Bears decided not to place him on injured reserve . His injury was apparently at least a bit worse than initially thought.
With Monangai out, the Bears will once again deploy D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson as their top two backs, with Zavier Scott filling in as the RB3.
The biggest concerns right now are for Muhammad and Jackson, both of whom are questionable.
Jackson appears to be trending toward playing, though, after he was able to turn in a full practice after being limited on Thursday and a non-participant on Friday.
We're less optimistic about Muhammad, who was unable to turn in a single full practice during the week and instead was limited throughout.
If Muhammad can't go, it'll be bad news for the Bears, as the rookie has been the team's best cornerback this year. His absence would push Tyrique Stevenson back into a starting role. Stevenson has not been good this season, nor has Jaylon Johnson, so Chicago would have a big problem on its hands on the boundary.
Edwards' return after a two-game absence will be especially big if Jackson is forced to sit. Noah Sewell would likely step into Jackson's role if he doesn't play.

title: There's a New Bears Sheriff in Chitown and He Doesn't Mind Saying So
full_text:
When Bears GM Ryan Poles did his due diligence on defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, one thing he heard over and over besides the ridiculous athletic ability was high-intensity leadership and character.
He even saw some of this himself during the joint practice the Bears held in Nashville in August.
"When your phone blows up and you have coaches and players, people that have been with him that talk about what he means to a football team and to the culture, you know exactly what he's going to do," Poles said. "And we felt that a little bit in joint practice as well."
GMs and coaches will all talk about character and leadership, and many of the players Poles brought to Chicago in free agency or by trade have been touted for similar reasons.
It seems now, however, they have added someone who holds people accountable, even those who were acquired to hold people accountable. Simmons hasn't been someone who trifles with this concept of leadership, and even said something along those lines to defensive leaders Grady Jarrett and Montez Sweat.
"Like I told Grady today, like, if I'm getting that slide (by interior blockers), I expect you to go win," Simmons said. "And that's pretty much what it is. Same with Montez. I'm like, if the tackles could hang on me and you can't get off the ball and go get a free sack, there's something wrong.
"And that's just a Thursday conversation that I'm having with these guys."
💪 The 10 most disruptive NFL defensive tackles in 2026, ranked by disruption EPA: 1. Jeffery Simmons, CHI (17.4) 2. Quinnen Williams, DAL (17.3) 3. DeForest Buckner, SF (15.1) 4. Dexter Lawrence, CIN (15.0) 5. Malcolm Roach, DEN (14.3) 6. Gracen Halton, SF (14.1) 7. Deone… pic.twitter.com/XNyN9o71BW
Some might call that an eye-opener, as openers go. Simmons did make it clear he wasn't saying those two were slacking, but was using his comments in the discussion as an example and would expect others to say this of him if they saw him not getting it done.
Certainly Simmons has been double-teamed. According to Pro Football Focus, he was double-teamed the 16th highest percentage of plays (66.67%) last season. He knows how to fight through it, though, because he ranked first in PFF pass rush grade, in total sacks and for pass rush win rate among defensive tackles. This year he is third in pressures (24) and sacks (20) and first in defensive stops (20).
Simmons doesn't need to be reminded what he must do for the team. It's planted on him to the tune of what the Bears gave up to get him.
No one’s been able to fill the void of @The_Dream99 on the #Bears since he’s left now they have Jeffery Simmons who brings the same style of tenacity/aggressiveness/playmaking to the #Bears defense. Love this move. pic.twitter.com/bA8HjMjYjB
“The trade told me everything I needed to know, especially the value — from giving away two first round picks," Sweat said. "I could also look on the other side of that and be like, ‘Man, I just got traded.’ But I could also look on the bright side of things: This team believes in what they have here, and they want it right now.
"My game, my passion, my energy, my leadership, I can only help this team even more than what it's got. This is a great locker room from quarterback all the way down, so my job is to come in here and be nothing more than myself, and I'm excited to be able to help this team compete for a championship, and that's every team’s goal in the NFL. I think right now, with the way this team has been competing, I've been watching these guys from afar. It's a great team, great locker room, and I'm excited to do my part to help this team get to its goal.”
He's there to do his part, and it would appear to make sure everyone does theirs. Every team can use this honesty.
"I don't know that I've had anybody that's been what I would consider this dominant." Dennis Allen on Jeffery Simmons 👀 pic.twitter.com/XGH2l0UtEq

title: Kyle Monangai Injury Update: Bears RB Will Miss a Fourth Straight Game
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will have to face the Seattle Seahawks without their star second-year running back. Head coach Ben Johnson ruled Kyle Monangai out for Week 8 on Saturday, according to Bears reporter Kevin Fishbain . This marks the fourth straight game that Monangai will miss ever since he first popped up on the Bears' injury report with a turf toe injury.
The last time we saw Monangai, he had pulverized the New York Jets in the Bears' dominant Week 4 victory at Soldier Field. On a day when D'Andre Swift had trouble with ball security, Monangai carried the rock a career-high 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns. His 5.4 yards per carry average through four games was near the top of the league at the time, and he appeared to be on the verge of a breakout season.
Luckily for the Bears, all hope for a strong running performance in Week 8 is not lost with Monangai's absence. Despite some issues this year, Swift remains a solid running back who had an explosive performance in the Bears' season opener . Even fourth-year veteran Roschon Johnson answered the call admirably in Week 6, carrying the ball 13 times for 51 yards, though he did lose a costly fumble.
Don't forget about the Bears' dominant offensive line, either, and how critical that is to the success of any team's running game. The right side of Chicago's line, 2025 All-Pro Darnell Wright and Jonah Jackson, are arguably the best tackle-guard tandem in the entire NFL when it comes to run blocking, and it's why Ben Johnson felt comfortable in the offseason openly admitting that they prefer to run to the right side.
It's okay if opposing defenses know this tendency in Chicago's run game; it's not like they're going to stop them anyway.
It may be for the best that Monangai doesn't play in Week 8. The Bears will likely want to lean on the arm of Caleb Williams in this matchup anyway, and their defense should be ready to go blow-for-blow with the defending champs since their blockbuster trade for superstar Jefferery Simmons . Besides, after Week 8 the Bears get a favorable Week 9 matchup against the hapless Tampa Bay Buccaneers, then they get their bye week.
By then, Monangai should be fully healed up and ready for a postseason push.

title: Bengals DE Shemar Stewart Active for Titans After Being a Healthy Scratch vs. Ravens
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Shemar Stewart is active for today’s game against the Tennessee Titans after being a healthy scratch a week ago.
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor and defensive coordinator Al Golden made it point to praise Stewart this week and point out that the decision to make Stewart inactive against the Baltimore Ravens had nothing to do with his practice habits or skillset.
“We're just in a really tough spot with our inactives right now,” Taylor said Wednesday. “Sometimes we're really healthy, sometimes we're beat up at a position where we need another guy up. So unfortunately we just had to pull from the D-line, and it's a really deep D-line group and it's really difficult to choose who's going to be an active there.”
Stewart, the team's 2025 first-round pick, has only appeared in three of the six games this season and has only played 17 snaps.
The hyperextended knee he suffered in the first training camp practice put him way behind after numerous starts and stops during his rookie season.
Golden said Stewart has done everything they’ve asked since returning to practice in early September, he has just needed time to get up to speed.
“I'm not discouraged at all in Shemar. I'm really not,” Golden said this week. “I think that was unfortunate. I was really hoping to see him take a big jump last week, and I have the same hope as I sit here today.
“I'm disappointed for him,” he added. “This has been a hard start. He's been really positive. He continues to get better, and when it's his turn, the important thing is that he doesn't leave the field again.”
With the Bengals favored by 12.5 points today against the Titans, the hope is that they can build a big lead, as they did against the Ravens last Sunday, and rest some starters ahead of the long flight to Madrid, Spain, for next week’s game against the Atlanta Falcons.
That would give Stewart a chance to get some needed game reps.
Linebacker Joe Giles-Harris, who was listed as questionable with a calf injury, is active and expected to play.
The other inactives are safety Kyle Dugger, who was ruled out Friday with a quad injury, along with healthy scratches center Connor Lew, offensive tackle Myles Hinton, defensive tackle Landon Robinson and wide receiver Mitch Tinsley.

title: Report: Bengals Among Confirmed Teams With Jonathan Taylor Trade Interest
full_text:
The Bengals have reported interest in Jonathan Taylor.
FOX Sports' Jordan Scultz posted on Sunday that multiple teams are interested in trading for the star Colts running back.
"As the Colts continue to field trade offers for star RB Jonathan Taylor, sources say the Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Bengals and Packers are among the teams that have checked in. The asking price is believed to be too high right now, but sources do believe a trade is leaning to be more likely than not at this point," Schultz posted on X .
Cincinnati is clearly trying to upgrade its lowly-ranked rushing attack with a proven talent like Taylor.
The 27-year-old is under contract for $15 million next season and $9.46 million during the 2028 season before hitting the 30-year-old wall that can crush running back efficiency. He and Chase Brown have been comparable in terms of impact, but a two-headed rushing attack with the rest of Cincinnati's weapons could make them the best offense in the NFL.
The Bengals just posted one of their best offensive halves of the century on Sunday and sit at 4-2 entering Week 8. The franchise may never have a lightning strike like this again with their 2026 schedule. It's the easiest remaining slate in the league based on just about every metric.
The defense has been a big part of that, and adding Taylor could help aid that unit as well.
"If we're going to continue to be great in the red zone and really good at short yardage, it's going to be really difficult for people to put points up on the board, and we got to take a lot of pride in that," Zac Taylor said this week. "And sometimes it's after long drives where you've been on the field yesterday for eight minutes, and it's defeating because they've converted third downs and gotten big plays, and you got to overcome adversity, and then you got to just buckle up and hold them to a field goal.
"That's what we did twice yesterday, and that turned out to be really significant in the first half to hold them to those field goals and not touchdowns."
Taylor has over 8,000 rushing yards since entering the league in 2020. He could essentially take Brown's spot as the lone feature running back next season after Cincinnati's current starter has his contract run out in 2027. We will see what the star rusher's price ends up being ahead of the trade deadline on Nov. 10.

title: Bengals-Chargers Trade Idea Would Bolster Cincinnati Defense With Veteran CB
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have the pieces on defense to help lead them to a Super Bowl this season. They added some talent in the offseason, but they might not be done adding to the roster yet. With the trade deadline coming up, the Bengals are a team to watch as buyers.
The Bengals' defense isn't a bad unit anymore. In fact, the unit is good. But they could use one additional cornerback to complement Dax Hill and DJ Turner.
Daniel Popper of The Athletic recently listed the Bengals as a potential trade fit for Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson, who's in the final year of his contract.
"Jackson is in the final year of a two-year free-agent deal he signed in 2025. He has missed the past two games with a hamstring injury," Popper wrote. "Jackson is one of the most compelling defensive backs on this list. He is on an expiring deal. He is relatively cheap, so he is an option for teams tight against the cap. And he is an experienced veteran who can acclimate quickly to a variety of schemes, though a zone-heavy scheme would be the best fit. Jackson has 23 career interceptions, tied for fifth-most among active players."
The Bengals could use an additional option at cornerback, especially if they can find one for a relatively affordable cost, both on his contract and in trade value. Jackson, considering he's a veteran on an expiring deal, wouldn't cost much to swing a trade for. His relatively cheap contract should also interest the Bengals.
Jackson may have some concerning injuries in his immediate future, but this is a flyer worth taking for the Bengals. When he's healthy, he's a reliable option with experience on a few very talented defenses around the league. The Bengals need another veteran option to complement their defense, and he's the perfect choice if they're looking to swing a trade ahead of the trade deadline.
Jackson has only played in four games this season, but when he's been on the field, he's been quite productive. It wouldn't hurt the Bengals to make an offer for him.

title: Bengals Named 'Best Fit' In Trade for 7-Year Veteran Commanders Cornerback
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals made a lot of upgrades to their defense during the offseason, and it's working out in a big way early in the season. Rather than being the laughingstock defense they've been for the last few seasons, the Bengals' defense now has the pieces to be dangerous.
But the Bengals still need to add one or two pieces to the defense to solidify it. They could pursue a trade before the upcoming NFL trade deadline if they're serious about winning this season.
Daniel Popper of the Athletic recently discussed Washington Commanders cornerback Amik Robertson as a potential trade candidate this year and listed the Bengals as one of the best fits for him if he is to be traded.
"Robertson signed a two-year, $16 million deal with the Commanders in free agency. He has been one of the few bright spots from Peters’ offseason," Popper wrote. "Robertson does not have any fully guaranteed money on his deal in 2027. The Commanders would take on $3 million in dead money in 2027 if they trade him before the deadline. Robertson is a capable man coverage corner who could help a number of teams in the secondary. He can play inside and outside."
Robertson would be the perfect third cornerback alongside DJ Turner and Dax Hill. Robertson is able to play on the boundary or in the slot, which makes him a very valuable piece to any defense. He can rotate in and out to make the lives of everybody else easier.
The Bengals wouldn't have to give up a crazy amount of NFL draft capital to acquire him either. He is a solid player, but he's not a superstar. He would fit the Bengals' defense, but he would also fit their payroll, as he's signed to a relatively affordable contract.
While this is just speculation at this point, the Bengals would be smart to pursue a deal like this over the next few weeks.

title: Bengals in Rarified Air As Double-Digit Favorites, and It Hasn’t Always Worked Out Well
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are 10.5-point favorites Sunday against the Tennessee Titans, which is a rare number for the franchise, especially of late.
In the immediate aftermath of the blockbuster trade that is sending Tennessee All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears, the line did not change.
Only once before in the Zac Taylor era have the Bengals been favored by at least 10.5 points, and it was nearly five years to the day prior to Sunday’s game.
It was Oct. 31, 2021, and the Bengals were 11-point road favorites against the New York Jets in Week 8.
And like this year, they were coming off a huge win in Baltimore that announced their presence as a Super Bowl contender.
In Week 7, 2021, the Bengals beat the Ravens 41-17 on their home field.
In Week 7 this year, the Bengals beat the Ravens 35-13 on their home field.
Cincinnati fans hope the parallel ends there.
Because in that Week 8 game at New York in 2021, Jets quarterback Mike White made his first career start and threw for 405 yards and three touchdowns in a 34-31 victory.
Sunday will mark just the 14th time the Bengals have been favored by as many as 10.5 points since 1990.
They are 10-4 in those games.
Week 8, 2017 vs. Indianapolis (-11) – Bengals 24, Colts 23
Week 7, 2016 vs. Cleveland (-11) – Bengals 31, Browns 17
Week 10, 2015 vs. Houston (-10.5) – Texans 10, Bengals 6
Week 9, 2015 vs. Cleveland (-11) – Bengals 31, Browns 10
Week 16, 2009 vs. Kansas City (-13) – Bengals 17, Chiefs 10
Week 13, 2009 vs. Detroit (-13.5) – Bengals 23, Lions 13
Week 12, 2009 vs. Cleveland (-12) – Bengals 16, Browns 7
Week 14, 2006 vs. Oakland (-10.5) – Bengals 27, Raiders 10
Week 2, 2006 vs. Cleveland (-10.5) – Bengals 34, Browns 17
Week 16, 2005 vs. Buffalo (-13) – Bills 37, Bengals 27
Week 14, 2005 vs. Cleveland (-12.5) – Bengals 23, Browns 20
Week 17, 1990 vs. Cleveland (-16) – Bengals 21, Browns 14
Week 12, 1990 vs. Indianapolis (-11.5) – Colts 34, Bengals 20
So for those who like to make a wager on the games, the Bengals are 4-10 against the spread when favored by at least 10.5 points.
Later Thursday, once the Simmons trade was made official and bettors started hammering the Bengals, the line jumped to 11.5.
Only 22 times in franchise history have the Bengals been favored by that many, with the most recent being the 17-10 win against the Chiefs in 2009.
The Bengals are 18-4 in those 22 games, but only 9-12-1 against the spread.
The Titans have been underdogs of at least 11.5 points 55 times in franchise history, going 7-47-1 in those games. That includes a losing streak of six in a row and 12 of the last 13.

title: Press Taylor Shares Zac Taylor's Hilarious Reaction to Jeffery Simmons Trade
full_text:
Chicago Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor had a fun exchange with reporters on Friday.
Taylor said he got a FaceTime call from his brother, Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor. It was uncommon for Press to receive a call from his brother on a Thursday while both coaches are game planning for their respective matchups.
Expecting some brotherly love or excitement for his success, Press was instead greeted by a smiling Zac Taylor, who said, "We play the Titans this week."  Of course, Zac was referencing the big trade involving the Chicago Bears and Tennessee Titans on Thursday that sent four-time Pro Bowler Jeffery Simmons to Chicago for two first-round picks and a day-three swap.
For Press Taylor and the Chicago Bears, this immediately strengthens their already stellar run defense and dramatically improves their pass rush, as Simmons already has four sacks this season. Chicago is looking to make it back to the playoffs but faces the gauntlet of one of football's best divisions: the NFC North.
The Bengals face just as tough a challenge as the AFC North, so every game matters, and Zac Taylor has every right to be excited that Jeffery Simmons is no longer a Tennessee Titan.
He even jokingly told his brother Press, "I am going to put in a couple more passes."
It is an easy joke to make when you look at how dominant Simmons has been this season and throughout his career.  According to PFF, Simmons has the 3rd-most pressures among all interior defensive linemen and ranks as the 12th-best interior defender in football. Knowing they won't have to account for the four-time Pro Bowler on every snap, the offense can be even more dynamic and dial up an aggressive passing attack with extra time in the pocket, leading to the thrill of Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Mike Gesicki.
"I don't have to block him, but we're definitely glad he made it a little better for us with the game plan," Chase said this week.
"Two hours of anxiety last night is gone," Bengals center Ted Karras said.
That's what happens when game wreckers are no longer on the field. The Bengals look to keep the good times going with a two-game win streak and get the Jungle Rocking on Sunday as they face a young Tennessee Titans team.

title: Zac Taylor Announces Light Injury Game Status List For Titans Matchup
full_text:
The Bengals are pretty healthy heading into the weekend ahead of their matchup with the Titans. Head Coach Zac Taylor spoke with the media after Friday's practice and confirmed backup safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is going to miss the game and Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is questionable.

Meanwhile, the Titans are dealing with a big injury to starting wide receiver Carnell Tate, who missed all of the practices this week with a shoulder injury. He is doubtful along with starting punter Tommy Townsend and running back Tyjae Spears.

The Bengals also do have to overcome the turnover in the backend of the tight end room.
"That'll certainly be a challenge losing a guy like Erick (all), who brought a lot of toughness to what we do, and then losing Tanner (Hudson), who plays a lot of different roles for us; really, he's so versatile, and we feel so good about him in the pass game too," Joe Burrow said this week. Cincinnati's elite passer is confident players like Jack Endries can step up in those roles.
"All the things that we talk about in the pass game, Jack seems just to see it and feel it like the quarterback does," Burrow said. But I'm excited to see what he can do."

title: Is There an Opportunity for the Bengals to Pull Off a Massive Blockbuster Trade?
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' Week 7 win over the Baltimore Ravens was massive. Now, it's time for the team to move on to their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.
With the win last Sunday, the Bengals moved to 4-2 on the season, and this week offers them a great chance to stay afloat in the fight for the top spot in the AFC North.
If the Bengals have more goals than just a divisional crown, there could be some moves made by the front office before the trade deadline that will make this team a stronger threat.
A lot of the talk about making a move for a running back has been in the headlines, but what about a trade for a tight end? One name that could possibly be on the block is Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta.
LaPorta has been at odds with the Lions as his recent comments about getting a new contract proved that the tight end is a tad disappointed.
"It’s disappointing that you go out there every week and bear the risk of getting hurt," LaPorta said on Pardon My Take. “I'm going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it’s going to be all good. I'll go get paid somewhere else. So whatever.”
That sounds like a player who is ready to move on if his current team doesn't show him the respect he feels he deserves. However, Lions head coach Dan Campbell doesn't seem to think his tight end's comments are anything to worry about.
For the Bengals , tight end is a position that recently took a major hit. With the recent news that Erik All's season has been derailed by a knee injury, the Bengals could use a major talent like LaPorta, but it may be costly.
Spotrac currently has LaPorta's market value at $15 million a season for three years. LaPorta will be 26 by the time the 2027 season begins. To put that in perspective, the Dallas Cowboys signed tight end Jake Ferguson at the same age for a $50 million deal.
Getting LaPorta will come at a heavy price. Not only will the Bengals be expected to give him a new deal, but the team will probably need to trade important draft capital.
LaPorta is sixth in receiving yards for tight ends this season and has three touchdown receptions. He would obviously be a massive upgrade at the position, but would the Bengals be willing to retain him with a new deal?
A trade for LaPorta is unlikely. However, if the Bengals want to go all-in, it couldn't hurt to ask if there is a market for the talented tight end.

title: Bengals Trade Fit for Emerging Linebacker is a No-Brainer Move
full_text:
Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. have improved this season for the Bengals , but both have still struggled in certain areas, specifically with missed tackles. Together, they've missed 14 tackles in six games, indicating that linebacker remains a weakness on defense, one that could cost them later in the season. One trade candidate could fix that problem, though, as The Athletic has labeled Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley a fit for the Bengals at the trade deadline.
Henley has flashed elite play early in his career. In 2024, he recorded 147 tackles with an 8.7% missed-tackle rate, an interception, and eight passes defended, allowing a 99.1 passer rating. His 2025 season started slow due to severe illness, however, he still recorded 103 tackles with only five misses. He also had two interceptions with five passes defended.
His play in 2026 started inconsistently, but from Week 3 onward, he corrected that and continued to show the traits of an ascending player at 27 years old. He has only missed two tackles all season compared to Knight and Carters 14 combined.
With Henley in the final year of his rookie deal and the Chargers having tremendously underwhelmed this season, now is the perfect time to acquire him at a low cost.
The difficulty of negotiating a contract extension, along with a rebuild set to take place in LA, could reduce the trade compensation to as little as a fifth-round pick. The Bengals could avoid sacrificing even a fifth-rounder in next year's draft by including Shemar Stewart in the deal.
There is also a precedent for what an extension for Henley could look like. If he hits his ceiling, the ideal contract should land somewhere in the range of what Zach Baun and Azeez Al-Shaair commanded at $17-$18 million a year.
Acquiring Henley would give the Bengals, at minimum, a starting-caliber player at the linebacker spot with a high ceiling as a potential rising star.
Should the Bengals look elsewhere for a linebacker instead of Henley, there are still starting-caliber options worth the investment.
Titans linebacker Cody Barton is one example of a trustworthy player at the linebacker spot as he has remained solid at the position in his eight-year career. He has missed no more than seven tackles since 2019 and will turn 30 in November. Barton has solid coverage skills, but his 4.2% career missed-tackle rate shows he can bring down ball carriers.
Another option is Chargers linebacker Troy Dye, who has routinely served as a solid backup with special-teams experience. The team could acquire him to replace veteran Swayze Bozeman, who is currently on Injured Reserve with a fractured forearm. At 30 years old, Dye would likely fill Bozeman's role better than Jack Kiser, whom the team claimed off waivers after Bozeman's injury.
Either Barton or Dye would be cheaper than Henley in a trade and may better align with what the Bengals want to add to their linebacker room.

title: Micah Parsons Picks Bengals to Achieve AFC’s Top Regular-Season Goal
full_text:
Micah Parsons sees the Cincinnati Bengals finishing atop the AFC. The Green Bay Packers star picked Cincinnati on his Bleacher Report show when asked which team would earn the conference's first-round bye.
The Bengals improved to 4-2 with a 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. Cincinnati erased a 13-0 halftime deficit by scoring 35 unanswered points, giving Parsons plenty to consider when making his prediction.
“I’m gonna say Bengals,” Parsons said in the clip. “I think they’ve been pretty much the most consistent.”
"Ja’Marr’s numbers may not be high. It’s because Tee’s been snapping,” Parsons said.
Higgins offered a strong example in Baltimore, catching six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown. Ja'Marr Chase added five catches for 62 yards and a score, while Joe Burrow finished with 292 passing yards and four passing touchdowns.
Burrow was particularly sharp after halftime, completing 16-of-18 passes for 249 yards. That efficiency helped Cincinnati turn a two-score deficit into a comfortable road win over a division opponent.
“The Bengal defense is playing great,” Parsons said. “It’s not the same Bengals. It’s not the same. I think they low-key win the division.”
The Bengals recorded four sacks against Baltimore and held the Ravens scoreless after halftime.  Cincinnati has 21 sacks through six games, with multiple sacks in each game and at least four in four of those games.
That pass rush gives Cincinnati another way to take control when the offense needs time to find its rhythm. Against Baltimore, the defense kept the deficit manageable until Burrow and his receivers turned the game around.
The uneven start also leaves Cincinnati with something to clean up. Chasing the AFC's top seed will require more complete performances, because even an offense with Burrow, Chase, and Higgins cannot count on five touchdown drives after halftime every week.
Cincinnati returns to Paycor Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 8. A win would put the Bengals at 5-2, giving them a chance to build on their breakthrough in Baltimore and strengthen their standing in the AFC playoff race.

title: Week 8 Browns vs. Steelers: What To Expect, Injury Report, How To Watch and More
full_text:
It's another rendition of a rivalry that runs deep.
Following a 27-24 victory at Huntington Bank Field for the Cleveland Browns just a few weeks ago, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be searching for revenge in the second meeting of the 2026 NFL regular season.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns and Steelers will face one another at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh for a Week 8 showdown. The two sides will renew the storied rivalry in the 151st all-time meeting. This time around, though, the narrative is centered on the Steelers' long winning streak at home and the Browns' opportunity to sweep the Steelers for the first time since 1988.
The Browns last won in Pittsburgh on Oct. 5, 2003, when then-quarterback Tim Couch threw for over 200 yards and two touchdowns, while the defense forced two interceptions in a 33-13 victory.
Looking to repeat such efforts, the Browns will need to come locked in and ready to go against an experienced, veteran-led Steelers squad.
From the jump, Sunday's game is going to be a fiery one.
Throughout the week, the two sides had been throwing little jabs at one another, with defensive linemen Jared Verse and Cam Heyward being at the center of the attention.
"I'm not worried about Cam [Heyward]," Verse said earlier in the week. "I'm not worried about their O-line. I'm not worried about nobody they got on their team. We out there to go dominate."
He went on to say that he has been waiting for the rematch, and that last time's meeting left a bad taste in his mouth due to some "dirty" plays.
In response, Heyward clapped back at Verse, pretty much calling him a baby.
"Double-teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game? Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it," Heyward said. "But we don’t whine about it, baby. It’s part of the game. And so, I’m looking forward to this game. It’s gonna be a fun game..."
But this isn't something unexpected.
In seasons past, the rivalry has run deep, with tensions never really running low. However, that isn't necessarily a bad thing, as a blood-boiling rivalry makes things entertaining for everyone involved.
Fortunately, things are looking clear for Sunday's meeting.
From 1pm through 5 pm, the temperature is expected to sit between 67 degrees and 69 degrees, with somewhat cloudy skies. The precipitation is at 10%, while the Humidity comes in at 53%. There are no expected storms.
While Browns Stadium always sees a good amount of wind, Acrisure will not.
The air quality is a strong 44, with the wind coming in at just three miles per hour. If there are any gusts, they are expected to be roughly eight miles per hour.
Date and Time: Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. EST
The game can be watched on television on CBS, with streaming options such as YouTube TV, Fubo, DirecTV and Paramount+ available as well.
The last time the Browns and Steelers clashed, multiple players went down with injuries.
For the Browns, the two standouts were defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr., who left the game at different points with lower-body injuries. Although Hall Jr. ended up finishing the game, both he and Graham would miss future games.
Heading into Sunday, both players are healthy.
Here is the rest of the injury reports as of the early morning hours on Sunday:
CB Echols (Hamstring) - Out LB Highsmith (Groin) - Cleared CB Ramsey (Wrist) - Cleared WR Skowronek (Calf) - Questionable DB Slaughter (Hamstring) - Out
S Delpit (Neck) - Cleared DT Graham (Ankle) - Cleared DT Hall Jr. (Ankle) - Cleared CB Harden (Hamstring) - Questionable OT Howard (Concussion) - Cleared LB Schwesinger (Ankle) - Cleared DE Verse (Knee) - Cleared DB Thomas (Ankle) - Questionable
Kickoff between the two sides is set for 1:00 p.m. EST, with the winner taking the top spot in the AFC North in a crucial part of the season.

title: Can the Browns Beat the Steelers? Traveling to Pittsburgh is No Easy Task
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have already weathered the storm that is the Pittsburgh Steelers once this season.
But that doesn't mean the second meeting is going to be any easier.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns will travel to Acrisure Stadium to take on the Steelers for the second matchup between the two sides during the 2026 NFL regular season. The Browns won the first meeting, 27-24, but since then, the Steelers have made many changes and improvements.
They head into Sunday's outing with a three-game winning streak in hand, a mark the Browns sit just a game behind.
When these two sides meet, though, records and successes that season are thrown out the window.
It is simply a good ol' fashioned rivalry, and anything can happen.
What is going to make the biggest difference on the first day of November will likely be confidence, especially in the way of the Browns.
As a young squad, they won't just face one of the league's most experienced, veteran-led teams, but also a team that has called their number time and time again in Pittsburgh. The Steelers have held onto a narrative for 22 straight regular-season games: not losing at home to the Browns.
The Browns have lost 22 straight regular-season games in Pittsburgh, and have not won a regular-season game there since Oct. 5, 2003 -- 8,248 days ago. They are one loss today shy of tying the NFL record for most consecutive road regular-season losses vs. a team in NFL history… pic.twitter.com/10avzSmShS
The Browns have not won a game in Pittsburgh since Oct. 5, 2003.
At that time, Tim Couch was the Browns' signal caller, throwing for two touchdowns and one interception in a 33-13 victory. The Browns would go on to win just five games that season, losing 11, but as the rivalry has shown in the past, sometimes that is one of the most important games on the schedule.
Browns defensive end Jared Verse sparked the fire up a bit earlier in the week, putting more weight on a good performance from Cleveland on Sunday.
"I'm not worried about Cam [Heyward]," he began. "I'm not worried about their o-line, I'm not worried about nobody they've got on their team. We're out there to go dominate."
Verse has yet to record a sack this season, but that doesn't mean he hasn't been impactful. On film review, the 25-year-old has been seen taking assignments away from other offensive linemen, freeing up his teammates to get into the backfield and go to work.
As a defense, the Browns rank 12th in points allowed this season, while the line itself ranks fifth in pressure rate. Even with Verse not putting any sacks on the board, the group is finding a way to disrupt opposing quarterbacks.
But in front of the Steelers faithful, Verse and the rest of the defense will certainly get an earful. They will have to show they can cut out the fans and trash talk and put veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers on his backside.
Browns head coach Todd Monken understands that the rivalry runs deep, but he is making it known that this new group of players has nothing to do with the long-winded losing streak.
Instead, he has been trying to set the stage for a new opportunity for the current squad to show the rest of the league how good they are, as a win against the Steelers would put them in sole control of the AFC North.
"Whether it's where we're at record-wise, comparing the past or the history against the Steelers—it's a divisional game," Monken said. "Fastest way to get in the playoffs is win your division. That's the fastest way to get in the playoffs. I mean, you're guaranteed in the tournament and we're a long ways away from that.
"That's not what I'm saying. That's why the game is what it is. And rivalries are made up of good teams playing each other and we're fighting like hell to be a really good team."
The Browns will look to snap a losing streak that has lasted longer than many players on the active roster have been alive.
Even with that, though, rookie wideout Denzel Boston understands just how important a win would be.
"We know coming into this game it’s going to be chippy considering what happened last game," he said. "...I had a conversation yesterday with people [about the losing streak]... which we aren't paying attention to any of those stats going into the game, but I can tell it is huge for the city of Cleveland."
Sunday will be the 151st installment of such a storied rivalry, with the two sides set to square away at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Eye-Opening Stat Shows What the Browns Need WR Jerry Jeudy to Rediscover
full_text:
A season where the Cleveland Browns won just three games and lost a whopping 14.
But although there were many, and I mean many, negatives following that season, one big-time positive was the breakout of wide receiver Jerry Jeudy.
The then-25-year-old went out and led the offense with 90 receptions, 1,229 yards and four touchdowns . He averaged 13.7 yards per reception and 72.3 yards per game. That type of productivity gave a glimpse into Jeudy's true potential.
Posted on X by Gridiron Stats and Info on Saturday, Oct. 31, the last time the Browns had a 150-yard receiver was Jeudy, back during the 2024 season. In a late-season Dec. 2 matchup with the Denver Broncos, he hauled in nine of 13 targets for 235 yards and one touchdown.
Last time each NFL team had a 150-yard receiver pic.twitter.com/gOIl3DRSHK
Even with such production, somehow, someway, the Browns would lose 42-31. But Jeudy still put a positive light on the game as he joined the record books, becoming the fourth player in franchise history to surpass 200 receiving yards in a game, trailing just Josh Gordon and Amari Cooper for the top spots.
However, just a few years later, now at age 27, Jeudy has seemingly fallen completely out of the Browns' offensive plans.
And looking back at 2024 and comparing his play to that of 2026 begs the question: can he ever return to that form?
Just three seasons ago, Jeudy was catching passes from a combination of Jameis Winston, Deshaun Watson, Dorian Thompson-Robinson and Bailey Zappe.
Now, in 2026, he has Watson as his starting signal caller.
Building chemistry has been difficult, especially with Watson missing the last two seasons. When Jeudy joined the Browns from the Denver Broncos, the controversial quarterback was already dealing with off-field issues and injuries, limiting the time they could spend developing a connection.
As long as Watson can stay healthy this season, the bond will gradually form.
Since getting just five targets for two catches and 26 yards across the first three weeks of the season, his involvement in the offense has shot up tremendously over the last four weeks. From Week 4 through Week 7, he has made 14 catches on 18 targets for 145 yards.
While at times he doesn't get the rock thrown his way until late, Watson has turned to him in critical moments, where Jeudy has then delivered.
The Browns know it, Watson knows it and Jeudy knows it: when the Browns need a play, they go his way. He has the experience and the resume to prove that he can be an elite weapon, especially downfield; that connection just needs a chance to fully grow.
I asked #Browns WR Jerry Jeudy about Cleveland’s fourth-quarter grit and ability to find a way to win: "We're just motivated. We're determined to win each and every week. We come with the mindset to win the game, no matter what the score is. We focus on each play." pic.twitter.com/d7mPzimahA
And fortunately, it seems that he will have every opportunity to make up for lost time.
Over the course of the last few weeks, rumors have swirled about whether or not the Browns' front office would start shopping him. While the Browns will at least listen to an offer if it is substantial enoug h, which makes total sense, they do not plan to actively look to move him elsewhere.
It seems that the 27-year-old will have a chance to remain in Cleveland and form a deeper bond with the young offense.
"With Cleveland in the postseason mix and Jeudy maintaining a good attitude despite the emergence of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston at wide receiver, sources say his chances of being traded is viewed as less likely," Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter recently wrote. "The Browns aren't shopping Jeudy at all, and the price is high. It would take a premium deal to get Cleveland to move on -- even if general manager Andrew Berry is open to discussing any deal.
"But as of right now, a Jeudy deal seems unlikely."
It sounds like Jerry Jeudy is locked into the Browns roster unless a team comes with a wild offer (which isn’t happening). Ian Rapoport ( @RapSheet ) and Adam Schefter ( @AdamSchefter ) reporting the Browns aren’t shopping the veteran receiver and "the price is too high." Browns… pic.twitter.com/qV98g4Ce6b
Jeudy's next opportunity to slowly start regaining that dominant form he displayed in 2024 will be this weekend on Sunday, Nov. 1, when the Browns travel to Pittsburgh to take on the Steelers.
The two sides will matchup at 1:00 p.m. EST at Acrisure Stadium for the second meeting of the season.
