title: 8 Players that Need to Step Up in Week 8 Against the Steelers
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns head into Pittsburgh to take on the Steelers, looking to fortify their first-place standing in the AFC North and put the league on notice. ESPN ranked the Browns last in the AFC North in their power rankings and the league is not buying their early success due to having to rely on game-winning drives.
The Browns are 2-0 within their division in the first half of the season and have beaten the Steelers in Week 4 in primetime. Their struggles in the Steel City have been well documented, but they do not apply to this new roster and coaching staff.
The Browns will need several of their young players to step up on Sunday to change history.
Graham started the season looking like a completely new defensive tackle with four sacks in the first four games. He got injured in the first matchup against the Steelers and missed a couple of weeks, returning last week and recording no sacks .
The defense got gashed last week in the running game and Jaylen Warren has been one of the NFL’s best recently. Graham needs to be able to limit their running game and force Aaron Rodgers to have throw in obvious passing situations. Graham needs to then do what he did best to start the season and get pressure from the middle of the pocket.
The offense became unlocked when the Browns forced the ball to Concepcion last week and he had over 150 yards of total offense. Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson have to put an emphasis on getting him the ball in space and letting his speed and elusiveness take over.
The Steelers’ pass rush will be looking to unsettle Watson and he has to get the ball out of his hands fast. Concepcion is the perfect outlet for Watson in the slot being around the line of scrimmage to turn a short pass into a big yard gain.
Fano has been a solid left tackle in his rookie season and he will be tasked with blocking TJ Watt and Alex Highsmith. They have to provide a clean pocket for Watson to be able to read the secondary and make good decisions with the ball.
They did a nice job in the first half of their Week 4 meeting, but the second half was a different story and the offense stalled with turnovers.
Howard got the clearance to start after not practicing all week with a concussion. The edges are going to test these tackles, and they have to come ready to play.
The veteran quarterback finally got his first 300-yard passing game last week and he did that by being decisive with the ball, taking the shots downfield when he could, and leading his receivers for yards after the catch.
The Steelers will try anything to get him off his game, and he cannot let the atmosphere get too big for him. Watson must have a plan at the line of scrimmage for where the ball needs to go in the face of pressure and not solely rely on his legs to bail him out.
Verse does not have a sack this season and at times gets lost in the shuffle of the line of scrimmage. He has been close on making big plays and has helped the line in general, make game-changing plays.
He needs to be effective against the run and make Warren try and beat them on the inside. If he can control the perimeter, then it will allow Grand Delpit and Emmanuel McNeil-Warren to play in the secondary and ball hawk. The first meeting ended with an interception by Delpit.
The offense looked completely different last week, with Judkins exploding for his best game of the season. They ran the ball with Watson under center more than they had in previous weeks and there were bigger holes for Judkins to hit.
The Browns have to stay out of third-and-long situations and Judkins has to build on last week and forget about the first handful of games.
The Browns are considerably better on offense when Fannin is involved. They have gone away from him in a couple of games, and the offense struggled. They made an effort to get him the ball last week, and he helped them on the last drive by breaking tackles and setting them up with a chip-shot field goal.
The task is tough, but the Browns have not seemed to care about the situation they have been put in so far this season. If these players perform to their capabilities, then the Browns can leave Pittsburgh with their stamp on the division and the rest of the NFL will take notice .
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Browns Final Injury Report Reveals a Few Key Concerns Against Steelers
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have one of their biggest tests of the season coming up this Sunday when they take on the Pittsburgh Steelers.
With both teams battling for the top spot in the AFC North, it’ll be crucial for the Browns to be as prepared as they can be heading into this contest. The most important thing for Cleveland will be the availability of their players.
A few names popped up on the injury report over the course of the week that were alarming, but some have since been cleared and will play. That won’t be the case for every player that was listed.
Friday #Browns @ #Steelers injury report pic.twitter.com/SDoQKuljwn
Whether it’s a starter or a depth player, everyone will matter in this game, as it can be a brutally physical game anytime the Browns face off against the Steelers.
Cleveland got the best of Pittsburgh a couple of weeks ago on Thursday Night Football, but this is a new week with new stakes. Here are a few names from the injury report to watch out for in this divisional duel:
In Cleveland’s last game against Pittsburgh, Graham suffered a lower leg injury that looked a lot worse , but he was ruled week-to-week following the game. Now, Graham looks primed to play against the team that took him out once again.
Graham hasn’t recorded any stats in their previous two games, but has been making progress over the weeks, even appearing in last week’s win over the Titans. Graham looked to have reaggravated his injury but was held out as more of a precautionary decision.
The Browns will have to do their best to stop the Steelers’ red hot run game, and Graham could be at the forefront of making that happen. Having their top defensive tackle back alongside the recently extended Maliek Collins will be key to beating Pittsburgh.
A hamstring injury has been limiting Harden this past week, which means he likely tweaked it during their game last Sunday. Harden is one of three Browns players carrying a questionable status heading into Sunday.
Harden has been seeing plenty of playing time for the Browns this season as their third string cornerback and would play a big role in the secondary if he’s available to play.
It’s never an easy task limiting future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but if Harden can play, he’ll be responsible for making it tough on Pittsburgh’s offense to throw the ball downfield.
As of today, it’s expected that Howard could miss this week’s game after suffering a concussion last week. He didn’t log a single practice this week and now is in jeopardy of missing this massive game.
His duties would be to block Pittsburgh’s all-pro linebacker TJ Watt on the outside, but that may be the job of Dawand Jones this week if he’s ruled out . Jones has done well when facing Watt in the past, which should give the Browns confidence in his abilities once again.
In the Browns’ last game against the Steelers, Hall Jr. stepped in for the injured Mason Graham and also got injured in that game. He’s done his best to get back on the field lately but hasn’t been cleared since.
It was also a lower leg injury that Hall Jr. suffered, which sparked Jared Verse’s comments regarding Pittsburgh’s dirty playstyle on defense. Regardless of how the team plays, Hall isn’t officially cleared to seek his revenge.
He carries a questionable status heading into Sunday as well, but if he’s good to go, it’s expected he’ll play an important role in limiting the Steelers’ offense.
Dominic Pagura is from Medina, Ohio and a graduate from Kent State University.

title: Way-Too-Early Veteran QB Options for Browns To Start in Week 1 of 2027 Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have shocked the football world, starting the season with a 5-2 record, but one thing still hangs over their heads: what they'll do at quarterback next season.
Cleveland will face a difficult decision about whether to re-sign Deshaun Watson to a new contract next spring and let him start in 2027. However, the Browns also have a handful of veteran options they could explore next year.
Cleveland will likely be in the mix to draft a rookie quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft, but it might end up selecting one in the middle of the first round rather than at the beginning. If that's the case, the Browns could use the 2027 season to let the rookie quarterback learn as much as possible behind the veteran they bring in to start next season. Here are some names to consider.
Deshaun Watson: Let's revisit the Watson situation. Coming into the season, the Browns had no intention of offering Watson a new contract after this year. But winning is crucial in the NFL, and securing five wins in the first seven games is significant. Watson will need to continue performing well over the next ten games for Cleveland to even consider re-signing him. If he does, he wouldn't be a bad option for the Browns as a bridge quarterback for a rookie next season. Spotrac listed his market value at $20 million over two years, or $10 million per season, so the Browns could get behind it.
Shedeur Sanders: The Browns still have Sanders on the roster, and head coach Todd Monken could use this season to prepare him to start in 2027. Cleveland drafted Sanders in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, and he started seven games last season. He was not ready to be a starting quarterback in his rookie season. Sanders was in a quarterback competition all offseason with Watson, and if Watson had performed poorly in the Week 2 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, there was a chance the Browns would bench Watson and move on to Sanders.
Just because Sanders is unlikely to start this season doesn’t mean the Browns have given up on him starting games down the road.
Mac Jones: It was a little surprising that the San Francisco 49ers didn't consider trading Jones this offseason, especially after he performed well backing up Brock Purdy last season. He appeared in 11 games, started eight, and finished with a record of 5-3. Jones threw for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and eight interceptions. However, he will be a free agent this offseason and could be looking for an opportunity to start somewhere.
Sam Darnold was on a similar path to Jones, bouncing around a few teams before landing with the 49ers as Purdy's backup. Darnold found his footing by signing a one-year deal with the Minnesota Vikings in 2024, where he started 17 games and went 14-3. He then signed a three-year, $100.5 million deal with the Seahawks in March 2025, and just 11 months later, he won the Super Bowl.
Jones could follow a similar trajectory to Darnold: start for the Browns for a season, perform well, and then secure a big payday from another team, especially since Cleveland could transition to a rookie it drafts in 2027 and let them start in 2028.
Davis Mills: Mills has been with the Houston Texans for the last five seasons and is set to enter the free agent market. He has appeared in 44 games, starting 29, with eight wins, 19 losses, and one tie. With C.J. Stroud expected to sign a long-term extension with the Texans soon, Mills will be looking for a new team, and Cleveland could be an option.
Stetson Bennett : Bennett and Monken go back to college football at Georgia from 2020 to 2022. Moken served as the Bulldogs' offensive coordinator for three seasons, while Bennett was the starting quarterback in 2021 and 2022, helping Georgia win back-to-back national titles. Bennett has been with the Rams the last four seasons and will be a free agent this offseason. He has appeared in only two games, throwing two passes for 13 yards, but if the Browns sign him, he could start for a few games until the rookie is ready.
Justin Herbert: Herbert may be looking at playing for a new team next season, as the Chargers are currently 0-6 and might be considering a total rebuild. If the Chargers identify a rookie quarterback they like at the top of next year's draft, they could trade Herbert to regain draft capital to build around the new quarterback. Cleveland has gone down this road before, trading three first-round picks for Watson, and it has backfired. But Herbert would likely get only two first-round picks and a little more capital since he turns 29 in March.
Cam Ward: The Browns almost had the opportunity to select Ward in the 2025 NFL Draft if they had lost one more game and secured the No. 1 pick instead of No. 2. The Titans chose Ward with the No. 1 pick, and he has been a disaster. Ward has started 24 games over the past two seasons, throwing for 4,348 yards and 19 touchdowns to 12 interceptions, and has only four wins to show for it.
Ward didn't find himself in the best situation when he arrived in Tennessee, as the Titans fired head coach Brian Callahan six weeks into last season. The Titans demonstrated how little they believe in Ward by trading their star defensive tackle, Jeffery Simmons, to the Chicago Bears on Thursday for two first-round picks. Perhaps a change of scenery could help Ward, and he wouldn’t cost much, as failed first-round picks usually don’t command high draft capital.
Bryce Young: There is a very low chance—about 1%—that the Panthers will move on from Bryce Young this offseason. The Panthers are currently 3-4. If this record doesn’t improve much and they're in a position to take a quarterback early in the first round, Carolina could move on from Young.
Young is in the last year of his rookie contract, but Carolina has picked up his fifth-year option for 2027. If the Panthers are not interested in extending Young long-term, he could become a trade candidate. A similar situation occurred in 2022 with the Browns and Baker Mayfield, who was also a No. 1 pick. The Browns decided not to pay him as he approached his fifth-year option, which led them to trade for Watson.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Can the Browns Break the Losing Streak? A Look at the Numbers Ahead of Rivalry Matchup
full_text:
After a historic 5-2 start to the season, the Cleveland Browns are once again looking to rewrite the history books this week.
Since their last win in 2003, the Cleveland Browns have not defeated the Steelers on the road in a regular season game. The last time they did it? Tim Couch led the Browns to a 33-13 win.
Let's look at the numbers to see if the Browns have a real chance to sweep their biggest rival.
Sixteen players on the Browns’ 53-man roster were not yet born the last time the Browns won a regular season game in Pittsburgh.
The Browns, led by Deshaun Watson , currently have five game-winning drives through the first seven weeks of the NFL season. This number leads the league.
However, there are some glaring numbers that stick out. Pittsburgh may go after some of these gaps and expose the current AFC North leader .
Looking at the Steelers, their games have been won primarily by their defense getting stops, with their offense narrowly getting the job done.
#Browns Jared Verse responds to Cam Heyward’s comments saying that they are going to address his comments after the last Steelers game. Verse called the #Steelers dirty and that he can’t wait to see them again after their Thursday Night win. pic.twitter.com/ZCQK4ILUuM
Despite the historic losing streak, this may be the best chance the Browns have of getting their long sought after win.
If the Browns can come out early, find a consistant source of offense, and simply score, they can look to control the game with a lead.
However, Pittsburgh's defense is one of the NFL's best. Especially when playing divisional games at home, they will be one of the toughest units Cleveland will face all season.
For Pittsburgh, they need to shut down Deshaun Watson and force him to turn the ball over.
The Biggest mistake teams have been making is letting Watson get comfortable. It isn't a coincidence that Watson is the best fourth-quarter quarterback in the NFL right now. Once he gets going, it is hard to stop him.
In the same breath, we have seen Watson get himself into holes many times before. That is why the first half will be a lot more important than people think.
The game will be decided between the Browns' offense and the Steelers' defense. On the opposite side, with Cleveland facing Aaron Rodgers, we pretty much already know what we are going to get.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: The Browns’ Uniform Combination for Sunday’s Game in Pittsburgh Isn’t a Coincidence
full_text:
With both the Browns and Steelers tied atop the AFC North at 5-2, there’s plenty on the line on Sunday , unlike in the majority of the matchups between the two teams over the last two decades, especially in matchups in Pittsburgh.
The Browns will wear orange helmets, white jerseys, and orange pants for the first-place showdown , the team announced on Thursday.
putting it on 😌 @RiddellSports | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/mphTCjkwNS
It’s the same combination Cleveland wore in their only two wins at Acrisure Stadium (previously Heinz Field), which opened in 2001: Jan. 10, 2021, in the AFC Wild Card playoff game and Oct. 5, 2003, in the regular season.
Without any actual fans in the stands due to COVID, the Browns beat the Steelers, 48-37, to advance to the Divisional Round of the playoffs.
It was a game Cleveland started off hot, as the Browns’ defense recovered a botched snap in the end zone for a touchdown on the Steelers’ first play of the game. They then took a 28-0 lead into the second quarter and led 35-10 at halftime before the Steelers tried to fight their way back in the second half.
The Browns were led by Baker Mayfield, who completed 21-of-34 passes for 263 yards and three touchdowns. Ben Roethlisberger, meanwhile, completed 47-of-68 passes for 501 yards, four touchdowns, and four interceptions. The Steelers had only 52 rushing yards compared to Cleveland’s 127 yards and two scores on the ground.
The Browns’ last win in Pittsburgh with actual fans in the stands, Cleveland took an early lead and never looked back, just like they did in 2021.
The Browns led 16-3 two minutes into the second quarter and then a 30-13 lead after three quarters before winning the game in dominant fashion, 33-13.
Cleveland was led by Tim Couch, who completed 20-of-25 passes for 208 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception, along with four carries for 11 yards and a score. William Green notched 33 carries for 115 yards on the ground.
The Browns haven’t swept the Steelers 2-0 in the season series since 1988. Aaron Rodgers is the only player on either active roster who was alive then. But it appears Cleveland is pulling out all the stops to try to do so on Sunday.
If the Browns find a way to win a game with fans in the stands in Pittsburgh for the first time in 23 years, they would not only take full command of the AFC North at 6-2, but their six wins would be Cleveland's most in a season since 2003, when the Browns went 11-6 during the regular season.
Residing in Northeast Ohio my entire life, I am a lifelong Cleveland and Ohio State sports fanatic. I fulfilled my childhood dream of graduating from The Ohio State University in 2013. I began writing about sports — specifically the Buckeyes and Cleveland Browns, Cavs, and Guardians — when I realized I could no longer play them.

title: Browns Rookie KC Concepcion Is Already Making His Presence Felt Off the Field
full_text:
KC Concepcion stole headlines this past weekend when he had his first breakout in an outing against the Tennessee Titans.
From Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Concepcion dominated, hauling in eight passes for 129 yards , helping lead the Browns' offense in a 27-24 victory. Now, on the season, the 22-year-old has 30 catches for 315 yards.
While he continues to make an impact on the gridiron, he is also doing it off.
Since arriving in Cleveland, Concepcion has used his platform to raise awareness about stuttering , an issue he has battled throughout his entire personal life.
"It feels amazing, honestly," he said on Thursday, Oct. 29. "Honestly, just having the speech impediment, fighting that battle daily, and then just seeing what I can do with my platform for people who may be going through some of the same things or people who may be going through a different adversity.
"Just me seeing those comments and me being able to inspire people all over the world, it just means everything."
#Browns WR KC Concepcion on inspiring people through his media availability sessions: "It feels amazing, honestly. Honestly, just having the speech impediment, fighting that battle daily and then just seeing what I can do with my platform for people who may be going through some… pic.twitter.com/CqmeJMlFqz
Being able to find enough success on the football field to draw eyes has given him a new audience to connect with. His willingness to speak openly about his experiences provides others an opportunity to navigate similar challenges and not feel alone.
"Being able to inspire people all over the world means everything," Concepcion said.
Posted in the late hours of Thursday, X user Steven Aquino quoted a post from the Browns, saying, "I’ve stuttered my entire life. It means the world to see a high-profile athlete do this—and have it normalized—and someone who “looks” like me."
I’ve stuttered my entire life. It means the world to see a high-profile athlete do this—and have it normalized—and someone who “looks” like me. I’m not even an NFL reporter, but I love this so much. Good on the Browns and KC Concepcion. I’d love to interview him one day. https://t.co/dgzFovDXcO
Some athletes use the national stage to promote their own brands or products, or simply continue to raise their status as performers. Concepcion, on the other hand, puts himself in compromising or uncomfortable positions just to continue to make others feel better about themselves.
That doesn't just make him a good person, but also a good teammate.
Rather than keeping his personal experiences behind closed doors, he gives people a direct, genuine look into who he is. This allows people to connect with his character and personality beyond what is seen on the field.
In a letter to @NFL general managers before the draft, KC Concepcion wrote about the type of player and person he is: “By now you’ve probably heard that I stutter. Everyone has. And look, I get it. It’s a good story. I’m not mad at it. And I appreciate the love. But every time… pic.twitter.com/LrJecMbxMu
“I have had this stutter since I can remember talking," he said, following a Scouting Combine back in the spring. "This is a part of me. This is who I am. I cannot control this. I wanna be a role model for those who may be scared to speak up, who may be afraid and not confident in themselves. I stand with you."
The Browns' future is bright, not just because they sit with a 5-2 record and top spot in the AFC North, but because the front office is building a core group of athletes who possess good character, strengthening the bond between players and the fanbase.
Concepcion and the Browns will look to keep the good vibes going this weekend when they take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in a Week 8 meeting at Acrisure Stadium.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns Quarterback Could Become Trade Candidate Amid Colts' Potential Rebuild
full_text:
After only seven weeks of the NFL season, the Indianapolis Colts have thrown a wrench in the league’s final 10 games. They have already traded Quentin Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers, and they have more players on the trade block.
The Colts are in "sell" mode after the termination of General Manager Chris Ballard. Jonathan Taylor could be the next Colt to leave for a contender before the November 10 trade deadline, but they may want to consider adding a Browns player amid their fire sale.
Daniel Jones has regressed since his injury last season. In 2025, the Colts got off to a hot 8-2 start and looked poised to be one of the top seeds in the AFC. Then Jones got injured for the season and they lost their final seven games. He has four touchdown passes with seven interceptions so far this season.
The Colts may want to consider trading for Cleveland Browns’ backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders. The Browns were expected to have been playing Sanders by this point in the season, but Deshaun Watson has gone 5-2 and is shaking off rust with every passing week.
“I believe the Indianapolis Colts should trade for Shedeur Sanders immediately,” - @EvCoRadio on the Browns QB2. Should the Browns trade Shedeur? pic.twitter.com/56Dd87cYuL
Sanders would have a chance to start for the Colts, and the Browns can recoup the fifth-round pick that they used on him in 2025.
ESPN Cleveland believes that the trade for Sanders would distract the Colts’ fans from holding the front office’s feet to the fire. The fans would have someone to root for in Sanders , and if he plays well, then they could have possibly found their quarterback of the future. The Browns may be ready to trade Sanders as Dillon Gabriel comes off the injured reserve and will take up a roster spot.
Todd Monken has not “gotten there yet” in deciding on the quarterback depth chart upon Gabriel’s return. He has been heralded for his processing of the offense, but his physical talent may limit his ceiling. The Browns are in “win” mode and may not have the time to develop and evaluate Sanders.
However, trading for a quarterback like Sanders just to distract fans may be too much of a reach for the Colts. They signed Jones to a two-year contract extension last offseason, averaging $ 44 million per year. If the Colts want a quarterback on a rookie contract, then they are better off drafting one in the first round, as the class looks to be an improvement over years past, and they will have a high pick due to their record.
Jones would then use the last year of his contract to start the season, similar to what the Las Vegas Raiders are doing with Kirk Cousins. The Colts will most likely be entering next season with a new coach and general manager, and they should let those people choose their own quarterback.
It is believed that Watson earned the starting quarterback role over Sanders due to the veteran’s ability to get in and out of the huddle and line up the offense.
If Sanders did not have a great grasp of the new offense after all the offseason and training camp, then getting traded to a new team mid-season would not be in his best interest. Sanders and Watson have complemented each other all offseason, and Monken has done a great job coaching them to success. He is better off staying in Cleveland, as the Browns do not have a quarterback set for next season.
The Browns do not have to make a trade just to make a trade before the deadline. The vibes are good in Cleveland, and they may not want to disturb that in any way . The Colts have stripped the roster down to the bolts and trading for Sanders would be too little too late.

title: Dallas Cowboys-Arizona Cardinals Announcer Pairing & Referee Assignment For Week 8
full_text:
Coming off a big road win against the Philadelphia Eagles , the Dallas Cowboys are hosting the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8. They're looking for just the second winning streak in the career of head coach Brian Schottenheimer, and it won't be easy.
They might be favored over the 2-5 Cardinals, but Arizona has had their number in recent years. The Cowboys have not only never defeated this opponent in AT&T Stadium, but they're just 1-8 since 2008 . The Cowboys have defeated them just once with Dak Prescott, doing so during the 2017 season.
In the past, the Cowboys have come out flat against the Cardinals, often appearing to believe their stronger roster will be enough for them to get the win. To avoid a letdown this weekend, they must enter the game fully focused. Either way, this could wind up being a close contest. With the stage set, let's see who will be on the microphone and which referee will call the action on the field.
It's a top crew for the Cowboys once again as Kenny Albert (play-by-play) and Greg Olsen (analyst) will be in the booth. On the field, they will be able to turn to Pam Oliver (reporter) for any news from the sideline.
Olsen, a former NFL tight end, has quickly emerged as a fan-favorite in the booth. He brings incredible insight to the game and is able to inject humor, without feeling "over the top."
The head referee in this one will be Ron Torbert, one of the veterans of the game. He began his career in the NFL as a side judge during the 2010 season and was promoted to a referee in 2014.
Torbert has been in action for a couple of high-profile Cowboys' games, including their 40-40 tie against the Green Bay Packers in 2025. He was also the referee when the Packers shocked Dallas during the playoffs following 2023 season.
The good news for Dallas is that Torbert's crew has called slightly more penalties on the road team, and the home team has a winning percentage of 66.67 percent this season .

title: Cowboys Trade Target Maxx Crosby Reportedly Off the Trade Market
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have been circulating in several rumors with the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaching, but no name has been connected to them more than Las Vegas Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby .
On Sunday, ESPN's Adam Schefter threw cold water on that idea, saying Crosby is happy in Las Vegas and is not seeking a trade. He also said that while teams might be calling about the star pass-rusher, the Raiders have no plans to move him at the deadline.
"Maxx absolutely does not want to leave Las Vegas under any circumstances," Schefter says one source told ESPN . "His hope, though not in his full control, is that he remains a Raider for life."
The relationship between Crosby and the Raiders was fractured near the end of the 2025 season when Crosby wasn't happy that they shut him down with a knee injury. Crosby did have surgery, but the relationship remained testy and ultimately led to a trade.
Dallas tried to bring him in, making a competetive offer , but in the end, the Raiders and Baltimore Ravens agreed on  deal. Baltimore was set to send Las Vegas two first-round picks in exchange for Crosby, but that deal never went through. The Ravens ultimately backed out after giving Crosby a physical.
Once that trade was negated, Crosby's stance seemed to change. He was focused on getting healthy and both he and the Raiders seemed willing to make their pairing work. Through the first seven games of the season, Crosby has looked healthy and has 18 tackles with two sacks.
Las Vegas was off to a hot 3-0 start, but their recent four-game losing streak has them sitting at 3-4 and reignited the trade rumors. Apparently, however, those dreams for teams such as the Cowboys are now dead.
With Crosby off the table, the biggest name left to watch for Dallas would be Josh Sweat , who will actually play against them on Sunday for the Arizona Cardinals .
Sweat has experience working with Christian Parker during their time with the Philadelphia Eagles, even winning a Super Bowl following the 2024 season.
The question is whether it would be wise to use a premium pick on Sweat. While he's a talented player, he's not the same caliber as Crosby and wouldn't exactly mask the coaching deficiencies that have plagued the Dallas defense this season.
At this point, the smart move would be to continue trying to fix things on a coaching level, since that's where the real issues lie.

title: Dallas Cowboys vs. Arizona Cardinals Predictions: Expert Picks For Week 8 Game

The Cowboys enter this game looking to start their first winning streak of the season while the Cardinals are looking to rebound after a loss and after losing five of six.

This is going to be a tougher game than the one the Cowboys faced last week with the Philadelphia Eagles because Jacoby Brissett is a more competent quarterback and Arizona is a healthier team on offense.

title: Insider Names Cowboys Among Top Fits for Dolphins All-Pro LB at Trade Deadline
full_text:
We are less than two weeks from the NFL trade deadline and the Dallas Cowboys continue to be a team to watch.
Despite being just 3-4, they're in a wide-open division where all three of their opponents have been dealing with significant injury losses. The Cowboys should be favorites to win the NFC East , but they continue to fall short on game day more often than not, thanks primarily to their subpar defense.
That's why they continue to be mentioned as players for a defensive game-changer at the deadline. While most predictions have them targeting a pass-rusher , Bucky Brooks sees the Cowboys going in a different direction. He recently named the top landing spot for several players on the trade block and for Jordyn Brooks of the Miami Dolphins, he sees the Cowboys as a landing spot .
Brooks was connected to Dallas throughout the offseason , but that rumor died when he signed a three-year extension. Even with the new deal, Bucky Brooks sees the All-Pro as a player who could be on the move, especially for a defense needing someone who can change the mentality.
"Despite signing a three-year extension this past summer that made him one of the NFL's highest-paid linebackers, Brooks could be on the move as teams search for an impact second-level defender. A first-team All-Pro player in 2025, the Dolphins team captain has amassed 891 tackles, 13 sacks, three forced fumbles and six fumble recoveries in 103 career games," Brooks wrote.
"His instincts, awareness and disruptiveness make him a perfect addition for any roster that lacks an alpha dog in the middle. While the team adding the 6-foot, 240-pounder must clear the decks to absorb his hefty salary, the hard-hitting tackling machine can instantly upgrade a defense seeking a 'heart and soul' player."
In addition to the Cowboys, the Buffalo Bills and Cincinnati Bengals were named as fits for the Miami linebacker.
Adding Brooks wouldn't be cheap at this point. His contract means any team that would be trading for him would have him for multiple years, so it would likely be at least a Round 3 pick, and likely another mid-round selection.
That would be worth it for the talent Brooks brings. He had 183 tackles and 3.5 sacks in 2025 and this season, has already recorded 52 tackles and one pass deflection in six games. He would be an instant difference-maker, but the Cowboys are already thin when it comes to draft capital.
They've also seen improved play from linebackers such as DeMarvion Overshown and Shemar James, not to mention Dee Winters, who had his best game in Week 6 before being sidelined with an injury. That said, it might be tough to see Jerry Jones giving up more draft capital when they already have seen progress at the position.

title: Cowboys Activate Defensive Reinforcement Off IR Among 2 Roster Moves Before Week 8 Game
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have made a few roster moves ahead of their Week 8 game against the Arizona Cardinals.
The team announced it has activated safety P.J. Locke off injured reserve, which gives Dallas' struggling defense a much-needed reinforcement for Sunday afternoon.
In addition to that move, the Cowboys have elevated tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad.
One of the team's offseason free-agent signings , Locke has not appeared in a game since Week 2 after suffering a foot injury in that contest that forced his placement on injured reserve.
Locke is one of two Cowboys safeties to land on injured reserve this season, along with Jalen Thompson, who has yet to be designated to return as he deals with a hamstring issue.
Thompson was placed on injured reserve after Week 3 and was initially expected to miss four to six weeks. He is now four weeks into that timeline, so he could be back in the next few.

Mitchell hasn't proven to be a reliable blocker during his four-year career, but he does have the ability to make a dent in the passing game if called upon.

title: NFL Insider Revives Maxx Crosby Trade Possibility For Cowboys Ahead of Deadline
full_text:
If the Dallas Cowboys do make a trade for an edge rusher before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, they have to swing for the fences.
That's because a minor addition isn't likely to change the fortune of a defense that has been awful this season . The problem is that elite edge rushers are rarely available, and when they are, teams are lining up down the block to acquire them and the price is high.
The Cowboys did try to pull off a blockbuster trade for Maxx Crosby back in March, but they were thwarted by the Baltimore Ravens, who ended up nixing the trade over a failed physical.
That seemed to close the door on a potential Crosby trade for the Cowboys, and that especially seemed to be the case after Crosby re-committed to the Las Vegas Raiders.
However, The Ringer's Tom Pelissero believes there is still a chance Crosby gets moved ahead of the deadline.
The reason for that has to do with the fact that Pelissero thinks the Raiders are still going to field calls on Crosby and if a big offer the likes of which the Chicago Bears sent the Tennessee Titans for Jeffery Simmons is on Raiders general manager Jon Spytek's desk, all bets are off.
"Maxx Crosby wants to be a Raider, he has no desire to leave, and he is definitely not forcing his way out. But GM John Spytek is sure to get calls over the next 10 days, leaving open the possibility of another blockbuster," Pelissero wrote .
"If a 29-year-old Jeffrey Simmons can get traded for two first-round picks and more, why can’t a 29-year-old Maxx Crosby?" Pelissero asked. "And if the Raiders were willing to trade him for that package in March, why wouldn’t they do it again now if the value is there to accelerate their rebuild?"
The Cowboys will probably have to throw a Godfather-style offer at the Raiders to get Crosby like the Bears did to the Titans in a deal that included two first-round picks and a swap of Day 3 selections.
The Ravens pulled off their March deal for Crosby after giving up two first-rounders, so that's the least the Raiders will likely take.
We say "the least" because it's possible the price has gone up since the Raiders might be less inclined to trade him because of the messy situation it would create now that Crosby wants to stay.
The Cowboys weren't willing to offer two first-rounders back in March and it's hard to know if their stance has changed since.
It's possible their stance has given how bad the Cowboys have looked on defense, but it's also possible it hasn't because of how little draft capital the Cowboys have currently. Granted, they do have first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, but Dallas has just 10 selections in total between those two years.
We tend to believe Crosby isn't going anywhere, but after seeing the Simmons deal go down, and knowing the sense of urgency Jones has expressed in recent years, never say never.

title: Cowboys Trade Rumor From NFL Insider Lays Out Unusual Possible Deadline Strategy
full_text:
One issue the Dallas Cowboys have as they navigate the next week-plus before the trade deadline is the lack of draft capital.
Because of his wheeling and dealing in recent years, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones doesn't have a ton to operate with, with the Cowboys having just four picks in next year's draft.
Dallas does have six in the 2028 NFL Draft, but the team is missing its second-round pick and we also know that teams prefer picks that come sooner rather than later in trades.
Because of the Cowboys' lack of draft capital, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones is hearing that the Cowboys might have a "difficult" time making trades at the deadline.
He also wonders if the Cowboys might try and make a player-for-player trade instead of the typical player-for-pick deals we see.
"Jerry Jones is always down to make a deal, but sources there think a pick-for-player trade would be difficult considering what Dallas has left," Jones said on Saturday. "Player-for-player trades have always been rare in the league, but if Dallas acquires help, maybe that’s their method."
Jones has poured cold water on the notion that the Cowboys are 100% locked into making a trade.
Jones continues to say he's open to making a trade , but Jones also said it's "unlikely we'll get the opportunity from outside coming in."
More recently, Jones admitted he isn't feeling an added sense of urgency after some  blockbuster trades around the NFL and "it would have to be a dynamic situation to give up (draft) picks."
This could be posturing from Jones, but it sure seems like the Cowboys owner is accepting the reality of the situation he's in.
It takes two to tango to make a trade and the price has to be right. Jones also has to weigh how much more he wants to dump into this team knowing another trade might not fix things.
The problem with a player-for-player trade is the Cowboys are very unlikely to land the kind of substantial addition they need.
That's because the Cowboys would have to give up one of their best players to get something significant done and how many of those guys can the Cowboys even afford to give up?
The answer is not many, if any.
One player who immediately comes to mind is wideout George Pickens, who is the best combination of valuable and possibly available on Dallas' roster.
Pickens is on the franchise tag , which means he's set to be a free agent in 2027 once again unless the Cowboys tag him or extend him.
We continue to believe the latter approach won't be something the Cowboys seriously consider because paying hefty money to two wideouts will seriously hinder Dallas' ability to improve other positions.
Chances are he won't be amenable to the tag again, which could lead to a holdout situation if the Cowboys take that route. If the Cowboys do keep him on the tag again, the price will be higher and all of the money will be on the books for 2027, which will seriously hinder Dallas' cap situation.
Trading Pickens right now would be a blow to the offense, but it's not like the Cowboys are having much success with him on the team, anyway, and that's because their defense stinks.
All that said, we find it highly unlikely the Cowboys will trade Pickens during the season and if a big trade does go down, it'll involve Dallas giving up more draft capital and maybe a lesser player thrown in to sweeten the deal.

title: Potential Fallout of Broncos Placing RB RJ Harvey on Injured Reserve
full_text:
The curious case of Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey has reached its climax.
Harvey, who reportedly suffered a knee injury during Thursday's practice, has been placed on short-term injured reserve and will miss at least the next four games, the team announced Saturday .
The second-year back had already been ruled out for Week 8 against the Kansas CIty Chiefs.
In corresponding transactions, the Broncos promoted safety Taylor Rapp from the practice squad to the active roster, while also elevating running back Cody Schrader and offensive lineman Gavin Ortega from the taxi squad.
As mentioned, Harvey popped up on the injury report earlier this week with a knee issue; he was limited in practice on Thursday and did not practice Friday. The injury is not considered to be abnormally long-term or season-ending, though severe enough to warrant placement on IR.
Speaking Friday, Broncos head coach Sean Payton failed to disclose an update on Harvey's outlook, saying only, "No status now."
First, the obvious: this further thins out a running back room that previously lost RB Tyler Badie to short-term IR -- a room now presumably led by rookie Jonah Coleman, with fading veteran J.K. Dobbins also slated for a significant workload.
Coleman and Dobbins (and, to a much lesser extent, Schrader) must pick up the slack after Harvey rushed for 87 yards and a touchdown while ranking second on the team in receiving with 25 catches for 217 yards and another score across six games thus far.
“I think I’ve been a broken record just relative to a lot of things offensively and us improving," Payton said Wednesday concerning the run game. "There was obviously a step last week. We have to continue to build on it, different type [of] defense in this game. I think it’s shifting the focus to the technique of where these ends play, the type of front we see. It’s different than the last couple of games.”
Second, there were conspiracy-level theories floating around social media that Harvey wasn't really injured and instead was being kept healthy as part of a pending trade for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor. Those ... can be put to rest.
The Broncos continue to be linked to a blockbuster Taylor acquisition, though if Indianapolis insists on a back being included in the deal, they'll need to settle for Dobbins or Coleman, provided the latter is made available.

title: Broncos' Jonathan Taylor Trade Pursuit May Be Heating Up, Insider Claims
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have officially put Jonathan Taylor on the trading block, per Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport .
The Denver Broncos are among a handful of teams that have "expressed interest" in Taylor and talks are "active and ongoing," per the report.
Schefter linked the Broncos to Taylor last Sunday morning, and on Friday, NFL On Prime 's James Palmer reported that Denver is " monitoring " the situation in Indy. It now sounds like the Broncos' interest could be much more active.
According to Schefter and Rapoport, the Colts have already received an offer that includes a second-round draft pick and additional compensation. The precedent Indy will surely point to is Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, when the San Francisco 49ers traded a second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round pick to the Carolina Panthers to acquire the star running back.
McCaffrey was two years younger — nearly three — than Taylor is now, though. Taylor is older and arguably has far more wear-and-tear on his NFL tires.
But there's no question Taylor still has juice. He's already rushed for 587 yards and eight touchdowns this season, though he's on pace for a career-low 4.2 yards per carry.
Taylor is under contract next year for $15 million and in 2028 for $9.46 million, though his cap numbers for those years is larger, due to the signing bonus the Colts gave him when he agreed to the two-year, $44 million extension they offered before this season started.
That definitely makes the Pro Bowl running back a bit more attractive. The rub certainly wouldn't be Taylor's salary — it would be the compensation required to get him in Denver.
Meanwhile, the Broncos are hoping to see continued signs of life from their running game. There are two games left to go until the November 10 trade deadline, so the team wants to see whether rookie Jonah Coleman can continue to spark the offense as he did last week, and whether veteran J.K. Dobbins can kick things into gear now that he's past the brutal six-game gauntlet of defenses he faced to start this season.
The Broncos recently invested in Dobbins, but they're not tied to him beyond the 2026 season, so if they were to acquire Taylor, they have the flexibility to move on. Plus, the Broncos have made running-back investments in each of the past two drafts, selecting RJ Harvey in the second round last year and Coleman in the fourth round this past spring.
Both Harvey and Coleman have shown flashes of greatness, but if either of them has true RB1 upside, it's the rookie. Coleman has only taking carries in two games this season, but he was impressive in both games and showcased a complete skill set.
If talks are active and ongoing, the Broncos may not have the luxury of waiting until after Week 9 to make a decision on Taylor. The Colts are big-time sellers right now, but it would likely take an extreme turning of events to get the Broncos to spend what it would take to land Taylor.
More likely, the Broncos end up erring on the side of patience with their running backs and ground game. The schedule opens up dramatically in Week 9, and this ground attack could go on a run.
But where there's smoke, there's fire. So we can't rule out the possibility of a Taylor-to-Denver trade. Stay tuned.

Each player was limited in practice Friday; Jones' injury first popped up Thursday, while Waddle and Allen were upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) earlier in the week.
Sai'vion Jones would likely start if Allen were forced to sit. Should Waddle miss Sunday's contest or be limited in any capacity, the Broncos should make a concerted effort to get WR Marvin Mims more involved .
“Sometimes it’s coverage and then it’s trying to find those personnel groupings where we’ve got a number of guys that are healthy and playing well. So hopefully we can find those opportunities," Payton said of Mims on Wednesday.
The team will make a final decision on the questionables at least 90 minutes prior to kickoff on Sunday, when inactives are due.
Denver also listed Mims (ankle), inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) as full participants. None of these players carry designations and will play at Empower Field at Mile High. Surtain is making his return following a three-game absence.
On the other side, Kansas City ruled out defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott, and listed cornerbacks L'Jarius Sneed and Mansoor Delane and defensive end R Mason Thomas as questionable. Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) is expected to play after sitting the last two games.
One of the aforementioned players is quietly an anchor on a defense that's arguably playing the best ball in the league over the last month. That player is Malcolm Roach, who's recorded 20 total tackles, (12 solo stops), 2.5 sacks, and four passes defensed across the first seven games of the season.
Roach, who's in his first year with the Broncos, currently ranks as the 42nd-best interior defensive linemen among 126 qualifiers, according to Pro Football Focus. His 69.4 pass-rush grade is good for 25th.
Payton knows the importance of Roach to his elite defensive unit -- especially so with Allen now nursing his hammy.
“I think I would say this: he does a lot of things well," he said Wednesday. "The other thing as an NFL player, you know exactly what you’re getting that’s very helpful then when you’re putting a gameplan together. Then all the other things with his personality and you guys have been around him, he’s consistent. I think that’s important to find those type of players in your front.”

title: J.K. Dobbins Sets Record Straight on Broncos RB Controversy
full_text:
J.K. Dobbins and the Denver Broncos have obviously heard to rumors over the past week.
Dobbins's body language in the Broncos' 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals last week was curious, and after a handful of early carries, the veteran's role gave way to rookie Jonah Coleman in the second half. Dobbins did get a goal-line carry in the second half, which he punched in from the 1-yard line, but aside from that, the Broncos mostly kept him on the bench while protecting a sizable lead.
Dobbins said there was a good reason for that, though. And he clearly doesn't appreciate the rumors that he's unhappy or that there's something greater at work to explain his diminished role last week. We've questioned it here at Denver Broncos On SI , too. We've also noted the rising trade rumors linking the Broncos to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.
"We were winning pretty good, right? Weren't we?" Dobbins asked 9NEWS ' Mike Klis on Thursday in a curious exchange from his locker. "Everybody wants me to play 17 games, correct? So can you take that into account before you start saying stuff like that? Because the coaches have a plan."
Dobbins referenced his " pinky promise " with the local press this past summer, a sacred covenant vowing to appear in all 17 games this season. He played the first 10 games of last year before suffering a foot injury in Week 10 that ended his first year as a Bronco.
The Broncos not only re-signed Dobbins, but they also gave him a 4x raise on a two-year, $16 million deal this past spring. What he's saying about the coaches' plan for him holds water; the Broncos want to get a good return on their investment, so in games where they're blowing out an opponent, there's not much reason to expose him to unnecessary wear and tear.
Dobbins still takes pride in coaching the young running backs behind him on the depth chart. Dobbins has looked out for RJ Harvey, and he says that veteran leadership applies to Coleman this year, too.
"This organization has a plan for me, and I'm always there to coach my young guys," Dobbins said. "I've said this from the beginning: RJ is my rookie. And we've got another rookie in Jonah. I'm coaching them to make their plays because I want to see them succeed."
Dobbins assured local reporters that his primary motivation is to win games.
"We were up by a lot," Dobbins said. "I want to win the game, and I also want to win in the playoffs and eventually get to the Super Bowl. So, to say... No, we're winning the game."
If the Broncos were losing games and Dobbins wasn't getting starter touches, it might be a different story, he said. But the Broncos are 5-2 and coming off a brutal initial six-game gauntlet to start this season, and that high level of defensive competition goes a long way toward explaining why he's averaged a career-low 3.3 yards per carry.
"I like to consider myself a pro," Dobbins said. "Now, if we're losing, and I'm not getting the carries, s**t, I'm going to be mad as f***. Sorry, excuse my language. But if we're winning and it's working,"
All three of Denver's top running backs contributed their fair share to last week's road win over the Cardinals. Harvey took a screen pass 52 yards to the house. Coleman led the team with nine rushes for 54 yards, closing the game out with some strong running to keep the clock running, while Dobbins scored his third straight touchdown of the season.
The Broncos have a talented backfield, which is one of the reasons why their rushing offense being ranked 24th entering Week 8 is so mystifying. However, Dobbins said there's a reason for that: the quality of opposing defenses the offensive line and backs have faced.
"I mean, shoot, we've got good running backs," Dobbins said. "When I get out there—I know you guys want to bring up the numbers and me having a lower average than normal, because I always have five yards a carry—like, I just played six great defenses, all in a row."
Dobbins believes that the familiarity that Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdaniel and the Los Angeles Chargers have with him only intensified his struggles against those two defenses. Plus, the Jacksonville Jaguars were interested in signing Dobbins this past offseason, so as a matter of pride, they were focused on not letting him have a big day, in his opinion.
"To think that an NFL coach—the Seahawks coach, I was with him in Baltimore, so he knows me well," Dobbins said. "The Chargers know me well. The Jacksonville Jaguars, they wanted me in the offseason. You think they're just going to let me run it up their tails? No."
Dobbins believes the noise surrounding him and the Broncos' ground game has been "blown out of proportion." As the Broncos' schedule opens up a little bit, his theory about the strength of schedule will be put to the test.
Dobbins gets a Kansas City Chiefs defense this week that's currently ranked 13th against the run, allowing just 99.5 yards per game on the ground. Then he draws the Carolina Panthers, whose defense is in shambles after firing coordinator Ejiro Evero on Friday .
The NFL trade deadline is two days after the Panthers game. Time will tell whether these Taylor trade rumors are smoke or fire, but if Dobbins wants to keep the Broncos from leaning in that direction, he'll have to make some hay over the next two games.
He's healthy, though, and with Coleman helping to shoulder some of the between-the-tackles load, Dobbins has a great opportunity to start turning the ship around. The veteran back believes there's still plenty of season left to get his numbers back up, and while that's true, the Broncos will likely be looking for assurances on that front over the next two weeks because after November 10, they won't have the freedom to make an in-season trade.
"We'll get it back above five (yards per carry)," Dobbins said. "It's a long season. I'm feeling great. The coaches are doing everything to keep me healthy, and when I'm healthy, I think I'm dangerous."
There's a reason the Broncos made Dobbins available at his locker on Thursday. The team may indeed be considering making a move ahead of the deadline, but they apparently wanted to nip the rumors surrounding Dobbins's purported dissatisfaction in the bud.
Dobbins is going to continue to start, but as I wrote earlier this week, if the efficiency isn't there, the Broncos have to be willing to lean on Coleman because the rookie's burst and twitchiness have given the rushing offense an explosive edge that has been completely lacking this season. That's been the case in the two games Coleman has received carries, anyway.
Harvey popped up on Thursday's practice report with a knee injury , so don't be surprised if Coleman again out-earns Dobbins in snap share because he's a more proficient receiver and pass protector. The Broncos have the horses in the backfield, but it's time to get more consistent production out of the group of talented players.
Dobbins may end up with more carries on Sunday against the Chiefs, but if Harvey can't go or is limited because of his injury, look for the Broncos to again rely on their fourth-round rookie.
At the very least, it'll be interesting to see how Dobbins responds against Kansas City after an awkward week. Iron always sharpens iron, but now he has something to prove.
What better way to do that than by having a big day in a game that will decide the AFC West leader at the midway point of the season?

title: Mile High Roundtable Drops its Predictions & Picks for Broncos-Chiefs Rematch
full_text:
The Denver Broncos entered the 2026 with a few prime objectives, the first of which is winning the AFC West.
The Broncos started on the wrong foot in that endeavor, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in the season opener on national television. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training.
Meanwhile, after starting the season 5-0, the Chiefs just suffered their first loss of the season to the Seattle Seahawks last week — a team the Broncos defeated the week prior. Now, the Chiefs head to Mile High to try to get back on the horse and avoid a two-game losing streak.
The 5-2 Broncos have won three in a row, and after sweeping the Chiefs last year, they're looking to balance the scales this season . A win would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West and put them on a path to repeating as division champs, especially given Kansas City's remaining schedule.
How will this Broncos-Chiefs rematch shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding at Mile High.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 5-2 : After falling flat on their face against the Chiefs in Week 1, the Broncos' revenge mission is timely. Coming off a lopsided defeat against the Seahawks, the Chiefs run into a Broncos' offense that's finally showing signs of life, with quarterback Bo Nix getting loose. On Sunday, the Denver D stuffs the Chiefs' run game, and Nix finds Marvin Mims Jr. to put the game away late. Pick : Broncos 27, Chiefs 21
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 5-2 : The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at Mile High since Sean Payton became head coach. Nix is 2-0 at home against Kansas City, and with his confidence flooding back on the heels of his historic game last week, he takes another step forward in Week 8. With the exception of that Week 1 performance at Arrowhead, Nix usually saves his best play for the Chiefs. In this game, J.K. Dobbins turns in his best performance of the season, alongside Jonah Coleman, as the Broncos' offense galvanizes around its defense. A Wil Lutz field goal seals the win as time expires.
Pick : Broncos 26, Chiefs 24
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 5-2 : Last week's game was fairly easy to predict if you've watched this team long enough. For the same reason, however, this week's game is much less so. Will the Broncos avenge their Week 1 blowout or suffer a season sweep to their nemesis in Kansas City? Which squad will show up, the Good Broncos or the Bad Broncos? The angel on my shoulder says the former; the devil says the latter. But I've touched the proverbial hot stove and gotten burned enough over the years, so what's one more time?
Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 19
Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 5-2 : It’s hard to predict what the Broncos will do this week with Zach Allen, Jaylen Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga all injured . This game may come down to which team is healthier. However, I expect a redemptive effort by the Broncos' defense after the embarrassment Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs put on them in Week 1. It was also against the Chiefs at Mile High when Nix turned the corner last season. Ultimately, it's an ugly one, but a win for Denver against the Chiefs, who lack pop offensively outside of Walker
Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 17
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 5-2 : The Broncos were not good in Week 1 but have played better since. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are still a quality team but not a dominant one. I think the Broncos' defense has put its season-opening issues behind them, and the offense is showing improvement. Here's to hoping Nix plays with more confidence, Jonah Coleman makes an impact, and Marvin Mims Jr. steps up again, with the Broncos finding a way to win at home . Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 20
Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 4-3 : I can't remember the last time a Week 8 game had so much on the line. The winner leads the division and has a very clear path to home-field advantage, in wildcard weekend, at least. Thankfully, this game is in Denver, and that home crowd will be alive and making life very difficult. The Broncos' defense will hold up its end, forcing a couple of turnovers, and making up for Week 1's lackluster showing. The Broncos' offense gets the run game going with Coleman back, and the play-action boot game finally yields some positive plays. The Broncos win a close one on a last-minute field goal. Pick : Broncos 24, Chiefs 21
Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 4-3 : The Seahawks proved that if you stop Walker, you almost completely neuter the Chiefs' offense. The Chiefs don't have the skill-position players to make you pay on a consistent basis. Denver did a fairly good job of bottling up the Chiefs' run game at the line of scrimmage in Week 1, but couldn't get Walker to the ground due to poor tackling. That won't be the case this time around. Bolstered by arguably the best home-field advantage in the league, I fully expect a rambunctious defensive performance and the Broncos to be in first place in the AFC West on Sunday night. Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 16
James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 3-4 : If the Broncos want to repeat as division champs, this is the game to make it so. The Broncos have been playing better football of late, and Nix certainly looks healthier, but they have fundamental flaws, and the Chiefs are one of the teams best primed to expose them. Moving to Coleman is a welcome change and should provide a shot in the arm for the running game, but the performance of Travis Kelce and Walker against Denver's linebackers key a Chiefs win, as Kansas City finds a way to generate the explosive plays the Broncos do not. Pick : Chiefs 31, Broncos 14
Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 3-4 : Nix bounced back against a terrible Arizona Cardinals defense, and the Chiefs are next. Kansas City's defense has struggled this season, so the opening is there for Nix to keep up his play. There's a chance to take the division lead in this one, but can the offense do enough, and can the defense tackle Walker and company? Denver wants to send a message that the first game was a fluke, with a 29.8% missed-tackle rate among other statistical outliers. However, Denver wins thanks to some big-time decisions from Sean Payton late, including going for a two-point conversion after a touchdown.
Pick : Broncos 32, Chiefs 24
Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 3-4 : The Broncos handled the Cardinals but now must turn their attention to the Chiefs, who embarrassed them to open the season. The Broncos showed more life on offense last week, but Waddle's likely absence means Mims has to step up and contribute. The game being played in Denver may be the difference-maker, and I'm going with the Broncos to take the AFC West lead from the Chiefs' clutches. Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 17

title: Broncos' Trade Interest in Jonathan Taylor is Real, Insider Claims
full_text:
Despite the return of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, the Denver Broncos are keeping one eye on the NFL trade market 11 days ahead of the deadline.
The Indianapolis Colts' fire sale is on; they've already dealt away All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and Pro Bowl defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. All eyes are now on star running back Jonathan Taylor, including those of the Broncos, according to NFL On Prime insider James Palmer.
"They are one of the teams, I'm told, that is monitoring the Jonathan Taylor situation. It's more than likely he stays there in Indianapolis, but they are keeping an eye there," Palmer said of the Broncos .
This isn't the first we've heard of a Broncos-Taylor connection. Before last week's game against the Arizona Cardinals, Adam Schefter linked the Broncos to Indy's Pro Bowl running back.
Entering Week 8's rematch with the Chiefs, the Broncos' run game ranks 24th in the NFL, averagin 94.9 yards per game. The Broncos believe their rushing struggles are largely attributed to the tough slate of elite defenses they faced through the first six weeks of the season, including top running back J.K. Dobbins.
There could be some truth to that, as the Broncos' ground attack finally showed some signs of life last week against the Arizona Cardinals, whose defense is not ranked high. However, there was a big outlier play in Bo Nix's 62-yard touchdown run.
Corresponding to Denver's improved rushing efficiency last week as the return of Coleman from injured reserve. He led the team in rushing and snaps , averaging 6.0 yards per carry on nine totes. Dobbins took a back seat to the rookie last week, but the veteran assured reporters on Thursday that he's not upset or dissatisfied with his current role, and cares only about winning.
Coleman certainly added a different energy and burst to the Broncos' offense, and it's likely the front office will be watching to see if the rookie and Dobbins can show some more signs of life between now and November 10 before making a decision on potentially pursuing a trade.
Sean Payton has always implemented a running-back-by-committee approach, and even though the Broncos just paid Dobbins, it's still been a rotation. If you trade for Taylor, though, you're wanting to keep him on the field and get your money's worth, but then again, putting him at the top of a committee, with the lion's share of the touches, could help preserve his health and extend his career.
Taylor would be costly, not only to acquire from the Colts, but he just signed a two-year, $44 million extension before the season started. He has a $16.1 million cap number this season. However, his cap numbers climb to $21 million and $22.98 million in 2027 and 2028, respectively.
The Broncos have a couple years left of cost control on Nix, even if they opt to sign him to an extension next offseason when he becomes eligible, so if they team was of a mind to go all-in, it could find room for Taylor. It really would come down to whether the Broncos believed Taylor would be the missing piece to put them over the top.
The three-time Pro Bowler and former NFL rushing champion is a great player, and if there's anything that coud hold back the Broncos from achieving their goals this season, it would be their bottom-10 rushing attack. Taylor would upgrade that immediately, and give Nix a proven foundation to build on.
Taylor and Dobbins are roughly the same age (27). Both will turn 28 in the not too distant future, so the Broncos would have to factor in his age and the high amount of wear-and-tear on Taylor's tires.
As we're seeing around the league, the contenders are swinging for the fences ahead of the deadline. The Chicago Bears gave up multiple first-round picks for Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, while the Seattle Seahawks just landed Nelson, and the San Francisco 49ers acquired Buckner.
The Broncos plan to be contenders now and in the future, but if they really want to capitalize on what remains of Nix's rookie contract, a big move like trading for Taylor would make sense. But it would be contingent on how the next two games unfold for Dobbins and Coleman.
If it's more rushing inconsistencies, it wouldn't shock me to see the Broncos swing for the fences on Taylor. The Broncos have two games between now and the deadline — the Chiefs this week and the Carolina Panthers next — but depending on the market for Taylor, they may not have the luxury of waiting until after Week 9 to make a decision.
That's why the Broncos are, ostensibly, monitoring the Taylor situation. Stay tuned.

title: 3 Keys to a Broncos Revenge Win Over Chiefs in Week 8
full_text:
Denver Broncos fans would like to forget the season opener at Arrowhead Stadium, when the Kansas City Chiefs dominated for almost the entire game. Aside from the Broncos getting an early touchdown, there wasn't much positive about their play.
Since then, the Broncos have gotten better, though they still have areas to clean up, particularly on offense. They may not enter this Week 8 matchup with their starting lineup fully intact, though, with several players limited in practice this week .
However, the Broncos still have a chance to win their rematch with the Chiefs if they can do a better overall job of execution. The Chiefs, to their credit, have played well since Week 1, aside from a bad outing against the Seattle Seahawks last week, but they aren't a juggernaut by any means.
Still, the Broncos have to make sure that things don't go down as they did in Week 1 if they want to win this game. Let's break down three keys to winning the rematch with the Chiefs, all harkening back to Week 1 when these teams first met.
One of the top reasons the Broncos lost the season opener was that the defense had no answer for the Chiefs' most notable free-agent signing of 2026. Walker, coming off a Super Bowl MVP award, immediately made an impact, and it came at the Broncos' expense.
Walker rushed for 173  yards on 23 carries with one rushing touchdown. If you take away his longest run of 60 yards, he still made a clear impact with 113 yards rushing on the other 22 carries. He also had three catches for 18 yards and a touchdown.
While Walker is not the only player the Broncos need to be concerned about, the fact is that the defense's inability to limit him was a big reason for the season-opening loss. When Walker was able to dictate the game, the Broncos' pass rush was effectively neutralized, and it mattered not who was protecting Patrick Mahomes, whose offensive line has dealt with injury issues this season.
Part of the reason Walker dominated was that the Broncos missed too many tackles or took bad angles when defending the run. They have cleaned that up in recent weeks, but they still need to be disciplined and avoid those mistakes if they want to contain him.
If the Broncos can bottle up Walker, the Chiefs will have to pass more often, and that would give the pass rush the chance to do more damage. It won't be an easy task, as Mahomes has taken just seven sacks in seven games, but the opportunities for the Broncos' pass rush will increase if the Chiefs can't get the running game going.
It's worth noting that Travis Kelce had a 59-yard gain on a reception in Week 1, but that again goes back to the lack of discipline by the Broncos' defense. However, Kelce was otherwise quiet. Thus, while Kelce can still do good things, Walker is the player the Broncos need to focus on containing to have a chance against the Chiefs' offense.
The Broncos had two players in Week 1 who didn't get any touches on offense. Both players are coming off good performances against the Arizona Cardinals last week.
The first is Coleman, who got just 6% of the offensive snaps in Week 1 and was otherwise limited to special teams. The coaching staff relied on J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, with the former held to 36 yards on eight carries and the latter getting just three carries for 18 yards, along with four receptions for 23 yards.
Dobbins hasn't been effective since then, but Harvey has shown he can make an impact. In the meantime, Coleman has proven he should have a bigger role in the offense, particularly after rushing for 54 yards on nine carries against the Cardinals.
The Broncos need to get Coleman more involved in the offense this week. His ankle didn't appear to be bothering him last week, and his presence could do a lot to take some pressure off Bo Nix if he can be the spark in the running game.
Mims was limited in the season opener as he was recovering from a foot injury suffered in the preseason. Now, though, Mims may be poised for an increased role as Jaylen Waddle's Week 8 availability is in question due to a chest injury.
Even if Waddle is cleared to play, his snaps may be limited. That means Mims could be in line for more snaps on offense. The fourth-year receiver has shown he can still contribute on offense, as he had two catches for 53 yards last week, including a 47-yard reception that showed Nix is perfectly capable of attacking downfield.
Coleman and Mims in the mix gives the Broncos more options on offense and that could be an important step to an improved offensive showing — as could the next person we'll mention.
While not everything that happened on offense in the opener was Nix's fault, he didn't look confident. After doing all right on the Broncos' only touchdown drive, he was hesitant to take shots, regardless of the situation, and demonstrated poor pocket presence.
It led to Nix being sacked three times — the most sacks the Chiefs have had in a single game this season. In fact, the Chiefs have seven sacks on the season, so while they can get after the quarterback, they aren't doing so at a high rate.
The Broncos need to give the respect due to Chris Jones, Nick Bolton, and George Karlaftis, but one way to counter what they can do in the pass rush is for Nix to play with more confidence, as he showed against the Cardinals.
The Chiefs have given up an average of 212 yards passing to opposing offenses, so while their pass defense is effective, it's not dominant. They gave up 365 yards passing to Kirk Cousins and 257 yards passing to Sam Darnold, and neither ranks among the top quarterbacks in the NFL.
If Nix plays with confidence, he should do better than the 131 passing yards he had in Week 1, especially at home. It may be asking too much to pass for 350 yards, but if he can get 225 yards or more, that could be enough if the run game comes through and the defense does its job.
All Nix has to do is be willing and ready to take shots downfield when the opportunity is there. The Chiefs' defense does deserve respect, but it's not the dominant unit it looked like in the season opener.
The Chiefs have shown they are a legitimate playoff contender, and one shouldn't read too much into their game last week against the Seahawks. However, one also shouldn't read too much into the Week 1 matchup between the Broncos and Chiefs.
The Broncos have shown they are a better defensive team than they were in Week 1, and they are starting to figure things out on offense. Now it's time for the Broncos to prove that the season opener is long behind them and that they can get it done against a top AFC team and their strongest divisional rival.
Playing at home will help, but so will sharper defensive play, a confident QB under center, and contributions from players who saw little to no action in Week 1. And if the Broncos get the win, they will improve their odds when it comes to the playoffs, the AFC West title, and a high seed.
