title: Broncos' Injury Concerns Grow as Two More Key Players Surface
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are gearing up for their Week 8 rematch with the Kansas City Chiefs . If the Broncos are going to avenge their ugly 31-10 loss in the season opener, they’ll need a little luck on the health front.
Three starters were held out of Wednesday’s practice , but things changed on Thursday, with two of those players participating in a limited role. That’s the good news; the bad news is that two new names popped up on the injury report.
Let’s take a look at Thursday’s practice report.
Harvey and Jones popping up on the injury report is concerning, especially after they were unlisted on Wednesday. Both were limited, though, so there’s no reason to fear for their Week 8 availability quite yet.
If Harvey is compromised this week, at least the Broncos have Jonah Coleman back. Coleman can pound the rock and doesn’t have to leave the field on third down because of his receiving and pass-protecting proficiency. Plus, J.K. Dobbins is more than capable of doing it all, too. Let’s hope it doesn’t come to that.
With Hufanga still not participating in practice, it’s not looking great for him this week. Friday will be the ultimate decider, but that’s why the Broncos really need Jones to take it easy on his hamstring. The thought of going against Patrick Mahomes without either of your starting safeties is enough to make any team sweat a bit.
Devon Key is healthy, and Taylor Rapp has done well in playing starter snaps since Hufanga got hurt, but the Broncos would much rather have their starters against Kansas City, or at least one of them. Jones is midway through what has easily been his best as a Bronco since joining the team in 2024.
Meanwhile, it’s great to see Allen and Waddle progress to limited on Thursday after being held out of Wednesday’s session. Both starters went down late in last week’s win over the Arizona Cardinals. Hopefully, there’s enough time for them to heal up in time for this massive Chiefs game.
Surtain remains fully on pace to return to the field this week. And the timing couldn’t be better, given the importance of this game.
If the Broncos beat the Chiefs at Mile High, they’ll take the lead in the AFC West. Dener’s road ahead is significantly easier than Kansas City’s.
The Broncos have a few toughies left on the schedule beyond Week 8, but the Chiefs still have to face the San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Rams, Buffalo Bills, and New England Patriots. With a win, the Broncos could have the chance to really pull away in their quest to defend their division crown and repeat as AFC West champions.

title: Courtland Sutton Rejects 'Fluke' Narrative Ahead of Broncos-Chiefs Rematch
full_text:
Few people saw the Denver Broncos' 14-win campaign coming in 2025.
Yeah, the Broncos won 10 games the year prior with a rookie Bo Nix, and made the playoffs as a wildcard team, but they were quickly eliminated from the tournament by the Buffalo Bills in Upstate New York . At that point, though, just making the playoffs was a triumph, after Denver had gone eight straight years without qualifying for the postseason.
The Broncos knew that if they were going to truly become a force to be reckoned with in the conference, they'd have to knock the Kansas City Chiefs off their eight-year perch as AFC West champions. That meant the Broncos had to take care of their own business and when they went head-to-head with the Chiefs, they had to prevail.
And prevail Denver did, sweeping the Chiefs for the first time in more than a decade. Patrick Mahomes suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 15, but Chiefs had already been eliminated from the playoffs. Several weeks before, the Broncos beat a desperate Mahomes-led Chiefs team at Mile High, signaling a changing of the guard.
The Broncos would finish the season 14-3, profitting greatly from an 11-game winning streak. Denver unseated the Chiefs as AFC West champions and earned the No. 1 playoff seed in the AFC, and even exacted some revenge on the Bills in an epic 33-30 overtime win in the divisional round.
We all know how the 2025 season came crashing to a quick and brutal end with Nix's ankle injury. But fast forward to 2026, and the Chiefs are back, sitting at 5-1 going into Week 8.
Meanwhile, the Broncos are 5-2 with the chance to pull away as division leaders if they can vanquish the Chiefs at home on Sunday . Some fans hoped that Kansas City's unraveling last year was a sign that the worm had turned, and that the Andy Reid dynasty was over, but Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton knew the Chiefs' identity was still intact.
"Honestly, they're just a really good team, well coached," Sutton said on Wednesday. "They've got a lot of talent over there. The things that they did for such a long time, that identity is still there."
At the same time, the Broncos have forged their own identity. Since Sean Payton arrived as head coach, the tide has turned against the Chiefs.
Payton snapped Kansas City's 16-game winning streak over the Broncos in 2023 with Russell Wilson as his quarterback. In 2024, the Nix-led Broncos split with Kansas City and nearly swept them, were it not for a freak blocked field-goal attempt at the end of regulation at Arrowhead Stadium.
Last year was it's own thing, with the Broncos not only sweeping their long-time division rival, but the Chiefs also missing the playoffs for the first time in the Mahomes era and only the second time since Reid became head coach. Like two ships in the night, as the Chiefs were going one way last year, the Broncos were headed the other direction, and along the way, a winning identity of their own took shape in the Mile High City.
"We know that we have put together a really good team over the past few years, and for us to get to the top of that mountain last year, we understood that we had to knock off who was already up there, and they were the team that were up there," Sutton said.
The Broncos won the AFC West crown in 2025, but according to Sutton, that hasn't changed their mindset as a underdogs. In the Broncos' quest to repeat as division champs, the Pro Bowl receiver doesn't feel like the NFL world is giving them the respect they deserve.
"For us to get that reign last year, I wouldn't say that it's changed our philosophy. I think that we have the right mindset of, 'Hey, yes, we may have won the division last year, but there still doesn't feel as if there's this respect of the Broncos are a really good football team,'" Sutton said. "I think people still think that we rode off a high and there was this fluke of what happened last year."
During the 2026 offseason, the talking points on the Broncos shifted dramatically around the NFL. They were viewed as a bona fide contender, and often ranked as one of the most talented teams in the league.
However, amid Nix's early-season slump and the offense's failure to launch, the NFL world quickly started selling their stock on the Broncos and seemingly writing them off. While it's true that the Broncos have fielded a championship-caliber offense yet, it's important to remember just how tough their initial six-game schedule was, with games against the Chiefs, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Rams, San Francisco 49ers, Los Angeles Chargers, and Seattle Seahawks.
Nix and the offense didn't play consistently well, but Denver kept winning. The Broncos weathered that gauntlet at 4-2 — which was about as well as anyone expected — and after beating the Arizona Cardinals on the road last week, they're now sitting at 5-2 with the chance to get even with the Chiefs and pull ahead in the division.
"So for us, it's, 'Hey, we've got to show up each week and go show everybody and prove to ourselves that we are who we say we are at the end of the day, and that last year wasn't a fluke. It wasn't just a flash in the dark,'" Sutton said.
The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at home since Payton became the head coach. And while people may still be doubting the Broncos, Sutton and company are focused on standing their ground at home, and sending the message that last year's AFC West title wasn't an anomoly.
"It's one of those things that we have to go stand up and stand on ten toes that we are who we say we are, week in and week out," Sutton said. "And this weekend it's against the Chiefs, a divisional game."
For the first time since Nix came to town, the Broncos were blown out by the Chiefs in Week 1. That 31-10 loss stung , not only because it came at the hands of the Chiefs, but also because it was under the bright primetime lights of Monday Night Football .
The Broncos are fully aware of their failure to launch in that game, and it sounds like they're relishing the opportunity to balance the scales in their Week 8 rematch with the Chiefs.
"I know that we have the character and the fight in that locker room to go out there and perform how we want to perform," Sutton said. "We know that we didn't like how we performed last time, but with it being a divisional game, we know that we've got to show up."
Suffice it to say, this iteration of Broncos-Chiefs is going to be a heavyweight bout. The Broncos have a lot to play for, including the division lead, while the Chiefs are coming off their first and only loss of the season.
Mahomes is undefeated against the Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium, and you know he'd love to get back in the win column at Mile High for the first time since 2022, and really signal to Chiefs fans and the NFL that Kansas City is back in the AFC West driver's seat.
Nix is a different quarterback at home. He was out of sorts in that ugly Week 1 loss, but a lot of water has passed under the bridge since then, and his confidence surrounding his ankle recovery is at a season-high after romping for a 62-yard touchdown last week and connecting on several explosive passing plays.
Week 8's action is going to be an epic AFC West throwdown.

title: Detroit Lions Week 8 Inactives List: Will CB Play Against Vikings?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have officially released their list of players who will not suit up against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field.
Detroit already ruled out safety Kerby Joseph, who was limited at practice all throughout his first week back in action.
Cornerback Roger McCreary is active this week, after being ruled as questionable on the injury designation report on Friday afternoon.
Among those ruled inactive in Week 8 include defensive end Ahmed Hassanein, defensive lineman Mekhi Wingo, safety Bishop Fitzgerald, offensive lineman Seth McLaughlin and tight end Jackson Meeks.
This week, the decision was made not to elevate any players from the practice squad.
Lions head man Dan Campbell expressed his thoughts about the Vikings in the lead up to the NFC North divisional contest.
"Minnesota, playing outstanding football. Kevin (O'Connell)'s doing a hell of a job. (Vikings defensive coordinator) Brian (Flores)'s doing a hell of a job. This thing, they play very complementary football. Everything is fueled by this defense," said Campbell. "That's the starting point. This defense is as good as it gets. They fly around the football. They're smart. I think eight out of these 11 starters for the most part are veteran guys, they're seven years or older and they've been in this system with Flores."
The Vikings have been adept at creating chaos for opposing offensive linemen. As a result, Flores is likely in line to be a head coach again soon.
"The versatility between (Linebacker Blake) Cashman and (Outside linebacker Andrew) Van Ginkel and (Safety Joshua) Metellus and (Safety) Harrison (Smith) and (Linebacker Eric) Wilson just allow them to do a lot. (Outside linebacker) Dallas Turner on the perimeter, (Defensive lineman Jalen) Redmond in the middle among others, they work well together," said Campbell. "And obviously the corner's outside there, (Byron) Murphy (Jr.) and (Isaiah) Rodgers and they roll those other ones. But they understand the system.
"They understand where they're going to exploit you at and then where you're trying to, 'Okay, this is where my outlet is.' They take that away too," Campbell added. "They exploit you and then take away your outlet. They're very good at it and they just create havoc and chaos. And inevitably what they want, and have done consistently, is they force you to make massive errors . It's one thing to get stops. They're forcing offenses, at the end of the day, it gets late. This is a tight game and it's just wave after wave."

title: Setting Lions Fans Expectations for Gibbs, Goff Against Vikings
full_text:
The Detroit Lions ' offense will face its toughest test of the season Sunday against the vaunted Minnesota Vikings defense.
The Vikings will roll into Ford Field with an unblemished 6-0 record, and Sunday's game could have massive divisional ramifications on both sides. A Lions win puts them one game out of first with a leg up currently due to the head-to-head tiebreaker, while a Vikings win puts them three games ahead of Detroit in the loss column.
As a result, there is a legitimate sense of urgency for Detroit to handle business and defeat the Vikings. A big key to that will be the performances of quarterback Jared Goff and running back Jahmyr Gibbs.
Against Brian Flores' defense, which features plenty of blitzes, the Lions could utilize the screen game as one way to get the running back going. Sports Betting Dime's Drew Ellis believes Gibbs is a good pick to go over his projected total of receptions, which is currently set at 4.5.
"The Lions are up against a blitz-heavy defense, so that means Jared Goff is going to have to get the ball out quickly," Ellis told Lions OnSI. "With that in mind, I expect quite a few screens and slants while getting Gibbs lined up in the slot. We’ve seen Gibbs carve up linebackers in the past with his route-running ability and Goff trusts him as a receiver. This season, Gibbs has had at least five receptions in all but one game."
Additionally, he believes that Flores' defensive pressures could get to Goff. The veteran has had some success against Flores in his career, but struggled in the two meetings between these teams last year including on Christmas Day when the Lions turned the ball over five times.
Goff is currently playing some of the best football he's played in his career, and has thrown 14 touchdowns against zero interceptions through six games. Ellis believes that could change Sunday, picking Goff to throw his first pick of the season and go over 0.5 interceptions.
"Jared Goff has been good at avoiding turnovers this season with 14 touchdown passes to 0 interceptions. The law of averages says that has to end at some point," Ellis explained. "Against this blitz-heavy defense, Goff will have to react quick and throw decisively. I think Minnesota will manage to fool him a time or two, which will lead to his first interception of the season."

title: Detroit Lions Week 8 Updated Depth Chart Against Vikings
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have a chance at another statement win Sunday.
After defeating the Green Bay Packers, the Lions will host the unbeaten Minnesota Vikings Sunday with a chance to come within one game of first place. It won't be easy, but the Lions are motivated for revenge after being swept by the Vikings last season.
Here is an updated look at the Lions' depth chart ahead of their Week 8 clash against the Minnesota Vikings.
Starter: Jared Goff. Backup: Josh Dobbs.
Can Goff keep his mojo? To this point, he hasn't thrown an interception in six games. It's one of the best starts of his career, and if he can keep it going against one of the best defenses in the league, he could thrust himself into the MVP conversation.
Starter: Jahmyr Gibbs. Backup: Sione Vaki. Reserve: Jacob Saylors. Inactive: Isiah Pacheco (Injured reserve).
Gibbs popped up on the injury report with a shoulder injury after not practicing Wednesday but was listed as a full participant each of the next two days and had no designation. This is a positive sign after an awkward fall at the end of last week's game, and the Lions will need him at full strength against this Vikings defense.
Starters: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa. Backups: Tay Martin, DeAndre Carter. Inactive: Tom Kennedy (Injured reserve), Kendrick Law (Injured reserve).
Like Gibbs, St. Brown was initially a non-participant in practice with an ankle injury. However, Dan Campbell noted early in the week that he didn't anticipate the durable wideout not being available, and he has no designation.
Elsewhere, Williams has hit his stride in recent weeks and looks to be a huge part of the plan against the Vikings. TeSlaa has provided supplementary contributions, primarily as a short-yardage and red-zone target.
Starter: Sam LaPorta. Backup: Brock Wright. Reserves: Tyler Conklin, Jackson Meeks.
LaPorta caught just one pass last week, though it was a big one on the team's final drive. Wright continues to be the second option, particularly in run-based packages. The Lions have utilized Conklin over Meeks as the third option in each of the last two weeks.
Starters: Penei Sewell (left), Blake Miller (right). Backup: Larry Borom. Inactive: Gio Manu (Non-Football Injury).
Sewell and Miller have formed a solid tandem throughout the start of their time playing together. Miller looks to be acclimating to life in the NFL well, while Sewell remains at the top of the league.
Detroit utilized Sewell as an extra tight end in a jumbo package near the goal line, subbing Borom in at tackle and sliding the Oregon product out. This could be something Detroit explores more often, as Sewell drew coverage which led to Jameson Williams' second touchdown against Green Bay.
Starters: Christian Mahogany (left), Tate Ratledge (right). Backup: Juice Scruggs. Reserve: Miles Frazier. Inactive: Ben Bartch (Injured reserve).
Last week, Scruggs didn't get any action in place of Mahogany or Ratledge as both played the entire game. If one were to go down, Scruggs would likely be the first one off the bench in their place.
Starter: Cade Mays. Backup: Scruggs. Reserve: Seth McLaughlin.
Mays had some ups and downs in his first game as a Lion last week, as he was partially responsible for both of the team's turnovers. Scruggs started the first five games and is likely the backup, as McLaughlin was made a healthy scratch last week.
Starters: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams. Backups: Skyler Gill-Howard, Levi Onwuzurike. Reserve: Mekhi Wingo.
The Lions continue to utilize their interior linemen in a rotation. Williams handles the run downs, with Gill-Howard playing the majority of pass-rush situations due to his athleticism and demonstrated ability to get after the quarterback.
We've yet to see Wingo active in a game this season. After playing just two games a season ago, the 2024 sixth-round pick may only get opportunities in the case of an injury.
Starters: Aidan Hutchinson, D.J. Wonnum. Backups: Tyler Lacy, Derrick Moore. Reserves: Eric O'Neill, Ahmed Hassanein. Inactive: Payton Turner (Injured reserve).
Hutchinson caught up with Wonnum and is now tied for the team lead in sacks with five. The Lions' defense has had success historically against Kyler Murray, and if they can keep him in check again Sunday it will go a long way toward earning a big win in the divisional race.
Starters: Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Trevor Nowaske. Backups: Malcolm Rodriguez, Amen Ogbongbemiga, Jimmy Rolder. Inactive: Damone Clark (Injured reserve), Devin White (Injured reserve).
Last week, the Lions played more nickel and as a result spent more time in two-linebacker packages with Campbell and Barnes. It was Nowaske that got the third-most snaps with 14, followed by Rodriguez, Ogbongbemiga and Rolder all with 12.
Nowaske's increased workload is intriguing, as he provides the team with athleticism as a sub linebacker.
Starters: D.J. Reed, Roger McCreary (Questionable, Foot). Backups: Ennis Rakestraw, Khalil Dorsey. Reserve: Rock Ya-Sin.
McCreary is the only player aside from Kerby Joseph listed on the injury report, and the fact that the Lions haven't elevated anyone from the practice squad indicates that he could be in position to play on Sunday.
Detroit got all of its cornerbacks at least 14 snaps against Green Bay last week, and it's expected that the rotation they deployed will continue against Minnesota.
Starters: Brian Branch, Chuck Clark. Backups: Keith Abney (Nickel), Christian Izien. Reserve: Bishop Fitzgerald. Inactive: Kerby Joseph (Physically Unable to Perform), Avonte Maddox (Injured reserve), Thomas Harper (Injured reserve).
Joseph took a step toward returning with his return to practice this week, but was ruled out and may take up the majority of his 21-day return window before the team decides whether or not to activate him.
We still haven't seen Fitzgerald, who was plucked off Pittsburgh's practice squad. At this point, he may be a future investment or could be a corresponding cut whenever Joseph is activated.
Kicker: Jake Bates. Punter: Jack Fox. Long-snapper: Hogan Hatten. Kick returners: Jacob Saylors, DeAndre Carter. Punt returner: Carter.
The Lions liked what they saw from Carter in his debut with the team. He showed some explosiveness, nearly popping a punt return as well as averaging 26 yards per kick return. The 12-year veteran could inject some new life into Detroit's return game.

title: Expert Predictions For Detroit Lions Matchup With Minnesota Vikings
full_text:
On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will attempt to notch two straight wins against NFC North divisional opponents when they take on the Minnesota Vikings.
The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), are coming off a 16-10 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Meanwhile, Detroit defeated Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers a week ago, 20-17.
Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 8 matchup with Minnesota.
The Lions have a chance to truly solidify themselves as division title contenders with a win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. Though the Vikings have underwhelmed offensively at times, they have found a way to start the season 6-0, thanks in part to a dominant defense that will be the best unit Detroit has faced to date.
As a result, the pressure will be on Detroit's offense to come up with answers for a group that is led by one of the best defensive minds in football in Vikings coordinator Brian Flores. Jared Goff holds the key, as if he can get the ball out quickly and find answers within the opposition he will have a good chance to lead his group to a dominant performance.
It's also an opportunity for the Lions' defense to make a statement against Kyler Murray. I think this game will feature turnovers on both sides, with the unit that gets the ball last ultimately finding a way to win. Detroit gets that advantage, as Goff leads Detroit to a game-winning field goal and a statement division victory. The Lions find a way to win ugly, and remind the league that they are capable of making a playoff run.
The Detroit Lions will face arguably their toughest test of the season yet when they square off with the undefeated Minnesota Vikings Sunday.
The Vikings’ defense has been the definition of elite this season, allowing a measly 12.3 points per game (No. 1 in the NFL). You combine that with a stingy pass defense, and Lions signal-caller Jared Goff should have his hands full in the Week 8 affair.
Plus, Detroit's defensive back and linebacker groups will need to bring their “A game” against Minnesota pass-catchers Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson.
It won't be easy for the Lions to emerge victorious in this divisional contest. However, I believe they will on the heels of strong efforts from their pass-rush and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs.
I believe that Gibbs will help seal the deal for Detroit with several key runs in the fourth quarter, ultimately setting up Jake Bates for the game-winning kick.
This is a game the Lions would ideally like to get out to an early lead, as the Vikings offense is far behind the defense.
Brian Flores is sure to bring the pressure from a variety of different spots, but Jared Goff should be able to make good decisions and distribute the football to Detroit’s skill position players.
The most interesting matchup may end up being the Vikings offense against Detroit’s defense, given that both units are the clear weaknesses of their respective teams.
Expect Jahmyr Gibbs to be responsible for another heavy workload at Ford Field.
The Lions take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in a headline matchup for Week 8. Overall, I see this being a slightly higher-scoring matchup than last week’s divisional showdown between the Packers and Lions.
The Vikings defense is not exactly stout, ranking 23rd in the league in total defense. Combine that with Detroit having a series of unforced errors while breaking Cade Mays into game action at center, and it is hard to see the Lions not outscoring their 20 points last week.
Kyler Murray is a mobile quarterback, and that has been a trend of a noticeable struggle for Detroit defenses. That said, the Vikings’ offensive greatness in their first six games also has come against the second-easiest schedule in the league.
I see Detroit giving the Vikings the first mark in the latter’s loss column, with Jared Goff making several key plays.

title: Roundtable: Should Detroit Lions Trade WR Isaac TeSlaa?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Detroit Lions Week 8 matchup with the Minnesota Vikings.
Christian Booher : I do not think the Lions should trade Isaac TeSlaa. Yes, there haven't been as many opportunities for him in the passing game with the quartet of St. Brown, Williams, LaPorta and Gibbs getting a majority of the targets, he still has a lot of value within the offense. For one, he is the third option in an offense that takes to the air a lot, and second the Lions are very light on depth behind him with Tay Martin and DeAndre Carter being the only options on the active roster. Both of those players are special teams-exclusive contributors at this point, and if something were to happen to St. Brown or Williams, it would be very difficult for Detroit to overcome.
Vito Chirco : I wouldn't go out of my way to trade the second-year wideout. However, I would certainly listen to offers for him if I were Detroit GM Brad Holmes. To a large degree, the Lions haven't needed TeSlaa this season, and because of such, he's only recorded 10 catches this season, including just one on a total of four targets the past two weeks.
I wouldn't say his days in the Motor City are numbered. However, I also wouldn't blame Holmes if he took calls on the second-year pro.
Emmett Matasovsky: Absolutely not, for multiple reasons. TeSlaa will net an overall negative return after sacrificing multiple third round selections to take him in the third round. He is a young player on the more raw side of things. Give him time.
He will make the occasional splash play, but his best work is as a blocker currently, and that blocking mentality is perfect for Detroit. His numbers do not reflect his value, and he has the capabilities to elevate those numbers, too.
Booher : I expect a low-scoring, methodical affair with both offenses trying to control the clock. Detroit needs to handle the Vikings' blitz-oriented defense to have a good chance, and while Jared Goff has been good at times against Brian Flores in his career, that's a task that is easier said than done. For Minnesota, they've leaned on their defense often throughout their unbeaten start and will need to do so again. Because the Lions will be under duress throughout the game when passing, getting an efficient performance from their run game and controlling the clock will be massive for their hopes of winning.
Chirco : I expect the undefeated Vikings to give the Lions a run for their money Sunday. I think the game will be competitive for all four quarters. And while I don't envision Minnesota's defense stymieing Detroit's offensive efforts, I believe the Brian Flores-coordinated unit will limit Jared Goff & Co. And consequently, I could very well see Goff throwing his first interception of the season.
This, to me, will be the toughest test of the season for the Lions offensively. Yet, in the end, I see Dan Campbell's team prevailing in the Week 8 affair.
Matasovsky :  I expect a game very similar to last week’s contest against Green Bay, but with higher scores. The Lions emerge victorious.
The Vikings are undefeated, which comes as a result of the team executing. However, the teams they are executing against are not exactly the top in the league, with their strength of schedule in the bottom two of the NFL.
Booher : I think Jared Goff will be the game MVP. He holds the key to success with how well is able to find answers within Minnesota's defense prior to the snap. If he can diagnose the defense early in the play-clock and make efficient decisions with the ball, he can drive the offense up and down the field and put up points. If he can't, he could be forced into multiple turnovers and as a result it would be very difficult for the Lions to overcome.
Chirco : I believe that Detroit's defense will come through with a solid effort, spearheaded by the likes of Alim McNeill and Aidan Hutchinson. However, on a day in which Jared Goff might not exactly thrive, I'm going to go with Jahmyr Gibbs as the Lions’ game MVP. I believe he'll do just enough on the ground to seal the deal in the Week 8 tilt.
Matasovsky : Jared Goff will be the MVP. The quarterback will feast on a defense that ranks in the bottom 10 of the league. The historically hot streak for Goff continues, and Jameson Williams will add his fifth touchdown in three games.
Booher : The Bears trading for Jeffrey Simmons is a very interesting decision. He is a proven dominant interior defensive lineman who can be a difference maker each and every Sunday, and this move has a chance to put the Bears over the top.
On the other side, they paid a premium price to acquire the 29-year-old and as a result it could come back to bite them. It's certainly a sign that the Lions need to be aggressive to keep up, and the pressure has rightfully been turned up on general manager Brad Holmes to make a move.
Chirco : My concern level is high. Before the trade, I already had thought the Bears were legitimate contenders. And with Simmons now, Chicago might not just be good enough to win the NFC North but also to make a deep playoff run.
When Simmons is on his “A game,” he is a difference-making interior defensive lineman. Thus, I wouldn't be surprised to see Simmons take the Bears to the next level, enabling Ben Johnson's team to enter the ranks of Super Bowl contenders.
Matasovsky : The Bears acquired a star with Simmons, absolutely. It is a nasty defensive line to defend when playing the Windy City. That said, am I engraving their name on the Lombardi? No.
The Bears are good, and they should be monitored. However, my concern this year is significantly lessened compared to if this happened in 2025. The offensive line and their interior is a strength, if PFF is to be believed.
Booher : I do think it's the right thing for the Lions to wait, albeit it is a risky maneuver in some cases. By waiting, they could benefit from a lesser market as opposed to paying a premium price earlier in the process. Additionally, they can take their time and truly assess what the best course of action is and what the team truly needs ahead of the stretch run.
Where it becomes risky is they could lose out on one of their top targets if a different team makes a better offer. That is the challenge of waiting, as by being patient Holmes risks being passed in the market. It's a tough line to walk, but it is how Holmes has traditionally operated with regards to the trade deadline.
Chirco : I don't think it's necessary. If a trade becomes available before then, I believe that Holmes should waste no time to pull the trigger. For example, if the Chargers’ Khalil Mack or the Eagles’ Riq Woolen becomes available in the days ahead, I believe that Holmes should get on the phone immediately to broker a deal. To me, there's no point in waiting if a player Holmes desires is available right now.
Matasovsky : That depends on two things. First, if the wins keep coming. The holes in the roster matter much less when Detroit is finding a way every Sunday. In the short term, adding a Simmons-like player only makes the margin of victory bigger, not the overall result.
The other thing that answer depends on is the value given up. If Detroit has to trade away more for waiting so long, It penalized them for being slow on the phones. As it stands, Holmes has worked the phones, although there is nothing concrete. If it is a return that makes sense when compared to other deals, dislike as long as the wins keep piling up.

title: Notebook: Maxx Crosby Rumors, Lions Roster, Jamo
full_text:
The 2026 trade deadline is quickly approaching, and much like previous years Las Vegas Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby's name is being shared.
Crosby had something of a tumultous offseason when the Raiders traded him to Baltimore, but the deal was canceled after he failed his physical with the Ravens. As a result, he returned to Las Vegas and has played in every game. Up to this point in the season, Crosby has notched two sacks and a forced fumble.
The Eastern Michigan product has an obvious tie to the Lions, as he was born in Lapeer, Michigan and played at Eastern. He has been a popular target for the Lions and their fans in trade discussions for multiple years.
According to a report from Tom Pelissero , he has no desire to be traded but the Raiders will listen to potential offers.
To get a sense for his market, it's important to note that when the Ravens and Raiders made the initial deal, Baltimore was sending Las Vegas two first-round picks. With less than a year passed since that deal, it will likely be a similar asking price for any interested team ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
Up to this point in the season, the Lions' pass-rush has been one of the best units in the league. Aidan Hutchinson and D.J. Wonnum are tied for the team lead with five sacks apiece, and the defense ranks tied-for-second with 21 sacks in total.
Lions' radio color commentator Lomas Brown made his pitch for Crosby to come to Detroit during a recent appearance on Woodward Sports Network.
“Man, come on Maxx. Come home Maxx. Maxx, we know your mom. Come on home, I’ve been talking to your mom, friend of the program," Brown said. "Come on home. She says she knows you want to come home. We want you home. You and Aidan, come on man, who's stopping that?”
Detroit Lions LEGEND Lomas Brown WANTS MAX CROSBY to COME HOME 👀 BIG LO WANTS A SPLASH MOVE 🙌 pic.twitter.com/yoEbT8GAO8
Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams continued his charitable efforts recently, taking time to contact a youngster who had been involved in an accident.
Trevor Travier Jr., a 12-year-old from Warren, has been in CSM Children's Hospital ever since an unfortunate accident where he was hit by a truck while riding his bike according to a recent report from WXYZ Detroit . One day during his stay, he received a FaceTime call from Williams that was facilitated by Lincoln Middle School's School Resource Officer, Adnan Durrani.
"I appreciate you being a fan of me, man. I'm looking out. I'm thinking about you," Williams was observed telling Travier on the phone. "I hope everything goes okay, man. I'm thinking about you in my heart, for sure."
During the call, the two discussed how Travier often dials up big plays for Williams while playing the popular NFL video game 'Madden.'
In addition to the call, the Lions also sent Travier a gift basket that included a bobblehead and a new Williams 'Rivalries' jersey.
For a second straight week, it appears as though the Lions have elected to not elevate any players from their practice squad. Teams can elevate players to get up to a total of 55 on their active roster on game days, but the Lions did not use this last week and appear to not have this week as well.
This is an intriguing development due to how the Lions have typically utilized their practice squad under the leadership of Brad Holmes and Dan Campbell.
Still, it's a promising sign as the Lions' roster is healthy with only one player on the active roster holding an injury designation this week, that being Roger McCreary who is questionable with a foot injury.

title: Two Lions Receive Unnecessary Roughness Fines Against Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions had two players receive a fine for actions in the team's Week 7 win over the Green Bay Packers.
On Saturday, the NFL revealed their fines for the previous week in action, and Lions safety Brian Branch was listed with a fine for use of the helmet. Derrick Barnes was also fined for a late hit, with both fines being listed under the umbrella of unnecessary roughness.
Branch was fined $23,882, while Barnes was fined $11,941.
On the Packers' side, safety Xavier McKinney was hit with a $25,000 fine for his postgame criticism of the officiating crew's performance after controversial calls were made against both teams throughout the tightly contested divisional matchup. Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse was also fined for taunting.
Barnes has been a key cog in Detroit's defense this year, which marks the second of a three-year extension he signed prior to last season.
Branch returned to the active roster on Sunday after missing the first six weeks of the year rehabbing a torn Achilles suffered in December of last season. He returned to practice after during Week 5, and the Lions utilized the bye week to help him further acclimate before sending him back into action.
In his first game back, Branch recorded his first interception on a leaping grab off a desperation thrown by Jordan Love. It was an exciting moment, with the fans showcasing their appreciation for his efforts after he made the play.
Branch is currently in the final year of his rookie contract , and reports indicate that the Lions are open to negotiating a new deal with him along with fellow 2023 second-round pick tight end Sam LaPorta.
The Alabama product has been a valuable Swiss-Army Knife in the secondary since the Lions traded up to get him in that Draft. After he spent his rookie season as the nickel cornerback, he transitioned to safety full time in 2024 and has been in that role ever since.
Branch's return was a big one for the defense, and Detroit could be on the verge of getting his counterpart back. Kerby Joseph returned to practice this week for the first time all season, and while he's out for Sunday's game against Minnesota, he could be in line to return throughout the next two weeks due to his 21-day return-to-practice window.
Detroit takes on the undefeated, first-place Minnesota Vikings at 1 p.m. Sunday at Ford Field.

title: How To Watch, Listen, Stream Detroit Lions Against Minnesota Vikings
full_text:
On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will take on a Minnesota Vikings team which has yet to lose a game this season (6-0).
Most recently, the Vikings defeated the woeful Indianapolis Colts, 16-10, in a Week 7 tilt. It marked the fifth straight game in which Minnesota's defense, coordinated by Brian Flores, allowed 16 or fewer points. And for the season, the Vikings have allowed a league-low 12.3 points per game.
Subsequently, it should be a battle of strengths when Flores’ unit squares off with Detroit's No. 2-ranked offense (30.7 points/game).
Lions head man Dan Campbell is well aware that the Vikings’ defense could create some headaches for offensive coordinator Drew Petzing's unit .
“They understand where they're going to exploit you at and then where you're trying to, 'OK, this is where my outlet is.' They take that away, too. They exploit you and then take away your outlet. They're very good at it,” Campbell told reporters earlier this week. “They just create havoc and chaos. And inevitably, what they want, and have done consistently, is they force you to make massive errors. It's one thing to get stops. They're forcing offenses at the end of the day, when it's late, it's a tight game, and it's just wave after wave and these offenses are cracking significantly. Turnovers, massive turnovers, so it's third-and-32. And that's where they want you, way behind the sticks.”
Undeniably, the Flores-led defense has been the calling card for Kevin O'Connell's team thus far in 2026. And it's even more so the case when you consider the fact that Minnesota has averaged just 20.8 points per contest, ranking 24th out of 32 NFL franchises. Plus, the Vikings have scored north of 23 points just once this season: in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers (39 points).
At this juncture, it appears that offensive outburst was just an aberration for a Minnesota team which has amassed the fourth-fewest total yards through six games (1,690).
Yet, Lions defenders can ill-afford to take the Vikings lightly and must still be focused on winning their assignments, particularly against Pro Bowl tight end T.J. Hockenson and All-Pro receiver Justin Jefferson. As Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said this week, “They can explode at any moment.”
There is certainly a lot of truth in that statement, too. Hockenson is one of the very best tight ends in the game today, and Jefferson is an elite pass-catcher who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons.
“Yeah, you can take numbers and throw them out the window because what they're doing is what it takes to win,” Sheppard expressed Thursday. “And that's why Kevin O'Connell is one of the best in the league and has been, because he understands what it takes to win with what he has. No matter the quarterback, just look at the past four or five years, no matter the circumstances, what does it take to win that week, that year? And they're playing the way they need to win the football game.”

title: 5 Players Detroit Lions Must Scout in College Football Week 9
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions square off for their second divisional matchup in as many weeks, taking on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings.
The Vikings sit alone atop the NFC, looking to keep their momentum, while the Lions showcased an ability to create stops last week against the Packers and need that same ability on Sunday.
Before the Lions play Sunday, though, the college football slate for Week 9 is set to begin. Multiple teams look to make a statement, with the College Football Playoff picture starting to matter much more this late in the season.
Here are five players that the Detroit Lions must keep an eye on during the Saturday slate.
Jefferson is the corner opposite Bulldogs star (and projected top-15 pick) Kelley Jones, and teams have started to turn to the former. Jefferson has responded in a massive way, currently ranking second among all corners in Pro Football Focus grade while breaking up seven passes.
Although Jefferson has yet to record an interception at the FBS level, the corner is physical, fitting the mold of what the Lions like in their corners. Opposing receivers have caught 50 percent of their passes against Jefferson, who has been tested 36 times this season.
He has allowed four touchdowns and been whistled for a penalty once, but has also yet to miss a tackle this season while having a solid NFL-ready frame at 6-foot-1.
Jefferson will square off against a ranked Texas team on Saturday night at 7:30 p.m. EST.
Cheeks is having a breakout season in his final year with the Badgers. Last season, the former UNC Tar Heel served a rotational role, and he has surpassed his pressure and sack total after seven games.
Notably, the pass-rusher recorded nine pressures against Michigan State and eight against USC. Cheeks ranks top 10 among all EDGE rushers in overall and pass-rush grade, and for good reason. His missed tackle rate has also dramatically decreased this year, from over 21 percent in 2025 to a mere 7.7 percent.
The Badgers find themselves in sneaky contention for the CFP with a favorable schedule the rest of the way, and Cheeks is a big reason why. To stay on the course, the Badgers must down Iowa at noon EST.
One of the linemen tasked with thwarting Cheeks will be Pieper. The lineman entered with high expectations after being graded as elite during the 2025 season, and he has met the mark thus far.
While his run block grade, his calling card from last season, has taken a small step back, it has been offset by his pass block grade taking a major leap forward. Pieper is a mauler in the run game, and ranks fourth among all interior linemen in PFF grades thus far.
The lineman keeps the officiating game easy, too, only being whistled for two penalties in over 1,250 career snaps. He was expected to make the bump to center this season with the Hawkeyes, but instead remained at guard.
Seeing that Pieper plays right guard, along with his current draft stock , the Hawkeye might not be in position to be in Honolulu Blue in 2027. As it stands, the Lions possess two of the top guards in the NFL, per PFF.
As mentioned above, the Hawkeyes take on the Badgers at noon EST.
Richard had a productive two years with Boston College before ultimately choosing to take his talents elsewhere, deciding on the defending National Champions. So far, that decision has paid off. Despite missing much of the Rutgers game and splitting time in the backfield, Richard has over 700 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the season.
He is a decisive runner, although he is slightly unproven in the pass game, with his 30-catch 2025 campaign being the outlier after a two-catch and five-catch 2024 and 2026, respectively. Richard has burst in space, although he is not going to be timing in the 4.30s most likely.
He has forced 35 missed tackles this year, which is among the top 25 in the country. Richard has another year of eligibility in his pocket, although the more “tread” left on a running back is positive in most draft circles.
Richard’s Hoosiers take on Minnesota at 3:30 p.m. EST on Saturday.
Another week of Youngstown State being featured. Leigh is relatively new to football, only playing his senior year of high school. That led to the 6-foot-7 lineman going to the FCS level, where he has become a force with the Penguins.
Leigh is a solid player that avoids penalties, and his size and length suggest that he remains at tackle in the NFL. The obvious concern is that his competition is not the greatest, along with his fundamentals being a step behind, pun intended, some of his peers. His inexperience suggests there is a higher ceiling, but it also means Leigh has a lower floor.
The lineman did not impress against Kentucky in his only FBS matchup of the year, and also missed time with an injury earlier in the season. He blocks for Beau Brungard, one of the most dynamic quarterbacks at any level of college football, with over 2,500 total yards and 30 touchdowns on the season.
With the relative lack of success associated with Larry Borom and Giovanni Manu, a late-round flyer on a tackle such as Leigh becomes intriguing. However, a raw player taken directly after the Manu experiment ends might not make Brad Holmes the most beloved general manager, if things do not pan out for the YSU product.
Leigh’s Penguins match up with North Dakota at noon EST.
Sports writer since 2022. Emmett Matasovsky started covering the Detroit Lions in 2025. He has extensive experience covering Michigan State Spartans athletics, including MSU basketball and football. Has demonstrated passionate, in-depth coverage of college athletics.

title: Is It Time for Packers to Smack the Panic Button at Kicker?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have a kicking problem.
With Trey Smack missing an extra point on Thursday, he is up to a league-high eight missed kicks his season. That includes six over the past four games, which begs this question (and the terrible pun from the headline):
Is it time for the Packers to hit the panic button?
The Packers traded up in the sixth round in this year’s draft to select Smack with the belief that he would upgrade an obvious weakness on the roster.
Everyone expected there would be some growing pains with a rookie kicker, just like there’s growing pains with a rookie at any position. However, those concerns to a large extent are a myth.
Over the last decade, 40 rookie kickers have attempted at least 10 field goals in a season. Will Lutz represents the league median with an 82.4 percent success rate. The overall median is 85.1 percent. For a kicker who attempts 35 field goals in a season, the difference in those percentages is one made kick.
Through eight games, Smack is 11-of-16 on field goals (68.8 percent) and 16-of-19 on extra points (84.2 percent). Among kickers with 10 field-goal attempts, only one kicker has a lower percentage. Among kickers with 10 point-after attempts, only three kickers have a lower percentage.
Just how bad has Smack been? For a team that enjoyed long runs of success by Chris Jacke, Ryan Longwell and Mason Crosby, here’s this nugget from The Associated Press’s Josh Dubow:
Trey Smack now leads NFL with 8 missed kicks (5 FGs, 3 PATs). That's most for a Packers kicker in first 8 games of a season since Max Zendejas had 9 misses in 1988
Against Detroit last Sunday, Smack missed from 26 and 35 yards. Other than a block, Smack’s miss from 26 is the only one from less than 30 yards this season.
Talk about a mental block. He could probably make 100 of those in a row in his sleep but, in the pressure-cooker of a division game at Ford Field, he misfired.
Coaches love to talk about having a next-play mentality. Matthew Golden dropped a touchdown pass against Carolina, only to catch a touchdown on the next play. Jordan Morgan can miss a block on first down but deliver a pancake on the next. Brandon Cisse can be flagged for pass interference on one play and make back-to-back plays in the end zone moments later.
It’s not that easy for a kicker, who might have to stew on a missed kick for an hour or a week.
“We’re better now,” special teams coordinator Cam Achord said on Wednesday, one day before the Carolina game and a few days after Smack in a three-point loss at Detroit became the first kicker since 2019 to miss two kicks of 35 yards or shorter in a game.
“I think for anybody, human nature, myself included, when you don’t go out and execute the way you want, you’re going to be a little bit frustrated, depressed or (feel) like you let people down. But as it goes on, you get back to it, and you can move forward. We’re good now. We’re in a good spot, and it goes back to having all the confidence in him and knowing that he is a confident person. So, I think we’re in a good headspace leading into tomorrow night. And I’m excited to see him kick.”
Smack missed his first extra-point attempt and was booed off the field. He bounced back to make the next three, with the fans celebrating with arguably the loudest cheers of the night. Was that a sign of that next-play mentality and a huge step forward? Or was that merely an NFL-level kicker doing something an NFL-level kicker is expected to do?
General manager Brian Gutekunst has to figure that out. He’s the one who gave up two draft picks to select Smack. He wouldn’t have done it if he didn’t think Smack had the talent and toughness to solve the Packers’ kicking problems. He wouldn’t have paid Brandon McManus’ $1 million roster bonus and then wished him good luck if he didn’t think Smack had what it takes mentally and physically.
Waiting for a young kicker can be a death sentence for a season, though. After a hot start to his rookie season in 2023, sixth-round pick Anders Carlson fell into a slump from which he couldn’t snap. So, it was no surprise at all that he missed a field goal in the Packers’ three-point playoff loss to the 49ers.
But, again, the Packers drafted Smack because they believed in him. He was the consensus best kicker in this year’s draft, so perhaps Gutekunst feels wedded to what Smack can become and inclined to wish away the struggles.
It’s different positions, obviously, so admittedly an absurd comparison, but Jordan Love threw eight interceptions in his first eight games as the starter in 2023. Should the Packers have benched Love at the time? They didn’t, of course, and their patience has been rewarded.
“A lot of people want to talk about the negatives and all that, which is fair. It’s very fair,” Achord said. “There’s no bones about that, but we’ve got to go back to the process that got us here and what we did 90 percent of the time.”
Should Gutekunst have drafted Smack in the first place, when history will tell you that the difference between a drafted kicker (median 85.0 percent on field goals over the last decade and undrafted kicker (85.7 percent over that same span) is negligible? Should Gutekunst have given Smack a free pass onto the roster by releasing McManus and Lucas Havrisik before the first offseason practice?
The answers are probably no and no but, at this point, those questions are irrelevant. What’s done is done. The Packers drafted Smack, they didn’t pressure him with a challenger and now a team with a small margin for error has one of the worst kicking situations in the league.
So, what should they do with him? Do they ride it out, betting that Smack will get “the contact back to where it was and where it can be,” as Achord put it? Or will they bet on whatever unemployed veteran kicker they can find to fix what ails the kicking game, like McManus did in 2024?
There’s no easy answer, especially at a position group in which Havrisik, with a career success rate of 79.2 percent on field goals in 12 games, might be the best option.
Maybe it’s a damned-if-you-do, damned-if-you-don’t proposition. The Vikings drafted Daniel Carlson in the fifth round in 2018 and cut him after two games. He became one of the best kickers in the league with the Raiders, including two All-Pro seasons.
Maybe that will be Smack’s path. Maybe a few extra points will get him out of his funk and he will be a weapon for this year’s playoffs and the next several years’ playoffs. Or maybe he’ll kick the Packers right out of the playoffs and the team’s kicker merry-go-round will keep spinning.

title: Packers Reaching Familiar Trouble Spot With Jordan Love
full_text:
Brett Favre. Aaron Rodgers. Jordan Love.
The Green Bay Packers have been set at the quarterback position essentially since 1992, with those three men having been excellent stewards of the organization.
Quarterback is the most important position in professional sports, so having a great quarterback is the single greatest trump card that any team can possess.
The Packers have essentially had great quarterback play with a few exceptions in every NFL season since 1992. That’s a big reason why they’ve been competitive for as long as they have been, with their 348 regular-season wins being only one less than New England’s 349 during that span.
Love appears to be the latest in that lineage. There is a long way to go before Love matches either of his predecessors. Those two will both be first ballot Hall of Famers. They have seven MVPs, two Super Bowl titles, and three Super Bowl appearances between them.
Favre’s number is retired and Rodgers’ number will be some day, as well.
Favre and Rodgers, however, provide a cautionary tale that appears to be rearing its ugly head in Green Bay this season.
Love has been excellent for most of the season. The Packers have relied on him more than they ever have since he took the reins in 2023.
Love does not have the gaudiest numbers this season, but he is playing incredibly well as he’s helped guide the Packers to a 5-3 record. He’s done so with no help from his running game, an offensive line constantly in flux and pass catchers who lead the league in drops.
As a result, Love has had to play the role of Superman to ensure the Packers are competitive, let alone win.
“Can’t say enough great things about him because he’s carrying the burden of everything right now, just dealing the ball and throwing a lot of great passes,” coach Matt LaFleur said after Thursday’s victory over the Panthers.
Does any of this sound familiar?
If you’ve followed the Packers for any period of time since Favre took over at quarterback, you’ve probably understood that every weekend the team had a chance to win because of who was under center. The concerns you had likely were related to the supporting cast – or lack thereof.
After going to back-to-back Super Bowls in 1996 and 1997, Favre saw the roster around him start to decay. That started at head coach, with Mike Holmgren replaced by Ray Rhodes and Mike Sherman. Neither coach was a savant like Holmgren.
The lack of passing-game weapons surrounding Favre by the end of his tenure, shoddy defenses and inconsistent run games helped prevent the Packers from reaching another Super Bowl. Favre was often asked to play Superman, and inevitably proved to be human.
Rodgers suffered a similar fate when he was the quarterback in Green Bay. His team won the Super Bowl in 2010 before Rodgers won the first of his four MVP awards.
From 2010 onward, however, the Packers never really had a full team surrounding him. He had to carry bad defenses, mediocre run games and catastrophic special teams to the postseason before they inevitably would run into better teams that could exploit those weaknesses.
Like Favre, Rodgers would prove to be human in the postseason, and the team around him was rarely able to save them from defeat if he did not play his best.
Through eight games this season, Love is working through that same fate. Offensively, everything falls on Love’s shoulders. Love is third in the NFL in passing yards per game and the running game is the worst in the league. So, you get this from NFL analyst Dan Orlovsky.
Jordan Love has accounted for 82% of Green Bay's yardage this season.
To be clear, Green Bay’s special teams is not very good, but at least its defense has been good to start the season.
Offensively, however, Love has been asked to carry a significant burden.
Their run game is threatening to compete for the least productive ground game in the modern era . Their offensive line has gotten him obliterated for most of the first eight games. Some of those issues have corrected themselves, but Love has spent most of the season under duress.
The best example of the Packers’ season, and how it could end, came on Thursday night against Carolina.
Love started the game on an absolute heater. He completed 17 of his first 20 passes. The three incompletions? Two drops and one catchable pass. Love’s excellence in the first half and early third quarter helped the Packers build a 27-10 lead.
In a normal setting, that should have been enough. Green Bay’s defense is excellent. A passable run game could help turn the Packers into a boa constrictor and squeeze the life out of the game.
Green Bay’s offense is not normal. Their run game was unreliable, Love cooled off and the Panthers got closer than they ever had any business being.
Can Green Bay survive with a putrid run game? Even Love doesn’t think so.
“Definitely. I think that’s an area we’ve got to keep getting better at, keep finding what’s working, but we’ve got to improve because, especially late in the game, you’ve got to be able to lean on that,” Love said after the game.
“We did some really good things and I think, obviously, late in the game, it wasn’t good enough. We weren’t able to finish the way we wanted so that’s something we’ve got to improve on, clean up as an offense and be better there.”
Love is capable of putting on Superman’s cape. He’s done so in Green Bay before. He’s had to do so throughout the season.
Whether it’s Tom Brady, Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, Favre, Rodgers or Love, the best quarterbacks eventually play below their standard.
Asking one man to carry the weight of an entire organization on his shoulders is too much to ask for anyone.
Ask both of the quarterbacks who were great that came before Love. They both should have more than one Super Bowl based on their talent level alone. Ultimately, a lot of factors play into why the Packers’ trophy case is not fully stocked the way that having back-to-back Hall of Fame quarterbacks would indicate it should be.
Moving from Rodgers to Love was supposed to come with the understanding that their quarterback was not going to have to play that role every week.
If the Packers want to win a championship this year, or in the near future, they better figure out a way to win when Jordan Love plays like Clark Kent.

title: Packers Trade for Jonathan Taylor More Likely After Latest Josh Jacobs Update
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers are in fact in on a potential trade for Indianapolis Colts superstar running back Jonathan Taylor, a source told Packers On SI on Saturday.
“It’s on the table,” a source said without going any further. Taylor won’t come cheap because other teams are interested and the Colts don’t need to make the deal.
According to Tom Pelissero’s Substack , The Sweep, the Colts already have rejected an offer of a second-round pick plus an additional draft pick.
“The Colts haven’t told other teams exactly what they want for Taylor,” Pelissero wrote, “but it makes sense they’d want something close to deal the Panthers got when they traded Christian McCaffrey to San Francisco in 2022 in exchange for 2023 second-, third-, and fourth-round picks plus a 2024 fifth-rounder.”
The return of Josh Jacobs to the lineup seemed to throw cold water on any interest in acquiring a running back. However, WGBA-TV Channel 26 in Green Bay obtained records from the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department from its investigation of the May incident that led to Jacobs’ no-contest plea for misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property. Those records show additional allegations from before he joined the Packers in 2024.
The Packers would be getting a younger player (Taylor will turn 28 in January and Jacobs will turn 29 in February), a player with less wear and tear (257 fewer touches), a more explosive player (4.8 yards per carry for his career compared to 4.2 for Jacobs) and a player under contract through 2028 (compared to 2027 for Jacobs).
Jacobs is one of the better running backs in the NFL. Taylor is one of the best.
Taylor rushed for 1,431 yards in 2024, 1,585 yards in 2025 and is on pace for 1,426 yards in 2026. His 4.2-yard average this season is the lowest of his career; he averaged 4.9 yards per carry last season.
Taylor has home-run speed. Since the start of the 2025 season, only Derrick Henry and Bijan Robinson have more 20-yard runs than Taylor. Only Henry has more 20-yard touchdowns. His big-play ability would work with Green Bay’s big-play offense.
Like Jacobs, Taylor is an adept receiver. He caught 46 passes last season, when he scored a league-high 20 total touchdowns.
He has 17 fumbles out of 1,691 career rushes. Jacobs has 17 fumbles out of 1,872 career rushes. So, from that perspective, both players are reliable ball-carriers.
As was shown with the return of Jacobs, the problem with the Packers’ running game is the guys doing the blocking and not the guys doing the running.
Green Bay is on pace to finish with the worst rushing average in NFL history. The rushing attack is as bad with Jacobs as it was without him.
On Thursday against Carolina, which entered the game with the worst rushing defense in the NFL, the Packers mustered 66 rushing yards with a 2.5 average. Jacobs carried the ball 21 times with a long gain of a pitiful 6 yards. Half of the team’s 26 rushing attempts gained 1 yard or less.
So, would Taylor actually solve the team’s problems? Or would the team’s limited capital to pull off a trade be better used on a high-quality run-blocking lineman?
Speaking of draft capital, the Packers do not have a first-round pick in 2027 following the Micah Parsons trade. They do have a second-round pick and will have multiple mid-round selections with the compensatory selections coming their way after losing Malik Willis, Romeo Doubs and Quay Walker in free agency.
Still, for a team with holes in the lineup, not having first- or second-round picks to provide young and inexpensive talent would be a challenge.
Taylor is under contract through the 2028 season, so the Packers would have him for two-and-a-half seasons.
If Taylor is traded, the acquiring team would inherit his two-year, $44 million contract, but the $15 million signing bonus would remain on the Colts’ ledger for cap purposes.
Taylor has a base salary of $6.98 million for this season; the acquiring team would only have to pay for the pro-rated portion of what’s left. Taylor has base salaries of $15 million in 2027, which would be guaranteed if on the roster after the Super Bowl, and $9.46 million (with a $7.5 million roster bonus) in 2028.
Taylor would be another expensive player on a roster filled with expensive players. However, the Packers could move on from Jacobs, who has a $12.2 million base salary for the 2027 season, to mostly fund Taylor’s contract.
According to records, three other women came forward with similar allegations. One told Hobart-Lawrence police about an alleged incident from January 2022, when Jacobs was with the Raiders.
From WGBA’s extensive story: “According to the records, the woman alleged Jacobs slapped her across the face and later took her cellphone as she attempted to leave his residence. The woman told investigators that Jacobs grabbed her by the hair, threw her onto a bed, pinned her down and later threw her onto the floor. The woman also alleged Jacobs spit on her and grabbed her by the throat.”
The Packers and the NFL conducted their own investigations; it’s not known if they were allowed to view these records and were aware of the past allegations when the league activated Jacobs and the Packers put him in the lineup. And if they were aware, did they deem them as not credible?
One source recently said that while the NFL classified its investigation as ongoing after removing Jacobs from the exempt list, the case had been closed unless and until it gained access to video of the incident involving Jacobs. Release of the video has been blocked by the victim and Jacobs.
It’s always been the expectation that the league would suspend Jacobs. The question was whether it would be a six-game suspension, with Jacobs’ time on the exempt list covering the punishment, or if he would be suspended for additional games.
The league on Saturday said it would “review these allegations.”
Jacobs’ legal team offered its response on Saturday: “The Brown County District Attorney’s office had these uncorroborated, old, and previously unreported allegations for months. They conducted their own exhaustive investigation, along with the police department, and the D.A. determined that only two misdemeanor charges were warranted. They then entered into a plea agreement with Josh Jacobs. Josh has repeatedly expressed his remorse and is honoring the terms of the agreement.”
Jacobs has played in the last two games.
“I’m excited to be back with the team, with the guys,” he said after his first practice on Oct. 21. “I want to say thank you to the organization really for supporting me throughout this whole process and how everything played out.
“With that being said, I can’t get into a lot of things like specifics of things but, obviously, I’m remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation. Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a 4-second, 3-second decision can alter your life, honestly. But with that being said, still a human being, man, still trying to learn, still trying to grow from the whole process.”
His touchdown celebration after his first touchdown against Carolina went viral; Jacobs said the Prime Video broadcast didn’t show the “whole celebration.”

title: Finally! Good News on Packers Star Micah Parsons’ Return From Injury
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur this week hinted that Micah Parsons would be back on the practice field following this weekend’s mini-bye.
Indeed, according to multiple national reports , Parsons will make his long-awaited return to the practice field next week with the hope of him making his season debut during the Thanksgiving Eve game at the Los Angeles Rams.
Because the Packers played on Thursday and will get the weekend off, there will be a bonus day on Monday. That’s Nov. 2, though the team probably will hold only a walk-through practice. That would make Wednesday, Nov. 4 – the start of the traditional practice week – the big day.
The Packers will play the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25. That means he will get a three-week ramp-up.
As NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said , the focus for this coming week leading into the New England game will be individual drills, which will help Parsons knock off some rust and gain additional comfort and confidence in the knee. The following week, when the Packers will host the Vikings, Parsons will be incorporated into team drills.
Then comes the Packers’ pseudo-bye week, meaning a few rest days before rolling into Rams Week with practices on that Saturday, Sunday and Monday before flying to Los Angeles on Tuesday to play on Wednesday.
The Packers have persevered without Parsons. They are 5-3, due in large part to a defense that has defied expectations.
The Packers are 11th in points allowed, skewed by an offensive implosion that gift-wrapped the Vikings a bunch of points in Week 1 and one terrible performance against Atlanta in Week 3. The past five games, they have not allowed more than 20 points.
The Packers rank ninth in yards allowed per game and third in yards allowed per play. They have allowed 303 or fewer yards in six of eight games. Rather incredibly, they are a solid 11th in sack percentage without anyone on the roster picking up the slack. Lukas Van Ness has a team-high 4.5 sacks, including one of the team’s six against Carolina.
The team’s four edge players each had a sack against the Panthers but have only a combined total of 9.5 for the season.
That will make Parsons a seismic addition – assuming he returns at anything close to peak form.
While the Seahawks acquired All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and the Bears landed All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, perhaps no move made before the Nov. 10 trade deadline will be more consequential than Parsons’ return.
The Packers were 9-3-1 when Parsons was injured at Denver last season, but they lost their final five games. Despite a myriad of problems this season, they are 5-3 and right in the thick of the playoff chase following the victory over Carolina.
Parsons tore the ACL and suffered meniscus damage against the Broncos, making it a more significant injury than the ACL tears sustained by teammate Tucker Kraft and Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes.
He had surgery on Dec. 29, meaning his first practice will be a little more than 10 months later and his potential season debut will be a little less than 11 months later.
When Parsons spoke to reporters during training camp, he had this revealing comment. Yes, Parsons has to get the knee back to full strength following the ACL injury. But he also has to get everything back to full strength so one problem doesn’t create another problem.
He believes assorted issues after not practicing for the Cowboys in training camp before last year’s trade might have led to the injury.
“I just think it was just accumulative things within my body – pushing through the no camp, the dealing with injuries throughout the season, and I just think my body just was overloaded, which caused my knee to give out,” he said. “But I don’t really think [about] why the situation happened. I think based off of how I feel at this point, I feel like a much better player in the sense of how I feel.
“I feel more stable. I feel stronger. I probably was blind to a lot of things that I probably should have been working on that I got a chance to correct and get stronger during this process.”
So, Parsons saw the potential upside of how the injury could impact the “longevity” of the 27-year-old’s career.
“I talked to a baseball guy,” Parsons continued. “He’s like, ‘We want a pitcher that kind of go through the Tommy John [surgery] because it’s like he got it out the way,’ you know? So, hopefully, I got my injury out of the way, and I can, based off what others try to say, give me another six to 10 years. So, I’m really excited about that.”
From the team perspective, the Packers don’t want to do anything to jeopardize their enormous investment following a trade that cost them two first-round picks, Kenny Clark and $188 million.
Parsons shares a similar train of thought. In a story this week by ESPN.com Packers beat writer Rob Demovsky, a source pointed to the rise and fall of Parsons’ close friend and former Cowboys teammate Trevon Diggs. He was one of the best cornerbacks in the league in 2021 and 2022 – he led the NFL with 11 interceptions in 2021 – but suffered a torn ACL early in the 2023 season, which ruined his career.
“I think watching one of his best friends go through what he went through, coming back early twice and where his career headed afterward, he already had in his head how to approach this situation,” the source said.
If the target game of the Rams becomes reality, Parsons will have missed the first 10 games of the season. But he’ll be back for the most important games, including a potential playoff run.
“It’s about knowing when to go and it's all about feeling great,” he said during training camp. “Like I don't think Gutey (Brian Gutekunst) or Nate (Weir) or Matt (LaFleur) wants me to go out there if I'm not at 100 percent and risk re-injury and lose me for the year and it's just a waste of a year.
“Everything is about playoffs and winning football games deep in [the season]. Yeah, those games are important, but maybe we don't see Dallas twice, but we see Chicago twice and the games that we have in December or even more playoff games and not to even just look that far ahead, but we got a tough schedule this year and I think for the betterment of everyone, everyone wants me at 100 and wants me in those games so we can make this championship run.”
