title: Texans Sign Former Cowboys RB Amid Backfield Depth Concerns
full_text:
The Houston Texans have made a new addition to their backfield on Wednesday despite being in the middle of their Week 8 bye .
And that signing just so happens to have come via waivers from their in-state neighbors in the Dallas Cowboys.
According to the Texans' transaction log, the team has claimed running back Emari Demercado off waivers after he was let go by the Dallas Cowboys earlier in the week.
We have claimed Emari Demercado off waivers and made other roster moves. pic.twitter.com/2V0C9WcsDm
Demercado, a 5-foot-9, 215-pound running back who's been in the league for the past four seasons. He spent his first three years pro with the Arizona Cardinals, where he played a total of 40 games and recorded over 1,100 yards from scrimmage throughout that span.
More recently, Demercado had been with the Kansas City Chiefs earlier this year as a part of their 90-man roster leading into the regular season.
He was ultimately sent to waivers by the Chiefs at the end of August, and would quickly be scooped up by the Cowboys, where he would play two games over the course of this season.
In those two games he played in between Weeks 1 and 2, Demercado put together five carries for 15 yards on the ground, but would not be activated past those pair of appearances.
Now, Demercado is able to land on his feel with the Texans heading into the second half of the season, as he'll be able to provide some sense of backfield depth that Houston was left without during their most recent game against the New York Giants.
Since the Texans' Week 5 win vs. the Tennessee Titans, the offense has been without their lead veteran in the backfield in David Montgomery, as he's been dealing with a groin injury to keep him sidelined for Weeks 6 and 7.
Montgomery has still yet to log a limited, let alone full practice, for the team since going down with his injury. And while the Texans do have a bye week ahead of them that provides extra time for him to get right, there are no guarantees he'll be ready to go before their next game in Week 9 against the LA Chargers.
Without Montgomery, the Texans were currently left with just two active running backs on their roster in Week 7. RB3 British Brooks has been on injured reserve since Week 4 with a hamstring injury, and Jawhar Jordan was just placed on Houston's practice squad injured reserve after suffering an injury in Week 6 vs. Jacksonville.
That meant Woody Marks and Dare Ogunbowale were the only names the Texans could lean on in their backfield for Week 7. And while that setup worked relatively well for most of the contest against New York, an injury scare for Marks in the second half put that need for a third rostered running back on full display.
Therefore, the Texans now have another running back on their 53-man roster to lean on in Demercado, who brings depth, experience, and another ball carrier to utilize in the event that Montgomery–– or any other running back in the mix–– is due to miss any more time moving forward.

title: Texans WR Jaylin Noel's Foot Injury Update Is Worst-Case Scenario
full_text:
In the midst of the Houston Texans' Week 7 loss to the New York Giants, the wide receiver room would see one of their key contributors leave the game early with a toe injury: second-year wideout Jaylin Noel.
Noel would inevitably not return to the game, was said to have been suffering from turf toe from head coach DeMeco Ryans after the game, and was waiting further testing to see just how long he would be sidelined.
And it turns out, Noel will be out for a significant amount of time. The Texans have announced that Noel will be placed on injured reserve due to the toe injury he sustained this weekend against the Giants.
But that's not all. According to the Houston Chronicle 's Jonathan M. Alexander , Noel's toe injury is expected to be serious enough to sideline him for the rest of the season.
It's yet another tough injury blow for the Texans to sustain to be without Noel for what appears to be the rest of the season.
Houston has seen multiple starters on both sides of the ball deal with extended absences over the past few weeks. That includes injuries to Jalen Pitre, Reed Blankenship, and David Montgomery, and now, the newest issue is within their wide receiver room.
But those injuries are expected to subside within the next few weeks. Noel, however, now seems to have reached the end of what's been a really inspiring second season when he's gotten a chance to be on the field.
Noel has gotten off to at hot start for his second season in Houston, finding his way to become a gradually more involved piece within the Texans' passing attack–– especially for the past three weeks.
On the season, Noel has put together 19 receptions on 23 targets, 331 yards and two touchdowns, while currently leading the NFL in yards per target (14.4).
But now, the Texans will be forced to move forward for the next 10 games on the schedule without him. Noel now joins his draft classmate, Jayden Higgins, on injured reserve while being expected to miss the season; both of whom entered this season expected to make a big leap in terms of their development.
And while Houston does have a deep wide receiver room to bank on in his absence, not having Noel does take away a big-time explosive piece offensively who was just beginning to catch his stride within the passing attack.
The silver lining for the Texans in a rough turn of events for Noel is the fact that their wide receiver room is extremely deep compared to where things stood at the start of this season.
They've got Nico Collins leading the way, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte due to remain key parts of the Texans' passing attack, and Marvin Harrison Jr. and Tank Dell are just beginning to catch their stride within the offense within their respective situations.
The two names that remain the most compelling to keep an eye on now that Noel is due to miss the rest of the season will be both of Harrison Jr. and Dell.
While both pass-catchers were extremely limited in Week 7's game plan against the Giants, their usage and involvement should only be expected to increase in the weeks ahead. Harrison Jr. is still learning his way around the Texans' playbook and overall offensive scheme, while Dell just came back for his first NFL game in over 670 days .
So the Texans might be able to navigate the storm offensively, even without one of their biggest bright spots on the offensive side of the ball so far this season. But there's no doubt that losing Noel's explosiveness and downfield ability is going to sting for C.J. Stroud and the rest of the surrounding offense.

title: Colts Week 8 Best Bets: Finding Value Amid the Chaos
full_text:

Usually, that would be enough reason to keep the card light. But this Colts fire sale has created some interesting betting opportunities.
Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner are gone, Josh Downs has requested a trade, and Jonathan Taylor is available for the right price. From a morale perspective, it feels like the life is being sucked out of this team.
From a betting perspective? We've managed to capitalize on the chaos, going 15-4 on Colts-specific bets and 17-16 overall through seven weeks.
Jacksonville's elite run defense against Taylor and this brand-new offensive line will dictate the Colts' side of the ball. On the other side, Trevor Lawrence gets a depleted secondary without Justin Walley or Cam Taylor-Britt.
We're hunting for value this week. Here are my five best bets for Week 8.
Jonathan Taylor in the end zone at plus money doesn't come around very often.
Yes, Jacksonville has one of the best run defenses in football, and Nelson isn't creating holes for Taylor anymore. But Taylor just put up 95 rushing yards and a touchdown against an elite Minnesota defense and has scored in each of his last two games.
Taylor has eight rushing touchdowns this season, tied for the NFL lead, and has scored 10 total touchdowns over his last 10 games.
He's also scored at least once in each of his last three matchups against Jacksonville.
I can't stay away from this at plus money.
The Colts badly missed Tyler Warren while he was sidelined with a groin injury.
Now he's back against a Jacksonville defense that ranks 19th in tight end coverage, and this line has hit in each of Warren's last three healthy games.
He also had 43 receiving yards the last time he faced Jacksonville.
With Downs requesting a trade and the wide receiver room depleted, I expect Shane Steichen to get Warren involved early and often.
We're going right back to one of our regular plays.
Shrader has cleared this line in 11 of his 15 games with Indianapolis and has made 19 field goals over his last seven games.
He finally missed a couple against Minnesota, but I'm putting my trust right back in him.
With this stagnant Colts offense, Shrader might once again be Indianapolis' main source of scoring. Getting this at plus money feels too good to pass up.
This matchup could get ugly for the Colts' secondary.
Lawrence ranks fifth in passing grade against man coverage, while Indianapolis plays man at the seventh-highest rate in the league, according to PFF.
He's recorded 24 completions in each of his last two games and finished with 28 and 23 in his last two matchups against Indianapolis.
Walley is out, Taylor-Britt is on IR and Sauce Gardner is just returning from injury.
Twenty completions feels very attainable.
This might be my favorite sneaky play on the card.
Tuten has cleared this number in four straight games with 48, 24, 18 and 17 receiving yards.
He also ranks second among running backs in PFF receiving grade, while Indianapolis ranks 30th in receiving yards allowed to running backs per route run.
Against a depleted secondary and inexperienced linebacker room, Tuten should have opportunities underneath.
The Colts might be falling apart, but there's still value to be found, and we're going to keep cashing while this franchise burns.
Good luck and bet responsibly.

title: 3 Matchups Colts Must Win to Upset Jaguars in Week 8
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are 2-5, their general manager is gone, and Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner have been traded. This franchise is falling apart from the inside out.
Although the rebuild has begun , the players left behind haven't appeared to quit. They just fought undefeated Minnesota in a 16-10 loss.
Now comes a 4-2 Jacksonville Jaguars team fresh off its bye. Do the Colts roll over, or fight for the team being dismantled around them?
If they choose to fight, here are the battles they need to focus on.
Minnesota blitzed Daniel Jones on an absurd 85.2% of his dropbacks last week. Now the Colts have to protect him without Quenton Nelson.
Jones averaged just 2.57 seconds to throw and was sacked four times. If he doesn't have time to make decisions, this offense isn't going anywhere.
Rookie Jalen Farmer is set for his first start at left guard , replacing a future Hall of Famer who owned that spot since 2018. Nobody expects Farmer to be Big Q, but hopefully Nelson left some of his greatness behind in that room.
Jacksonville has just 11 sacks through six games, but Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker can still wreck a game. This new combination has to hold up.
Trevor Lawrence has repeatedly hurt the Colts through the air, and he's thrown 14 touchdowns against just four interceptions this season.
Per Pro Football Focus, Lawrence ranks fifth in passing grade against man coverage. Indianapolis plays man at the seventh-highest rate in the league.
Sauce Gardner returns from a calf injury , and all eyes should be on him. As a likely franchise cornerstone of the next era, Gardner needs to remind everyone why Indy invested so much in him.
Speaking of which, rookie linebacker CJ Allen is set to make his first start after seven weeks of rotational play. Colts' defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo said earlier this week that Allen was in line to start against the Minnesota Vikings, but a late week ankle injury sidelined him once more.
After a brutal stretch of (mainly injury-related) setbacks to kick off his career, CJ Allen is set to make his first start, and, if all goes as planned, begin to showcase that he'll be the incoming era's next leader of the defense.
With longtime franchise pillar DeForest Buckner now across the country, Justin Walley ruled out, and Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve, there isn't much room for mistakes.
If Lawrence starts picking the Colts apart, Jacksonville can do whatever it wants offensively.
This is probably the most important matchup of the afternoon.
Jonathan Taylor is at the center of NFL trade rumors as we approach the November 10th deadline, but the Colts' longtime captain and star rusher is focused on his work. Taylor has not requested a trade, but trade talks grow louder as we inch closer to the aforementioned deadline.
Jacksonville owns the league's second-highest run-defense grade (76.3), per PFF, and allows a league-best 3.2 yards per carry. That's a brutal assignment for Jonathan Taylor and an offensive line adjusting to life without Quenton Nelson.
Taylor has 587 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, including 95 yards and a score against Minnesota.
When JT gets rolling, the Colts move the chains, score points and compete. When he's shut down, defenses force Jones to throw, pressure piles up and the offense becomes stationary.
Simple formula: Get JT hot, compete on Sunday.
Indianapolis hasn't won in Jacksonville since 2014. The rebuild may already be underway, but this team can still decide whether it goes down swinging.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Week 8 Final Injury Report: Colts Welcome Back Key Starters
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts and Jacksonville Jaguars have released their final injury reports ahead of Sunday's AFC South matchup, with both teams receiving some important reinforcements and facing questions about key contributors.
Indianapolis will welcome back several players who missed last week's loss to Minnesota, while Jacksonville could be shorthanded at a key position as it prepares to host the Colts.
Most notable for the Colts, both Sauce Gardner and Tyler Warren are off the injury report and will play in Jacksonville. Both had missed last Sunday’s loss to the Vikings; Warren missed the prior loss to Tennessee as well. Both provide much-needed boosts to a passing attack and secondary that are currently fairly thin, especially with Anthony Gould and Justin Walley both set to sit out.
Gould, Indy’s primary punt returner, likely gives away to special teams ace Ashton Dulin in the return game. Walley’s absence is significant given the Colts’ backup nickel Cam Taylor-Britt is on injured reserve. It will likely be up to rookie Kapena Gushiken to hold down the slot, though defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo may switch up personnel to account for the lack of options there.
Bryce Boettcher could miss his second straight game and leave the linebacker group down a rotational piece. The Colts released Germaine Pratt from their practice squad after he appeared in last week’s game, so the contingency plan there is unknown. West Weeks is the only linebacker on Indy’s practice squad, so look for Austin Ajiake and Tahj Chambers to potentially get some defensive snaps.
Drew Ogletree is set to miss his first game of the season with a knee injury. That should open the door for Will Mallory to see an extended run, especially as the Colts continue to evaluate what comes next for their franchise.
Also of note, both Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs will play this week, head coach Shane Steichen said. Downs officially requested a trade Wednesday while Taylor has been the subject of trade speculation ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
Jacksonville takes the slight edge in terms of health going into Sunday's matchup as just Antonio Johnson has been ruled out. The Jaguars list Jalen Huskey, a rookie who’s yet to appear in a game this season, as the backup strong safety, though third-string Kaevon Merriweather has much more NFL experience and is more likely to receive the start. Still, when Merriweather eventually rotates out, Indy’s pass game must test Huskey in his first professional action.
Jakobi Meyers is listed as questionable with hamstring and ankle issues. He logged back-to-back limited practices Wednesday and Thursday but missed practice Friday, making his status for the weekend unclear.
If Meyers is eventually ruled out, the pressure will be on Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. to pick up the slack. Thomas had a stellar rookie season but has been on the decline ever since. He’s started only three of Jacksonville’s six games so far, recording just nine catches.
The other interesting wrinkle a possible Meyers absence adds to the equation is the role of Travis Hunter. If the Jaguars need more bodies at receiver, that could impact the number of snaps the two-way Hunter can play defensively.

title: Colts’ Rebuild Creates Defining Opportunity for Young Trio
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have begun shifting their focus toward the future.
The trades of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner mark a significant change in direction for the franchise. While the departure of two longtime leaders leaves big shoes to fill, it also creates opportunities for younger players to establish themselves.
With larger roles now available, a handful of young Colts have a chance to earn their place in the organization's long-term plans.
The Colts will get their first taste of life without Quenton Nelson on Sunday, with rookie Jalen Farmer expected to step into the starting lineup at left guard.
The fourth-round pick has spent his rookie season learning behind one of the NFL's best offensive linemen, but Nelson's departure suddenly gives him an opportunity to establish that he's starting material.
Farmer has played just three offensive snaps this season, making Sunday's assignment a significant jump in responsibility. He also spent his college career at right guard, meaning the transition to the left side could come with some growing pains. However, Indianapolis has been preparing him for that possibility throughout the season, and offensive line coach Tony Sparano Jr. has expressed confidence in his ability to make the adjustment, even though Nelson is truly one-of-one.
"You don't replace Quenton. It's not about that. This is an opportunity for (Farmer) to begin his journey, and those are two independent journeys."
Farmer won't come close to replicating Nelson's impact this early in his career. But if the rookie can hold his own against NFL competition, develop consistency and demonstrate the potential to become a long-term starter, the Colts will have solved one key problem ahead of their rebuild.
Trading DeForest Buckner creates an opportunity for Adetomiwa Adebawore to take another significant step in his development. The fourth-year defensive tackle is in the midst of a breakout season, already tying his career high for sacks in a season (4) through seven weeks in a rotational role.
With Buckner now gone, Adebawore is the next man up. He'll have to take on a larger share of the responsibility, seeing an increase in snaps and more attention from opposing offensive lines. The Colts need to find out if they envision Adebawore in their future plans.
There's also a financial component to consider. Adebawore is playing out the final year of his rookie contract, giving him an opportunity to strengthen his case for a long-term deal. Whether that comes in Indianapolis or elsewhere remains to be seen, but the remainder of the season will go a long way toward determining his value.
If Adebawore continues developing into a reliable three-down defensive tackle, the Colts may have found an important piece of their next defensive core.
The Colts invested a second-round pick in CJ Allen with the expectation that he would eventually become a leader of their defense. The rookie linebacker has had a rocky start to his NFL career, battling injuries throughout training camp and the regular season while struggling to find consistent playing time.
Allen was expected to make his first career start against Minnesota last week before suffering an ankle injury in practice. Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo confirmed this week that Allen was in line to start, making his anticipated return against Jacksonville another opportunity to establish himself.
In what remains of this season, the Colts needs to identify its long-term answers at linebacker. Allen was drafted to fill that role, and the coaching staff has continued to express confidence in his development.
As long as Allen can stay healthy, the starting MIKE spot for years to come is his to lose.

title: Colts, Jaguars Mid-Week Injury Reports Ahead of Divisional Showdown: CJ Allen's First Start?
full_text:
With an AFC South matchup looming Sunday, the Indianapolis Colts and Jacksonville Jaguars are looking to get key players back on the field. Thursday's injury reports offered a better idea of where both teams' health stand heading into the divisional showdown.
Several notable players are working through injuries on both sides, making Friday's final practice an important checkpoint before the weekend. The latest developments could have implications for both teams as they prepare for a game with significant divisional stakes.
The Colts are entering a new era after trading away longtime franchise pillars in LG Quenton Nelson and DT DeForest Buckner, and it's looking like we'll see more young players get their opportunity down the stretch .
After a walkthrough Wednesday, the Colts received encouraging news Thursday, with cornerback Sauce Gardner, guard Matt Goncalves, wide receiver Anthony Gould, and defensive tackle Tim Smith all upgrading to full participation. Gardner missed last week with a calf injury, so his return is crucial for a secondary that's been banged up in recent weeks.
Tight end Tyler Warren remains limited with a groin injury after missing the last two games, making Friday's practice an important checkpoint for his potential return.
Meanwhile, linebacker Bryce Boettcher and cornerback Justin Walley have yet to practice this week. Their continued absences could affect Indianapolis' depth at linebacker and cornerback, particularly with Walley dealing with a knee injury sustained against Minnesota.
Veteran cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt was placed on Injured Reserve earlier this week, keeping him out for at least the next four games. Although the Colts are set to have their starting outside duo available in Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, the slot role remains up for grabs.
If Walley cannot go, the Colts may turn to rookie UDFAs Kapena Gushiken or Kenneth Harris. Both young defenders have flashed at times this season, but neither has carved out a definitive role.
When it comes to linebacker, the Colts are trending towards finally starting second-round pick CJ Allen.
Allen was kept out of most training camp with lingering injuries (groin, hamstring), which led to defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo turning to veterans Akeem Davis-Gaither and Jaylon Carlies while the rookie is slowly but surely ramped up.
The Colts' first pick (53rd overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft has been sidelined for the majority of his rookie season so far, having only played in 11.14% of possible defensive snaps.
Lou Anarumo said earlier this week that Allen was set to make his first start against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7, but a late-week ankle injury forced the Colts to pivot.
After back-to-back full participation to start the week, one that coincides with the Colts' ongoing fire sale, it appears Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon and Co. are officially welcoming in the new era by turning to the promising young players on the roster.
Allen's promising health news is one sign for this, and the Colts' mid-week release of veteran linebacker Germaine Pratt is additional proof.
The Colts will have one more practice Friday before Sunday's road matchup against the Jaguars. The final injury report should provide a clearer indication of which players are trending toward playing and which could be in danger of missing another game. But for now, the prognosis appears positive.
Thursday’s practice report for #INDvsJAX . pic.twitter.com/9hwSTY3ezW
The Jaguars had two players upgrade to full participation Thursday, with cornerback Montaric Brown and tight end Brenton Strange both practicing without restriction. Brown was limited Wednesday with a hamstring injury, so his progress is notable. Brown's availability would give Jacksonville another option in the secondary against Indianapolis' passing attack.
Wide receiver Jakobi Meyers remains limited with a hamstring injury after being listed with the same designation Wednesday. His status is worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's divisional matchup, as the Jaguars look to have their receiving corps available against a Colts defense dealing with injuries of its own.
Meanwhile, safety Antonio Johnson missed his second consecutive practice with an ankle injury. His continued absence could affect Jacksonville's secondary depth, while long snapper Ross Matiscik, defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro, linebacker Jahlani Tavai and running back LeQuint Allen Jr. remain limited. We'll have a much clearer idea of who's available and who's not ahead of Sunday after Friday's practice session.

title: Colts Face Franchise-Altering Contract Decision on Breakout Star
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have plenty of questions to answer as they begin reshaping their roster, but Adetomiwa Adebawore has emerged as an intriguing piece of the team's future .
The young defensive tackle has steadily worked his way into a larger role and is in line to take over starting responsibilities from the recently traded DeForest Buckner . Adebawore's recent progress has positioned him for a big payday, but how much his value could continue to rise may determine what it takes for Indianapolis to keep him around.
A fourth-round pick in 2023, Adebawore is coming off the best season of his young career and has taken another step forward in 2026.
Between his increased production and the current state of the Colts' defensive line, Adebawore has the opportunity to be one of the pillars the Colts build around moving forward.
Adebawore recorded four sacks in 17 games last season, including seven starts, matching his previous career high in tackles for loss with five. Through seven games in 2026, he's already matched that sack total with 10 games left to go.
The most encouraging part of Adebawore's emergence has been his ability to generate pressure in a rotational role. He's played roughly 36% of Indianapolis' defensive snaps this season, yet he's in a three-way tie among all NFL players for the most sacks by a defensive tackle (4).
#Colts DT Adetomiwa Adebawore has the 2nd-most pressures (12) on the team (excl. Buckner) after seven weeks despite only playing 35.9% of snaps. He leads the defense in sacks (4.0), pressure rate (13.0%), and quick pressures (6), and has the second-most stops (13). pic.twitter.com/cqamb6tThI
Adebawore's performance against the Minnesota Vikings last week offered another example of that progress. He recorded two sacks and five pressures, consistently disrupting Kyler Murray to keep the Colts neck-and-neck with the league's last remaining unbeaten team.
The Colts have a potential building block developing along their defensive front. Adebawore is producing at a level that demands attention, and with his role expected to grow following Buckner's departure, he has an opportunity to strengthen his case for a significant second contract.
Adebawore's emergence hasn't gone unnoticed around the NFL. According to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo, teams are already doing their homework on the Colts defensive tackle in case Indianapolis makes him available before the trade deadline.
"If he's made available, this is a guy that other teams might want to pry away from the Colts," he said.
From The Insiders on @nflnetwork : The #Colts ’ trades this week have other teams surveying their entire roster ahead of the deadline. DT Adetomiwa Adeboware has piqued interest in a breakout, contract year. Big payday coming for him soon, whether in Indy or elsewhere. pic.twitter.com/1KE7ojytWK
While the Colts haven't necessarily decided to move on from Adebawore, the leaguewide interest is another indication of how his value has changed. He's just 25 years old and coming off a productive stretch, and still has room to grow, making him an appealing target for teams looking to strengthen their defensive fronts.
That interest could carry over into the offseason if Indianapolis doesn't secure an extension. Should Adebawore continue producing and reach free agency, the Colts could face competition from multiple teams looking to add an ascending interior pass rusher.
A bidding war isn't guaranteed, but the early interest suggests his market could become increasingly difficult for Indianapolis to navigate.
Furthermore, Tennessee Titans star defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons was traded to the Chicago Bears for multiple first-round picks on Thursday. Even though Adebawore still aspires to be the level of player Simmons is, his emergence coupled with the dwindling defensive tackle market could see premium draft capital come calling Indianapolis's way.
With the Colts entering a new phase as a franchise, Indianapolis needs to act fast if they view Adebawore as a future building block.
Adebawore wouldn't be the first defensive tackle to turn a gradual rise into a lucrative payday. Osa Odighizuwa and Milton Williams offer two useful benchmarks for what the Colts could pay their young defender.
A third-round pick in 2021, Odighizuwa steadily improved over his first four seasons in Dallas before signing a four-year, $80 million extension in March 2025. He was coming off a career-best 4.5 sacks in 2024 and had started all 17 games for the third consecutive season.
Like Adebawore, Odighizuwa developed into a productive interior pass rusher as a mid-round pick. However, he'd established himself as a full-time starter before signing his extension. If Adebawore seizes his opportunity following Buckner's departure, he could earn a similar deal, with Odighizuwa's $20 million annual average serving as a useful benchmark.
A breakdown of the takedowns. pic.twitter.com/11Mbysb1BL
Williams offers a higher-end comparison. After recording five sacks in 2024, he signed a four-year, $104 million contract with New England in March 2025, averaging $26 million annually. He'd combined for 6.5 sacks over his first three seasons in Philadelphia and started just 19 games across his first four years.
Williams' deal shows how quickly a defensive tackle's value can rise with consistent production. However, he entered free agency as one of the top players available at his position after helping Philadelphia win a Super Bowl, making his contract an upper-end comparison for Adebawore.
Ultimately, Adebawore's earning potential will depend on how much more he proves before the Colts decide whether to extend him, potentially waiting until the offseason when they can evaluate his full body of work.
If Adebawore sustains his production and establishes himself as a starter, a four-year deal worth $40 million to $60 million could be a reasonable projection. That would put his annual average between $10 million and $15 million, below Odighizuwa's $20 million benchmark but reflective of Adebawore's limited starting experience.
A four-year contract also makes sense for both sides. Indianapolis could secure a young defensive tackle through the next phase of its rebuild, while Adebawore would receive long-term financial security at 25 years old with another opportunity to reach free agency before he hits 30.
The Colts must also weigh the cost of waiting. An extension now could provide some cost certainty before Adebawore's role expands, but another productive season could make him more expensive to retain.
With Buckner gone, Adebawore has an opportunity to prove he deserves a long-term investment .

title: Colts' Asking Price for Two Defensive Linemen Just Went Up
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have already shipped out two of their biggest names, and Thursday's blockbuster trade between the Tennessee Titans and Chicago Bears may have just made their next moves a whole lot more interesting.
The Titans are sending All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears in exchange for 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, plus a 2027 fourth-rounder. Chicago also receives a 2028 fifth-round pick.
Two first-round picks for a defensive tackle.
For Indianapolis, that deal could have serious implications for the trade value of Grover Stewart and Adetomiwa Adebawore, two defensive linemen who could be wearing different uniforms by the Nov. 10 deadline.
Simmons is undoubtedly one of the best interior defenders in football. The 29-year-old earned first-team All-Pro honors in 2025 after recording a career-high 11 sacks and already has four through seven games this season.
But that massive return gives Indianapolis something to work with as teams continue searching for defensive line help.
Now, Stewart and Adebawore aren't Simmons. Nobody should expect an early pick for either player, but the Titans may have just helped the Colts squeeze a little more value out of potential buyers.
The Colts only got a fourth-round pick back for DeForest Buckner, but they also chose to do right by him and Quenton Nelson, thus leaving some better packages on the table as they parted ways with two of their franchise cornerstones.
If Indianapolis waits until closer to the trade deadline on November 10th at 4 PM EST, they may just be able to drive up the price, even if marginally.
Because if this really is a true fire sale, Indianapolis needs to capitalize on every opportunity .
Stewart has spent his entire career in Indianapolis after being selected in the fourth round of the 2017 draft. For nearly a decade, he's been one of the most reliable run-stuffers on this defense.
But at 33 years old, entering the final months of his three-year, $39 million contract, it's time to move on.
I have nothing but appreciation for everything Stewart has given this franchise. Unfortunately, he simply doesn't fit the timeline of what this team is becoming.
By the time Indianapolis is ready to compete again, Stewart could very well be approaching retirement.
ESPN's Adam Schefter has already named Stewart among the Colts who could be moved before the deadline. After Thursday's blockbuster, Indianapolis should be looking to maximize his return .
Fourth-year defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore presents a completely different situation .
At 25 years old, Tomi has recorded four sacks through seven games despite playing a limited number of defensive snaps. His 86.3 pass-rush grade ranks third among interior defenders, according to Pro Football Focus, and he is tied for second among defensives tackles with 4.0 sacks.
#Colts DT Adetomiwa Adebawore has the 2nd-most pressures (12) on the team (excl. Buckner) after seven weeks despite only playing 35.9% of snaps. He leads the defense in sacks (4.0), pressure rate (13.0%), and quick pressures (6), and has the second-most stops (13). pic.twitter.com/cqamb6tThI
That's exactly the kind of young, disruptive player Indianapolis should consider building around .
However, he's also entering free agency after this season, and NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reports that teams are already doing their homework on him in case Indianapolis makes him available.
From The Insiders on @nflnetwork : The #Colts ’ trades this week have other teams surveying their entire roster ahead of the deadline. DT Adetomiwa Adeboware has piqued interest in a breakout, contract year. Big payday coming for him soon, whether in Indy or elsewhere. pic.twitter.com/1KE7ojytWK
Would I love to see Tomi become a cornerstone of this next Colts defense? Absolutely.
But after watching Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner get shipped out, it's becoming increasingly difficult to consider anyone untouchable.
The Colts don't even own their 2027 first-round pick, making every additional draft selection that much more valuable.
If another team comes calling with an offer Indianapolis can't refuse, take it.
The next general manager deserves every possible resource to turn this franchise around. If the Colts are committed to tearing this thing down , they might as well squeeze every last bit of value out of it.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Why Colts Should Trade Jonathan Taylor Before the Deadline
full_text:
As the Indianapolis Colts continue their fire sale ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Jonathan Taylor's future with the team is in the balance.
After moving on from Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner , the Colts are facing another major decision about the direction of the franchise. Taylor's situation is more complicated than a typical veteran trade, and the latest reporting has only added to the uncertainty surrounding his future.
Jonathan Taylor has emerged as one of the most intriguing names ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, with multiple teams reportedly exploring the possibility of acquiring the Indianapolis Colts running back.
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Minnesota Vikings are among the teams that have considered a potential trade for Taylor. His superstar status makes him an appealing option for contenders looking to bolster their backfields for a championship push.
Despite that interest, the Colts don't appear eager to move their star running back.
Colts Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Taylor as "a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild," according to ESPN Insiders Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter , the latter of whom added that Indianapolis could change its stance if the right offer comes along, leaving the door open without signaling that a deal is imminent.
Head coach Shane Steichen reinforced that uncertainty Wednesday, telling reporters that Taylor had not requested a trade. "Those are hypothetical things right now," Steichen said. "I know there's stuff floating around out there, but JT's on our football team."
For now, the reporting points to a clear divide. Teams are interested in Taylor, but Indianapolis is reluctant to move him. Of course, that could change in the next week and a half, but for now, reports remain unfounded until proven otherwise.
The strongest argument for trading Jonathan Taylor is the opportunity to turn the Colts' most valuable trade assets into draft picks or other players to get Indy through the rebuild stage. Taylor, given his age and elite production, could bring back another significant return as the franchise reshapes its future.
The Colts need draft capital. Plain and simple. Indianapolis has already traded away its 2027 first-round pick at last year's deadline in the deal for cornerback Sauce Gardner, leaving the franchise without a high draft slot in 2027. Trading Taylor could help replenish that draft capital and give the front office more resources to address the rest of the roster.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported that acquiring Taylor would likely require premium draft compensation, making him a potentially valuable bargaining chip.
Additionally, Taylor's timeline may not match the rebuild. The 27-year-old is still in his prime, but running backs tend to have shorter productive windows than players at many other positions.
If Indianapolis needs multiple seasons to rebuild its roster and return to contention, Taylor will be approaching the latter stages of his career by the time the team is ready to compete again. Trading him now would allow the Colts to capitalize on his current value rather than risk that value declining while the franchise works toward a turnaround.
In other words, the return Taylor would net could be more valuable than keeping him. Taylor is one of the league's most productive running backs, which makes him an attractive target for teams trying to contend in 2027. That gives Indianapolis a chance to acquire premium draft picks or other young talent that could contribute over the next couple of years. With the Colts already willing to move established players, holding onto Taylor simply because he's a star would mean passing up a chance to accelerate the rebuild.
If a team is willing to pay a premium for his services, the Colts have a legitimate reason to consider it.
Trading Jonathan Taylor would give Indianapolis another opportunity to add draft capital, but it would also mean losing one of the NFL's most productive running backs. The Colts need assets to rebuild their roster, but they also need proven talent to help the team compete again. Whether a trade makes sense ultimately depends on what Indianapolis could get in return.
Taylor is still producing at an elite level. Through seven games, Taylor has rushed for 587 yards (5th in NFL) and eight touchdowns (T-1st), putting him among the NFL's most productive running backs. He remains a central part of the Colts' offense and has continued to produce despite the team's struggles. Finding a replacement capable of matching that production would be difficult, even with additional draft capital.
Taylor signed a two-year, $44 million extension in August, keeping him under contract through 2028. Unlike Nelson and Buckner, who were both in the final year of their deals, Taylor isn't approaching free agency. The Colts have time to evaluate the direction of the rebuild without having to trade him before the deadline to avoid losing him for nothing.
A rebuild also doesn't have to mean starting over completely. Taylor is 27, meaning he could still have several productive seasons ahead of him. If Indianapolis can accelerate its turnaround, he could remain a key piece of the offense when the team returns to contention. Keeping a proven star also gives the next edition of the Colts a foundational player rather than forcing the front office to find replacements at every position.
Ultimately, Indianapolis shouldn't trade Taylor just for the sake of it, only if they receive an offer that will benefit the organization moving forward.
At this point, the Colts have more incentive to trade Jonathan Taylor than to keep him.
Indianapolis has already begun dismantling its veteran core, and moving its most valuable remaining player would give the franchise another opportunity to acquire assets for the rebuild. Taylor's stardom makes him difficult to replace, but that alone shouldn't hold the Colts back from making a deal.
The biggest factor is the team's timeline. Taylor is still in his prime, but Indianapolis has significant work to do before it can realistically return to contention. Taylor's career timeline and the Colts' rebuilding timeline don't line up.
By the time the Colts are ready to contend again, Taylor could be nearing the end of his most productive years. Trading him now would allow the franchise to capitalize on his value while giving the next front office more resources.
Taylor's most comparable trade package is that of Christian McCaffrey's blockbuster haul from 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
The bidding for Taylor likely starts with multiple Day 2 (Rounds 2-3) draft selections, but if a contender comes calling with what they believe will be a late first-round pick, the Colts would be irresponsible to turn it down. Even then, multiple Day 2 picks would be a strong haul.
Keeping Taylor would make more sense if the Colts believed they could turn things around quickly. But the recent trades of Nelson and Buckner suggest Indianapolis is looking beyond the current roster. Holding onto Taylor while moving other established players would make less sense if the goal is to accumulate assets and reshape the team for the future.
Taylor is one of the league's best running backs, and Indianapolis should take the best return package possible. The Colts need to build for their next competitive window, and moving Taylor is an important step toward doing that.

title: Fire Sale: Potential Trade Packages for 3 Remaining Colts Stars
full_text:
Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner are gone. Two pillars of the Indianapolis Colts over the past decade were shipped out on Tuesday , and nobody feels untouchable anymore.
Indianapolis received a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder for Nelson, plus a 2027 fourth-round pick for Buckner. Both were on expiring deals, but that return still hurts.
At 2-5, the rest of this season could get brutal. All Colts fans can do is appreciate what these guys gave us, collect draft picks and hope the next regime gets it right.
With the Nov. 10 deadline approaching, here are three hypothetical trade packages these Colts might demand.
Proposed Trade: Denver Broncos send a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 fourth-round pick.
I'm not trading JT for a couple of mid-round picks. Unlike Nelson and Buckner, Taylor is under contract through 2028 after signing a two-year, $44 million extension in August.
Through seven games, he has 587 rushing yards and a league-leading eight touchdowns. He's 27, still the centerpiece of this offense, and by far Indianapolis' most valuable trade asset.
Denver is among the teams ESPN has linked to Taylor, although no offer has been reported. Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Taylor hasn't requested a trade, and Adam Schefter reports that owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon wants to keep him .
"[Carlie] Irsay-Gordon views [Jonathan] Taylor as a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild," Schefter said.
Fine by me. But if somebody wants JT, I'm demanding a massive haul. Ideally, you'd send him to an NFC team, but if an AFC contender comes calling with an offer you can't refuse, you have to consider it.
Also, the Colts don't own their 2027 first-rounder, so I want one back for the league's best RB.
Taylor netting a first-round pick would certainly be unprecedented and would no doubt be considered an overpay, but if the Colts play their cards right, they may just convince a potential suitor to pull the trigger.
Taylor's most comparable trade package is that of Christian McCaffrey's blockbuster haul from 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
The bidding for Taylor likely starts with multiple Day 2 (Rounds 2-3) draft selections, but if a contender comes calling with what they believe will be a late first-round pick, the Colts would be irresponsible to turn it down.
Proposed Trade: Pittsburgh Steelers send a 2027 fifth-round pick and 2028 sixth-round pick.
This one stings. Josh Downs has been one of my favorite young players to watch, and I never expected him to be part of this teardown.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday that Downs requested a trade , confirming that his days in Indianapolis are numbered.
Sources: Colts WR Josh Downs is requesting a trade from Indianapolis. pic.twitter.com/rwGaVGMTFf
The 25-year-old has 26 catches for 307 yards and no touchdowns through seven games, and his rookie contract expires after this season.
Multiple AFC teams, including the Pittsburgh Steelers, are reportedly interested in trading for Downs, according to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz .
Two Day 3 picks aren't exciting, but they're better than gambling on potential compensatory help down the road.
I still believe Downs can become one of the league's best receivers in the right offense.
Proposed Trade: Green Bay Packers send a 2027 sixth-round pick.
Big Grove has been holding down Indianapolis' run defense since 2017. He deserves plenty of appreciation for that, but at 33 and on an expiring contract, it's probably time to part ways.
His value is primarily against the run, not as a pass rusher. That limits the market, but I think a sixth-round pick is a reasonable return for a veteran who can still contribute against the run.
Moving Stewart would leave another hole along this defensive line. But a rebuilding team needs those draft picks, and getting something now beats watching another veteran walk in March.
None of this is easy to watch. If Tuesday taught us anything, it's that nobody's legacy guarantees they'll finish their career in Indianapolis.
The memories aren't going anywhere. The front office just needs to turn these departures into future Colts legends.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Biggest Colts Winners of Fire Sale: Two Young Players Get Massive Opportunity
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts may be punting on the 2026 season, but their future has some bright spots on the roster.
Colts' Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon has kicked off the team's rebuild with a fire sale of the roster's best players , trading away longtime franchise pillars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner on Tuesday.
The Colts are aiming to add any draft capital they can for the next era by shopping their top players, and this exodus began with the trading of the franchise's most pivotal staples.
Indianapolis's immediate outlook looks bleaker than ever before, but there are two players who have been granted a massive opportunity as a result.
If these two Colts can prove their worth, the next regime's year-one outlook may not be as dire as these trades suggest it'll be.
The biggest winner of the DeForest Buckner trade is Colts defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore.
The fourth-year interior defensive lineman has been an intriguing player since the Colts drafted him in the fourth round (110th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft.
Adebawore's absurd athletic profile was enough to entice, but his pass-rush potential excited most.
The talented young pass rusher flashed his intriguing skills across his first two seasons in the NFL, but he still had a long way to go in run defense before he could be considered for a bigger role.
Of course, the longtime interior duo of DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart made it nearly impossible for any defensive tackle to carve out a three-down role in the Colts' defense, but Buckner's departure changes everything.
Not only is the opportunity there, but Adebawore has earned the increased role in question.
Adebawore's first two seasons suggested that he'd likely be a designated pass rusher for the foreseeable future, but a quiet, mini-breakout in his third season single-handedly changed his trajectory.
Below are Adebawore's pass-rush numbers throughout his first three seasons (2023-25) in the NFL:
2023 (rookie): 20.7% playing time, 1.5 sacks, 7.6% pressure rate, 3 defensive stops 2024: 17.9% playing time, 1.0 sacks, 6.7% pressure rate, 4 defensive stops 2025: 46.8% playing time, 4.0 sacks, 10.2% pressure rate, 24 defensive stops
The upward trajectory was apparent, and Adebawore has locked in to fully break out after seven games in the 2026 regular season.
Adebawore struggled to find playing time to start the new year, but has since earned the trust of defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo and the rest of the staff.
After seven weeks, Adebawore is undeniably the Colts' best pass rusher. He is currently tied for second with the most sacks among interior defensive linemen league-wide and leads the team in most major pass-rush statistics.
#Colts DT Adetomiwa Adebawore has the 2nd-most pressures (12) on the team (excl. Buckner) after seven weeks despite only playing 35.9% of snaps. He leads the defense in sacks (4.0), pressure rate (13.0%), and quick pressures (6), and has the second-most stops (13). pic.twitter.com/cqamb6tThI
We've known that Adebawore has some nasty pass-rushing chops, but the biggest development has been his improvement in run defense.
Adebawore has blossomed into a legitimate starting defensive tackle, and it comes at no better time as the Colts have parted ways with their longtime pillar across the defensive line.
However, the Colts' newfound star is on an expiring deal. Adebawore is playing in the final year of his rookie contract, so a big payday is set to come his way.
The Colts are understandably busy shopping their failed era's best assets, but if they want to truly maximize the next regime's early outlook, extending Adebawore should be near the organization's top priorities moving forward.
A similar big opportunity has presented itself for one of the Colts' players still on a rookie contract: first-year guard Jalen Farmer.
Unlike Adebawore's situation, Farmer still has to prove himself as a legitimate NFL player
The Colts drafted Farmer in the fourth round (113th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft, envisioning that he'll become OL Coach Tony Sparano Jr.'s next installment of successful draft-and-stash projects .
Indianapolis was prepared to treat Farmer's rookie season like a redshirt year as they roll with their proven veteran unit, but Quenton Nelson's departure has changed the trajectory entirely.
Instead, a Hall of Fame-sized hole now sits across the Colts' interior offensive line, and Farmer is set to take over as we approach the midway point of the 2026 regular season.
Although he is an unproven rookie, Tony Sparano Jr. has the utmost faith in Farmer's ability .
As Sparano Jr. famously said following the Colts' combine interview with Farmer, "Let me tell you this much. Draft him, and I'll make it work."
Sparano Jr.’s conviction in Jalen Farmer is so apparent, not only by his own words, but also by the #Colts war room’s reaction when he arrives to celebrate said draft selection. 🎥: @Colts https://t.co/RxH86gKHkC pic.twitter.com/EFmmsUSYYe
In just a few short years with the Colts, Sparano Jr. has successfully developed the likes of LT Bernhard Raimann, RG Will Fries, RG Matt Goncalves, and C Tanor Bortolini.
Second-year tackle Jalen Travis has had an up-and-down start to his first season as a full-time starter, but there's still hope that he can become the ideal longtime Braden Smith replacement.
And it's easy to see why Sparano Jr. believes that Jalen Farmer will be his next successful project.
Farmer sports a strong athletic profile, has ample experience at the position (although he's mainly played right guard), and possesses a ton of raw power.
The Colts' rookie guard will be going from special teams duties to filling the void that Quenton Nelson left.
Even though this season is lost, the Colts have granted themselves a promising evaluation period of pieces that could stick with them through this ongoing fire sale and kick off the new era.
Farmer and Adebawore have a 10-game trial period to prove that they deserve to be long-term pieces of the rebuild.
Noah Compton is the Publisher of Indianapolis Colts On SI. Noah is from the Indy area and has been covering the Colts since 2022, including stops at FanSided, The Blue Stable, and SBNation.

title: Veteran Jaguars WR Jakobi Meyers' Week 8 Status vs. Colts Revealed
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have announced their list of inactives against the Indianapolis Colts for Week 8, and there is one key name left off the list.
Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers is officially active for the Jaguars after being listed as questionable with an ankle/hamstring injury earlier in the week. Meyers did not practice on Friday, but he is set to play for the Jaguars in their key Week 8 AFC South battle with the Indianapolis Colts.
Having Meyers available is good news for a Jaguars' passing game that has been ascending all season long. Meyers has been one of the Jaguars' most reliable and impactful pass-catchers since he was traded to the roster last November and he is a key reason Trevor Lawrence has been playing at an MVP-level ever since then.
With Meyers set to play, that does create some other questions in the receiver room. Meyers and Parker Washington are the clear top-two wideouts, and then the Jaguars will have to figure out how they want to deploy Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Cameron, and two-way star Travis Hunter against a struggling Colts team.
The official inactives for the Jaguars on Sunday are as follows: safety Antonio Johnson, defensive end Wesley Williams, defensive tackle Albert Regis, wide receiver CJ Williams, cornerback Alijah Huzzie, and linebacker Jamal Hill. The Jaguars will have cornerback Montaric Brown back on the field.
The Jaguars will certainly need Meyers and the rest of Lawrence's supporting cast in Week 8. While the Colts have been sending away their top players all week long while keeping their other top players waiting to see what will happen to their future.
"I think we have a ton of confidence and belief that we're a really good team. And how good is that? I think we all want to find out," Lawrence said earlier this week when discussing the Colts matchup. "And the only way that happens is if you put the work in every day, put your best foot forward and just take it one week at a time and we'll see where we stack up at the end of this thing.
"I think that's where there's a lot of confidence in our team, but there's also the reality that you have to take it one day at a time. It doesn't matter how good you think you are. You look at our schedule, we got 11 games left, and there's a long road before we even talk about postseason and all that stuff. So, we got a lot of work to do, and I think our team is just focused on today and then tomorrow and getting ready for Sunday as opposed to the big picture of what we could do.”

title: Jaguars-Colts Week 8 National Predictions Roundup: Will Jacksonville Complete the Sweep?
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are seen as big favorites entering Week 8 which, as is usually the case in the NFL, stiff far from a guaranteed win against an AFC South rival.
The Jaguars are set to host the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium in Week 8, with the Jaguars fresh off a bye and also playing at home for the first time since Week 3. With the Colts in complete teardown and rebuild mode, the Jaguars are clearly expected to roll past them this week, something head coach Liam Coen knows he has to be guarded against.
"It's innate as a coach. I've been a part of it so many times, especially as an assistant where you're so hyper-focused on your group, like, ‘Hey, I hope my group plays well today. I hope my position plays well today.’ As a head coach in general, I hope we all play well, but I kind of expect us to. I do," Coen said Friday.
"I don't expect us to walk out on the field and give lack of effort or guys not run to the football. And is it going to happen on some plays? Yeah. But as a whole, as a group, I do expect these guys to walk out on the field on Sunday and give their best effort for the most part. And is it always perfect? No. And that's what you're striving for, that perfect balance, but it's such an imperfect game. It is nice to know, this is the way I feel, that our guys are going to play on Sundays.”

title: Why the Jaguars' Week 8 Colts Matchup Could Define Their NFL Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have more than just AFC South questions to answer when they take the field in Week 8.
The only focus for the Jaguars on the field against the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium on Sunday will be finding a way to get the team's first AFC South win of the season under their belt. Sitting at 4-2 and against a 2-5 Colts team, a win on Sunday would go a long way for the Jaguars when it comes to their push for another AFC South title.
But off the field, the trade deadline is nearly here and there are quite a few positions of need for the Jaguars, starting with the defensive line in the wake of recent AFC South blockbusters. So, why could Week 8's battle with the Colts impact Jacksonville's trade plans on Nov. 10? We break it down below.
One way the Jaguars' trade deadline plans could be impacted Sunday is by the performance of their defensive line against the Colts and Daniel Jones in passing situations. The Colts' offense is built to lean on Jonathan Taylor and the running game, but it remains to be seen if he is active and has a large role during trade talks. And if he is, the Colts could still get forced into a pass-happy game depending on how the Jaguars' offense plays early on.
If this happens, the Colts will be put into more passing situations than they would likely want with injuries at wide receiver and a rookie now in at left guard after the trade of Quenton Nelson. The Colts have allowed the second-highest pressure rate and 12th-highest sack rate in the NFL early in the season, while Jones has been prone to forcing bad decisions and turnovers when under pressure.
The Colts average just 2.9 yards per pass when under pressure this season according to NextGenStats. So they are prone to sacks, turnovers, and do not get many big plays off when pressured. That should be a get-right game for the defensive line, and if it isn't then the Jaguars could have some real issues.
Simply put, if the Jaguars struggle to impact Jones with their pass-rush on Sunday then they will have to raise the urgency to add a pass-rusher at the deadline. Regardless of whether it is edge help or interior defensive line reinforcements, this game and matchup should tell the Jaguars how badly they need to add some help.
This one is interesting . One of the biggest questions of the week is whether Brian Thomas Jr. will have a large role on offense after playing zero snaps in the second-half against the Houston Texans in Week 6 in London. He has dealt with drop issues all season, the Jaguars really like both Josh Cameron and tight end Nate Boerkircher in multi-tight end sets, and Travis Hunter is coming off his second-best game ever as a wide receiver.
Still, Jakobi Meyers is questionable with an ankle/hamstring designation and did not practice Friday. If the Jaguars keep Meyers out or limit his role, would they then have the confidence in Thomas to go back to him as a key part of their offense? He has had a ton of success against the Colts in his career, even making big plays against them during their struggles a year ago.
What would a Thomas showcase against the Colts mean? Would it convince the Jaguars to continue to keep Thomas off the trade market like they have over the last year, or would it force receiver-needy teams to ante up ahead of Nov. 10? There are a number of outcomes that could come from a strong Thomas performance, making this a situation to watch.

title: Jaguars GM Slips Interesting Hint on Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The AFC South has made a few blockbuster trades in the lead-up to Week 8, and none were bigger than the Jeffery Simmons trade.
The Jaguars' AFC South rivals Tennessee Titans traded away star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears for two first-round draft picks and some change, the largest NFL trade since Myles Garrett was dealt to the Los Angeles Rams.
While the Jaguars were never going to be a part of the Simmons' sweepstakes in any real way since they are AFC South rivals with the Titans (similar to the DeForest Buckner situation) , the blockbuster has potentially revealed a very real hint about the Jaguars' trade deadline plans.
Speaking on Jaguars HQ alongside Executive Vice President of Football Operations Tony Boselli, the conversation came to recent trades in the AFC South, including the trade of All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears for a pair of first-round picks. Jaguars general manager James Gladstone made an interesting comment that, whether in truth or in jest, could have shown where the Jaguars' priorities are.
"If only it were in a different division," Gladstone added. "In that the typical approach of  inner-divison trades isn't generally on the table.
"It is nice to not have to play him twice a year. That is a net positive," Gladstone said to end the note.
It is worth noting that The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that the Jaguars were one of a few teams who contacted the Tennessee Titans about the availability of Simmons. That isn't ultimately all that surprising since Simmons is one of the best players in the NFL and it is likely fair to say quite a few teams inquired about him, but it still speaks volumes in the wake of Gladstone's hint.
Pelissero: Jaguars were among several teams that called the Titans about potential trade for Jeffery Simmons. pic.twitter.com/B0US3moCIF
Jacksonville was never going to be able to land Simmons for the reasons outlined, but the fact that the Jaguars were reportedly interested in the move should make it clear that the Jaguars are looking for some kind of a deal for an interior defensive lineman. This would also match the report from SI's Albert Breer earlier this week, where he listed the Jaguars and New York Giants as teams looking for defensive tackle help. Like the Jaguars, the Giants have been connected to Simmons in a number of reports.
There are not any other defensive tackles on the market quite like Simmons, of course. One of the biggest talents at the position whose name had also been floated in trade talks was Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne, but he has since sustained a season-ending foot injury that would nix any deal. But this does not mean that Jaguars' interest in adding to the defensive tackle interest should be squashed.
Gladstone and the Jaguars waited until the day of the deadline last season to reel in wide receiver Jakobi Meyers. They have close to a week to do the same for a defensive tackle this season, with Gladstone's hint about the Simmons move making it clearer and clearer that this is what the Jaguars' best-case scenario would be,

title: Trevor Lawrence Could Make a Major MVP Statement in Jaguars-Colts Showdown
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Indianapolis Colts are far from a premiere matchup on a big stage for Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence; he will get that in four days in Baltimore.
But coming out of the bye week, a surging Lawrence has a chance to do two important things for an early-season MVP case that has been building over the last one-and-a-half seasons under head coach Liam Coen: win and throw touchdowns.
A win over the Colts would put the Jaguars at 5-2 entering a primetime matchup with Lamar Jackson and a good Ravens team in four days. If the Jaguars take care of business, they could be 6-2 within the next few days. But that starts with a clash with the Colts, and Lawrence could be the prime benefactor from a strong Jaguars' performance.
The primary question is whether the Colts will blitz Trevor Lawrence or not. The Colts are one of the lowest blitz-rated teams in the NFL, blitzing on just 23.5% of dropbacks (No. 28 in the NFL). The Colts did rank No. 10 in 2025, and their two-highest blitz gameplans were their two games against the Jaguars and Lawrence.
Lawrence made the Colts pay against the blitz last year, though, and the Colts and defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo have mostly stuck with four-man pass-rushes to get after the quarterback. Perhaps that changes with injuries in the secondary and the departure of DeForest Buckner and decides to just throw everything and the kitchen sink at Lawrence.
Colts send three into the A-gaps to be sure a free rusher comes down the pipe. Still not sure how Lawrence got this much on this ball with this throwing motion. A true flick of the wrist. pic.twitter.com/zWdhWkpVNR
"It's more just, okay, how do Lou and those guys want to either protect or attack in a lot of ways? Are they going to play it a little bit more safe and sound and let those guys go play football and play coverage and be able to do those things? Or is it like, we're going to heat you up and here we go? We're going to apply the pressure regardless of who's in, put our guys in the back end in some difficult spots, but hey, we're just going to go attack," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Friday.
"I think it'll probably end up being a balance of both of those things, just knowing some of the personality of those guys and what they want to get done on defense. It can create some challenge because you're like, all right, you're trying to create matchups and get the best matchups when you're not exactly sure who's going to be in there."
But no matter what the Colts do, it feels like there is a good chance Lawrence is able to attack them through the air. Lawrence has had some of the best games of his career against the Colts, and this includes his performance against them in Week 14 in the Jaguars' statement 36-19 win that saw them really take control of the AFC South.
According to NextGenStats, Lawrence has posted a 119.1 passer rating when not blitzed this season, the highest among qualified passers, with 11 touchdown passes (tied for the most).
In addition, Lawrence has been pressured on 27.4% of his dropbacks without a blitz (5th-lowest), while the Colts have generated pressure on 24.4% of opponent dropbacks this season, the lowest rate in the NFL and the lowest by a defense in a season since at least 2018. The Colts 58 pressures on defense is the fewest in the NFL this season, and they're the only defense with fewer than 60 pressures.
When Lawrence has struggled at times in the Coen era has been when the pressure rate has been high. Lawrence's two worst performances by EPA/Dropback this season were in Weeks 5 and 2, and those were also the games with his two-highest pressure rates. The same trend followed in 2025: When the Jaguars kept Lawrence clean, he carved defenses up.
There is reason to believe the Jaguars can get that done on Sunday. If they do, we could be in store for a vintage Lawrence performance that once again puts the Jaguars over the top in the AFC South. The Jaguars can start carving their way to a high seed in the AFC during the next 11 weeks, but it must start in Week 8 against a vulnerable Colts team.
Lawrence's MVP case right now is clear. The Jaguars would put themselves right in the thick of things for the AFC's No. 1 seed with a string of wins over the next few weeks, and Lawrence currently ranks No. 7 in EPA/Play and No. 10 in success rate amongst quarterbacks. He is the productive leader of a high-scoring offense that is winning more often than they lose, which is an MVP case any year.
If Lawrence is throwing three or four touchdowns in a statement home win, nobody will care that the Colts are hosting a fire sale. They will care that he is continuing to play the best football of his career before a big game against the Ravens.

title: 5 DTs the Jaguars Should Target at Trade Deadline After Daron Payne's Injury
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Count one big name off the 2026 NFL Trade market.
Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne reportedly suffered a serious foot injury in practice this week, and will head to injured reserve with what could be a season-ending injury. As a result, Payne will not be moved to any team at the deadline.
#Commanders standout DT Daron Payne suffered a significant foot injury today in practice that will knock him out for the foreseeable future and likely land him IR, sources tell me and @MikeGarafolo . Payne will undergo more evaluations tomorrow. But another tough blow for… pic.twitter.com/ENPd0FB1eV
While the Jaguars have never once been officially connected in any trade interest for Payne, the productive Pro Bowler is in the middle of another productive season and would have made a ton of sense for a team like the Jaguars.
With Payne no longer an option, who are other defensive tackles worth taking a look at ahead of the trade deadline? We break down a few names below.
We of course could not mention the defensive tackle position and not talk about Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. I struggle to see a scenario where the Eagles can pay him this offseason considering the bill that is due for them sometime around the corner. Stranger things have happened, perhaps, but Ojomo to me still feels more likely to be traded than to be an Eagle in 2027, no matter where he goes.
I think Ojomo is a good fit for the Jaguars from a number of perspectives. He would come with a high price tag down the road if the Jaguars hope for him to be anything other than a rental, but that is a problem they can figure out later. For now, Ojomo would help make the Jaguars a better team against the run and the pass, which is the goal above all else when it comes to a trade deadline move.
The Buccaneers have two more games to play by the NFL Trade Deadline. If they drop those games they will be at 2-7 and not in great shape moving forward, even with the state of the NFC South which, well, is not great. The Buccaneers are not 2-5 right now because of their interior defensive line, with the Buccaneers having two of the more talented players who could reasonably be moved.
Vita Vea is obviously the big name, and for good reason. A Vea/DaVon Hamilton defensive tackle duo would be outrageous, and he does impact the pass-rush. He likely would cost a bit more, though, and there is his 2027 money to consider. Robinson is cheap and in the final year of his deal, but he has been productive against the run and the pass and has connections via his time with the Los Angeles Rams.
We have mentioned Zach Sieler before , and I still think he makes a lot of sense as long as the Jaguars are okay with the money attached to him moving forward. He is signed through the 2029 season and is 31 right now, but the Dolphins are also in a rebuilding year that would likely benefit more from having draft picks tomorrow as opposed to Sieler on another struggling team next season.
Sieler can be impactful agianst the run and pass, and he played for the Dolphins at the same time that both Anthony Campanile and Mathieu Araujo during their time in Miami. He would give the Jaguars a solid fit both in terms of scheme and need, as well as an off-field locker room leader who knows what it is supposed to look like.
Roy Lopez is one of the more underrated defensive tackles in the NFL, and there is reason to believe he would help a team like the Jaguars quite a bit against the run. He won't attract quite as much attention from teams as a pass-rusher, but he would give the Jaguars improved depth in the middle of their defense on a cheap deal. He would give the Jaguars more bang for their buck price-wise than most other options, and a rebuilding team like the Arizona Cardinals would be unlikely to ask for all that much.

title: Jaguars-Colts Friday Injury Report: 1 Player Must Step Up in Antonio Johnson's Absence
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars will be without a big piece of their defense against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8.
The Jaguars officially ruled defensive back Antonio Johnson out for Sunday's game vs. the Colts , with the fourth-year safety set to miss the AFC South battle due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 6 in London against the Houston Texans. Johnson has not practiced for the Jaguars this week, being listed as a non-particpant in all three practices.
With Johnson officially out on Sunday, the Jaguars will more than likely turn to safety Kaevon Merriweather to start against the Colts, but who exactly is the veteran safety and what does he bring to the table?
The Jaguars have seen their safety group get hit with injuries at different points this season, and Merriweather has been one veteran who has helped steady the waters. The fourth-year safety signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2023 and appeared in 42 games with the Buccaneers in three seasons. This included 14 games with the Buccaneers in 2024 when Jaguars head coach Liam Coen was the team's offensive coordinator.
“Need Kaevon to continue to step up and evolve. But being with him in Tampa, he was a guy that really helped on teams and played his tail off there but was also able to step in and he started, I think, like eight games for us that year in ‘24 at safety. The game wasn't too big for him," Coen said on Friday.
Merriweather also spent time with the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions during parts of his career, and he signed to the Jaguars practice squad early in September. He was eventually moved up to the active roster, and he now looks like he will have to play a significant role in some facet against the Colts at home on Sunday.
"And then when you went and watched him transition to Houston and then watched him throughout the preseason and the regular season on special teams, you could tell he took on some of the identity and ways in which Houston plays," Coen said. "That physicality, running to the football, burning it down and going and playing your ass off. That was something that was intriguing for us as well. And I've always just thought the game wasn't ever too big for Kaevon, never really got too high, too low. And he's done a nice job stepping in for us.”
Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile was asked about the safety position earlier this week and noted Merriweather's name when the topic of Johnson potentially missing the game came up. After showings against the Philadelphia Eagles and Houston Texans, Merriweather has left an impression.
“Every game's different and I think we're fortunate where we got a really good room there, and I think Kaevon [Merriweather] has done a good job coming in here as a new guy who's stepped up and given us the opportunity to have another guy that can kind of play some of those roles," Campanile said/
"I think even watching him in the last game, you see some physicality, and I think he's learning everything we're doing. He's worked really hard at it. I think Perk [Defensive Backs Coach Anthony Perkins] has done a great job with him, getting him up to speed. So, there's some other guys in that room who help us that way. Like any game, you're always adjusting.”
Johnson has been a key piece of the Jaguars' defense, especially when it comes to his ability against the run and as a blitzer. There is no replacing Johnson, but the Jaguars will look to Merriweather to play a real role Sunday, and play it well.
