title: 1 Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Theory About the Jaguars Completely Misses the Mark
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Brian Thomas Jr. is a polarizing topic when it comes to this year's trade deadline, and understandably so.
Thomas was one of the best receivers in the league during a record-setting rookie season in 2024, making him the lone bright spot of what was otherwise one of the most lost seasons in franchise history. He has struggled in the 1 1/3 seasons since then, though, and there is constant debate on what the Jacksonville Jaguars may do with him come Nov. 10.
But with that said, there is one Thomas theory that has been floated this week that, well, just misses each and every possible mark. That theory, of course, centers around the Jaguars' motivations with Thomas, something that can't be represented as anything but patience.
The theory comes from NBC Sports' Mike Florio , and comes during a larger conversation about receiver-needy teams at the trade deadline like the Kansas City Chiefs. While making the case that the Jaguars are being too stubborn when it comes to a potential asking price for Thomas, who has never been confirmed to be in any trade talks to begin with, Florio went as far as to say the Jaguars are holding the third-year wide receiver hostage.
Strange is not a bad way to describe where things have gotten with Thomas, who truly looked like he was set to be one of the faces of the franchise as a rookie in 2024. The only times the Jaguars have ever talked about Thomas and trades in public have been when they have completely and utterly denied any such interest in dealing Thomas, most commonly during the 2026 offseason.
Thomas was an amazing player during the 2024 season. He is still clearly an amazing talent, because the Jaguars would not have poured so much into him over the last two seasons otherwise. But for one reason or another, it just has not clicked with him and the the offense since Liam Coen took over last season.
It is not for a lack of effort on either side. Coen said at the NFL Scouting Combine in 2025 that the passing game would go through Thomas, and it did for the first two months of the 2025 season. Thomas' struggles began, though, and the addition of Jakobi Meyers and ascencion of Parker Washington changed the dynamics of the passing game.
The Jaguars did not give up on Thomas as a part of their future, though. Thomas has also never once been questioned for his effort or want-to. Thomas is one of the best blockers in the receiver room and has poured in plenty during his three seasons with the team. It is not as if the Jaguars have phased Thomas out right off the bat or Thomas ever became anything but a top-self teammate and member of the locker room.
Come for Jakobi Meyers' catch, stay for Brian Thomas Jr.'s block 😮‍💨 RT to #ProBowlVote | #JAXvsTEN on CBS pic.twitter.com/oIgYMJvCam
That is where Florio misses the mark. He says the Jaguars are holding Thomas hostage, but would he say that about quite literally any other player whose name has come up in trade rumors? Are the Indianapolis Colts holding Josh Downs hostage? Has Thomas ever once requested a trade and been denied it, as so often happens in the NFL?
The answer to all of these questions is no. The Jaguars have truly tried to make it work with Thomas, and there is a true chance they go right back to trying to make it work in Week 8 against the Colts. Leveraging Thomas' fit and future with the appropiate value for a player of his talents is far from a hostage situation. It is instead the reality of every-day business in the NFL.
We will find out how the Thomas story will unfold over the next 10+ days. If no trade goes down then, the Jaguars will clearly continue to make Thomas a part of what they do, even if it isn't as large of a role as he once held, or even started the season with. Trade connections would surely pick up again next offseason, but that is a problem for tomorrow.
The Thomas situation has made little sense in terms of how it has played out, but that doesn't mean we should misrepresent the situation.

title: Jaguars Mailbag: Colts Game Could Impact the Trade Deadline in More Ways Than One
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- It is starting to get wild in the NFL.
The NFL Trade Deadline is right around the corner and the action has ramped up throughout the AFC South. With the deadline looming, as does the Jaguars' Week 8 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts in an important divisional battle. We take questions on both of these big events and much more in this week's Jaguars Mailbag.
Are the Jaguars generating enough pressure without relying on sacks, or is their defensive approach leaving too much on the table?
A: I do think the pressure has been relatively fine. I think if the Jaguars had less passes thrown over the secondary's head in the last few weeks, the worries about low sack totals would go away some. But whenever big plays are consistently getting made, the pass-rush is going to draw focus when they are not making the plays to offset any potential coverage woes. The Jaguars could be better here, but I do not think it is an issue of approach. I also think the Jaguars get several sacks this week against Daniel Jones.
Do you foresee any random changes with the offense or defense coming out of the bye? Like certain players getting more snaps/substitutions etc
A: I think we could start seeing more and more snaps for Ruke Orhorhoro and Albert Regis. I think the Jaguars are really happy with the momentum that Orhorhoro was able to build before the bye week, while Regis has gotten praise from both head coach Liam Coen and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile for his work in practice. This would mean, to me, fewer snaps for both Arik Armstead and Matt Dickerson.
With all the talk of adding a player to the DL - who do you think ends up with the most sacks at the end of the year, and what is their total?
A: Josh Hines-Allen with 9.5. I think he heats up as the year goes on, especially if the Jaguars add some help to change the way protections are shifted to him. Travon Walker isn't a bad shout, either, though I do think Hines-Allen will be set for more chances to close in on sacks than Walker over the next few months.
Some no so serious questions: What's your go-to restaurant? Favorite food? Favorite/Least Favorite moment covering the Jags so far? Jaguars Uniform (Past, present, Rivalries™, etc.) takes? With the holidays approaching, any holiday takes you need to get off your chest?
2) Favorite moment: covering the AFC South title win in 2022. Least favorite? Covering Day 3 of the 2023 NFL Draft. They made a million picks and half of them were grotesque. Some were awesome, though.
3) I love the teal helmets they are wearing Sunday. Still not sure what the heck those white helmets were in 2024.
4) This is the best stretch of holidays. Halloween into Thanksgiving into Christmas.
Is D-line the only trade Gladstone would make or is their another position that could significantly improve the team?
I think the Jaguars could add a number of different positions at the trade deadline that would make them a better team. Defensive end? Check. Defensive tackle? Double check. Safety? Sure! Cornerback? Yep. Even offensive tackle. The Jaguars are a good team, but like any team they still have some flaws to address.
What are the odds of Camp and Udinski leaving in the offseason? And if so, any in house successor candidates or just outside hires?
A: I think the chances are high, especially if the Jaguars keep winning. I would say Udinksi would be the most likely coach to leave since teams tend to lean toward young offensive hires and Udinski would check both of those boxes. I think Campanile will get some interviews, though, and there is always the chance that he gets the nod. I think Shane Waldron getting promoted to offensive coordinator would be a natural move, while defensively I could see Coen going for an outside name with ties. Ejiro Evero , perhaps?
Oklahoma drill, Apollo vs Ketchup…who wins?
A: Ketchup in a landslide. Apollo is a lover, not a fighter. Actually, he isn't even a lover. He just is kind of happy to be there. He is more of a backup quarterback than a lineman. Apollo and Ketchup are mine and Gus Logue's dogs, by the way.
If Montaric Brown comes back fully healthy, do you think Jarrian and Lewis rotate in or is someone the odd man out
A: It does look like the Jaguars will have Montaric Brown back on the field this Sunday against the Colts, which I think is a big deal even with his earlier struggles this season. Without Brown on the field, the Jaguars have been forced to only really rely on their top-three cornerbacks no matter the situations, playy-calls, packages, or matchups. By having Brown available, I think it just gives the Jaguars more options. I think Travis Hunter plays every snap, and then the other three guys play rleatively the same amount of snaps as one another.
if Jags trade for budda or any other safety, who goes to the bench between Eric Murray and Antonio Johnson?
A: I think if there had to be one guy who would see fewer snaps over the course of the year as a result of a safety getting added to the mix, it would be Eric Murray. Antonio Johnson has been their best safety this year, whether in coverage or in space as a tackler. He’s also arguably the best blitzer on the entire defense. With that said, I think the Jaguars’ response to a good problem like this would be to lean on all three safeties, whether with rotations or with three-safety sets.
How many targets does Hunter get on offense rest of season?
A: I am going to say …. 30. There are 11 games left, so at least two per game on average and then a few games where he gets more than that. I could see it get closer to 40 if there are weeks like Houston where he just seems to be the hot hand when it comes to the passing game.
I know I have an issue w/being patient & instant gratification, especially w/3 trades this past week, but any surprise the Jags didnt make a move at the bye? Do you think they're waiting on players availablily? Price to go down? They trust their guys/self-scout made during bye?
A: I think they just aren't in a hurry, and they shouldn't be. We still have a week-and-a-half until the trade deadline, and the Jaguars did not make their move for Jakobi Meyers last year until the day of the deadline despite having checked in with the Raiders as early as the 2025 training camp. I think a move happens, but not until closer to the deadline.
Why aren’t linemen and linebackers wearing full face face masks anymore?
Do opposing QBs having quick release time because of our pressure rate or are receivers getting open that fast because of off coverage? I have to imagine, the reason we get so many picks is because our CBs are counting on the quick release time and can sit on short routes
A: You are exactly right. Anthony Campanile said that a lot of the times aquarterbacks are getting the ball out fast is because the Jaguars' defense is intentional about forcing it out of their hands quickly. This suggests to me that Campanile puts most of the onus for the big plays on the secondary behind the pressures and the blitzes.
How serious are trade talks for btj? Any teams at the forefront?
A: This is just my own take, but I do not think the Jaguars will be actively looking to shop him. I think he is enough of a talent and a big name that his production shops him for the Jaguars, and eventually teams will be aggressive in gauging his value. Since we have yet to see a trade completed, I would say the only assumption to make is that they have yet to get a very serious offer for him. Will that change? Stay tuned over the next few weeks.
If Brian Thomas rebounds and plays well this week, it could obviously affect his trade value, but do you see that having any effect on if he remains a jaguar or not?
A: This is a great quesiton. I really do not think the Jaguars will sell low on Brian Thomas Jr., and I believe it will take something worthwhile for the Jaguars to officially give up on him. With that said, I think even if Thomas has a breakout game for the first time in a long time, he…

title: 3 NFL Trade Deadline Deals the Jaguars Should Explore Right Now in Wide-Open AFC
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The NFL trade market has heated up in a big way this week, with three All-Pros traded from the AFC South alone since Tuesday.
Whether the Jaguars will get in on the trade action remains to be seen, but it is always fun to project anyways. The Jaguars have made a number of trades since James Gladstone took over, with the Jaguars' general manager completing nine non-draft day trades involving players since he was hired.
This includes trading for Jakobi Meyers at the trade deadline a year ago, a move that instantly gave the Jaguars a boost and has paid off since. And while it was a draft-day trade, Gladstone's biggest move as general manager was the 2025 blockbuster for Travis Hunter.
James Gladstone's Player Trades
2026 5th-Round Pick, 2026 6th-Round Pick
CB Tyson Campbell, 2026 7th-Round Pick
CB Greg Newsome, 2026 6th-Round Pick
2026 4th-Round Pick, 2026 6th-Round Pick
In short, the Jaguars have been pretty agressive in terms of trades. They made a move last season with the idea of winning, and it would make sense to do the same this year. But which targets would make the most sense, and which deals could make it happen? We break it down below.
The Offer: Brian Thomas Jr.
Let's get weird? I would also think picks have to be involved, with the Jaguars perhaps sending a seventh-round pick and getting a fourth-round selection in return. Thomas would have much, much more value in terms of draft picks landed in a trade if this was just a player-for-picks deal, but adding a productive veteran like Payne would be enticing. Payne is still in his prime at 29 and is a legit difference-maker against both the run and the pass, but he is under contract for just 11 more games.
Landing Payne as a rental would likely not be ideal, even if the Jaguars would likely be able to recoup something for him in the form of compensatory draft picks in the future. But with several expiring contracts along the interior defensive line, the Jaguars could look to Payne as a defensive version of Jakobi Meyers: a productive, experienced player who can bring an instant impact and sign a deal shortly after as a result.
Letting go of Thomas will always sting a bit for the Jaguars if it does happen. That is why if the Jaguars do trade Thomas, they must get something worthwhile in return. Considering Payne's fit and talent and the need for a difference-maker insider, he would certainly qualify as worthwhile. This could help push the Jaguars' defense over the top and have a minimal impact on the offense. This wouldn't be as explosive as a Jeffery Simmons deal, but Payne could have a similar impact in terms of improving the entire unit.
The Offer: 2027 3rd-Round Pick
Another defensive tackle, and for good reason. As SI's Albert Breer noted, "The Giants and Jaguars are sniffing around on defensive tackles—Jacksonville’s looking for pieces for its defensive front in general." It makes sense considering the Jaguars have a short-term need for a spark inside, as well as a long-term need for a new centerpiece for the interior defensive line. When it comes to potentially available defensive tackle targets, Ojomo is up there with Payne while also being four years younger and still ascending as a talent.
The Jaguars' fit with Ojomo makes a ton of sense off the bat. He has been disruptive against both the run and the pass, he is young and is still getting better each season, he fits the scheme like a glove, and he would give the Jaguars a talent boost at a key position of need. The question, of course, has to do with the fact that he is in a contract year. This could impact what the Eagles do quite a bit considering the options they would have if they didn't trade Ojomo.
If the Eagles opt not to trade Ojomo, then there are only two outcomes for them ahead: signing him to a big deal to give them the most expensive defensive tackle room in NFL history, or letting him walk in free agency for what very likely could be a future third-round compensatory pick, depending on how big of a deal he signs and what other moves the Eagles make. This is exactly what happened with Milton Williams, and it is not hard to see Ojomo cashing in like he did.
If you are the Jaguars, I think you accept the fact that the Eagles' asking price would be a third-round pick today. Jacksonville could live with that depending on how they play free agency next March and depending on just how much Ojomo would improve them. He is worth the swing, though.
The Offer: 2027 5th-Round Pick
It is really easy to make the case for the Jaguars to add a guy like Budda Baker. They are hurting at the safety position, having all three of their top safeties available for just the first three games of the season. Since then, Eric Murray has missed some time, Antonio Johnson is now banged-up, and Caleb Ransaw is on injured reserve. Adding a safety would help the Jaguars quite a bit in the short-term.
Then you add in the fact that Budda Baker has been one of the NFL's best and most productive, reliable, and durable safeties of the last decade, and it is easy to see the fit. Baker played the Rams twice a year during James Gladstone's and Liam Coen's time in Los Angeles, and the 30-year-old would clearly carry a ton of respect in the Jaguars' building, while serving as a legit fit and play-maker.
The Cardinals are not going anywhere during the next season-and-a-half Baker is under contract, and he would allow the Jaguars to confidently play three-safety sets once Johnson is healthy. A trio of Johnson, Murray, and Baker would be quite the group for the Jaguars at the safety position as they look to make a run for the AFC South down the stretch of the year.

title: Chiefs' Cornerback Depth Takes Considerable Hit With Latest Injury News
full_text:
A pleasant surprise of the Kansas City Chiefs' season thus far has been their cornerback room. For the most part, players like Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams are providing surplus value and helping shape what could turn out to be a premier duo for years to come.
One weakness of the unit, however, is the slot position. Veteran L'Jarius Sneed, who signed back with his first NFL franchise earlier this year, has struggled in his second stint with the team. Unfortunately, he won't have an opportunity to improve that level of play in the next handful of weeks.
Per a post on X from the Chiefs on Saturday, Sneed is going on the injured reserve list. As a result, he'll miss at least Sunday's contest versus the Denver Broncos and upcoming games against the New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals.
We have signed Practice Squad player CB Melvin Smith to an active roster contract. We have activated Practice Squad player DE Tyreke Smith via Standard Elevation. We have placed CB L’Jarius Sneed on Reserve/Injured. pic.twitter.com/oczbgGKFOf
Taking Sneed's place on the active 53-man roster is practice squad cornerback Melvin Smith. In the same sweep of announcements, Kansas City revealed that defensive end Tyreke Smith was activated from the practice squad via standard elevation.
Sneed, who turns 30 in January, has 32 tackles and three pass breakups across 258 defensive snaps in the Chiefs' six games this year. According to NFL Pro , offenses have targeted Sneed on 29.2% of his coverage snaps, the highest rate for anyone with 100-plus reps since at least 2018. Pro Football Focus is harsh on his coverage, too, citing him with 36 receptions and a 110.0 passer rating given up.
The news doesn't stop there for the Chiefs, as their top 2026 NFL Draft pick will also sit out this weekend's clash in Denver.
In a separate post , Kansas City shared that rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane was downgraded to out for Week 8 due to a shoulder injury. It's something that's been an off-and-on issue for months, with head coach Andy Reid saying Friday the team would " see how he does " before making a final decision on his Sunday availability.
Delane, the No. 6 overall pick in April's draft, recorded an interception on the very first drive of his NFL career in Week 1's blowout win over these same Broncos. The LSU product has played 287 defensive snaps for coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, good for 83% of those available, in his five games.
Delane's had a very strong debut season overall but did get his proverbial " welcome to the league " moment(s) against the Seattle Seahawks and reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba in Week 7.
When asked about the opportunity to line up against elite wideouts, Delane said he embraces the challenge to hone his craft.
"I think some people may get discouraged from passes caught on them," Delane said. "But I told coach Spags, ‘Man, put me in those tough situations.’ I'm not asking for a cloud. I'm not asking for Cover 2. Go back out there and play man, and that's what we did. A lot of teams [are] kind of scared to do that, but I feel like we didn't shy away from it. We learned from it, but at the same time, there are going to be times in my career that I'm going to better handle that stick, and I'm definitely going to learn from that.”
It's unclear whether Delane's injury will hold him out of Week 9's meeting with the Jets; his practice participation next week should give a stronger signal either way.
To cap off this injury roundup, second-round defensive end R Mason Thomas (personal) will travel separately and join the team in the Mile High City.

title: Ranking the Chiefs Players Most Likely to Be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
While all 32 NFL teams are primarily banking on their internal candidates to either sustain momentum or help turn things around, there's still time to acquire some assistance from the outside. For clubs like the Kansas City Chiefs, a trade might be what makes or breaks the season.
As the calendar flips from October to November, the NFL trade deadline (November 10, 3:00 p.m. CT) is rapidly approaching. With needs at wide receiver and potentially elsewhere, could general manager Brett Veach make any moves to improve the roster?
If not, what about recouping some NFL Draft capital for the future and shedding a bit of weight in the process? Chiefs On SI has singled out five Kansas City players who might be appealing to other organizations for various reasons ahead of the cutoff.
When the Chiefs first signed cornerback Kristian Fulton to a two-year deal in the 2025 offseason, this couldn't have been the path they envisioned. The former Los Angeles Chargers standout was hurt coming into the year and spent most of the season buried on the bench, only to show flashes at the end of the campaign and leave just as many questions as answers entering the spring and summer.
Seven weeks into the 2026-27 regular season, has Fulton managed to clear anything up? It's complicated. He's been available for 135 defensive snaps — 40% of those possible — and has surrendered just four completions on eight targets for 18 yards ( Pro Football Reference ). He's served primarily as depth, although L'Jarius Sneed's struggles and rookie Mansoor Delane's fluctuating health might make Fulton someone to keep around.
Still, per Spotrac , Fulton only has $5.42 million remaining on his deal and could be an intriguing pickup for any corner-needy club. He easily makes the most sense as a trade chip, in this writer's view.
Update: Sneed has since been placed on the injured reserve list , further emphasizing the potential need for Fulton.
Considering that quarterback Justin Fields has played only one regular-season snap as a Chief, any team acquiring him would be doing so strictly out of circumstance or approval of his past performance. The last time we saw the former first-round pick for an extended stretch was this preseason, when he went 13-for-16 passing for 105 yards. Prior to that, it was a nine-game starting stint with the New York Jets that saw him own an 89.5 passer rating.
Still, Fields remains a mobile dual-threat signal-caller with experience in a multitude of offenses. If there's a franchise out there with an injured starter or a pressing need for a backup, making a swap like this is sensible. He's a free agent in the spring, so this wouldn't net anything more than a very late draft pick.
It's hard to see Fields being dealt twice in one calendar year, but weirder things have happened.
For one reason or another, the Chiefs' original fourth-round selection of tight end Jared Wiley in 2024 hasn't panned out. The former TCU product battled injury earlier in his Kansas City tenure, and he's been primarily a warm body in the position room in 2026. Entering Week 8's showdown with the Denver Broncos, Wiley's appeared in one game, playing seven snaps on special teams and two on offense.
Is there a team out there that thinks it can unlock something with Wiley? He turns 26 two days after the publication of this story and has one year remaining on his deal after 2026. Perhaps an offensive coaching staff is optimistic it can harness whatever's left of his athletic profile and make him a decidely rosterable player.
Jared Wiley is a TE prospect in the 2024 draft class. He scored an unofficial  9.52 #RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 55 out of 1116 TE from 1987 to 2024. Splits projected https://t.co/AUYy1C4co1 pic.twitter.com/GYtwZ0nzRn
I personally don't believe Wiley has any trade value, but again, it's hard to completely rule out.
The case of safety Jaden Hicks, another 2024 fourth-rounder, is curious. As a rookie, he looked like a budding star at the position, yet he's been anything but that ever since. Last year was a rough one for him, although he went on to produce some highlights this preseason and got a vote of confidence from defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo in the process.
Hicks' workload is at a career-high 69% mark by snap share, although it's down to 41.6% over his last three games. Pro Football Focus credits him with nine "stops" in six contests, paired with a healthy 77.5 tackling grade, although his coverage chops are still questionable at best.
Given that Chamarri Conner is slated to become a free agent in March, it may not be too wise an idea for Kansas City to give up on Hicks right now. Should an opposing executive come with a surprising offer, however, Veach would have to at least consider it.
This one seems like the most difficult needle to thread in terms of likelihood. Not only can defensive back Chris Roland-Wallace do a bit of everything in the secondary, but he's a Spagnuolo favorite and also plays for Dave Toub's special teams unit. Add in that he's entering restricted free agency in the spring, and it makes more sense for the Chiefs to retain those rights and leave it up to the market than move him in 2026.
For all the play-related reasons, though, Roland-Wallace might appeal to another front office. This season, in particular, he's been a heat-seeking missile on screen passes and is always a threat to crash downhill with reckless abandon. He's lined up 48 times in the box, 40 in the slot and 12 along the edge of the defensive line. Last year, he had 60 reps as a traditional free safety as well.
Finding a cost-effective jack of all trades is infinitely easier said than done.

title: The Chiefs’ Biggest Matchup on Each Side of the Ball Against the Broncos
full_text:
The Chiefs' Week 8 trip to Denver is as big a mid-season game as Kansas City has played in recent memory.
According to The Athletic’s 2026 NFL Simulator , the Chiefs’ odds of winning the AFC West skyrocket to 84 percent with a win over the Broncos. With a loss, those odds drop to 48 percent, and the race likely stays neck and neck until the end of the season.
The Broncos will be a desperate opponent, which is always a scary situation for a team like Kansas City. In the same vein, head coach Andy Reid and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo understand the magnitude of the game, so they likely will not hold back either.
Here are the two biggest matchups the Chiefs could exploit to take complete control of the AFC West.
The Chiefs found out last week what happens when an opponent shuts down its rushing attack. It may have been a matchup issue, and no defense in the league may be better suited to shut down Kenneth Walker than the Seattle Seahawks . Slowing him down is much easier said than done.
With the run game not working, Reid handed it to Kenneth Walker just 14 times, even though it was a tight ballgame for most of the contest. They got away from many of the under-center formations that had been working.
Walker finished with 36 yards, a season low by far. That led Patrick Mahomes to attempt 33 passes in a predictable game plan that Seattle had no trouble figuring out, and it visibly frustrated Mahomes and the Kansas City offense.
Denver defensive coordinator Vance Joseph will surely not deploy the same strategy he did in Week 1, when the Chiefs scored 31 points and Walker ran for 173 yards. That said, the Broncos are the league's 28th-ranked rushing defense. Walker forced 14 missed tackles in that Week 1 game, and the tackling woes have continued for Joseph’s defense.
Denver leads the league in missed tackles with 60 through seven games. There will be adjustments, but this may simply be a great matchup for the Kansas City offense. Walker is still second in the NFL in rushing yards, and he should pick up right where he left off before Week 7.
This matchup is a similar theme. The Chiefs got after the quarterback against Denver in Week 1, but they couldn’t do it at all against the Seahawks.
While Kansas City’s defense still ranks among the league’s best in pressure rate, they are second-to-last in total sacks with eight. Oddly enough, they have two games with four sacks and four games where they were completely blanked. Luckily for the Chiefs, one of those four-sack games came against the Broncos and Bo Nix.
Nix has been sacked only four times in the six games since, but he has performed poorly when pressured, which clearly plays into what Kansas City’s pass rush has actually been able to accomplish.
According to PFF, when kept clean, Nix has six touchdowns and one interception. When pressured, he has one touchdown and two interceptions. When pressured, he has six more turnover-worthy plays, a quarterback rating 53.2 points worse, and gets the ball out nearly a full second slower.
Many of those poor numbers have come against the blitz. Nix has been blitzed on 90 dropbacks this season, averaging just 4.1 yards per attempt with a 46 percent completion rate, and he has been sacked three times in those instances.
With so much riding on this game, Spagnuolo could unleash some of his patented exotic blitzes. The biggest question marks are how creative he is with his calls and whether Chris Jones can finally get going, or whether it will once again be the George Karlaftis show, with a splash of pressure from R Mason Thomas.
If Kansas City can get back to pressuring Nix, the offense may not need its best day to win. Keeping Denver’s offense stuck where it has been all season, 30th in total offense and 25th in scoring, is the number one key to this game.

title: ESPN Matchup Predictor Analyzes Chiefs vs. Broncos Divisional Showdown in Week 8
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs cruised to a 5-0 start to open the 2026 NFL campaign, but they ran into a brick wall last week in a prime time showdown with the Seattle Seahawks . Before Andy Reid's squad could even blink, the Chiefs are suddenly in danger of surrendering the AFC West lead when they take on the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High tomorrow.
These division rivals have already faced off earlier this season, when Kansas City took care of business 31-10 in the regular season opener. However, the Broncos have strung together a three-game winning streak during which they have allowed fewer than 16 points per contest. Many Chiefs fans have grown increasingly concerned about the state of the offense after its horrendous three-point showing on Sunday Night Football . When opposing defenses take away Kenneth Walker, KC has struggled to get anything going and create explosive plays.
This will undoubtedly be the most pivotal game of the Chiefs' season to date. Let's dive into what the ESPN Matchup Predictor believes will transpire in this AFC West clash.
Even with a comparable record on paper, the matchup predictor still gives the Chiefs a slight edge tomorrow evening.
ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 55.7%, Broncos 44.0%.
The Chiefs have now been matchup predictor favorites in every game they've played this season.
Amid a week filled with the Chiefs being embroiled in controversy , it's important to remember that a crucial contest awaits them. They desperately need to avoid falling in their second consecutive loss and relinquishing the division lead.
Things can only trend upward for this Chiefs offense, which mustered up 213 total yards and one field goal a week ago. Now that the outside noise about Kenneth Walker's return to Seattle can be put to bed, the hope is that he and Patrick Mahomes will get back to what they were doing earlier this year.
As for Denver, much has been made about Bo Nix and his inability to move the ball downfield, but the Broncos have been winning in spite of his questionable quarterback play. His defense bailed him out time and time again in an overtime thriller two weeks ago, when the Broncos outplayed the Seahawks and won on a walk-off field goal by Wil Lutz.
Ja'Quan McMillian read this PERFECTLY. SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1igvuDtROG
It makes you wonder how a team that ranks in the bottom three of the NFL in offensive yards has a 5-2 record with several solid wins. While the Broncos look mediocre using the eye test, their record keeps proving everyone wrong.
There's no question that the Chiefs have the better offense of these two teams, but the bigger question is whether they can find their footing early or if Denver's defense will stifle it from the jump. If the Broncos can force the Chiefs into playing their brand of football and turn this into a closely contested, defense-oriented matchup, that's where things could get dicey for KC.

title: 3 Wide Receivers on the Block the Kansas City Chiefs Should Consider Trading For
full_text:
Between injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton and a lack of pass-catching depth , the Kansas City Chiefs' receiving corps has been a nightmare in 2026.
KC's offense had been able to manufacture enough points on the board to win games the first five weeks, but that positive momentum came to a screeching halt last week against the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs scored just three points and were stifled all night by the reigning champions, exposing glaringly obvious flaws that need to be addressed. With the NFL trade deadline looming on Nov. 10, time is running out for the Chiefs to make a deal and bolster their aerial attack. Unless it comes in the form of a free agent signing in Tyreek Hill , the only way Andy Reid's offense can realistically improve through the air is via a trade.
It's the time of the year when fans dream about ambitious trades that seem too good to be true. Here are a trio of players that could land in Kansas City ahead of its playoff push.
Following his 1,287-yard, 10-touchdown Pro Bowl rookie season, everything has gone downhill for Thomas since. He's become the subject of heavy trade rumors amid his ongoing decline.
The Jaguars have tried to make things work with the former LSU star, but they simply haven't found a way to get him involved. He's gone consecutive games without a catch and has three receptions in the past four contests.
A 6-foot-2, 209-pound wideout, Thomas has blazing speed in the open field and could serve as a boundary target for Patrick Mahomes with his vast catch radius. We've had him circled as a potential buy-low Chiefs trade candidate since before the 2026 campaign began, and his value won't be any lower than it is right now. By no means am I advocating for the Chiefs to pursue Thomas, though. He wouldn't necessarily be a "dumpster-dive" move per se given his younger age and the draft capital the Jags invested, but the days of him being touted as a future top-tier receiver are numbered. Additionally, Kansas City would have to convince Jacksonville to send a 24-year-old former first-round pick to a receiver-needy team they could face in the AFC Playoffs, something they'd likely be reluctant to do.
In the realm of realistic trade options, Downs probably tops the list. He has openly requested a trade out of Indianapolis and shouldn't command too steep of an asking price since he will be an unrestricted free agent this offseason. Downs' numbers this year are modest (26 receptions, 307 yards), but the advanced metrics tell a different story. He is elite at creating separation out of the slot and is one of the best pure route-runners at his position. In the Colts' Week 2 overtime loss to the Chiefs, Downs auditioned against his potential future team with a seven-catch, 72-yard outing.
Josh Downs Route Running. pic.twitter.com/nDEwFDKnUq
While Rice receives plenty of action in the slot, adding Downs to the mix would allow Eric Bieniemy to diversify his concepts. The Chiefs lack man-beaters who can consistently win one-on-one matchups in open space, and Downs would fix that problem.
He certainly wouldn't be a name that KC supporters swoon over, but Downs would be a significant upgrade over what they are currently working with. After shipping Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner out of town earlier this week, it's only a matter of time before Indy sends Downs elsewhere.
If Brett Veach wants to go all in and make one of the biggest splashes in recent Chiefs trade memory, he needs to acquire Jets wideout Garrett Wilson. Of all the receivers seemingly on the trade block, there is no doubt that Wilson is far and away the most coveted.
A three-time 1,000-yard receiver, Wilson is in his fifth season with the franchise. As he noted earlier this week in a press conference, he loves playing in New York but doesn't love it as much as winning. He'd certainly have a better chance at competing for a Super Bowl in Kansas City catching passes from a future first-ballot Hall of Famer.
"Yeah, I want to be here. I want to win games. That's the one thing we've been missing on here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest. But I'm hopeful." - Garrett Wilson https://t.co/K8XI58FqwA pic.twitter.com/Cw79Ip03gg
The Ohio State product is a true No. 1 target and has shifted more toward a primary X receiver role after often playing in the slot in past years. Regardless of where he would line up in KC, he'd undoubtedly rank among the most dynamic weapons the Chiefs have had in the 21st century.
The asking price to land a player of Wilson's caliber — let alone one with team control until 2030 — would be otherworldly and quite uncharacteristic for Veach . But if this front office is hell-bent on making a push for another Super Bowl and maximizing its championship window, it's at least worth checking in with the Jets to see whether there's any room for negotiation.

title: Peter Woods Sees Something Special Brewing Between Chiefs’ Young Defensive Stars
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs went all in on their defensive unit during the 2026 NFL Draft, selecting defensive players with all of their top three picks. General manager Brett Veach was determined to reload and pave the way for a new generation of defenders to take over.
The crown jewel of KC's draft class was LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane, who was the franchise's earliest-ever selection on a corner. Despite battling a shoulder injury that has bothered him since the Chiefs' minicamp in June, Delane has been highly effective and shown promising traits when he's been on the field.
In last week's loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday Night Football , Delane did experience some "welcome to the NFL" moments when squaring off with Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He didn't line up with him every rep of the night and held his own at times, but JSN was certainly the toughest challenge Delane has faced in his young NFL career. The Seahawks' superstar finished the contest with 150 yards and a touchdown. Regardless of his showing last game, fellow first-round rookie Peter Woods — who was selected 23 picks after Delane at No. 29 — remains fully confident in his defensive counterpart. During his media appearance on Friday , the rookie defensive lineman discussed why he has so much faith in Delane and what the two can become as they continue to develop together.
"I'm always there for him. He's a tremendous player," Woods said about his teammate. "I trust him with the backside of me because that's what he does. I'm ready to see him continue to blossom and bloom into the player he's going to be, as well as myself. We're doing that together since we came in together."
Admittedly, it has been a quiet first six games for the Clemson product to this point. Woods has played 46.3% of the defense's snaps while rotating with Khyiris Tonga on the inside, but it hasn't resulted in much production. He currently has three solo tackles, two QB pressures, and half a sack across 190 defensive reps.
#Chiefs DT Peter Woods describes what he's learned about the Broncos rivalry. He tells @Leabonics , "If I'm being honest, I don't really like none of the teams that we play." pic.twitter.com/ZedqlfseI7
It's always difficult to judge interior linemen by statistics in a limited sample size, but Pro Football Focus grades echo this sentiment, too. Woods' 50.8 defensive grade ranks No. 96 out of 126 qualifying defensive tackles in the league, and his 43.4 run defense grade is one of the NFL's worst marks.
Even with Woods' early struggles, he has plenty to learn from veterans like Chris Jones . He talked about how he and the rest of the defensive linemen have responded after the rookie suffered his first NFL defeat. "It was rather interesting being in the locker room and listening to some of the things the leaders were reiterating about getting back on track and getting hit in the mouth and figuring out what we can do to be better," Woods stated. "I think one of the older guys gave me advice that whenever you lose a game, that's when you should look in your personal mirror most and figure out how you can benefit the team to get a win."
No matter how you spin it, Woods has been a defensive staple on a 5-1 Chiefs group at just 21 years old. As he and Delane get better and gain more experience, they could both be forces to be reckoned with for years to come.

title: Major Chiefs and Broncos Injuries Could Change the Trajectory of the AFC West
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will have an important AFC West showdown on Sunday afternoon, but both teams are approaching game day with significant and potentially game-changing injury unknowns.
After being a full participant on Wednesday, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday or Friday. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed that the issue is with the same shoulder that limited Delane during training camp and preseason activities before knocking him out early in Week 1 and sidelining him through Week 2.
Delane has played nearly every defensive snap in the Chiefs' games since Week 3, including a full 100% workload last weekend in Seattle. Reid said that the team would "just see how he does here going forward." Delane was later ruled questionable, implying that he could be a true game-time decision.
Veteran cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) was limited on Friday and is also questionable for Sunday's game, as is rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas. However, Reid clarified that Thomas missed Friday's practice due to a personal issue and said that he would be at the game on Sunday.
"He'll meet us there in Denver," Reid said.
The best news from the Chiefs' game day designations relates to wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee), who was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before participating fully during Friday's practice. Rice was given no designation for Sunday's game, meaning that he is expected to suit up in Denver.
Rice hasn't seen the field since suffering a hamstring injury against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4.
Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) participated fully on Friday and received no designation after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) was a full participant all week and also received no designation.
The only fully negative news on the Chiefs' Friday injury report is unsurprising: defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott won't play, as expected, as he works back from his ACL recovery .
Meanwhile, in Denver, the questions continue, with a pair of absences now confirmed .
The Broncos ruled out safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and running back RJ Harvey (knee), dealing a blow to each side of the ball.
Harvey is a pass-catching back who is Denver's second-leading receiver on the season, while Hufanga has two interceptions and a forced fumble in the five games he's played this year.
Defensive tackle Zach Allen (hamstring) is questionable after missing Wednesday's practice and being limited on Thursday and Friday, while wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) is also questionable after the same practice schedule.
Tackle Garrett Bolles (hip) was limited all week but was also ruled questionable for Sunday's game. On the other end of the spectrum, star Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) was a full participant throughout the team's week of practice and was given no game day designation, meaning he should make his return on Sunday.
Allen, Waddle, and Bolles are all vitally important players for Denver, with Allen operating as the keystone of the Broncos' defensive line. Waddle leads the Broncos in catches and receiving yards, while Bolles has played every offensive snap of the season so far while protecting Bo Nix's blind side.
If any of those three players can't suit up on Sunday, the Broncos could be left significantly shorthanded. If they do play, the health of Rice and Delane will become even more noteworthy for Kansas City.

title: Patrick Mahomes Voices Thoughts on Josh Simmons Situation; Optimistic About 2026 Return
full_text:
One of the more concerning storylines in what has otherwise been a strong 5-1 start to the season for the Kansas City Chiefs has been Josh Simmons' back injury. A bulging disc in his lower back has kept the left tackle off the field the entire campaign, and the team placed him on Injured Reserve last week after his recovery stalled despite a brief return to practice in limited capacity.
Up until a few days ago, there was still optimism around the fanbase regarding Simmons' situation, as the training staff reportedly doesn't believe he'll need surgery for his injury and thinks he can heal with rest. However, the perception of Simmons took a turn for the worse when Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport revealed a dispute that went down in practice. According to the report, Simmons was in a team meeting with his feet propped up. Head coach Andy Reid took exception to this, and so did quarterback Patrick Mahomes. The superstar signal-caller allegedly asked Simmons to put his feet down and told him to leave the meeting in order to get treatment.
The latest development was bound to come up when the two-time MVP spoke to the media on Wednesday. He didn't directly confirm or deny the details of the exchange, but acknowledged that difficult conversations had taken place and that the team needs to do a better job of keeping those things in-house moving forward.
"Stuff like that doesn't really bother because I'm so in the moment. I think we've had the right conversations now," Mahomes stated. "We're moving in the direction. You have to have hard conversations at some point... We've built this culture of coming together as a family, and kind of doing whatever we can to make sure that not only the player but also the person is going in the right direction. You want to keep those conversations in the building, and so that's something we'll be better at moving forward."
Patrick Mahomes was asked about the story that came out Sunday morning between him and Josh Simmons. He told @Leabonics , "You have to be able to have tough conversations so that you can have better conversations going forward." pic.twitter.com/95NrEXWX4d
Rather than a hostile back-and-forth, Mahomes insisted that this was more of an open dialogue typical of the culture Reid has built throughout his years as head coach. He made sure to clarify that there was nothing malicious about the altercation and that things like that happen fairly often in the locker room.
Mahomes' outlook is far different from the one some Chiefs fans have taken amid the growing uncertainty surrounding Simmons. With the former first-round pick yet to play this season and now facing at least four more games on IR, questions about his future in Kansas City have grown. KCSN's very own Tucker Franklin and Matt Verderame recently pondered whether Simmons has played his final game in the red and gold. That isn't the perspective Mahomes has, though. He remains steadfast in his belief that Simmons has been working hard during this recovery process and will be back to help the team at some point.
"I'm extremely confident because I've seen the work he puts in," Mahomes said, according to 96.5 The Fan . "He's doing his rehab, he's doing his work, he's doing everything he can to be back on that field. He'll have a couple weeks here now while he's on IR where he can get himself back to the physical shape that he can be in. He'll be mentally confident to go out there and be the best version of himself, when he's able to do that, he'll be back on the football field."
Much has been said about the situation, and it certainly hasn't been a good look for the Chiefs. They invested a first-round pick in Simmons in last year's draft, and he was solid when he played across his eight starts as a rookie. However, he dealt with personal issues and a wrist injury that forced him to miss extended time, and it's starting to feel like his absence in 2026 is for something beyond football as well. In the meantime, undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has been filling in at left tackle . He's stepped into a difficult role early in his career, but Simmons was drafted to help protect Mahomes for years to come. It is no secret that the Chiefs' best version of themselves includes Simmons on the blind side of KC's franchise cornerstone.
The public narrative surrounding Simmons has become increasingly negative, which is why Mahomes made sure to tread carefully with his words. While his comments don't put to rest the rumors about the tackle's long-term future in Kansas City, they do shed light on how Mahomes saw things through his own lens.

title: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes React to Chiefs’ Controversial Justin Tucker Signing
full_text:
Amid Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker's ongoing struggles, the franchise made a surprising move this morning by signing Justin Tucker to the practice squad . The former Baltimore Ravens standout hasn't kicked in the NFL since the 2024 season after serving a suspension for violating the league's Personal Conduct Policy.
Many Kansas City fans thought it was well overdue for the team to bring someone in to make Butker's job less secure. However, the signing has already faced significant backlash from the media. He was cut by Baltimore in May 2025 due to a combination of his declining performance and the allegations of sexual misconduct involving 16 massage therapists . When head coach Andy Reid stepped to the podium for his press conference today , he fielded questions about Tucker for approximately five consecutive minutes. One of the more notable questions he faced was about the message Tucker's signing sends to female Chiefs fans.
"He's done his suspension. Took care of that business there," Reid responded. "I'll leave it at that for you."
Reid emphasized that he and the front office had done extensive homework on Tucker's past before they decided to offer him a spot on the practice squad. He wouldn't quite elaborate on what this "homework" entailed, but insisted the team had spoken with multiple people before making its decision.
"We try to do our homework the best way we possibly can," Reid said. "Talked to a lot of people to make sure things are okay." KC's head coach said that the team brought in three kickers earlier this week to try out for a spot. Reid believes that Tucker was the best of the bunch by a long shot. He wasn't exactly effective in his last full season when he finished with a subpar 73.3% field goal percentage (22-for-30), and it's been a while since he's kicked in live action.
If there's anything this signing does, it makes it clear that Butker's future with the team is no longer guaranteed. He's cost the Chiefs too many points in recent years for this situation to be ignored any longer. Since the start of the 2025 campaign, Butker's 15 missed kicks and extra points are the most of any player in the NFL.
Even after bringing Tucker on board, Reid maintains that he is still confident in his longtime placekicker and believes Butker's recent shortcomings stem from inconsistent form and technique rather than a mental issue. "Listen, we love Harrison. I've told you before, he's one of my favorite guys," he said about Butker. "Sometimes, things don't go quite the way you want them, and you work on that. He understands the business and how it works. We had a practice squad position open, so for security, we brought [Tucker] in and put him in that spot. Butker gets it and he knows that's part of the business."
He also confirmed that the "up-and-down" Butker will receive most of the first-team reps in remaining practices leading up to the Broncos game and that he should be the only kicker active this Sunday.
Coincidentally, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and Tucker have a history that goes beyond their time spent on opposing sidelines. The two (and Travis Kelce) were famously involved in a brief pregame confrontation over warm-up space in the 2024 AFC Championship Game, where KC would advance to Super Bowl LVIII in a 17-10 victory.
While there appeared to be bad blood between the two parties at the time, Mahomes chalked it up to competition and brushed the tension aside. "We haven't had a lot of conversations because he was on the Ravens, but it wasn't like we ever had any beef," Mahomes confirmed today. "At that moment, it was just competitors being competitors. He's been a big-time kicker for a long time... At the end of the day, we're just playing a game, and you want to compete and win."
Mahomes, who has always done an excellent job avoiding controversial answers to the media, wouldn't go in-depth on his thoughts about Tucker's signing and reaffirmed his trust in the front office. "We have a lot people that have been added in and out," Mahomes stated. "I try not go get too high or low or anything. I know [Brett] Veach does a great job of bringing players in."
There was always going to be an uproar over the Chiefs signing a shunned player whose NFL career appeared to be all but over. We'll soon find out whether Tucker is ever elevated to the 53-man roster and if he'll be an outside distraction moving forward.

title: The End of the Road: Latest Roster Moves Signal Multiple Chargers Done for the Year
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are set to take on the Los Angeles Rams in week eight. The Chargers, coming off a bye in week seven, have dealt with significant injuries in the first half of the season and had over half of the original 53-man roster on the injury report or injured reserve by week six.
Los Angeles will see some limited reinforcements return to the field against the Rams but the injuries have continued to mount and several have suffered setbacks. The most notable setbacks have been to team leader and All-Pro defensive back Derwin James Jr. and to rookie wide receiver Brenan Thompson.
full game status for week 8 at LAR pic.twitter.com/kRgRS940zR
James was placed on injured reserve on the eve of the game against the Rams and Thompson, out since week two, tried to return in week five only to suffer a setback, was surprisingly active for week six but logged zero snaps and now has suffered another setback in rehab with a hamstring injury being added on to his quad injury.
The Chargers decision to move Derwin James to injured reserve is peculiar in timing considering he has been out since Week 3. The NFL rules stipulate that teams are allowed eight activations from the injured list per season and two additional activations for the postseason. The Chargers do not appear to be poised to make the postseason therefore they have a maximum of eight activations off of injured reserve and have already used three of them.
Los Angeles has already activated offensive lineman Branson Taylor and fullback/tight end Scott Matlock, both of whom were placed on injured reserve to start the season. In addition to Taylor and Matlock, the Chargers activated wide receiver Keandre Lambert-Smith.
James being added to injured reserve now leaves the Chargers with eight players from their original 53-man roster on injured reserve with only five activations remaining. Of those eight players six were considered starters. Tyler Biadasz is clearly done for the season but of the other players, who has played their last snaps for the 2026 Chargers? •	Defensive back Derwin James Jr. •	Fullback Alec Ingold •	Offensive lineman Trey Pipkins III •	Linebacker Denzel Perryman •	Quarterback Trey Lance •	Offensive lineman Trevor Penning •	Tight end David Njoku •	Tackle Rashawn Slater
There are so many unanswered questions with this group of players. If the season is lost, is it worth it to rush Rashawn Slater, who is already coming off major injury, back onto the field? Derwin James is a cornerstone player. Alec Ingold was intended to be the glue of the blocking department but did not look good when healthy. Pipkins and Penning have essentially been replaced by rookies.
The Chargers are only entering Week 8, there is no telling how many more players will end up on injured reserve. Who Los Angeles brings back to the active roster with their five remaining activations will be a major chess move for the remainder of the season and likely an indication of intentions for the upcoming offseason.
Not only could several of these players have played their last snaps for the 2026 Chargers, several of them are on expiring deals or deals with a contract out in the offseason. There is a high likelihood that several of these players on injured reserve have played their last snaps in Los Angeles.

title: Chargers Confidence Meter: A Win Against the Rams Could Mean A Lot For Their Future
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have an opportunity to finally secure a win and silence a small portion of doubt. A matchup against the Los Angeles Rams could have a much bigger impact on how the rest of their season unfolds.
Especially when it comes to the team’s confidence , playoff outlook, and even their future draft position.
For the Chargers, this is the type of game that can help determine what kind of team they really are. Facing another competitive team gives them an opportunity to prove they can put together a complete performance when it matters.
One of the biggest things the Chargers need to focus on is establishing consistency on both sides of the football. Offensively, they need to give Herbert opportunities to make plays without putting the entire responsibility on his shoulders. Establishing the run game, protecting the quarterback, and finding ways to create explosive plays will be important against a Rams defense that can make things difficult.
Defensively, the Chargers cannot afford to let the Rams dictate the pace of the game. Getting pressure on the quarterback, limiting explosive plays, and forcing difficult third-down situations could make a significant difference. Games like this are often decided by which team makes fewer mistakes. The Bolts are dealing with secondary issues, so that certainly does not help. Defensive Coordinator Chris O’Leary has a great scheme and should be able to adjust to the situation regardless.
However there is one main caveat.
If the Chargers continue winning games, their position in the upcoming draft could change significantly. While a better draft position can give a rebuilding team access to higher selections. They are in a position where competing and building momentum should be the priority. Winning games can also help the organization evaluate its current roster and identify which positions actually need attention when draft season arrives.
There is always a balance between winning now and building for the future. The Chargers want to be a team competing for championships, and getting meaningful wins against quality opponents is part of that process. A victory over the Rams would not automatically solve every issue surrounding the team, but it could provide another reason to believe in what this roster is capable of accomplishing.
This is bigger than just another game on the schedule.
The Chargers have an opportunity to make a statement, build confidence, and give themselves something to carry into the second half of the season. Now they have to go out and prove it.

title: NFL Trade Rumors Say Chargers’ Weird Behavior Confuses Other Teams, Too
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers entered this season looking a little lost and confused and have wound up confusing their own fanbase with their approach to the NFL trade deadline , too.
Now…the Chargers are confusing other teams at the deadline, too.
All of the rumors and buzz and speculation so far around the NFL trade deadline have made it clear that the Chargers, in fact, are not looking to sell off any pieces despite sitting at 0-6 and first in the NFL draft order.
That, while not choosing to make any changes over a bye week with names like offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.
Now, the rumor mill is even reporting about the confusion other teams have about the confusing Chargers.
The Chargers aren’t selling.
That much has been obvious. But here’s a fun follow-up from The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones : “The Chargers have confounded teams by not engaging in trade talks. The Bolts are 0-6 but are telling teams Khalil Mack isn’t available. It’s hard to envision that remaining the case over the next 10 days.”
Things are so weird around the Chargers that they’re confounding other teams.
Here’s where there is an actual concern. It’s one thing to publicly posture like a team won’t sell. No need for the negative PR or to hint to the locker room that this is a lost cause and the franchise is waving a white flag. Plenty of teams act like this in public but still talk the trade talk behind the scenes and off the record.
The fact the Chargers have other teams shocked with how they’re moving behind the scenes feels problematic, though. If they’re shutting down any and all trade talk, even off the record, it concerningly matches their lack of change in the face of problems at 0-6.
The Chargers can’t afford to sit still and do nothing . They have one of, if not the worst, rosters in football. They’re sitting on cap space they won’t spend and also hoarding trade assets like Khalil Mack who, frankly, deserves to go to a better organization.
Selling off at 0-6 clears the books, adds future assets, clears more playing time for younger players and boosts the odds of landing the No. 1 pick. Remaining this adamant about not selling, to the point other teams are a little surprised about how they’re moving, is perhaps the most damning thing about the Chargers in 2026.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Don't Give Up On Omarion Hampton Just Yet
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have an important matchup ahead of them in Week 8 as they prepare to take on the Los Angeles Rams.
For fantasy football managers, there are a handful of Chargers players worth keeping an eye on.
However, some options are considerably more appealing than others . Here’s a look at five Chargers players and whether they deserve a spot in your starting lineup this week.
Omarion Hampton remains one of the more interesting fantasy options on this Chargers offense. Through six games, Hampton has recorded 289 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 80 carries.
The biggest concern has been his efficiency, averaging just 3.6 yards per carry. Still, his workload gives him opportunities to produce, especially if the Chargers can establish their running game early.
Hampton isn’t necessarily somebody I would consider an automatic start, but his touchdown potential makes him worth keeping in consideration. I’d feel comfortable using him as a flex option this week.
Justin Herbert is usually a quarterback fantasy managers don’t have to think twice about starting. Unfortunately, his performance through the first six games has made that decision a little more complicated.
Herbert has thrown for 1,141 yards with five touchdowns and eight interceptions. Those numbers are nowhere near what fantasy managers expected coming into the season. The Chargers have struggled to find consistency offensively, and Herbert has been unable to produce the type of numbers that make him a dependable fantasy option. Until things start turning around, I’d look at other quarterback options this week.
Ladd McConkey is an interesting option heading into this matchup, especially with his return to the lineup after suffering a concussion.
McConkey has recorded 200 receiving yards and a touchdown this season. His ability to create separation and give Herbert a reliable option underneath makes him an important part of this offense.
However, staying healthy has been a challenge, and the Rams aren’t exactly an easy matchup for opposing receivers. I wouldn’t expect a huge performance immediately, but McConkey is worth considering as a flex option for managers who need help at wide receiver.
Quentin Johnston has shown that he can make big plays, but his involvement in the Chargers offense has been difficult to predict.
He’s recorded 165 receiving yards on eight receptions, averaging an impressive 20.6 yards per catch. The problem is that his opportunities have been limited, making it difficult to trust him on a weekly basis. With Ladd McConkey and Tre’ Harris also available, Johnston could have some competition for targets. He’s capable of making an impact, but I’d rather wait for more consistent involvement before putting him into my starting lineup.
Oronde Gadsden II has shown some promise this season, recording 12 receptions for 103 yards and a touchdown. While those numbers aren’t particularly eye-catching, he has shown that he can contribute when given opportunities.
The biggest question is how consistent his involvement will be moving forward. With Charlie Kolar also in the tight end rotation, Gadsden isn’t necessarily guaranteed the kind of workload fantasy managers need.

title: Why Did The Chargers Opt to Not Fire Mike McDaniel During the Bye Week?
full_text:
Now that the Los Angeles Chargers are heading into Week 8 refreshed from their bye week, it is expected that most teams will come out firing on all cylinders after their week off. However, as a winless team, the Bolts were expected to make drastic coaching-related moves , considering how poor the season has gone.
The team opted to keep everything the same. So that begs the question: why did the Chargers opt to keep Mike McDaniel? Even with the perfect opportunity to fire him?
The Chargers have seemingly always been cursed with poor injury luck and an inability to stay healthy over the course of an NFL season. This year has been more of the same, but coming off their BYE, the team is finding some players back from injury, hopefully giving much-needed 'juice' to one of the league's worst offenses.
Tre Harris, Ladd McConkey, Joe Alt and Branson Taylor are all players who are expected to start (or play an important depth role in Taylor's case) and improve this offense. With the team sputtering early, it could be easy to blame injuries and give McDaniel some more time with an offense that is less banged up.
The Athletic's Chargers beat reporter, Noah Furtado, recently wrote a very insightful article about McDaniel's offense and the learning curve involved with perfecting such a complicated scheme. He interviews players like Daniel Brunskill and Jake Browning as guys who are familiar with the concepts, with both of those individuals giving detail into the complexities and the time it takes to get used to then.
Brunskill, in Furtado's article, mentions: “That takes a little while to get used to, how to run, because when you run you don’t really have a base,” he said. “It took a season. I mean, you learn it by camp and you can run it, but you’re still kind of learning all the ins and outs of it. … The thing with this offense is … that run off the ball is something that you just have to be doing all the time to really get it down.”
With such a complex scheme, could it be possible for the Bolts to liken to the side of patience and give McDaniel and his offense more time to gel?
When someone gets fired, the team obviously needs someone else on staff to take on that role. With head coach Jim Harbaugh never having called plays before, it will fall on someone else in the building. The question would be, who?
The first name that comes most is Adam Gase, former Dolphins and Jets head coach, known for colossal failures during his time as such. His claim to fame is his time as the Broncos' offensive coordinator, helping late-career Peyton Manning achieve success.
Another name could be Shane Day, the Chargers' QB Coach / Passing Game Coordinator. Justin Herbert loves Day, giving an easy path to offensive chemistry, while possibly also giving Herbert some extra 'want' to stick around, considering the team would obviously be doing so to keep him happy.
Even with those two options, it is hard to believe that any of them would be viable candidates to improve the offense, with Day never calling plays at the NFL or college level and Gase not having a strong resume as someone who can make a functional NFL offense in recent memory.
The final part of the equation is McDaniel's contract. It is unknown how much he is being paid, but it is safe to assume that the Chargers spent a pretty penny to get him as their offensive coordinator. He was highly sought after , and usually in those cases, the highest bidder wins.
That said, the Chargers are known as a very "cash-rich" team, making it more difficult to make decisions that require essentially wasting money on coaching.
Overall, it is in everyone's best interest for McDaniel to turn things around. Hopefully, with this belief in him post-bye week, it actually happens.

title: If Mike McDaniel Still has Smashmouth Football in Him, Now is the Time for Chargers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 and their offense has looked lost the entire season. Los Angeles has dealt with significant injuries all season with over half of their initial 53-man roster either on injured reserve or the injury report for week six.
Los Angeles' injury luck started when starting center Tyler Biadasz went down with a significant season-ending knee injury during a joint practice with the 49ers during training camp. The Chargers were forced to shuffle the offensive line with the season less than three weeks away and plug in rookie Jake Slaughter as the new starting center.
The injury to Biadasz seems to have been the catalyst for the wheels falling off of the offense's wagon. We never got to see Biadasz in game action, he did not play any snaps in the first preseason game and was injured before the second. But the reports from that joint practice, before the injury were that the Chargers offense was handily beating up the 49ers. The reports made sense coming on the heels of the Chargers backups physically dominating the Houston Texans in the first preseason game.
"The Chargers, they out-physicaled us the entire game."- Texans head coach Demeco Ryans pic.twitter.com/6Sh456WY3q
Biadasz' going down seems to have been the one injury that the offense and offensive line could not have survived, which raises more questions about roster construction and the interior offensive line as a whole. Regardless, the interior offensive line has not been good. Unfortunately, the injury bug did not stop with the line and attacked the wide receiver room as well.
The Chargers' original six wide receivers have all dealt with injuries this season. Not one of the six has played fully healthy every week and the lack of reps and continuity has ruined the timing of the offense. The disruption in timing paired with a run game that has not been a strong point and consistent interior pressure is largely how the Chargers still have not found their groove on offense.
The past two games before the bye in week seven featured four rookie starting offensive linemen. The Chargers will get Joe Alt back this week at one of the tackle spots, assuming he takes his right tackle spot back. it is possible that second-year lineman Branson Taylor figures somewhere into the lineup but if the lineup remains the same with the exception of Alt's return, the Chargers will still be starting three rookies on the offensive line, the entire left side of the line.
The Chargers rookie offensive linemen have played better than was expected but still have their rookie shortcomings. The good news is tackle Travis Burke and guard Logan Taylor are very capable run blockers. Burke is a mountain of an offensive lineman and generates significant movement at the point of attack. Note Burke's run-blocking grade on the chart below.
OT Percentile Grades in Pass & Run Blocking pic.twitter.com/Qti6mB1CT4
The strengths of the rookies could be the key to getting the Chargers back on track offensively, or at least help them find some sort of rhythm. Los Angeles will be getting some limited reinforcements back as wide receiver Ladd McConkey and Tre Harris are both scheduled to make their returns to the fields this week against the Rams. Tight end Charlie Kolar and wide receiver Quintin Johnston both emergeed from the bye without injury designations.
The question will be how does Mike McDaniel and the Chargers adjust following the bye week? Does McDaniel have any downhill smashmouth football left in his arsenal? The Chargers rushing attack has been much more successful to the left side and between the tackles. Compared to a similar offensive system in San Francisco, the Chargers run the ball between the tackles almost 20 percent less.
Based on EPA or expected points added by personnel groupings, the Chargers most efficient run formations are in 13 personnel lining up with a running back and three tight ends followed closely by  22 personnel featuring two tight ends and a fullback.
The Chargers should line up with Charlie Kolar, Hayden Rucci and Scott Matlock on the field and run right behind Travis Burke or Joe Alt, both of whom have comparable run blocking grades.
The Rams run dime personnel packages on defense nearly 50 percent of the time, meaning they have extra defensive backs on the field and create pressure by rotating and sending different players to the line of scrimmage. If they want to give the Chargers lighter defensive personnel packages, the Chargers should lean into what strengths they have.
The Rams sent most of their starting defensive line to injured reserve. They still have Aaron Donald and he can still wreck an offensive line's gameplan but Myles Garrett will not be back yet so the focus can be on Donald.
The offense under Mike McDaniel has not gone smoothly. There is blame to go around to every corner of the team and organization. But, if the Chargers and McDaniel found positives to lean into coming out the bye, now is the time to implement them.
Based on the available personnel and data from first six weeks, ditching the higher frequency of outside zone in favor of more inside zone or gap runs may be beneficial. It does go against the Miami version of McDaniel, can he tap into his Shanahan roots as a playcaller against the Rams?

title: NFL Trade Rumors Update Tells Unfortunate Story About Jim Harbaugh's Chargers
full_text:
It feels like a matter of time before the Los Angeles Chargers host a fire sale at the NFL trade deadline .
Nobody told Jim Harbaugh, Joe Hortiz or the Chargers, though.
Despite the stubbornness coming out of Los Angeles right now , everyone seems to agree that the Chargers will trade Khalil Mack before the deadline.
Not as likely, though just as smart, would be the Chargers trading away Quentin Johnston, getting anything in return for the obvious-feeling departure for the former first-round pick in the near future.
But exiting the bye, the Chargers have kept the messaging as positive and simple as possible despite the 0-6 record. Little is changing, and they still aren’t selling.
The Chargers might be so bad that they clutch the No. 1 pick in a year when even the Tennessee Titans are having a “down” year. They might clutch the No. 1 pick so strongly that even the “tank bowl” against Miami later this year has become less important.
But the Chargers aren’t selling yet.
So says the latest NFL trade rumors update from Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer .
“The Chargers have shut down trade inquiries for their veterans, even as the team sits at 0–6,” Breer wrote. “So while there are questions about guys like Khalil Mack and Quentin Johnston, for now, GM Joe Hortiz and coach Jim Harbaugh appear unwilling to wave any sort of white flag.”
If nothing else, this is just more reinforcement that Mack and Johnston remain the most appealing and obvious Chargers trade candidates.
At wideout, trading Ladd McConkey isn’t realistic. He’s the centerpiece of a depth chart rebuild there. They need to see more reps for guys like Tre Harris.
And on the defensive edge, letting go of Tuli Tuipulotu instead would only make sense if contract extension talks have gone absolutely nuclear. Mack leaving would mean more work for first-rounder Akheem Mesidor and others.
Other than that…the Chargers don’t really have any trade candidates. There’s a depth cornerback here or there that might interest other teams. Maybe a depth running back. But this…sort of speaks to just how bad the roster is, right?
The Chargers will change this tune ahead of the deadline. Falling to 0-7 after a date with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday is the next one to circle in red on the calendar.
