title: 3 Eagles Offseason Decisions Have Come Back to Haunt Them by Halloween
full_text:
Things haven't gone the Philadelphia Eagles' way during the 2026 NFL season. The team has been completely decimated by injury issues, and they've also been plagued by some questionable decisions that were made by the organization over the offseason.
In honor of Halloween, let's look back at three offseason decisions that have already come back to haunt the Eagles this season.
Philadelphia's decision to trade for , and immediately extend, linebacker Jonathan Greenard on a four-year, $98 million deal back in April has aged like milk. Greenard has been a complete non-factor for Philadelphia so far this season, in part because of injury issues and partly because of poor play.
Greenard has appeared in four games for Philly thus far and tallied just one tackle, one QB hit and one forced fumble. That's certainly not the production that you would expect from a player making as much as Greenard.
In fairness, the entire defense has struggled throughout the season, so it's tough to single out a specific player, but the Eagles had high hopes for Greenard when they signed him, and he certainly hasn't lived up to them thus far. It's safe to say that the organization might have a bit of buyer's remorse at this point.
Linebacker Nakobe Dean is having a stellar season in his first year as a member of the Las Vegas Raiders. Here's a quick summary of Dean's productive play as of late from CBS Sports :
"Dean is in the midst of a standout season, as he's recorded double-digit stops in four of his past five games and is tied for third in the NFL with 68 tackles through seven contests."
Dean has done a bit of everything for the Raiders' defense. Meanwhile, the Eagles sorely miss Dean's production on the field, as their linebacking corps has been struggling with consistency issues all season.
As an organization, you can't pay everyone. But, Dean was a player that the Eagles drafted and developed, and then they let him leave. That decision could continue to haunt Philadelphia.
The Eagles had a ton of options, and a ton of needs, when it came to their second-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. They opted to use that pick on tight end Eli Stowers from Vanderbilt, and thus far that decision hasn't paid off. Stowers has appeared in just one game for Philadelphia on the current campaign and he hasn't recorded a single reception.
It remains to be seen if the Stowers pick will ultimately pay off. Perhaps he'll eventually be the team's succession plan for Dallas Goedert. But it's tough to look at all of the needs on Philadelphia's roster this season and not think that their second round pick could have been better utilized elsewhere other than on Stowers.

title: 3-Step Guide to What a Successful Eagles Trade Deadline Should Look Like for Howie Roseman
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles haven't been winning on the field, as they've dropped five straight games heading into their Week 8 matchup with the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football. But, they could still win from a strategic standpoint with some shrewd move making ahead of the NFL trade deadline next month.
Here's a look at three simple steps that Eagles general manager Howie Roseman needs to follow in order to ensure a successful trade deadline for Philadelphia.
The Eagles are a proud organization. They have been arguably the most consistently competitive team in the NFC since the turn of the century. This isn't an organization that is going to throw in the towel a single second before it has to.
But as an organization, the Eagles also pride themselves on being forward-thinking, and sometimes you just have to embrace the reality that's right in front of you. The Eagles aren't going to win the Super Bowl this year. It would take a miraculous turnaround, the likes of which has probably never been seen before in the league. It's just not their year, as injuries have ravaged the team. That happens sometimes in the NFL. Roseman has to accept this fact and prioritize the team's long-term outlook, as opposed to devoting more resources to what certainly feels like a lost season.
Prioritizing the team's long-term outlook doesn't necessarily mean having a complete fire sale, however. There are plenty of players on Philadelphia's roster that Roseman should want to hold onto moving forward. After all, the Eagles have made the playoffs in five straight seasons. They don't need a complete teardown. A retooling is probably a more apt description of what they need: Keep the core building blocks on both sides of the ball and look to better complement them next season and beyond.
When it comes to who the Eagles should label as keepers, there are some no-brainers like wide receiver DeVonta Smith, cornerback Quinyon Mitchell, quarterback Jalen Hurts and defensive tackle Jalen Carter. Other players who the team should want to continue to build with could include linebacker Zack Baun, defensive tackle Jordan Davis, running back Saquon Barkley, cornerback Cooper DeJean, offensive tackle Jordan Mailata and linebacker Nolan Smith.
With keepers identified, Roseman can now move on to the final step.
Any players that Roseman doesn't see a future for in Philadelphia beyond the current campaign, he should try to flip them for draft capital and/or young players with high upside. Guys like Riq Woolen, Hollywood Brown and potentially even guard Landon Dickerson could fit the bill there. That's not necessarily an indictment of any of those guys, but if they're not going to be back with the Eagles, the team might as well try to get something in return for them.
The Eagles have several areas that they'll need to address in upcoming drafts, and the more picks they have to address those areas, the better. In my eyes, stacking some picks in exchange for guys who won't be around long-term while holding onto key contributors on both sides of the ball would be viewed as a successful trade deadline for Roseman and the Eagles.

title: 3 Potential Riq Woolen Trade Partners Could Be on Eagles' Radar in Coming Days
full_text:
Heading into the 2026 NFL trade deadline, there are plenty of hopeful contenders across the league's landscape that could use an athletic cornerback with championship experience. As a result, Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen could be a hot commodity .
" Contract-year players like Hollywood Brown, Tariq Woolen and Dallas Goedert could be had ," Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer reported about potential deadline trades on Friday.
When the Eagles signed Woolen to a one-year deal over the offseason, they expected to be in the contender conversation themselves, but things haven't quite worked out that way this season for Philadelphia. As a result, the team could be willing to part with Woolen and other veterans who likely don't have a long-term future in Philly for the right price.
Here's a look at three potential trade partners for Woolen that could pop up on the Eagles' radar leading up to the deadline.
The Steelers traded away cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys last month, and they're in the market for a replacement heading into the trade deadline. Perhaps they can work out a deal with the Eagles for Woolen.
As a contending team, the Steelers are likely looking for a player with championship and playoff experience who could slide seamlessly into the secondary. Woolen fits the bill there, as he was a member of the defensive unit that helped the Seahawks win the Super Bowl earlier this year.
Woolen could fit in nicely with the Steelers, and since he's on a one-year deal, trading for him wouldn't require a long-term commitment from Pittsburgh's front office.
The Detroit Lions were interested in trading for Porter Jr. from Pittsburgh before he was ultimately shipped to Dallas at the end of September. Head coach Dan Campbell admitted as much.
"[General manager] Brad [Holmes] was—he’s been on it for a while," Campbell said of a potential Porter Jr. trade. "And it was—that’s been ongoing, and everything's got to align right and the Cowboys did what they wanted to do. But we were very much in on it."
While the Lions didn't land Porter Jr., they're presumably still in the market for a cornerback to strengthen the secondary. In fact, according to Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press , cornerback is Detroit's most pressing need heading into the deadline. So, perhaps the Lions will call the Eagles about Woolen, who probably has a higher ceiling than some of the other options on their roster.
Like their AFC North rival in Pittsburgh, the Ravens could also be in the market for a cornerback heading into the trade deadline. The Ravens fancy themselves as a Super Bowl contender, but the secondary has been an issue for the team, and Woolen could provide them with some size and experience at the CB spot.
The Eagles don't play the Ravens this season, and Baltimore is in the opposite conference, so they wouldn't have to worry about playing against Woolen after trading him this season, unless both the Eagles and Ravens made it all the way to the Super Bowl, which seems exceedingly unlikely at this point in time.

title: Nick Sirianni Hasn't Lost One Coach's Faith Despite Eagles' 5-Game Losing Streak
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — With the Eagles mired in a five-game losing streak and a 2-5 record that mirrors their worst start under Nick Sirianni, special teams coordinator Michael Clay offered a pointed defense of his head coach’s approach, emphasizing consistency and a return to the process that fueled a 2021 turnaround.⁠
The Eagles opened the 2026 season at 2-0 before dropping five straight, including an ugly  38-21 home loss to the Cowboys on Monday night. Star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots ; Tanner McKee has taken over under center; A.J. Brown was traded in the offseason and the roster has been further depleted by attrition and the retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson.
With the season on the precipice, Philadelphia sits third in a wide-open NFC East ahead of a Sunday night prime-time road game against the Commanders .⁠
Clay, the Eagles' well-regarded special teams coordinator, was asked what stands out about Sirianni’s leadership during the skid earlier this week, and stressed that the head coach has kept a steady hand through adversity.
“Nick is the same person each and every day, regardless of if you’re 2-5 or you’re 7-0,” Clay said. “He approaches the day the same way, approaches the meetings the same way in terms of he’s not going to waver off what he truly believes in, and we’re going to back him in those scenarios and get these guys playing to an ability they know how to play."
Staying steady is not easy in a high-pressure environment like Philadelphia, which is used to success and expects it in perpetuity.
The parallel to 2021 is hard to ignore. That season, Sirianni’s first as head coach, the Eagles also sat at 2-5 before winning seven of their final 10 games to finish 9-8 and reach the playoffs. The injury situation is far more difficult this time, making a similar turnaround even more difficult.
Clay, who returned to Philadelphia on Sirianni's first staff, was asked how the staff approached the climb in 2021.
“I think it’s just doubling down on what you really believe in and selling it to the guys that this is how our process is and how we’re going to be able to dig ourselves out of it,” Clay said. “The players take pride in what they put on tape or whatever it may be, Monday, Sunday, Thursday night, whatever it is. It’s just one of those things.
"We have a great group of guys in here that are going to take some leadership roles in terms of getting everybody out of this little rut that we’re in. The most important game is the one on Sunday, more than anything else. Can’t look forward—Can’t look behind. The results are the results; you’ve got to live with them, but now you have the opportunity to change those results into a favorable way on Sunday night.”
Sirianni has struck similar notes in his own recent comments , telling reporters after the Cowboys loss that the group talked about remaining “the same version of yourself every single day” and referenced the 2021 finish as an example of growth through process rather than panic.
Sirianni has repeatedly framed the team as “results-aware but process-driven,” stressing his core values of tough, detailed, and together over reactive changes.
“Let me say it this way: to give yourself the best chance to win each week, you have to have a great process,” Sirianni said Friday when asked about his process by Eagles On SI . “That guarantees you nothing, not one thing. It doesn't guarantee you anything, but it puts you in the best position to win each and every week. You can't completely correlate that. My thing is, if we go and do everything the right way throughout the week and we end up losing the game, I can handle that.
“When our preparation isn't the way that we want it to be, or our week isn't the way we want it to be, and it can be a lot of different things. It's not just studying tape on your own time. It's not that. It's just the focus in a meeting, the focus in a practice, or anything like that by all parties. If you don't do that, which every season there's games where that happens, then you don't give yourself the best chance to win. Let me be very clear: it's not a results-based thing.
“We are very results-aware, but we are process-driven.”
Clay’s remarks arrived amid growing external scrutiny around the Eagles.
Some analysts and former players have questioned the team’s culture and Sirianni’s job security after the longest losing streak of his tenure.
Inside the building, however, the message from Clay and others is one of continuity: the daily approach does not shift with the record; the focus stays on the next game.
Whether that formula can produce another late-season surge without Hurts remains the central question heading into the Commanders matchup.
For now, Clay’s public backing underscores the staff’s bet that the same steady presence that helped right the ship five years ago can do it again.

title: 3 Biggest Eagles Priorities for Howie Roseman Ahead of Trade Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline represents a chance to switch things up . That could mean contenders addressing weaknesses by acquiring stars, or last-place squads shipping off trade chips to improve in the future. The Eagles find themselves somewhere in between with a disappointing 2-5 record.
Philadelphia General Manager Howie Roseman will face a few tough decisions. A five-game losing streak, compounded by quarterback Jalen Hurts's season-ending injury, leaves the Eagles' playoff hopes dwindling. A divisional loss to Washington in Week 8 could cement the team as a seller .
However, that doesn't mean that there should be a complete fire sale. Roseman has shown that he can quickly retool the roster to compete in the NFC East year in and year out. Here's a look at what his three biggest priorities should be ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10.
There's no way around it. The Eagles have veterans on expiring deals who could net them draft capital at the deadline. Cornerback Riq Woolen has been up and down in coverage, wide receiver Marquise Brown has barely seen the field, and tight end Dallas Goedert is 31 years old.
These aren't pros that Roseman can sell high on from a performance perspective. Instead, his biggest priority should be capitalizing on contenders' needs, similar to the Cam Jurgens trade . Baltimore was in desperate need of a center, so Roseman netted a second-round pick and a late-round pick swap.
It could be as simple as shopping Brown to an offense in need of a vertical threat or Woolen to a defense lacking depth in the secondary. Roseman has developed his reputation as a cunning negotiator for a reason. He needs to be the one making calls, not the one waiting for them to come in.
Saquon Barkley is perhaps the Eagles' biggest trade chip . The three-time Pro Bowler has rushed for over 1,000 yards in three of his last four campaigns and remains elite at making defenders miss. A nagging hamstring issue and a recent back injury have limited Barkley's impact this season , though.
Now is not the time for Roseman to drop the hammer with a Barkley trade. He's banged up and approaching 30 years old. It would be surprising to see contenders blow Howie's socks off with an offer when ball-carriers like Indianapolis' Jonathan Taylor and Tennessee's Tony Pollard are available.
This is something that goes beyond trade value. The Eagles would absorb a 2027 dead cap hit of $26 million if Barkley is dealt. There's no one waiting in the wings, either, as Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley remain on injured reserve. Barkley is a locker-room leader and remains crucial to Philly's success.
It would be short-sighted for Roseman to trade away a few veterans and call it a day. The Eagles have clear needs to address for both 2026 and beyond. Philadelphia ranks 31st in sacks per game (1.1), 27th in rushing yards per game (87.7) and 26th in opponent passing yards per game (239.9).
Philadelphia cannot afford to give away high-end draft picks to put a band-aid on a beat-up roster. Targeting under-the-radar players hidden on depth charts or stuck in unfavorable spots is the way to go. Sometimes the moves that don't cause an uproar across the NFL end up being the most impactful.
It's important to note that the Eagles aren't out of the NFC East race yet. Wins over the Commanders and Giants would put them at 4-5 heading into their bye week. Adding depth behind Barkley in the backfield or another young pass rusher on an injured defensive line could provide a crucial boost.

title: Recently Signed Eagles Will Be Key to Navigating Devastating RB Injury Situation in Week 8
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — This Eagles season can be defined by three words: Next. Man. Up.
In the running back room, those three words can be reduced to two : Apocalypse. Now.
If the situation wasn’t so serious, it would be laughable. Maybe it is, because if you’re not laughing, you might feel like crying. Not that the Eagles are doing either of those things, but when the team has three running backs on injured reserve (Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley, and Damen Pierce), another with a bad back (Saquon Barkley) and one who was waived injured (Carson Steele), well, it’s an apocalypse.
“It’s my first time really experiencing it,” center Drew Kendall said. “But I’m only in my second year.”
You could play in the NFL for a decade and not experience what the Eagles have gone through. They are down their top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks; offensive linemen have been shuffled in and out to cover for Lane Johnson’s in-season retirement , the trade of Cam Jurgens, and injuries.
But it’s the running back position that’s been ground to a pulp. Their two backs in Sunday night’s visit to the Commanders will be Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue, whom the Eagles already believe in.
“We're constantly coaching every member on the roster,” offensive coordinator Sean Mannion said. “So, when we get Elijah here, and I think it was midway through the offseason program, it's not, 'Hey, we're going to wait and get you up to speed until it's your time to be up on game day.'
“We're constantly priding ourselves on developing every member of our roster. [Running backs/assistant head coach] Jemal [Singleton] does an outstanding job with that room. I know we've had some new faces. Blue, we picked up later on. Elijah, he was here in the offseason, then away, and then back. But it's a credit to all of our position coaches, Jemal specifically with the running backs, that with some roster turnover, with guys needing to step up, they're all mentally capable of stepping in there and executing.”
Mitchell is no stranger to injury. Even as a rookie sixth-round pick of the 49ers in 2021, when he ran for 963 yards and five touchdowns in 11 games, he battled a broken finger, fractured ribs, a concussion, and a knee injury. In the following years, he dealt with MCL, groin, and hamstring strains.
He started training camp with the Eagles but was waived due to injury on Aug. 11. He was brought back to the practice squad on Oct. 20 and is now the likely starter against the Commanders.
Pressed into action last Monday night, when Pierce got hurt in the Eagles' loss to the Cowboys, Mitchell ran for 11 yards and caught three passes for 23 yards on 14 snaps.
Since the Cowboys released Blue this past summer after taking him in the fifth round of the 2025 draft, he's been on and off the Eagles’ practice squad and 53-man roster a couple of times already.
The Eagles hosted him for a top-30 visit when he entered the draft out of the University of Texas. He is expected to have an opportunity to run the ball and maybe return kicks on Sunday night due to the "Apocalypse Now" situation.
“Yeah, man, it’s part of the game—injuries happen,” Blue said. “I’m just trying to do everything I can to pick up the slack and make sure there is no drop-off.”

title: Will The Eagles Develop Buyer's Remorse With Jalen Carter?
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — The common sentiment is that Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter could, and maybe even should, be one of the NFL’s most dominant defensive players. Right now, that remains only a projection more than three years into his career and just months after Carter became the highest-paid defensive tackle in league history.
After Carter was dominated by an admittedly talented Dallas interior offensive line, it’s fair to ask whether Eagles GM Howie Roseman could eventually face buyer’s remorse. Carter failed to record a pressure, much less a sack or tackle for loss, as Cowboys guard Tyler Booker frequently drove him off the line of scrimmage. Dallas finished with 204 rushing yards, including a career-high 155 from Javonte Williams in a 38-21 victory.
"People's standards are bigger than what ours are coming into the season,” Carter said Wednesday. “We all know it's a fresh new season, it's a fresh restart no matter what we did last year, the last 3-4 years don't matter. It's a whole new season, whole new group, new faces, new chemistry in the locker room. It's a restart for us.
“We obviously know we got good players. But we don't go out there saying just because we have good players, we're going to do this on the field. It's not showing right now."
Because of his reputation in Philadelphia, some questioned Carter’s effort, overlooking how quickly the 22-year-old Booker has developed into one of the league’s better guards. Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio dismissed any lack of effort but again pointed to Carter’s week-to-week inconsistency.
“He’s just got to get the mindset to where he’ll be consistent all the time," Fangio said. " ... You just need to have the right mindset.”
Fangio has made similar comments before, but the stakes feel higher after Carter signed his four-year, $152 million extension in July. Through the Eagles’ 2-5 start, Carter has three sacks and three forced fumbles. Those numbers look acceptable for a defensive tackle on the surface, yet two sacks and two forced fumbles came in Philadelphia’s Week 5 loss to the Jaguars—the high point of his season, when he looked like the best player on the field for the first 30 minutes.
Producing at that level only 14.3% of the time underscores that Carter possesses superstar traits but remains far from being a consistent superstar. The Eagles need him to reach that level if they are to maximize their defensive ceiling and justify the organization’s massive investment.
“Not to downgrade Jacksonville or whatever, but the game plan coming throughout the week from the opponents was different. Cowboys played it smarter,” Carter said on Wednesday. “... Whatever you want to call it, and they wanted it more.
Somewhat flippantly, Carter described his performance this season as “trash.” That is not an accurate assessment, but the response reflected a laissez-faire attitude unlikely to play well in Philadelphia.
“Y’all ask me this every year, and I say trash,” Carter said when asked about his performance. “I think you asked for this last year and the year before and I gave you the same answer: Trash. Not to my expectations and I guess not to what the fans want.
“Don’t really matter what they want.”
Lost in that phrasing was Carter’s point that he is trying to meet his own standard, which he views as higher than outside expectations. He declined to speak with reporters after the Cowboys loss, then offered a more defensive explanation Wednesday when pressed on accountability.
“I don’t think I’m a public spokesperson,” Carter said. “I think y’all just want to talk to me because we’re losing.”
Accustomed to winning at Georgia and in his early Eagles career, Carter acknowledged the different atmosphere during a five-game skid, but said the setbacks are not affecting him.
“It was my first time losing,” Carter said when asked whether a 2-5 record has taken a toll on him. “So, obviously, it feels different. It’s a different atmosphere in the locker room after the game and what you guys say online and stuff like that, but it don’t affect me at all.”
For $152 million, maybe it should.

title: Steelers Without Veteran WR for Third Consecutive Week
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are trending in the right direction when it comes to many of their injured players. After head coach Mike McCarthy providing an encouraging update about the list of players on the Injured Reserve, it appears that the organization might get a dose of returning players sooner rather than later.
Despite the progress, the Steelers still have to reach deep into their depth to field a full active roster, and the injuries have impacted the lineup on both sides of the ball.
One player that has gone overlooked amongst the group of injured players is wide receiver and special teams ace Ben Skowronek. The 2025 Pro Bowler has missed two consecutive games, but returned to practice in a limited capacity during the team's Week 8 preparations.
Still, he's not quite ready to return to the lineup. After the Steelers released their inactive list for Week 8 against the Cleveland Browns, Skowronek's third straight absence became official.
One area the team needs to improve the rest of the way is across the board on special teams. The early season was a tough stretch for veteran kicker Chris Boswell, but he's settled in as the season's continued. Punter Cameron Johnston has been rock-solid as well, but the rest of the units have struggled to find consistency.
That's where the Steelers miss Skowronek the most. He made the Pro Bowl last season as a gunner on the punt team, showing just how versatile he is in those situations.
The team has found an impressive new gunner to join them in safety Robert Spears-Jennings, but they still need Skowronek's presence to bring this special teams group from concern to strength. Especially after Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter were previously ruled out of the Week 8 contest with injuries, this special teams group is in desperate need of upgrades.
This will be the third game that Johnson is elevated to the active roster from the practice squad. For that reason alone, this is a very important for Johnson personally. After this, the Steelers will either have to release him or sign him to a one-year contract that guarantees his spot on the active roster for the foreseeable future.
But Johnson hasn't shown much, aside from lining up in special teams situations. In two games so far, he's produced zero catches or plays on offense. The big-bodied receiver brings size and experience, that's undisputed, but he hasn't done much to move the needle on offense.
Quarterback Aaron Rodgers is still searching for depth options he can rely on. Johnson gets that shot, alongside fellow journeyman receiver Brandon Smith . Smith produced his first two NFL catches in Week 7, and the Steelers would love to get some offensive impact from another unexpected source.
In order for him to get that chance, he'll need to see the field just a bit more. According to data from Pro Football Reference, he's played in just 11 offensive snaps over the past two weeks.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Elandon Roberts' Chances of Returning to Steelers Lineup Dropping
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers surprised many when they released inside linebacker Elandon Roberts before the start of the regular season. A two-year starter with the organization once upon a time, many penciled him in to the 53-man roster without any debate during training camp and the preseason.
That wasn’t the case, as the Steelers moved on from Roberts before Week 1 of the regular season. But the divorce didn’t last too long, as the team signed Roberts back to the practice squad right after their Week 5 victory over the Indianapolis Colts.
Given the timing of Roberts’ return, there was reason to believe that the defense would make some changes at inside linebacker. Instead, the starting duo of Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson have been motivated by and improved by Roberts’s presence and experience.
The chances of Roberts getting a spot on the active roster moving forward continue to drop, especially after another week passes without being elevated. It might be a pipe dream for Roberts to get on the field with the Steelers, but that isn’t stopping him from making a huge impact on the middle linebacker group.
One of the key differences between this year’s team and last year’s version is the intangibles. The camaraderie in the locker room and the blend of youth and veteran leadership has played a part in this team’s 5-2 start.
Adding Roberts has only improved that facet of this year’s squad. Much like how Brock Hoffman has helped to steady rookie Max Iheanachor, Roberts has steadied Queen and Wilson.
That was never more evident than in Week 7, arguably Wilson’s best game in a Steelers uniform and a standout performance from Queen. That production was partly fueled by Roberts’ game film breakdown, and he explained on an appearance on the Deebo & Joe podcast what he shared with the rest of the linebackers room. Speaking about New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, Roberts picked up on a key bad habit that the Steelers took advantage of.
“One time, he (Shough) checked, and he didn’t even look up,” Roberts explained. “The coach talked to him the whole time. So, after 15 seconds, he’s gotta make the checks himself.”
The Steelers responded by disguising coverage until there was under 15 seconds on the play clock. That confused Shough enough times to make a difference in both the running and passing game.
Roberts didn’t record a tackle, but he made one of the biggest contributions to the defense’s win over the Saints.
The Steelers are still looking for consistency in production, but there is no denying that the inside linebacker room showed elite potential in Week 7. If that is the level of play the team will get from Queen and Wilson the rest of the way, how could the Steelers possibly move away from that tandem?
Week 7 was the middle linebacker show for the Steelers. Queen finished with a team-leading 10 tackles, seven recorded individually, 1.0 sacks, a tackle for loss, a quarterback hit and a pass defended. Wilson matched that with six tackles of his own, a pass defended and an interception.
That interception was a thing of beauty, as well. Wilson perfectly played his coverage while reading and anticipating Shough. Putting himself in position to make a play on the ball, it still took an impressive feat of athleticism to catch and maintain possession of the ball.
When you are getting turnovers, tackles and a tone-setting performance from your inside linebacker duo, you ride the wave. Who knows how long it will last, but it’s forcing the team’s hand.
It’s also forcing Roberts off of the active roster. The fanbase admires him and the organization clearly values him, but don’t expect Roberts back on the field in a game setting any time soon.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers May Be Team to Watch for Brian Thomas Jr.
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are looking for a wide receiver at the NFL trade deadline. That doesn't come as a surprise, as the team has searched high and low for answers at the position for several years in a row, but this year there seem to be bigger names on the market, and Pittsburgh is interested.
The Steelers have already been linked to Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs after the 25-year-old requested a trade from the team. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Steelers showed interest early, and they're likely still in the mix as the deadline draws closer.
Now, there's another name that has emerged. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Steelers are a team to watch for Jacksonville Jaguars' former first-round pick Brian Thomas Jr. The Jaguars haven't decided whether or not they will trade Thomas Jr., but Pittsburgh may be interested if they do.
"You have teams in the receiver market like the Kansas City Chiefs that need one, that I believe have multiple lines in the water as fas as receiver; the Pittsburgh Steelers are looking around," Fowler said on ESPN. "The Jaguars have not totally committed to trading Brian Thomas right now, but he's in and out of the lineup and would welcome a team most likely."
Reaction to latest Jonathan Taylor news…teams I’ve talked to value Taylor at a ‘2+’ clip - second-round pick and more. Plus, the latest on the receiver market and Brian Thomas Jr. pic.twitter.com/mijzgfp2r9
According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones, the Jaguars are looking for a Day 2 NFL Draft pick in return for Thomas Jr. The Steelers currently have two third-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft after receiving one from the Dallas Cowboys in exchange for Broderick Jones.
The upside of Thomas Jr. is still exciting for any team looking for answers as the wide receiver position. This is a former first-round pick who had over 1,200 yards and caught 10 touchdowns during his rookie season. At 24 years old, Thomas Jr. is playing in just his third season, leaving the 2027 season left on his rookie deal, and making it possible to pick up his fifth-year option this upcoming offseason.
That should intrigue the Steelers. This team has several starter-worthy options in DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman Jr., Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson, but two of those players are on Injured Reserve, and Pittsburgh is in the business of finding a solution at the position now and long-term, and Thomas Jr. may fit both of those needs.
However, he comes with a big "if." Since the arrival of Liam Coen as head coach, Thomas Jr. has fallen out with the offense. This season, he's totaled just nine receptions for 105 yards and a touchdown.
He has not caught a pass since Week 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals.
So, the Steelers would be taking a chance that Thomas Jr. just needs a change of scenery to find his production again and turn his career around before the end of his rookie deal.
Pittsburgh could take the risk and may want to depending on how the other wide receiver options look. Thomas Jr. fits what they need and comes with plenty of upside. So, it's no surprise the Steelers are a team to watch if the former first-round pick is available come the deadline.

title: Steelers' Darnell Washington Fined for 'Vulgar' Touchdown Celebration
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Darnell Washington was momentarily the talk of the Pittsburgh Steelers' Week 7 victory after his touchdown reception from Aaron Rodgers that gave the black and gold a 10-3 lead in the second quarter.
While it didn't turn out to be the only big play of the game, it was one the NFL had their eyes on afterward. The league announced their Week 7 fines for players and issued a $14,926 citation to Washington for his celebration after the touchdown.
The NFL issued the fine for unsportsmanlike conduct, stating  "Illegal celebrations and vulgar acts."
Here's a look at Washington's celebration after the play:
The NFL fined Steelers TE Darnell Washington $14,926 for unsportsmanlike conduct (illegal celebrations and vulgar acts) — showing off the size of his footballs after a touchdown last week in Paris. pic.twitter.com/MdtmcZXFjA
The league also issued a $4,916 fine to wide receiver Brandon Smith for use of the helmet.
Washington finished the game with only that one reception for four yards and a touchdown. Still, his contributions were enough to help Pittsburgh beat the New Orleans Saints, 16-10 and move to 5-2 on the season.
As for the response on Washington's fine, fans aren't too thrilled about it.
One directed a message toward the NFL, calling them "CLAHNS," while another said "NFL= soft."
"Really? Really? This is getting ridiculous," another asked, while another said, "Dawg cmon" with multiple laughing-crying emojis.
ARE WE SERIOUS???? https://t.co/Byfm2kYfVq
While being handed a fine before a game isn't enjoyable, Washington's role within the Steelers' offense is too important to be distracted. This team is without two of their top wide receivers in Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot). Pat Freiermuth is healthy and playing, but was dealing with a calf issue two weeks ago.
Aaron Rodgers is relying on Washington in the passing game, but the Steelers are also looking at Washington as a key piece of their running game. Essentially another left tackle, as many refer to him as, Washington is consistently used as a blocker for Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle, helping to formulate one of the NFL's best rushing attacks.
As the Steelers hunt for the top of the AFC North and beyond, Washington is going to be a critical piece of their team. While a fine like this may stop this particular touchdown celebration, Pittsburgh needs plenty more reasons to celebrate a Washington score this season.
Pittsburgh will host the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Week 8. They head into the bye week afterward before returning to action for their second game against the Cincinnati Bengals. They are 0-1 against the Browns and 1-0 against the Bengals so far this season.

title: Steelers Sign Veteran WR After Three Call-Ups
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers might be exploring the trade market ahead of this year's NFL trade deadline, but there are no reinforcements coming for their Week 8 contest.
Instead, the Steelers must rely on their organizational depth once again to help them earn a fourth consecutive win. Since the team placed pass-catchers Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson on the Injured Reserve, there has been an extreme lack of depth in the wide receiver room.
Welcoming the Cleveland Browns to Acrisure Stadium, the offense will turn to another depth player to take sole hold of the AFC North division. After elevating him for three games from the practice squad, the Steelers officially added Brandon Smith to the active roster after they signed him to a one-year deal.
The Steelers have been very pleased with Smith since he first signed a Reserve/Futures contract with the organization ahead of the 2026 campaign. At training camp and the preseason, he stood out. He was consistently one of the better performers at camp and despite being released as the roster was cut down to the initial 53-man roster, Smith was quickly re-signed to the team's practice squad.
As injuries have mounted, Smith has been a steadying presence. In his third game on the active roster, Smith finally made his mark on offense. Against the New Orleans Saints, Smith made the first two catches of his NFL career. He finished the Week 7 contest with two receptions on two targets for 24 yards, with one of those catches being a crucial 20-yard connection with Aaron Rodgers.
That moment displayed what Smith brings to the Steelers right now. He's a solid route runner with an above-average frame (6'2", 220 pounds) that fits the mold of current receivers. While the team tries to continue feeding DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard, he can go into the gritty areas of the field.
Most importantly, Smith has to bring his size and strength to the run game. The Steelers demand a ton from their receivers as run blockers, and Smith has fared well. He's missed some assignments, but he's also made some key blocks on long Jaylen Warren runs.
To keep playing on game days, he has to make himself indispensible in the running game.
Playing in his fourth game with the Steelers, Smith is hoping to establish more chemistry with quarterback Aaron Rodgers. The team's offensive leader has spoken highly of Smith since training camp, and with his two targets in Week 7, Rodgers displayed some trust in the 27-year-old.
But to become a more productive member of the offense, Smith has to become more of a trusted target for Rodgers. That takes time, something he doesn't have the luxury of right now, but it also takes just a few plays to build that confidence. They got off to a good start in Week 7, and it needs to continue to keep this passing game afloat until they are fully healthy.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Could Get Trade Calls About Star Edge Rusher
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers may have a name to watch for at the NFL trade deadline . With options at outside linebacker, NFL insider Tom Pelissero says Alex Highsmith is the name to watch before Nov. 10.
Highsmith, 29, has been a staple of the Steelers' defense for the last few seasons, but after signing Nick Herbig and T.J. Watt to contract extensions the last two offseasons, it's uncertain how much longer he'll be in Pittsburgh.
"Other teams have inquired about trading for Highsmith since last year, and the Steelers' answer has always been no," Pelissero writes . "But they currently have a logjam at edge rusher, with T.J. Watt turning back the clock with a stellar performance this season at age 32, while younger players Nick Herbig and Jackn Sawyer have part-time roles. Highsmith is still in his prime at age 29 and figures to be the subject of more calls leading up to the deadline."
Highsmith is dur $8.8 million for the remainder of the 2026 season and will head into the final year of his contract in 2027, being owed $15.5 million with no guarantees.
Whether with the Steelers or another organization, Highsmith will likely request a contract extension in the 2027 offseason . That doesn't help his case about staying in Pittsburgh long-term, but it doesn't necessarily mean the team will move him now and not during the offseason instead.
You can already start to see the issue with having so many outside linebackers on the roster. The Steelers started the season with Highsmith and Watt on the outside and Herbig playing a hybrid-style role off the line of scrimmage. He didn't take up an inside linebacker spot, but more so was used as a floater where he would either drop into coverage or rush.
After Herbig started the year slow, he reverted to more time playing as an edge rusher behind Watt and Highsmith, but with Jack Sawyer also in the mix, the rotation of four leaves limited reps for their young depth pieces.
Never say never in the NFL, but the Steelers are likely going to shut down most offers for Highsmith pretty quickly. A team would need to really impress them with their initial offer to get a conversation going, and if that team is willing to overpay some, Pittsburgh may have a hard time saying no.
Highsmith probably requires a second- or third-round pick in return, and maybe more because the Steelers view him as a key piece to their playoff push in the second half of the season.
It's not likely Highsmith gets dealt this season. The offseason is a different story. And again, if a team comes calling with a big offer, you never know if the Steelers would be willing to take the risk of moving on mid-season.

title: Steelers vs. Browns Bold Predictions: Aaron Rodgers Hit New Milestone
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers face one of their toughest tests in Week 8, as they take on the Cleveland Browns and attempt to assert themselves as a top team in the AFC North.
The Browns are no easy challenge this time around, and the Steelers learned that firsthand several weeks ago. The Browns won their first meeting on Thursday Night Football, but the matchup shifts to Acrisure Stadium for Week 8, and the Steelers intend to exact some revenge on their divisional foes.
Both squads enter with a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. It’s a measuring-stick showdown between the Steelers and Browns, and bold actions will be taken.
Both of these franchises bring strong defenses to their Week 8 contest. The Steelers rank in the top 10 in total yards allowed per game, rushing yards allowed per game and points allowed per contest. They also rank 11th in passing yards allowed per game.
Similarly, the Browns rank in the top 15 across multiple defensive categories. It’s going to be a matchup of two stout defensive units, right?
Well what would be more surprising than these two teams putting up an offensive showdown? That’s what could be in store for these two teams, despite all signs pointing toward the opposite. The Steelers rank 22nd in the NFL in points per game, posting an average of 21.9. The Browns trail, recording the 28th-best average of 19.0 points per game. But, the Steelers have also reached the 24-point mark four times in seven tries, and they could put up even more in Week 8.
If the Steelers are going to buck the trend and put up points, there are two approaches to help accomplish that. One is to exploit their 19th-ranked run defense, which has to be at the top of their game plan as Jaylen Warren continues to put up MVP-caliber production.
Another avenue, the more unexpected one for the offense to take, is to push the ball downfield with the passing game. In the team’s first matchup against the Browns, Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf posted five receptions on nine targets for 115 yards. And they managed to break off his biggest play of the game by getting him away from Cleveland’s top defender, Denzel Ward.
If the Steelers can capture that again in Week 8, quarterback Aaron Rodgers could have a magical day. In 2025, Rodgers never hit the 300-yard mark. His 2026 season high so far is 299 yards, which he threw for during that previous contest against the Browns. In the three weeks since, he hasn’t surpassed 255 yards, but this could be the one where he eclipses 300 yards.
If Rodgers is throwing that many yards, one of his receivers has to have an outstanding day on the stat sheet. After he earned more and more trust, Bernard could face a favorable matchup if he doesn’t go against Ward too often.
He’s gotten close, putting up two 80+ yard games so far this season. This week, it finally happens. The second-round pick eclipses 100 yards for the first time in his young NFL career.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Zach Frazier Might Become Steelers' Greatest Ever, Says One Player
full_text:
One of Zach Frazier’s Pittsburgh Steelers teammates believes he’s destined for greatness.
During an appearance on Terron Armstead's "The Set” podcast, Elandon Roberts stated that he thinks Frazier has a chance to become the best center in Steelers history.
“[If] Zach Frazier keeps doing what he’s doing, he might be the greatest center in Steelers history,” Roberts said . “I’m telling you. He ain’t getting the credit he deserves.”
Roberts thinks Frazier deserves a slew of accolades for his performance in the middle of Pittsburgh’s offensive line as well.
“That man should go All-Pro and Pro Bowl. First-team, I’m telling you,” Roberts said.
In order for Frazier to climb the ranks of the top centers Pittsburgh has ever had, he’ll really need to go above and beyond.
Mike Webster is arguably the best player at the position in franchise history. A fifth-round pick in the 1974 NFL Draft, he remained with the team through the 1988 season.
Over that span, Webster was a four-time Super Bowl champion, six-time first-team All-Pro and nine-time Pro Bowler. He was eventually inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame as a member of the Class of 1997.
Webster’s successor, Dermontti Dawson, was selected in the fourth round of the 1988 NFL Draft and took the former’s spot once he left the team ahead of the 1989 campaign.
Over his 13 seasons with the Steelers, which was the entirety of his career, Dawson was a six-time first-team All-Pro and seven-time Pro Bowler before being inducted into the Hall of Fame as a member of the Class of 2012.
More recently, Maurkice Pouncey was a stalwart at center for the black and gold from 2010, when he was a first-round pick, through the end of his career in 2020.
During his tenure with the Steelers, Pouncey was a two-time first-team All-Pro and nine-time Pro Bowler.
He's not a slam dunk Hall of Famer, but there is a chance that he'll be enshrined in Canton one day.
A second-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Frazier established himself as one of the league's premier centers right from the jump.
He's only improved during the 2026 campaign, and he's right up there with Creed Humphrey as the best player at the position in the league right now.
In order for Frazier to fly past the likes of Webster, Dawson and Pouncey and become the top center in franchise history, as Roberts believes he can be, though, he'll need to start racking up the accolades.
He was a member of PFWA's All-Rookie Team, though that's all he has to his name at this point.
Frazier must re-sign with Pittsburgh too, but it's essentially a formality that he'll sign a massive new deal with the team next offseason heading into the final year of his rookie contract.
The 25-year-old is in the midst of an All-Pro and Pro Bowl-caliber campaign, as Roberts noted, though he has to play at that level for another decade or so to really put himself into the conversation with the likes of Webster, Dawson and Pouncey.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: The Most Steelers Should Pay in WR Trade
full_text:
If there's any position the Pittsburgh Steelers should splurge on before the November 10 trade deadline, it's wide receiver .
This is far from the first time the Steelers have had a clear need at receiver this time of year. They haven't exactly gone to great lengths to fill that hole in the past, though, as the organization acquired Mike Williams from the New York Jets for a 2025 fifth-round pick during the 2024 season and did not bring in anyone at the position in 2025.
Sitting at 5-2 and with a chance to make some noise in the AFC, perhaps more so than in recent seasons, Pittsburgh must strike while the iron is hot.
How much should the Steelers be willing to part with in order to add a potential difference-maker at receiver, though?
General manager Omar Khan isn't afraid to wheel and deal when necessary, even if his track record of asset management isn't the greatest.
Whether it's been sending away players such as Joey Porter Jr., George Pickens, Broderick Jones, Kaleb Johnson and Minkah Fitzpatrick or bringing in big-name veterans such as DK Metcalf, Jalen Ramsey and even Michael Pittman Jr., Khan has been quite active on the trade market over the last year or two in particular.
As a result of some of those aforementioned deals, Pittsburgh currently owns 18 total picks between the 2027 and 2028 NFL Drafts, with nine in each year.
With both first-round picks, three second-rounders and three third-rounders included amongst their treasure trove of selections, Khan and the Steelers have plenty of resources to go out and make a huge splash via trade if they so choose.
They're not going to part ways with their first-rounders in all likelihood, but that doesn't mean they can't or shouldn't still give up a significant haul at this year's deadline in order to give themselves the best odds of snapping their seven-game playoff losing streak.
In terms of what's required to reach its ceiling both as an offense and as a team, generating more explosive plays in the passing game has to be the No. 1 priority for Pittsburgh.
Aaron Rodgers and company have operated rather well in the short and intermediate areas of the field through the air in Mike McCarthy's system, though stretching the field and getting chunk plays has still proven to be a struggle.
For that reason, finding a playmaker at receiver and putting them next to the likes of DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard as well as Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. once they're off the reserve/injured list would create the Steelers' most complete group of weapons at the position in quite some time.
It will likely cost Pittsburgh somewhere in the ballpark of a third- or fourth-rounder in order to land Josh Downs from the Colts , who's on an expiring contract. If that's what their receiver move ends up being, it'd be more than enough to satisfy their need.
At the same time, if a player like Ladd McConkey were to ever hit the market, the Steelers shouldn't shy away from the price tag if it were to take a second-rounder and then some to bring him in.
While giving up a first-rounder would be hard to stomach, doing so with the aim of acquiring a receiver of DeVonta Smith's caliber is something Pittsburgh should seriously consider.
In the end, there really shouldn't be a limit for what the Steelers are willing to part ways with for a receiver. They have a shot at contending in the AFC if they make the right move, and the organization must be uber-aggressive as a result.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Lose Two CBs to Injury Against Browns
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers need a strong secondary for their next game, but they won't have two important defensive depth pieces.
The Steelers announced that both cornerbacks Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter are out with hamstring injuries for their Week 8 matchup against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium.
Echols will miss his second game , after not featuring in the 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France, in Week 7, after suffering the injury in the 26-19 overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium in Week 6.
Slaughter suffered his injury in the win over the Saints and both players didn't practice on Oct. 29.
The Steelers still have their main secondary healthy, with Asante Samuel Jr. and Jamal Dean as starting cornerbacks, Jalen Ramsey at nickelback and Jaquan Brisker as safety.
Pittsburgh's issue is that they don't have as good of depth with Echols and Slaughter out, which could poise problems for them if there are injuries to the starting core.
Ramsey doesn't have a backup nickelback after Echols and Samuel loses his third-string replacement.
Sean Murphy-Bunting, whom the Steelers signed off of the Buccaneers' practice squad on Oct. 5, is next on the depth chart behind Samuel.
Pittsburgh may turn to Daylen Everette and Terell Smith, who are listed behind Dean on the depth chart, as depth for Samuel and Murphy-Bunting if they suffer any injuries.
The Steelers do have a few players they could activate from the practice squad for this game if they need more depth against the Browns.
Sebastian Castro, Darius Rush and Car'lin Vigers could all be elevated for this next game.
The Steelers have one of their biggest games of the season against the Browns this weekend, with both teams 5-2 and tied for the AFC North lead .
Cleveland holds the tiebreaker over Pittsburgh after their 27-24 win in the first matchup of 2026 in Week 4 at Huntington Bank Field.
The Steelers also face divisional competition from the Bengals, 4-2, and even the Ravens, 4-3, who have stumbled a bit without quarterback Lamar Jackson.
Pittsburgh has a real chance to show midway through 2026 that they are the favorite to win the AFC North and be one of the best teams in the NFL.
The Steelers defense has been excellent this season and they need to be so again when they face a solid offensive attack from the Browns.

He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

title: 3 Games Seahawks Fans Should Watch in Week 8
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are not appearing on TV screens today as they prepare for their Monday Night Football matchup against the Chicago Bears in primetime tomorrow night.
Even though the Seahawks aren't on the NFL schedule today, there are some games that should be intriguing for the 12s to watch. Here's a look at three that stand out above the rest.
Perhaps the most highly anticipated matchup of the day features two AFC powerhouses: the Baltimore Ravens and the Buffalo Bills. The Bills are 5-1, coming off their bye week, and they hope to maintain their status as one of the best teams in the league.
Meanwhile, the Ravens have struggled in recent weeks, falling to division rivals the Cleveland Browns and the Cincinnati Bengals in consecutive weeks. In both of those games, they did not have quarterback Lamar Jackson, who is expected to return from his ankle injury in this matchup. With Jackson on the mend, it should create an enticing matchup between two teams that could see each other in the playoffs this winter.

On top of that, the Cowboys are vying to stay in the mix in the standings for the NFC East, which appears as wide open as any division in football.
The only undefeated team left in the league is the Minnesota Vikings, but they are underdogs against the Detroit Lions on the road at Ford Field. The Lions are 4-2 after a big win last week against the Green Bay Packers and are hoping to make a statement with a victory against the Vikings in Week 8.
The Vikings are doing it on defense, while the Lions have one of the best offenses in the league. That clash should create an exciting matchup between the two rivals.

title: Are the Seahawks Officially out on RB Jonathan Taylor Trade?
full_text:
For four consecutive years, the Seattle Seahawks have been a major player during the NFL Trade Deadline. Earlier this week, general manager John Schneider showed that the team remains willing to trade for high-level talent at the NFL Trade Deadline. The Seahawks traded for eight-time Pro-Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts . Nelson is an immediate upgrade for the offensive line.
​There was talk that the Seahawks might not be done making trades to improve the roster, especially being two weeks away from the deadline at the time. There was talk that the Seahawks might trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. Despite a great fit , the Seahawks might be out on Taylor.
​On Sunday, ESPN’s NFL insiders Ian and Raport Adam Schefter reported that the Colts are open to trading Taylor. Schefter mentioned that some teams are active in trading for the three-time Pro-Bowl running back. These teams include the Denver Broncos, the Green Bay Packers, the Minnesota Vikings and the New York Giants. Seattle seems to be the biggest omission from the list of teams that haven’t reached out to Indianapolis.
​While this doesn’t mean that the Seahawks are out on Taylor, it seems they are more focused on their roster than making changes to it. The Seahawks could get veteran running back Zach Charbonnet and rookie running back Jadarian Price back from injury for Week 8’s Monday Night Football game versus the Chicago Bears. The front office and coaching staff might want to see their new rushing additions of Nelson, Charbonnet and, possibly, Price in a game before a decision.
​There is still time for the Seahawks to decide if they want to trade for Taylor, especially after their game versus the Bears. The Seahawks might be cautious of trading for an older running back and what they would have to give up. Indianapolis already reportedly turned down a trade deal that includes a second-round pick and an additional pick.  This likely means that the Colts are wanting more picks or at least one first-round pick.
​The Seahawks have multiple picks on day-two and day-three of the NFL Draft, but first-or-second-round picks. The front office might replace an early pick with Price, but that would mean giving up on the young back before he has been given several chances to show himself . Price was drafted to be a dynamic starting running back for several years in the Seahawks’ backfield.
​Seattle ranks 17th in the league in rushing yards per game (113.7), while bad offensive line play, turnovers and a lack of explosiveness have plagued the offense . If Nelson’s addition to the roster plus Charbonnet and Price’s return doesn’t improve the running game, then there are problems beyond the players. If the Seahawks trade assets for Taylor and the problems persist, then it’s not a good look for the Seahawks’ future this season.

title: Seahawks' Plans for Jadarian Price in Week 8 Being Misinterpreted
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (4-3) will once again have another primetime game, this time on Monday at home against the Chicago Bears (5-2) . There is a lot of excitement for the Seahawks as they are set to debut newly traded left guard Quenton Nelson and running back Zach Charbonnet from injury. The running game should take a huge boost with more efficiency at the offensive line and more explosiveness at running back.
​The Seahawks could also see the return of rookie running back Jadarian Price , who is coming off a chest injury that forced him to be placed on IR. Since Price’s injury, the running game has been poor. If Price comes off IR and plays, the Seahawks’ offense should see much more improvement. Some Seahawks fans see a reason to believe that Price’s future is as early as Monday.
​During Saturday’s press conference, head coach Mike Macdonald was asked about the plans for both Charbonnet and Price. Macdonald said the coaching staff has a plan for Charbonnet, but it was different with Price. He said , “And with JD, I think if we were to make a move, I think that would happen on Monday.”
To many, this would imply that the Seahawks are waiting to see if he recovered from his injury enough to play and potentially start.  The front office can make changes to the roster in terms of who to move  up or down the 53-man roster. Price can be activated on the day of the game .
​To others, this might be the belief that the Seahawks are limiting Price to use as a trade asset. The Seahawks are among the teams that might trade for three-time Pro-Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor from the Indianapolis Colts. The Seahawks’ running game has struggled even before Price’s injury. Seattle could trade Price along with a high day-three NFL Draft pick to the Colts instead of a first-round pick.
​There is some discourse that the Seahawks should cut their losses with Price after only three games played and get a star running back for a win-now team. If the Seahawks traded for another Colts star, it would make them the team to beat.
Price, however, hasn’t gotten many chances to show his potential with Seattle’s offense. The first two games with Price were when Seattle was trying to get quarterback Drew Lock comfortable with the offense. Week 3 against the Washington Commanders was when he was benched for his fumbling issue.
​At this point in the season, Price is the only saving grace of a 2026 NFL Draft class that started rough. With safety Bud Clark and cornerback Julian Neal injured and the rest of the drafted rookies not ready,  Price is the only player who can make this draft class look somewhat successful.
​The Seahawks want to see what they have in Price, especially with one of the most elite run-blockers in Nelson leading the charge. Price showed great flashes of replacing Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III before Sam Darnold’s injury, his turnover issues and his own injury. The trade for Nelson was a promise for Darnold to improve, but also for Price.

title: Seahawks Give Word on Jadarian Price and More Before Bears Game
full_text:
Coming a day later than typical due to the Monday Night Football tilt, the Seattle Seahawks released their third and final injury report, which will go a long way in shedding light on the likely availability of several key Seahawks. The Chicago Bears gave their own injury updates as well, so let’s have a look at what’s brewing. Starting with the Seahawks…
There’s some good news here, to be sure. Quenton Nelson (knee) , Brady Russell (wrist), Connor O’Toole (hamstring), Chazz Surratt (calf), Drake Thomas (ankle), and Leonard Williams (achilles) are locked and loaded. DeMarcus Lawrence and Jaxon Smith-Njigba , never injured in the first place, have no game status either.
But the most exciting thing for many Seahawks fans will be Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Jadarian Price (chest) having no game status and being expected to roll in full. It hasn't been a smooth ride, but it looks like we'll have our entire backfield available this week. Also massive is Byron Murphy (back) having no game status. That should be more than enough to quell concerns.
Those who are questionable going into Monday's game include Anthony Bradford (knee) , Drew Lock (right elbow), Brandon Pili (back), and Pat O’Connell (toe). Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) is doubtful, so tenatively cross him off. Charles Cross (ankle), Velus Jones (hamstring), and Rashid Shaheed (knee) are out, but that’s been assumed to be the case since the week started.
There was a lot less drama this week for the Chicago Bears, and that has held through this final practice of the week. They have one player with an out designation, and as expected, it’s Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe). Obviously, the Bears are somewhat used to not having him, but he remains a very valuable and important part of that offense as a change-of-pace back.
The questionable slate is not without concerns, of course. Malik Muhammad (toe), who has been the best cover corner in Chicago so far this year, was limited all week and is considered a 50/50 to play. D’Marco Jackson (ankle), a starting linebacker, got a full practice in but is still considered questionable. I imagine he plays, but it’s worth monitoring.
Speaking of linebacker, T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Jack Sanborn (concussion) have no status after full practices all week. The primary relief for Bears fans, however, is Colston Loveland (neck), who was a full go today and has no status. Neck injuries are no joke, but it looks like Loveland’s issue was a very minor one and he’ll be suited up Monday.

title: Seahawks' Jarran Reed Linked to Several Teams in NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
Teams have just over a week left to improve their rosters through the NFL Trade Deadline. The Seattle Seahawks (4-3) already made moves by trading for eight-time Pro-Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. This move might be the best overall trade this Trade Deadline.
There are some reports that believe the Seahawks could move some of their players to help their salary cap situation for another trade or to give Nelson a contract extension. Some reports might indicate veteran defensive tackle Jarran Reed is on another team’s radar to trade for.
​Reed is one of the top leaders on the Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense . He is also one of the most underrated players on the interior defensive line. Reed has played all 11 games, accounting for 11 total tackles, four quarterback hits, one tackle for loss and one sack. He can be the one-technique defensive tackle and the three-technique defensive tackle.
​He is a huge part of the Seahawks’ defense, and other teams understand how efficient a player he is. CBS’s Jonathan Jones notes that teams are interested in trading for Reed to to address needs of reliability in the middle of the defense. He can also be an instant veteran defensive leader for another team.
​The Seahawks weren’t likely going to trade any players before the Nelson trade, but now the front office has to start thinking about the future. Nelson is in the final year of his contract, and the Seahawks shouldn’t think twice about getting him to an extension . The biggest problem is affordability while still having room for other veterans next season.
​Moving veterans like Reed would help the front office create some salary cap space while getting some picks in return. Reed is in the second-year of a three-year, $22 million contract . If the Seahawks traded him before the deadline, the team would save  $3.26 million in cap space for the rest of this season while taking a $4.13 million dead cap hit. Next season, however, the Seahawks would save $8 million, creating $45.48 million in salary cap space and only take a $1.5 million dead cap hit.
​The downside to the move is the Seahawks lose a reliable run-stopper and underrated pass rusher from the middle of their defense. This might be the price for trading for an elite guard like Nelson, but it’s something they should consider if they want to secure one of the league’s best guards and get future capital as a result.

title: Seahawks Mailbag: 4 Questions Leading Into The Bears Game
full_text:
It was a very important win that the Seattle Seahawks just notched, restoring confidence and belief that this team might be able to mount a meaningful title defense. I asked my discord server what their biggest questions about the team are right now. Let’s take a look at what’s on the mind of the fans. The wording of the questions has been lightly edited for this article.
“Is moving Zabel to center the long term plan? If so, what happens to Jalen Sundell?”
I’ve always thought that Zabel would end up at center in the NFL due to his short arms. I was thrilled when he was able to play left guard last season with some success, but center might be the position he can excel at, especially in this type of offense. Look for him to learn the position in the upcoming offseason and be the guy in 2027.
As for Sundell, he’s an Exclusive Rights Free Agent this offseason, so retaining him is trivial and can be done without Sundell’s say-so. Olu Oluwatimi is a free agent this offseason, so keeping Sundell as a backup for at least one season is completely reasonable. It’s not like Sundell is an elite player who has a right to demand a starting job. It all fits together to me.
“What are we gonna do with Avery Smith? Is he playing at all?”
Obviously, there’s some degree of frustration when your team makes a trade for a player that ends up giving the team nothing. But at this point, that’s probably where we are with Smith . No reason to believe he’s bad, and it can’t be a problem to have extra depth in a season like this, but Smith’s only real chance to hack it on an NFL defense is in the slot.
Between Nick Emmanwori and Devon Witherspoon, the Seahawks have the nickel corner thing on ice. If you want to speak about cornerback in general, they’ve also gotten shockingly good play from Nehemiah Pritchett. But remember, Smith’s rookie contract is still active, so he has a chance to be here for a couple years beyond this one. His time will come.
“Is there any thought of giving Nehemiah Pritchett more opportunities?”
I think the hangup here is that Mike Macdonald really wants corners who can tackle and come up in run support, and he’s probably over the moon with having three corners in his nickel packages who are great tacklers. Pritchett is a liability in that area, so despite his excellent play in coverage so far this season, he’s getting sparse opportunities right now.
Last season, the Seahawks did rotate Josh Jobe and Riq Woolen at corner, so they’ve shown a willingness to get creative and accept some suboptimal performances to try to get their best players on the field. I would be all for putting Pritchett in the Woolen role, but even if that doesn’t happen, it’s a reasonable bet that Pritchett gets called again this season anyway.
“Should we still pursue a RB in a trade, or do we roll with what we got?”
I wouldn’t object to a mild improvement to the depth with someone like Tony Pollard, since that should be very cheap and won’t require any investment beyond this season. I could be talked into something a little more mid-level, like Bucky Irving, as well. But the question we have to answer first is whether or not we really need to be adding on here anymore.
Whatever you think of Jadarian Price right now, the Seahawks just spent a first round pick on him six months ago and clearly think highly of him. Zach Charbonnet has proven capable of being effective in a timeshare backfield. Emanuel Wilson has shown he’s a capable back when used the right way. And a healthy George Holani is a workable third down back.
Maybe it’s not the greatest backfield ever, but shouldn’t it be good enough? And should we really pump more resources into it right now? I’m not convinced it’s the right play. The Jonathan Taylor buzz in particular is a little confusing to me, as he doesn’t fit the offense and would be pricey to obtain. On this count, I’m dancing with the women we brought.

title: 5 Score Predictions for Bears vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are preparing for their Week 8 matchup against the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football.
With the game slowly approaching , some members of the Seattle Seahawks On SI staff gave their predictions for how the contest would end up.
In terms of an opposing offense, this will be a massive challenge for Mike Macdonald's No. 1 ranked defense. Chicago is third in the league in total yards per game and first in the NFL in rushing. But only five teams are allowing fewer yards per game on the ground. Both clubs are pretty adept at taking away the football. This week, Sam Darnold plays turnover-free football, Caleb Williams throws a fourth-quarter pick and sets up Jason Myers's game-winning field goal at the gun.
I'm expecting a defensive struggle in this one between two teams that have been inconsistent on both sides of the football all year long. The Seahawks proved in their latest game against the Kansas City Chiefs how dominant their defense can be, holding Patrick Mahomes out of the red zone for the first time in his career.
The Bears' offense has the ability to pop off at any given moment, and Caleb Williams has thrown for 300 yards in each of the last two games. Seattle's defense will be primed and ready for the matchup, which should be close but low-scoring.
The Bears are the best run team in the NFL, and the Seahawks are holding opponents to 3.5 yards per attempt. Something has to give in this one, and after what Mike Macdonald and Aden Durde did to the Chiefs last week, my money is on them. This one will be a defensive battle most of the way and will be close until Seattle makes some key plays in the final 15 minutes to pull away.
The Seahawks get new additions to the run game, but it’s wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba that has a stellar game versus the Bears, who have one of the worst secondaries in the league. The Dark Side Defense has some tough moments getting Caleb Williams down on the ground. Their great secondary locks down the Bears passing game in the final quarter.
The Bears are a very blitz heavy team that can be attacked on the back end, and the Seahawks have been a very good offense against the blitz over the last year and a half. Caleb Williams' penchant for holding onto the ball plays right into our hands defensively. Add in primetime at home and I think we're good.

title: Why Seahawks Should (and Shouldn't) Trade Anthony Bradford
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks' offensive line looks a little different after acquiring Quenton Nelson in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald stated that Nelson will be the team's new left guard , while second-year pro Grey Zabel will slide in at right guard. This leaves Anthony Bradford as the odd man out, but the Seahawks still feel strongly about their long-time starter that has now been demoted.
"It's not an easy situation," Macdonald said via the team's website. "I thought Anthony played really good football for us and he has, and he's earned a significant role on our team, a starting-level role. And so it's one of those 'through not around' type of things with AB (Anthony Bradford) that is not easy. So really no way to sugarcoat it. And I think he believes us when we say this is how much we love him as teammates.
"The guys love him in the locker room. He's a fantastic teammate. We don't expect him to be jumping for joy in the situation because that's not realistic, but he's going to be a great teammate and he's going to stay ready and we know how this league works. I mean, you're a play away from him playing every play again. So it's not an easy situation, but he's a tough cookie and the guys will have his back as well."
With the trade deadline approaching on Nov. 10, it might be in Seattle's best interest to explore a possible deal to send Bradford to a new home as he gets ready to be a free agent this offseason.
Bradford has gone through ups and downs as the team's starting right guard over the years. He was viewed as the unit's weak link last season, but he was still the starter when the team won the Super Bowl.
The Seahawks could have negotiated an extension at some point during the offseason, but they opted not to. It is widely expected that he will play for a different team in 2027. The Seahawks could do right by Bradford by sending him to a new team that is in need of a starting right guard now, so he can audition for a team with more of an opportunity going into next season.
Seattle values depth, so that is the argument for keeping Bradford: he could step right in if needed at multiple positions along the offensive line. Seattle doesn't gain a whole lot from trading Bradford because they could possibly get a compensatory pick in 2028 should Bradford leave in free agency.
A trade now would just get the Seahawks a pick maybe a year earlier, but Seattle also has a boatload of picks coming due to the volume and quality of players that left in free agency during the spring.
I can't see the Seahawks trading Bradford unless he requested a deal himself. The team will likely want to keep him around for depth because that is more valuable than the late-round pick they would get to add to their pretty full cupboard of future selections.
