title: Seahawks Get Jaxon Smith-Njigba Some Help in 2027 NFL Mock Draft
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are focused on the second half of the season, but they are also looking forward to the NFL draft in the spring.
It remains to be seen where the Seahawks will end up in the first round, but with a boatload of picks , they are keeping their radars wide open. One player that could make sense for them is Rutgers wide receiver KJ Duff, who was listed as the No. 17 overall pick by Seahawks contributor Tim Crean in his latest mock draft.
"No wide receiver in the NFL is more relied on than Jaxson [sic] Smith-Njigba. The Seahawks need to find him a running-mate, because he can’t continue to carry the passing game all by himself. The 6-foot-6 KJ Duffy [sic] is an interesting player here, because the big target is so different than JSN that he just might be the perfect No. 2 in Seattle," Crean wrote.
Through seven games, Smith-Njigba has 78 targets, while no other teammate of his has more than 30. His 867 yards are well ahead of everybody in the league by over 150 yards.
When it comes to the team, no other receiver has more than 200 yards on the season. Smith-Njigba getting a super majority of the receptions, targets, and yards is not a surprise given his talent, but it might help Seattle to bring in another target to take some heat and attention off of JSN.
As a huge 6-6 target, this could be a massive boost for the Seahawks when it comes to their red zone offense.
The team signed Rashid Shaheed to a 3-year, $51 million contract and made Smith-Njigba the highest-paid wide receivers in the NFL this past offseason, adding another first-round pick to that mix. That might not make sense when there are other positions of need.
The team will need to replace DeMarcus Lawrence on the pass rush unit next season, as he is headed for retirement. Getting a young pass rusher who can develop might make more sense to the team in the long run.
A player like Yhonzae Pierre from Alabama has been linked to them in the past, and he could be someone to look out for in the future.

title: Jonathan Taylor Trade Would Help Seahawks, But Here's Why It Won't Happen
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have been linked to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor as a trade target for the past couple of weeks.
The Seahawks and Colts recently agreed to a deal involving All-Pro offensive lineman Quenton Nelson , but Taylor was not part of the trade. Bleacher Report writer Alex Kay suggested a trade that would send Taylor to the Seahawks for Emanuel Wilson and second- and fourth-round picks in next year's draft.
"Bringing Taylor into the mix would significantly elevate a Seahawks ground attack that is averaging a middling 113.7 yards per game right now. That is nearly 10 yards below what the team rushed for during the 2025 campaign and almost 20 yards fewer than it averaged during its three-game postseason run," Kay wrote.
"While the move would cost the Seahawks some premium picks, upgrading Wilson to Taylor would have a transformative effect—catapulting Seattle back near the top of the Super Bowl favorites list."
The Seahawks have a chance to win a second straight Super Bowl, and they can't sit on the sidelines and let other teams make the big plays instead of them. Last year, the Seahawks acquired Rashid Shaheed from the New Orleans Saints, and that move ended up paying off big time.
This year, they have shown aggressiveness in acquiring Nelson, but it might not hurt to get an improvement at the running back position, which has been an inconsistency for the team all season long.
Trading for Taylor ensures that another team that could be competing with them in the NFC playoffs, like the Minnesota Vikings, doesn't get him. That might be the ultimate reason, which would put the Seahawks on a path to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl for a second year in a row.
Taylor is going to cost the Seahawks a pretty penny. He is under contract for $44 million over the next two years, which is far more expensive than what Kenneth Walker III cost the Kansas City Chiefs. The Seahawks were unwilling to match a deal similar to what Walker got with the Chiefs, so it wouldn't make sense for Seattle to raise their salary standards for Taylor.
On top of that, the team should be getting Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back in the lineup at some point in the next couple of weeks. That should help the run game tremendously, which would negate the need to make a trade for Taylor, even if it is the splashy, sexy move that many football fans would love to see.

title: 49ers GM John Lynch Highlights Brock Purdy’s Best Qualities
full_text:
It wouldn't be unfair to suggest that San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is the best quarterback of the Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch era.
Out of all the quarterbacks who have started since 2017, Purdy is the best. Since 2022, he's taken the 49ers to the Super Bowl, the NFC Championship Game and the Divisional Round in four seasons.
In his career so far, Purdy has completed 1,065 of 1,564 pass attempts (68.1%) for 13,433 yards, averaging 8.6 yards per attempt, with 99 touchdowns, 41 interceptions and a 104.8 passer rating.
Stats and achievements aside, Lynch highlighted multiple qualities Purdy possesses that have helped establish him as one of the league's elite quarterbacks.
"You have to be able to retain and take in a ton of information," Lynch explained to NBC Sports Bay Area . "You watch us do all those motions—Brock's handling that. He's the orchestrator, and I don't think people understand how much information [that involves]. He's got an ability to do that.
"Kyle is demanding, and Brock can take that without taking it personally, and I think that's really important. That may be one of his greatest qualities as to why he thrives with Kyle.
"And then, he's extremely talented. You see him, the way he goes and extends plays. He's done it in each and every game, aside from being able to stay in the pocket and progress.
"He's competitive. He always finds a way to get better," Lynch continued. "I think, this year, he kind of took it personally that people are saying he's a layer thrower. I'm seeing him come out with shoulder turn and driving the ball this year.
"I think that's what the great ones do. They identify things they want to work on, and they get it done. I could talk about Brock all day long, and I'm probably going too long, but he's easy to do that with."
The desire to keep improving and not letting criticism get to you is exactly what stands out. It's a small element of the exact culture Shanahan wants to embed in his team.
Purdy and Shanahan are a perfect match, and it cannot be emphasised enough how important it is for the two to remain together for as much of their careers as possible. If they can continue building on their existing partnership, a Super Bowl victory could certainly be on the cards.

title: John Lynch Sounds Off on His 10-Year Partnership With Kyle Shanahan on the 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have had John Lynch as their general manager and Kyle Shanahan as their head coach for a decade.
Both arrived in 2017 and helped restore the organization, making it a championship contender and taking the City by the Bay to two Super Bowls, two NFC Championship Games, and, most recently, the Divisional Round last season.
Though the ultimate prize has eluded the 49ers so far, the overall commitment is to bring a sixth Lombardi back.
Reflecting on his partnership with Shanahan over the last 10 years, Lynch told NBC Sports Bay Area : "They say time flies when you're having fun, and I think that. But it doesn't feel like 10 years. Crazy that we've spent a decade here. I'm very grateful for that.
"It's been a lot of fun, and when you play football, you become very close with people because you go through really good times, you go through real hard times, and you go through everything. There's a multitude of things.
"And the most important thing is that you do it together. And whether good or bad, that you stick together and you have each other's back. That's kind of the Forty-Niner way, and we certainly do. We've had each other's back from the start and really proud of that.
"We have had a range of emotions and outcomes of getting to Super Bowls, the elation of that, the heartbreak of not winning those Super Bowls. But I think we both talk about those experiences—if you can stick together and if you are aligned, they only make you stronger. And I feel like that more than ever. We're extremely aligned.
"We're about the same thing, and how we're going to accomplish it, and how we're going to go about it, and that's really cool that after this much time, that we're as strong as ever."
Shanahan recently, rather secretly, inked a contract extension at the start of the season and is now the longest-tenured coach in franchise history. It's not known when that contract expires. Lynch, however, his contract expires after this season, so one can imagine he will have a new contract coming his way.
The next tangible goal for the duo is to win a Super Bowl. They've come close on multiple occasions, but with the 49ers off to a 6-1 start, this could finally be the year they finish the season by bringing a Super Bowl title back to San Francisco for the first time this century.

title: 4 Games 49ers Fans Should Watch in Week 8
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers will be winners this week as they're currently enjoying their crucial Bye . However, that means 49ers fans will not get to watch their favorite team.
They've been treated to some elite football every week, and now it will be empty. But just because the 49ers aren't playing doesn't mean there aren't important games to watch. That said, here are the four games 49ers fans should watch in Week 8.
This isn't an exciting matchup at all, but the Raiders are the first team the 49ers will face when they emerge from their Bye Week. Seeing how the Raiders perform will give a better idea of how Week 9 will go.
Maybe the Raiders will surprise everyone in this game. Or it will more likely be the usual from them this season. In any case, it's always good to preview an upcoming opponent to see how difficult or easy it will be for the 49ers.
In a few weeks, the 49ers will head to Mexico City to play the Vikings. Minnesota arguably has the best defense in the league, which is going to be tested against the Lions' electric offense.
The Vikings are the last undefeated team, so they're a strong force that mustn't be overlooked despite their weak offense. This matchup will give 49ers fans a better understanding of what's in store for the 49ers down the road.
Plus, the Lions might be a playoff opponent for the 49ers. This is the most insightful game of Week 8 to show where the 49ers stand in the NFC.
Another upcoming opponent for the 49ers is the Cowboys. They'll face them in Week 10 after the Raiders, which is always a premier matchup.
49ers fans can key in on the Cowboys' offense, which has a bunch of firepower, but also bear witness to the mediocrity of their defense. Facing the Cardinals is a minor bonus, as there's not much to learn about them.
Last but not least is the battle on Monday night between the Bears and the Seahawks. This is the most exciting matchup of Week 8, which is part of why 49ers fans should watch.
But most importantly, they're two of the top NFC teams. The 49ers will obviously play the Seahawks again, and they might play Chicago in the playoffs, making this a must-watch game.

title: Predicting the 49ers' Wins and Losses After the Bye Week
full_text:
The Bye Week arrived at the perfect time for the San Francisco 49ers .
After starting the season 6-1 , they receive crucial rest. That will be extremely beneficial as they begin their second- half season push with the playoffs ahead.
They'll surely love to replicate their run as they did in their first seven games, but their schedule will be much tougher. Let's dive into which games the 49ers will win and lose when they emerge from their Bye.
This is about as easy a matchup that the 49ers could've asked for emerging from the Bye. They get to open up at home against the Raiders, who have been in freefall since Week 4.
The Raiders have a putrid defense and cannot run the ball. Aside from Brock Bowers, they don't have a lethal threat to worry about. The 49ers should have no problem defeating them.
It shouldn't be too difficult to beat the Cowboys either. Although they will be a step up in competition from the Raiders. Dallas has some ballers on offense.
But the 49ers have dogs on defense that will exploit how soft the Cowboys are. This should be a fairly easy win for the 49ers to get on the road.
For their second international game of the season, the 49ers will host the Vikings in Mexico City. Minnesota's defense has arguably been the best in the NFL.
Brock Purdy and Kyle Shanahan have also struggled heavily against Brian Flores. That alone will be why the 49ers lose, despite the Vikings' offense being incredibly average at best.
As great as the 49ers were against Seattle in the first matchup, I don't believe they'll have their number this time. The Seahawks will make the proper adjustments and be more motivated than last time. A season split seems fitting between these two juggernauts.
This game has a sloppy outing for the 49ers written all over it. They'll be coming off a war against the Seahawks and will travel to the East Coast, which is always tough, to play a fairly solid Giants team. They might lose this game, but I don't think the Giants are good enough to pull it off.
The Rams may be more motivated in this game than in Week 1, but they're not good. They bought into their offseason hype, and it shows. It'll be a closer matchup than in Australia, but the results will remain the same as they were then.
This doesn't deserve much of an explanation. The Chargers are the worst team in the NFL. There's no way they will salvage their season or have the ability to play well against the 49ers.
This is the premier game on the 49ers' second-half schedule. Not only will it be a good measuring-stick game against a good team, but the 49ers need to finally prove they can beat the Chiefs, and I think they will. What better way to do it than at Arrowhead?
It's over for the Eagles. They won't have Jalen Hurts, and none of their star players are performing up to their ability. This might be an easier outing for the 49ers than against the Chargers.
This game screams "throw away" for the 49ers. Either a bunch of their starters won't play, or they will only play for a time. It has nothing to do with how the Cardinals are.

title: The 5 Best-Performing 49ers at the Bye Week
full_text:
Achieving a 6-1 record at the Bye Week has the San Francisco 49ers in excellent standing.
They couldn't have asked for a better start. A significant reason for their awesome start is thanks to five players who have been their best performers this season. Let's dive into who these five players are.
No stats are needed to explain this. Fred Warner has been a monster this season. Ball carriers hate to see Warner coming because they know he's going to lay a massive hit on them.
Or he's going to punch the ball out, which I am convinced is because his hands have a magnet that is attracted to the material of a football. It's the only way to explain why he's so insanely accurate with those peanut punches.
Warner has been so elite this season that he will have a strong case to be the Defensive Player of the Year if he keeps it up. He leaves everyone in awe with every performance. At this point, I'm out of words.
Aside from his performance in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders, Renardo Green has been on a tear this season. He's easily been the 49ers' best defensive back.
Green is currently tied for the most interceptions (3) in the league, and of the 195 qualified defensive backs, he has the 17th-lowest passer rating allowed (55.1).
He's always had the talent. All Green needed was the right coach to unlock him, which is what makes defensive coordinator Raheem Morris a match made in heaven for him.
It's probably safe to say that Mike Evans has been the best free agent signing by the 49ers under Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch. He's been sensational.
Similar to Warner, you don't need to look at the stats to know or see the impact Evans has made. He's been exactly what the 49ers wanted and more.
Look no further than what he did against the Seattle Seahawks. He said in the offseason that he thinks he's their missing piece and has proven it so far.
I'd argue he's been the 49ers' MVP this season. The 49ers' offense has been elite with him on the field, but in the six quarters without him, it's fallen off significantly.
The 49ers will need to hope and pray that Evans can overcome his Achilles tendinitis quickly. They will have no shot at winning the Super Bowl without him.
It's undeniable that Brock Purdy is playing at a different level this season. He's been sharper than he's ever been, with how accurate his throws have been, the limited mistakes he's made, and his overall playmaking ability.
It's why he's been referenced as the NFL MVP so early in the season. With how sharp Purdy has been playing, he's become a driving force behind the 49ers' offensive success after Evans.
Trent Williams is always a top-five performer on the 49ers, but rather than obviously pointing him out, the entire offensive line deserves recognition. They've been amazing through seven games this season.
They're allowing the lowest pressure rate (26.7%) in the league. Purdy has only been sacked seven times and pressured 62 times on 232 dropbacks.
Pass protection aside, they've done a fine job of opening up rushing lanes for Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. They're easily the best-performing unit of the 49ers entering the Bye Week.

title: 49ers Fans' Bye Week Cheer Guide: Who to Root For Around the NFL
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers ' Week 8 bye couldn't come soon enough as I was about to sign to the practice squad as a wide receiver. I mean, 33-year-old Dad-bod fits the age criteria and the drop off can't be much from what we saw last Sunday in Atlanta.
All jokes aside, hopefully the boys get healthy this weekend before they take on the team that left the Bay for the Vegas lights.
Here are three games to keep your eye on.
The Minnesota Vikings are now gaining respect around the NFL as the only team left without feeling defeat. The Vikings (6-0) travel to Detroit (4-2) to take on the Lions #1 passing offense. Tale of two stories in this one, as it'll be good (Lions offense) vs good (Vikings defense) and bad (Lions defense) vs (Vikings offense).
A Lions win here would help the 49ers NFC Standings as this would be a division loss for the Vikings.
This will be an interesting matchup in the stands, without the 49ers, Raiders, Cowboys, and Steelers as the visiting team. What jersey will everyone be wearing while attending the game?
Nonetheless, the Chargers (0-6) will be fresh off a bye and still winless. I know Jim Harbaugh is pressing for the Chargers to sneak out a win. Mike McDaniel and Justin Herbert will need to be on the same page and not look like the 28th total offense that they are.
Sure, the Rams got "back on track" last week in Las Vegas, but that was against the league's 30th-ranked total defense. The Chargers aren't a world beater by any means, but they come in twice as good, ranked 15th.
Finally, we are back to a great Monday Night Football matchup. Regardless of who wins or loses, the 49ers will benefit.
While the Bears on paper may be a bigger threat to the 49ers because of Chicago's offense and their resurging defense, they are not in division. It's as simple as that.
Seahawks falling to 4-4 would give the 49ers a three-game lead over the second-place NFC West team and provide some space for error, like the loss to the Atlanta Falcons. Plus, the last thing the 49ers need is for the Seahawks to win this game and start playing with that arrogant confidence similar to their Super Bowl run a season ago.
With the 49ers on a bye, hopefully you get to enjoy some stress-free football, besides your fantasy team of course. Make sure to put the Lions, Chargers, and Bears on your Week 8 cheer card.

title: The 4 Worst-Performing 49ers at the Bye Week
full_text:
With the San Francisco 49ers on their Bye Week , it makes for the perfect time to review who their worst performers have been this season. Let's dive in.
By far, kicker Eddy Pineiro has been the worst 49ers player this season. It's been astonishing to see after he was a hero last season when the 49ers finally moved on from Jake Moody.
Pineiro has missed three of his nine field goal attempts this season for a 66.7% conversion rate. But his most egregious performance has come on extra-point attempts.
He's missed 21 of 25 attempts, for an 84% conversion rate. Pineiro has the yips this season and has shown zero signs of getting himself out of it.
It's only a matter of time before he costs the 49ers a game. The one saving grace is that, of all the 49ers who needed the Bye Week, it was Pineiro.
He can use this time away to reset his mind. Usually, the yips is a mental issue, so by being away, Pineiro can forget all of his woes and bounce back for the second half of the season.
What a frustrating player wide receiver Jacob Cowing has been. Most of his issues have been as a punt returner, where he oddly fields punts around the five-yard line rather than letting the ball bounce into the end zone.
Cowing has cost the 49ers valuable field position on numerous occasions this season. His worst play this year was in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks.
Cowing was fielding a punt in the first quarter, and rather than calling an obvious fair catch, he elected to field the punt, allowing a Seahawks player to force a fumble.
Seattle would recover the ball with perfect field position and would score a touchdown shortly thereafter. Cowing has been a negative factor for the 49ers.
Whenever Deebo Samuel gets healthy, they need to have him be the return specialist instead of Cowing. Otherwise, they will make games much more difficult to win.
Cornerback Jack Jones was so bad this season that the 49ers chose him as the player to release when they officially acquired DeForest Buckner.
Jones couldn't make a single positive play after a pretty solid Week 1 outing. The final straw was when he was a penalty machine in the 49ers' loss to the Atlanta Falcons. The 49ers will no longer be subjected to his errant play.
It's not that Nick Bosa has been a bad performer this season. In fact, in the two games he's played, he's been good. However, it's because he's only played two games that he's been a "bad" performer.
Rather, he's been a massive disappointment, so he gets an asterisk in this list. Bosa cannot be relied upon when he returns because it's likely he will get hurt again. He's such a letdown.

title: 49ers TE George Kittle Teams Up With Novartis For Prostate Cancer Awareness
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle has teamed up with Novartis, the NFL's first-ever pharmaceutical partner, to raise awareness of prostate cancer and encourage men to take action through blood-test screening.
"My family connection to prostate cancer comes from my grandpa, my dad's dad. He had prostate cancer about eight to ten years ago and thankfully survived it. He has since passed away, but that was simply due to old age," shared Kittle in an interview with 49ers on SI .
"When he passed, I started talking to my dad more about my grandpa and his experience with prostate cancer. It was around the same time I started talking with Novartis about a potential partnership, so the two things went hand in hand. It was a strange connection at just the right time.
"I learned that one in eight men will test positive for prostate cancer, which I think are incredible odds. I had no idea that was the case."
Kittle's aim with this campaign is to encourage open conversations with friends and family about getting a blood test. Novartis states that "prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer death among men in the United States".
He wants to encourage people to be more open about the subject and help break down the stigma surrounding it, ultimately encouraging them to speak to a doctor if needed.
"To an extent, I think things are getting better [with more awareness]. More people are becoming aware and wanting to learn more," shared Kittle.
"But, like I said, I've never really had a conversation about it with my friendship group. We never talked about it until I started working with Novartis and brought it up. I asked my friends, 'Have you guys ever thought about this?' and they said no.
"I told them they should maybe have a conversation with their dads and bring it up with them. It's a pretty simple blood test.
"I think we're possibly getting past the taboo, but at the same time, you still have friends who say, 'I'm good. I don't need that. I don't need to talk about it.'
"It's like, 'Hey, man, I just want what's best for you. I want you to live a long life so we can go and play plenty of golf together.' So, if you need to get a blood test, just go and get one. It's pretty easy."
The campaign highlights the importance of early detection and encourages men to find out more at RelaxItsaBloodTest.com . Novartis states that "early detection leads to a greater than 99% relative 5-year survival rate."
Kittle followed up with some powerful words, highlighting the importance of awareness, early detection and supporting those affected by cancer: "We're all in this life together, and I'd much rather help as many people as I can than just focus on doing things on my own.
"If I can spread a little awareness and encourage a few guys who otherwise wouldn't get tested to go and have a blood test that might save their lives, then I think that's absolutely worth working with Novartis for.
"It's something that affects all of us, so we just want to spread awareness and keep people up to date with current developments and what's going on."

title: These Big Surprises are the Reason the 49ers are 6-1 at the Bye
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers don't have a game this week, as they're in the middle of a much-needed Bye . That makes it the perfect time to look at the four biggest surprises from their season so far. Let's dive in.
All offseason, fans portrayed the 49ers' offensive line as one of the worst units in the NFL. They were pounding the table for the team to sign or draft an offensive lineman to boost the position.
The 49ers didn't add anyone worth noting to the position, so it was believed that the offensive line would be putrid this season. The reality is that the offensive line was always fine.
Sure enough, they're proving that not only are they fine, but they're a stout unit. They didn't allow a single sack of Brock Purdy through the first four games of the season.
That had only happened four other times in the NFL since 1990. It was insane to see how great they were in pass protection, and it hasn't let up much.
Purdy has dropped back to pass 232 times and has only been sacked seven times and pressured 62 times. The 49ers' offensive line allows the lowest pressure rate (26.7%) in the NFL.
They have played a significant role in the 49ers' 6-1 start. Who could've foreseen that coming, especially after they were scrutinized in the past year.
Unlike the offensive line, which was undeserving of their criticism, the 49ers' safeties were absolutely valid for theirs. It was easily the worst position on the 49ers entering the 2026 season.
Ji'Ayir Brown was a known liability who was never getting any better. Malik Mustapha forgot how to tackle and take proper angles last season. Marques Sigle showed a lot of promise, but struggled in pass coverage.
Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris had his work cut out for him with this group. And boy, has he made a difference. All of the safeties have performed admirably well this season.
Brown isn't playing lights out, but he hasn't been anywhere close to the issue he was last season. Mustapha looks like a ferocious tiger out there. He's taken off.
And before Sigle got hurt, he was playing incredibly well-rounded. He took the proper next steps that were needed. The safeties look immaculate this year, and it's taken the 49ers' defense to another level.
It's uncommon for the 49ers to receive massive gains from their rookies. However, this year's draft class has been giving them amazing contributions.
Gracen Halton has been a stud, Jaden Dugger is extremely versatile, Romello Height is hitting his stride, and Kaelon Black adds a new dynamic to the offense.
Just imagine if De'Zhaun Stribling were healthy. The 49ers' rookies have been awesome this year and are playing a key role in the team's success so far.
It's not surprising to see Brock Purdy perform well. He's proven to be a really good player before, but this season, he's clearly taken it up a notch,
He looks way more comfortable this season than he has in any other. Part of that is thanks to his offensive line playing great, but even when the protection or play breaks down, he's cool as a cucumber.
Purdy has also been delivering a bunch of dimes this season, mostly to Mike Evans. His hot start has fueled MVP narratives, which is ridiculous considering it's early in the season for that topic.
In any case, Purdy has been sharp. He looks improved this year by playing within himself, and that has allowed the 49ers' offense to thrive.

title: The 49ers Would be Foolish not to Go All In for a Wide Receiver
full_text:
The 49ers are 6-1, they just added DeForest Buckner, and they’re sitting in their bye week. On paper, it’s a team ready to chase a championship. But the receiver room tells a different story, and the Nov. 10 trade deadline is the last chance to fix it.
The Falcons Game Was a Warning
San Francisco’s first loss of the year, 29-20 in Atlanta, came with only four active wide receivers. The offense gave the ball away four times, two of them Brock Purdy interceptions. A team with a healthy receiver room doesn’t play that way. That game showed what happens when the Niners lose even a little depth at the position.
Mike Evans has been everything the 49ers hoped for when they signed him. He has 27 catches for 420 yards and three touchdowns in six games, and Kyle Shanahan has talked openly about how much he trusts him. But he’s been dealing with injured ribs and Achilles tendinitis, which kept him out of the Falcons game. John Lynch said this week that the goal is to calm the Achilles down and that Evans is making progress.
Maybe he comes back strong for Week 9 against the Raiders. But Achilles problems have a way of lingering, and Evans is in his 13th season. Planning a title run around his health is risky.
Deebo Samuel was off to a great start in his return to San Francisco. In four games, he caught 16 of 20 targets for 206 yards and three touchdowns, and he added nine carries for 78 yards. Then he hurt his hamstring against the Seahawks and has been out since. Shanahan says he has a chance to return in Week 9, but “a chance” isn’t a plan.
De’Zhaun Stribling looked like a star in the preseason. The No. 33 pick put up seven catches in a single half against the Titans, and Purdy raved about him. Then he hurt his ankle in Week 1 and missed at least a month on injured reserve. He’s a rookie, and rookies are going to be inconsistent in December and January, especially in the playoffs. Stribling should be part of this team’s future, not the main reason it wins now.
The Seahawks are the defending champions, and their defense has owned this team lately. They beat the Niners 13-3 in Week 18 last season and then 41-6 in the divisional round. The Niners did win 32-29 in Seattle in Week 5, but it took two fourth-quarter scoring drives, and it cost Deebo his hamstring.
San Francisco will probably see Seattle again in the playoffs. Against a defense that good, the offense needs receivers who can win one-on-one and run every route. Being deep isn’t enough.
Garrett Wilson is the best fit I can think of. He’s 37-for-51 for 444 yards and three touchdowns on a bad Jets team, and he can win from any alignment. Evans is a big-bodied red zone threat, and Deebo is a gadget player who needs the ball in space. Wilson would be the true No. 1 who runs the full route tree, and Purdy would have a target he can trust on third down.
He’d also solve next year’s problem. Evans is 33 and Deebo has missed time again. Wilson is the long-term answer.
Wilson isn’t cheap. He’s reportedly making around $30 million a year, and the Jets will want a first-round pick. I’d give them one. My offer is a 2027 first-rounder plus a mid-round pick, something like a third. I wouldn’t include Stribling or any young starters. The Niners’ draft picks matter less than the title window they have right now.
This roster has elite players at several spots, a quarterback who’s playing well and a coaching staff that knows how to win. The one thing that can derail it is the receiver room. If Evans’s Achilles flares up in January or Deebo’s hamstring doesn’t hold, the Niners will be trying to beat Seattle with a rookie and a thin group behind him.
The deadline is Nov. 10. If the front office passes on a move like this, it’ll be a mistake.

title: Buccaneers Reveal Good News Right Before Falcons Matchup
full_text:
Every game is a must-win game for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at this point, but this game on Sunday vs. the Atlanta Falcons could very well make or break Tampa Bay's season.
The Bucs are 1.5 games out of first place in the NFC South. The Carolina Panthers lost their Thursday Night Football game to the Green Bay Packers (and fired a good number of their defensive staff as a result), so if the Bucs beat the Falcons, they'll be just 1.5 games back from the NFC South lead.
Naturally, Tampa Bay will want every starter it can have to try and win this game. And it looks like one questionable key offensive player will indeed play today against the Falcons.
Right tackle Luke Goedeke has been dealing with a calf injury for the last two weeks. He didn't play against the Panthers and did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday this week, but he did practice Friday — and now, he's slated to play.
Goedeke is active against the Falcons today. With no practice squad elevations, he'll almost certainly play against Atlanta, giving the offensive line a big boost against a Falcons front that can get a lot of good pressure with four players.
Swing tackle Ben Chukwuma played in Goedeke's stead last week. He won't have to do so again this week, as Goedeke will anchor down the right side while All-Pro Tristan Wirfs holds down the left side.
Goedeke will be a crucial player. The Bucs may need to establish the run in inclement weather, and Atlanta boasts the fourth-best run defense in the NFL by rushing yards per game. If running back Bucky Irving is going to get going, he'll need Goedeke's help to do it, and that could be the key to controlling the clock and beating an Atlanta team that just knocked off the San Francisco 49ers the week prior.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. at Raymond James Stadium.

title: 2 Position Groups That Need to Step Up for Buccaneers to Beat Falcons
full_text:
After a brutal start to the 2026 NFL season for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , there's all of a sudden a slight glimmer of hope.
After pummeling the Panthers in Carolina last weekend 43-13, the Bucs are now looking to string together back-to-back regular season victories for the first time in over a year. More importantly, with the Atlanta Falcons coming to town on Sunday, the Buccaneers will have a chance to make up even more ground in the division with the Panthers having already lost this week's matchup to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday.
Even though the Falcons and Panthers both sit at 3-4 atop the NFC South standings, the Falcons have a -2 point differential on the season compared to Carolina's -15. Interestingly enough, the Buccaneers, who are looking up at both teams with their 2-5 record, are +11 in the point differential category.
A win against Atlanta this week would be massive for the Buccaneers to close the gap in the NFC South standings. And with four divisional games still to be played, Tampa Bay would all of a sudden have a very realistic path to push for the top seed in the South by season's end.
Conversely, a loss to Atlanta would not only put the Bucs even further behind these teams in the standings, but it could signify the end of their competitive window this year and potentially turn the Bucs into sellers ahead of the Nov. 10th trade deadline.
In other words, even though we aren't quite at the halfway mark, the result of this Sunday's game against the Falcons could very well determine the fate of the 2026 Buccaneers.
Let's take a look at two key position groups that will need to step up in order for the Buccaneers to get a much-needed victory this weekend.
Although Todd Bowles' defense has really established itself as one of the league's better all-around units, there are still flaws to be found.
Most obvious among them is veteran LB Alex Anzalone who, despite signing a substantial contract to become a key leader of this defense in the offseason, has struggled mightily in all facets. Far too often, Anzalone loses his footing, fails to shed blocks, takes poor angles and misses tackles. Even more concerning is that he's been more of a liability in pass coverage than the asset that he was advertised to be coming over from Detroit.
Thankfully, his rookie running mate, Josiah Trotter, has been superb . That being said the Buccaneers have struggled as a unit when it comes to defending opposing tight ends. Meanwhile, Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts, though inconsistent, always seems to be a problem for the Buccaneers.
Trotter needs to keep playing how he has been, but Anzalone must step up in order to contain Pitts, who remains one of the most gifted pass-catching tight ends in the game. Throw in the challenge of defending the best running back in football, Bijan Robinson, and the importance of the Buccaneers' linebacker duo stepping up on Sunday becomes that much more obvious.
Even after Mike Evans surprised everyone by leaving Tampa Bay in the offseason, the Buccaneers remained confident in their WR room because of the quality depth they'd assembled leading up to that moment. Unfortunately, though, the Bucs' talented collection of pass catchers hasn't come close to producing the results everyone expected.
Although Chris Godwin has proven in the past to be a game changer, we've yet to see that version of the Bucs' veteran this season. The team's supposed number one WR, Emeka Egbuka, is unlikely to suit up in this game due to a foot injury and Jalen McMillan remains without a timetable for return.
Young receivers like Tez Johnson and Ted Hurst have both performed well in limited opportunities, but they'll need to be targeted more in this game in order to take the top off the defense and open up other opportunities for Zac Robinson's offense .
Although the Buccaneers managed to dominate the Panthers last weekend while passing for just 64 yards in the game, that's unlikely to be replicated against the Falcons, who present a much stouter run defense. As a result, the Bucs will need to attack the Falcons through the air in order to keep them honest. With Mayfield still nursing a thumb injury on his throwing hand, even more of that responsibility will fall on the Bucs' pass catchers.
In order for the Bucs to be effective through the air against Atlanta, they'll need to take some shots downfield to both Johnson and Hurst while utilizing Chris Godwin at all levels of the field. If those players are able to create separation against the Falcons' defensive backs, it will make life that much easier on Mayfield and significantly increase the Bucs' chances of winning this critical game.

title: How Buccaneers' Bucky Irving Seperated Himself in the NFL This Month
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have won two games. In those two games they won, there was a common denominator.
Running back Bucky Irving didn't get to do much in 2025, as he was injured early in the season and came back late while he was recovering. This year, though, he's played in every game, and he's made his presence known in more ways than one.
The Bucs have won twice in October, and during this month, Irving has been the reason why. He's had some huge games, and as it turns out, he's separated himself from the rest of the NFL in a big way.
Irving put up 378 rushing yards in the month of October. That's the most in the league among any player in that same time frame.
OK, Bucky pic.twitter.com/UBuSl8fr5T
Irving has 21 more rushing yards than the next-highest player, New York Jets running back Braelon Allen, at 357. Rounding out the list are Carolina Panthers running back Chubba Hubbard (356), Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson (355), Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (345) and Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker (341).
The brunt of these rushing yards came in two games for Irving. Irving exploded against the Dallas Cowboys, running for 165 yards on 21 attempts. He also went wild against the Panthers, scampering for 106 yards on 24 attempts.
So far this season, Irving has put up 558 rushing yards for 4.7 yards per carry. He also has four touchdowns on the ground this year.
The Bucs paired Irving up with Kenny Gainwell this offseason in free agency with the expectation that Gainwell would get some significant looks, but so far, Irving has gotten the brunt of the work in Zac Robinson's offense. Given that he's been one of the best running backs in football this year, it's unlikely that Irving will see some reduced carries anytime soon.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. on Sunday in Raymond James Stadium. The Falcons have one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, so it will be hard for Irving to get going — but he's proven this year that he can make it happen at any moment.

title: Buccaneers Will Face This Falcons Star at Home For the First Time on Sunday
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are no strangers to playing the Atlanta Falcons. The two teams have been locked in a divisional rivalry for years in the NFC South, and they've had plenty of notable battles in that time frame.
They are mostly strangers, however, to Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. The Falcons drafted Penix in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft, but ever since then, he's played the Buccaneers just one time — he was the quarterback for the Falcons last year when the Bucs beat them 23-20 in Atlanta to open the season.
Now, Penix is set to start against the Bucs for just the second time on Sunday. And that start is a milestone for both him and the Buccaneers.
The Buccaneers will host Penix and the Falcons on Sunday, and it will mark the first time that Tampa Bay has played Penix at Raymond James Stadium. The Bucs haven't beaten the Falcons in Raymond James Stadium since Oct. 9, 2022, but the Bucs have generally faced Kirk Cousins or Desmond Ridder in that time span.
This will also be Penix's first time at Raymond James Stadium, which means it will be the first time he's had an NFL homecoming. Penix grew up in the Tampa Bay area in Dade City, so this will be his first NFL game in his home region despite being drafted by the Falcons three seasons ago.
Penix may have grown up in the Tampa Bay area, but he insinuated at a press conference earlier this week that, because of Tampa Bay's lack of success during most of his life, he did not grow up a Bucs fan.
"Nah, I was never a Bucs fan," Penix said this week in the lead-up to the game. "I think the year I was born was the year they won the Super Bowl. And after that, as I was growing up... I wasn't a fan of the Bucs."
Michael Penix Jr. when asked if he was a Bucs fan growing up in Dade City, just north of Tampa “Nahhhh I was never a Bucs fan” pic.twitter.com/W11ZlVY6jO
The Bucs, however, seem to be fans of his. Head coach Todd Bowles had a lot of good things to say about Penix, and he's certainly keeping Penix's skill set in mind as he game plans to defeat him for the second time in his career.
"He can throw the ball. He's got great zip on the ball and great timing on the football – [a] strong arm," Bowles said. "He can get out of the pocket. He runs a lot better than you think he can run. He's really not giving the ball away. They're doing a great job taking care of the football, which is going to be critical in this game. We’ve been getting [interceptions], but they're a hard team to get them off of, and he's playing winning football."
The Bucs will face off against Penix and the Falcons at 1 p.m. on Sunday in Tampa.

title: Buccaneers' Rookie Already Establishing Himself As Major NFL Draft Steal
full_text:
Regardless of where they went to college, who coached them, or what position they played, the NFL is a massive adjustment for every first-year player.
The intensity, speed, physicality, intelligence and technique of NFL players are world-class, and even if a particular player was utterly dominant at the collegiate level, that doesn't necessarily mean it will translate to the next level. In fact, it often doesn't.
This is largely why the NFL Draft is so unpredictable. Not just in terms of predicting what positions or players teams will select, but also for NFL GMs and front office executives trying to forecast which prospects will continue to ascend at the NFL level and which will not.
With the 2026 NFL season just about at the halfway point, we've now got enough of a sample size to begin reflecting on this year's rookie class, assess how the prospects selected are making out as NFL players, and give credit where it's due.
This is exactly what ESPN sought to do this week when they ranked the top 10 rookies in the NFL so far.
Located within the ranking behind former Ohio State defenders Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, both of whom occupy the top two spots, and just behind Browns' WR Denzel Boston, who was listed third, you'll find impressive Buccaneers rookie LB Josiah Trotter ranked as the fourth-best rookie of the 2026 draft class, according to ESPN.
With 62 tackles, one sack, and one interception, Trotter has made his impact felt early and often this season, outplaying his veteran LB partner, Alex Anzalone, by a massive margin.
Here's what NFL expert Matt Bowen had to say about the decision to rank Trotter as the fourth-best rookie so far.
"Trotter's play recognition stands out on the tape," Bowen wrote. "He is quick to diagnose against the run, getting eyes on formation keys and pulling guards to make tackles. His 43% run-stop win rate ranks 10th among all linebackers, and he has the physical play style to drop the hammer on contact."
The article also mentioned Trotter's impressive performance in coverage, which is something that was considered a potential knock on him coming out of Missouri as a prospect.
"Plus, Trotter has created some on-the-ball production in coverage, which includes a pick-six on quarterback Joe Burrow and the Bengals," Bowen wrote. "He's an ascending player who can also be schemed as a blitzer in Todd Bowles' defense."
For prospects taken outside of the first 32 picks, it usually takes a little extra time to earn the respect of those around the league. These players aren't given the benefit of the doubt or viewed with a biased lens in the same way first-rounders are. This makes Trotter's ranking in the top five all the more impressive, as he was taken with the 46th overall pick.
Some valuable context that should be viewed in a very positive light by Bucs fans is the fact that every other player listed in ESPN's ranking of the top-10 rookies was drafted ahead of Trotter. This means that not only did the Buccaneers draft themselves an exceptional player at a key position, but they got incredible value on that selection.
Considering this is the first season in 15 years where the Buccaneers are playing without Lavonte David manning the middle of their defense, they should count their lucky stars, because it appears as though they may have found a player to take his place.

title: Buccaneers Have One Distinct Advantage Over Falcons
full_text:
Zac Robinson spent two seasons as the offensive coordinator for the Atlanta Falcons. Since joining the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the offseason, it's taken some time for Robinson to fully understand the new tools he has to work with in Tampa Bay.
Although Robinson's tenure didn't get off to the roaring start he imagined as the 2026 season has gone on, we've begun to see glimpses of what he's capable of when it comes to running an efficient offense that plays to the strengths of the roster.
In the Buccaneers' two victories this season against the Cowboys (24-16) and Panthers (43-13), Robinson did a tremendous job of sticking with what worked.
The fact that he managed to scheme up a plan of attack in Dallas with UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels as his starting quarterback proves he has the flexibility to alter his approach depending on who he has available on a given day. The same could be said for how he attacked the Panthers' defense with Mayfield still recovering from a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand.
Although the 43-point outburst against the Panthers last weekend was impressive, nine of those came directly from the defense or special teams. Still, Robinson's group was responsible for 34 of those points, and they managed to do it with just 64 yards passing.
The Bucs' run-first approach in this game established dominance at the line of scrimmage while featuring all three running backs — Bucky Irving, Kenneth Gainwell, and Sean Tucker — in different roles. With 258 rushing yards total, it's safe to say that Robinson was wise to stick with the run. This approach also helped to take some stress off Mayfield, who was surely battling through plenty of discomfort.
After the Panthers lost to the Packers on Thursday night, the Bucs have a golden opportunity to make up ground on the two teams ahead of them in the standings when they face off with the Falcons this Sunday at Raymond James Stadium.
Not only is the Buccaneers' defense absolutely humming coming into this game, but the team finally has a bit of momentum following their domination in Carolina last week. The Falcons have a ton of weapons, especially on offense, but the Buccaneers will have one key advantage heading into this matchup — familiarity.
Robinson knows each of the Falcons' best offensive players, RB Bijan Robinson, QB Michael Penix, WR Drake London and TE Kyle Pitts extremely well. He knows their strengths, weaknesses (aside from Bijan, who seemingly has none), tendencies and preferences. That means he also knows what looks give them the most trouble.
This could be hugely advantageous to the Buccaneers, as it would be wise for Todd Bowles to include Robinson in plenty of defensive meetings this week to ensure that the Bucs' defensive game plan is tailored specifically for the opponent they are facing.
Thanks to Zac Robinson's time in Atlanta, the Falcons are an opponent they should know inside and out. And in the NFL, you better capitalize on every advantage you have.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. in Tampa Bay on Nov. 1.

title: Our Buccaneers vs. Falcons Score Predictions Are In
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a must-win game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. A win puts them within striking distance of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead, while a loss would put them even further behind this season.
It should be a close one against a better Falcons team, and our panel of writers reflect that. Here are our picks for Tampa Bay's big matchup against Atlanta:
Despite the Bucs' dismantling of the Panthers last week, I still find it difficult to have much confidence in them heading into the matchup against the rising Atlanta Falcons.
The offense can only lean on the run game for so long, so they must figure out how to attack defenses through the air.
The defense and special teams have been great as of late and will need to show up in a big way again.
While I do think the Bucs have a better shot at beating the Falcons now than I did a couple of weeks ago, I think the Falcons' defense will find a way to slow down the run game and force the Bucs to throw the ball.
That hasn’t been great for them this year, and ultimately will be the downfall of them this week.
Despite having a fantastic game last week, I think the Buccaneers will come back down to earth in this matchup. I don’t believe Baker Mayfield is fully healthy yet, and they drop this one because of it.
The Buccaneers and Falcons are a fun matchup. Todd Bowles' defense has really turned it up in recent weeks, while the Falcons have several dangerous weapons on offense.
Assuming Mayfield’s thumb feels quite a bit better than it did a week ago, I think the Bucs’ offense can do just enough to squeeze out a victory while extending the Bucs’ record to 2-0 in the division and narrowing the gap between them and the NFC South-leading Panthers.
I think the Bucs do end up winning this game, and it has to do with Todd Bowles’ rush defense, which has been excellent this year.
Adding that with strong secondary play and getting Antoine Winfield Jr. back to help defend Atlanta’s passing attack, it looks nice.
It’s going to be a close one, but I like Tampa Bay and a bold prediction of Cade Otton having a good showing.
Tampa Bay didn't have to pass much against the Carolina Panthers to beat them. Atlanta has a strong rushing defense, so they won't let the Bucs beat them that way — Tampa Bay will have to go through the air.
I'm still not confident that Zac Robinson's offense can do that against this Falcons team. Baker Mayfeld is still recovering from injury and BIjan Robinson can change games on his own — Bucs drop this one in Raymond James.
This is among the closest prediction slates we've had all year. Some of us believe the Bucs will keep the momentum going, while other writers think Tampa Bay will falter as it has multiple times this year.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. in Tampa Bay on Nov. 1.

title: Buccaneers Reveal Good News and Bad News Before Falcons Game
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to play a crucial game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.
With a Carolina Panthers loss on Thursday night against the Green Bay Packers, the Bucs remain just 1.5 games out of the division lead. If Tampa Bay wins on Sunday against the Falcons, they'll be within half a game of the NFC South crown.
The Bucs lost their game at home to the Falcons last year during the infamous "3rd & 28" scenario, but they beat the Falcons on the road to begin that season. They had a lot of help from their rookie wide receiver that year, but one year later, that wideout won't be available for Tampa Bay during this matchup.
Todd Bowles confirmed that wide receiver Emeka Egbuka will be out for Sunday.
Egbuka was a big contributor in Tampa Bay's win against the Falcons last year, but he won't be playing in this game. Egbuka suffered a concussion against the Pittsburgh Steelers and appeared to clear protocol on Thursday, shedding a black non-contact jersey for his regular one, but he wasn't participating at all on Friday.
Egbuka has also been dealing with a foot injury on top of his concussion. Bowles said Friday that Egbuka cleared concussion protocol, but that his foot is still injured.
Tackle Luke Goedeke, meanwhile, was out last week against the Carolina Panthers with a calf injury and he did not participate in the first two days of practice. He did participate in this last day of practice this week, and Bowles said that he has a chance to play on Sunday, which is very encouraging for the Bucs — Goedeke has been an excellent right tackle this season.
If Goedeke can't go, though, Ben Chukwuma will fill in for him instead. Chukwuma filled in for Goedeke against the Panthers last week, and he played well — Bowles praised his effort the following Monday. He'd be up again to replace Goedeke, and if Goedeke cannot go, the team would certainly feel good about his abilities heading into Sunday.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. in Raymond James Stadium Nov. 1. They won't have their star wideout, but they could have one of their best offensive linemen.

title: Bucs Finally Have a Huge Advantage Against Falcons Nobody is Talking About
full_text:
Tampa Bay has always been a hot spot for transplants from up north. With that, those people have brought their fandom for other teams to the community that boasts three professional sports teams of their own.
That has been obvious for years whenever you tune into Tampa Bay Buccaneers home games.
While plenty of Bucs fans make up the crowd, over the years, there has consistently been a large contingent of opposing fans in the stands.
It's becoming an issue that has brought frustration amongst Tampa Bay fans, and that couldn't have been clearer than when the Pittsburgh Steelers fans practically took over Raymond James Stadium.
However, in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons, the Bucs will likely have an advantage in the stands.
Despite Atlanta being relatively close to Tampa compared to numerous other organizations, their fanbase is not known to travel well, and those Atlanta natives don't make up a large portion of those who have moved to the area or visit during the cooler months of the year.
It should align with the Bucs having their most fans in the stadium this season. That is big for a team that can live and die by momentum.
Fans and crowd noise can carry a team to victory, and the Buccaneers will be hopeful that their fans bring it on Sunday as they search to start 2-0 in the division and continue their midseason turnaround.
It's the most important game up to this point in the season. With the Panthers losing to the Packers on Thursday night, the Bucs could find themselves right at the top of the division if they beat the Falcons on Sunday.
With a win, the Bucs, Falcons, and Panthers would all have three wins on the season, but the Bucs would be 2-0 in the division. There is nothing quite like the NFC South.
There is a ton on the line this week, so the fans must bring the atmosphere to help the players on the field continue their recent surge of great play at every level.

title: Buccaneers Have a Major Problem Nobody Expected This Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' passing offense is averaging 150.4 yards per game. That is the worst in the entire NFL and is certainly not what fans and the organization had in mind this season when thinking about the offense.
There are a lot of factors as to why this aspect of the game has been so disappointing. Baker Mayfield missed three games due to a dislocated thumb, you had undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels filling in and the offensive line has struggled to keep either quarterback upright to make plays.
However, there are too many good players in this offense for the passing attack to be this poor. Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin Jr., Ted Hurst III, Tez Johnson and Cade Otton have simply not been getting the football enough, and that is both on the quarterbacks and offensive coordinator Zach Robinson.
One thing the Bucs have been doing well under Zac Robinson is running the football. The team is coming off one of the best team rushing performances in franchise history, and head coach Todd Bowles even went so far as to say the run game is their calling card.
"I mean, I think that's our calling card. We play a lot better when we run the ball very successfully, whether we're home or on the road," Bowles said. "We haven't had much success at home, running the football or winning at home, but we've got to turn that around and win a home game."
Robinson has also said that this offense needs to be established through the run game.
"Yeah, if we can do that every week, that would be outstanding," Robinson said. "You always want to be able to establish a run and be able to have things that play off of the run game. Then, there [are] going to be weeks where, shoot, you might not have as many run opportunities and you're going to get back on track. That's the nature of the NFL — everything is week to week. If we can play like that, it'll definitely help us out in the long run."
Time will tell if we do see legitimate improvement in the passing game going forward. But it seems like right now the team is content to be a run-first offense and take shots in the passing attack when they can.

title: Titans' Road Duel vs. Bengals: 2 Ways Tennessee Can Spark Hope... Even in a Loss
full_text:
We'll say it over and over again: Moral victories don't count for much. At the same time, the Tennessee Titans have counted few actual victories this season. At 1-6, and now having traded away their best player, it's about taking what you can if you're Tennessee at this point.
What's exciting about the guys that remain? What can Robert Saleh and Mike Borgonzi build on alongside their newly-acquired draft assets? Are the young players still developing as needed? These are the questions Tennessee should be asking right now.
Of course, an actual win is the ultimate positive - but without the shorthanded Titans surprising a 4-2 playoff team on the road, here are two ways Tennessee can generate some positivity even if they do fall short today.
In the absence of Simmons, the Titans desperately need other members of the defensive line to step up. This is a unit that looked weak enough with Simmons as-was; without him, the outlook is bleak for the forseeable future.
Still, with Jonah Laulu being picked up off waivers and Nazir Stackhouse seeing a recent uptick in snaps ( and production ), there are pieces here that have the opportunity to prove themselves.
Between now and the offseason, guys on the d-line are essentially auditioning to keep their spots post-draft and however else Saleh decides to shake things up prior to his second year. Few players are safe (outside of veterans like John Franklin-Myers and Jermaine Johnson II).
That makes for shifting sands in the future, but a massive window for multiple players right now. Seeing Laulu, Stackhouse, or someone else produce would be a solid sign of progress in Week 8.
To say that the stove is boiling under Cam Ward right now would be an understatement. Not only has his recent play caused doubt about his future as the team's leader, but the Simmons trade opened the door to worry about how this franchise actually feels about him.
It's no longer unfair to say that Ward could soon be short on time as the undisputed starter in Nashville. He's thrown for 200+ yards only one time this season. His 4-5 touchdown-to-interception ratio is the simplest way to show he's fallen behind in year two.
But with a solid showing at Paycor Stadium fresh off a roster-shaking move? Ward could buy himself a bit of faith amidst a sea of unanswered questions for Tennessee.
The climb is tough with his favorite target, rookie WR Carnell Tate, confirmed to sit for the contest. All the same, the gate remains open for Ward to re-earn the hope that he gave this franchise when he was taken first overall last year. That hope would go a long way for the Titans right now.

title: Predicting Titans' Starters vs. Bengals: Who replaces Jeffery Simmons at DT?

title: 1 Titans WR Has the Perfect Window to Audition for a Trade in Week 8 vs. Bengals
full_text:
Few people, if anyone, expected Jeffery Simmons to be the first Titan that Tennessee would trade this season. It could probably be safely argued that few people expected the team to move their longtime cornerstone at all. Yet, here they stand short of Simmons heading into Week 8.
In a seriously shorthanded matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals - as both WR Carnell Tate and RB Tyjae Spears are out with injuries - this road duel feels most important as it relates to the November 10 trade deadline. Who is realistically next on the chopping block for Tennessee?
The big names seem to be Tony Pollard, Amani Hooker, and even Alontae Taylor. However, nobody has a better opportunity on paper to audition for their potential next team than Calvin Ridley.
Ridley entered this season as a starter in the Titans' offense on the outside, though he's quickly faded out of relevancy in favor of second-year WR Elic Ayomanor. Ridley now remains involved in a limited fashion, boasting little more than his veteran presence.
He's technically questionable for tomorrow's contest, but was a full participant in Friday's practice. The stars are aligning for Ridley to take the field.
With only five receptions for 81 yards on the year, it's clear that Ridley's role with the Titans has almost totally waned. But at 31 years old and operating on a restructured contract, the value of Ridley may not be lost on a more competitive team in need of complimentary minutes at WR.
Tate being on the bench is obviously bad news for the Titans, but it almost certainly means more clock for Ridley. If Tennessee starts playing from behind (as is unfortunately expected), Ridley will have perhaps his best chance of the year to get going.
It could not come at a better time for either party. Tennessee appears to be on the brink of a full-on fire sale, and a "look what I can do" outing from Ridley would help light that fuse.
Ridley did eclipse 1,000 yards just two years ago in his first (and only) 17-game season with the Titans. Staying healthy has been a problem, with his most recent injury being hip-related, but the vet is paced well to surpass the mere seven games he played last season. He's only missed one game in 2026 up to now.
If Ridley does play in Week 8, an increase in snaps poses him well for a near-future trade. The former Alabama sensation simply doesn't fit the system in Nashville anymore. We'll watch closely to see if this comes to fruition as the trade deadline puts pressure on every possibility.

title: 3 Keys to a Surprise Titans Win Over the Bengals in Week 8
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans aren't expected to come out on top in Week 8, to say the least. The NFL's Preview Picks are 10-0 in favor of the Cincinnati Bengals, with not a single prediction even allowing the Titans the benefit of a single-digit loss.
It's an anticipated blowout across the board, but Tennessee can't be counted out just yet. This is a team with their backs against the wall coming off a trade that, from all angles, is meant to improve the roster down the road. Will a cornered group finally fight back this week?
We won't know until tomorrow, but here are three boxes Tennessee would have to check if they were to pull off a surprise victory on Sunday.
Tony Pollard is coming off his best game of the season for Tennessee, and one of the best games of his career. With Tyjae Spears confirmed to sit, Brian Daboll's offense should continue to lean into their veteran RB without a shadow of a doubt.
Will Pollard replicate his career-high-tying, three-touchdown showing in Cincy? Probably not, but he doesn't necessarily need to in order to put Tennessee in a solid position to compete.
So long as Pollard is able to chunk out medium gains and capitalize when he's called on in late-drive, short-yardage situations (assuming the Titans get into those scenarios), he'll have checked his box. Daboll should be scheming heavily for Pollard if Tennessee is to stay afloat on the road.
Of course, forcing a turnover without Jeffery Simmons is going to be a whole lot harder. But last week, the Titans' two takeaways were generated by CB Cor'Dale Flott and LB Anthony Hill Jr.
Both those guys are running it back this week. On the defensive side of the ball, Tennessee has to continue finding ways to disrupt. This is especially crucial in taking on the Bengals' elite offense.
Having scored 30+ points two straight weeks, the Joe-Burrow-led Bengals will attempt to carve the Titans up by way of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins every chance they get. Cincinnati is fifth in passing yards per game in the NFL, with an average of 264.
It's the tallest task to ask of a unit short Simmons. Even so, Robert Saleh was brought to Nashville on the basis of his defensive expertise. If the Titans ever needed a great defensive scheme to cover up holes in the personnel, it's in Week 8.
Cam Ward doesn't have to be electric this week. Again, the Titans will fare the best if they're able to stay in this contest by way of Pollard's work on the ground.
But the Titans still need Ward to be better than he has been. Tennessee needs consistency. The second-year QB has thrown a pick in five straight contests; doing away with his mistakes, as well as working against Tennessee's typically abysmal first halves, would go a long way.
If Ward can come out warm - not necessarily hot - and put enough pressure on the Bengals' defense that opposing DC Al Golden doesn't just stack the box to stop Pollard on every important down, he should at least be able to stop this thing from getting out of hand.
Factor in a flipped field or two from the defense, and you never know... even if you feel like you almost certainly do.

title: 3 Storylines to Watch in Titans' Week 8 Matchup vs. Bengals: The Spotlight is Hot on Cam Ward
full_text:
After suffering a last-second 27-24 defeat to the Cleveland Browns at home, the Tennessee Titans are essentially in football's dreaded no man's land. The Titans sit toward the bottom of the AFC standings with a 1-6 record. They are essentially eliminated from playoff contention, and it's not even November yet.
Nonetheless, this matchup could carry serious future playoff implications for the Bengals and draft positioning for Tennessee. While the Titans are on a two-game losing skid with a struggling young quarterback, Cincinnati is jockeying with the Browns, Steelers and Ravens in a competitive AFC North title race.
Here are three major storylines to keep an eye on as the Titans head into The Jungle on Sunday.
Throughout the season, RB Tony Pollard has had a heavy workload despite being considered near the end of his prime for his position at age 29. Pollard has the 10th-most carries in the NFL this season, and I suspect that isn't unintentional.
Against Cleveland last week, Pollard had a monstrous three-touchdown performance with 155 yards from scrimmage. It was Pollard's first three-touchdown game since 2022 and his first time gaining 100-plus all-purpose yards all season.
The Titans have already declared themselves as a seller at the NFL's upcoming trade deadline by swapping the franchise's best player, DT Jeffery Simmons, to the Chicago Bears for three future picks, including two first-rounders.
My theory is the Titans will continue to feed Pollard as the primary back against Cincinnati to bolster his stats and drive up his trade value . Prior to playing Cleveland, Pollard had only one touchdown all season and was yet to rush for more than 80 yards in a single game.
In the previous two games against the Browns and Colts, Pollard has been handed more carries than earlier in the year.
In my opinion, the value for a 29-year-old running back wouldn't be incredibly high; it would realistically be about a fifth-round pick exchanged for Pollard. However, if the Titans are truly looking to get younger and build more draft capital, expect Pollard to be moved before the November 10 deadline.
As previously mentioned, Tennessee traded their perennial Pro Bowl defensive tackle to the Bears. Simmons was leading the Titans with four sacks prior to the trade. Simmons led Tennessee with 11 sacks last season, as he was named a First Team All-Pro for the first time in his career.
Needless to say, the Titans defense will not be the same without their all-world defensive anchor. According to PFF , Simmons has the third most pressures of any defensive tackle in the NFL. Next in line for Titans' sack leaders are DE Jacob Martin with 3.5 and DE Jermaine Johnson II with three, respectively.
However, Martin and Johnson II aren't defensive tackles. The Titans were already thin at defensive tackle prior to the trade with Chicago, which poses major concerns for filling an already massive loss without Simmons.
Two weeks ago, Tennessee cut DT Jordan Elliott after an incident outside of the training facility. Elliott was signed to a two-year contract worth up to $8.5 million this offseason.
Fellow 2026 free agent signee DT John Franklin-Myers has been playing through injuries and only has one sack this season. To address the vacancies, Tennessee resigned DT Jimmy Horne from the practice squad. He has five tackles in two games played this season.
In addition to signing former Raider DT Jonah Laulu, who recorded four sacks in 2025. Laulu only played five games for Las Vegas this season before getting cut and becoming a Titan. It will be interesting to see how effective Tennessee will be to attack the Bengals' QB Joe Burrow on Sunday. The Bengals have only given up 10 sacks this season, which is the third fewest in the league .
Despite Tennessee having their highest-scoring game of the season against the Browns, second-year QB Cam Ward threw for only 181 yards, zero touchdowns and an interception. He also took a critical sack near the goal line right after getting stuffed on a sneak... the Titans were unable to score on that trip.
Ward has thrown an interception in each of the last five games while only tossing three touchdowns in that stretch. His sophomore season has been a disappointment, to say the least.
Currently Ward has fewer passing yards and as many interceptions and touchdowns through seven games as his rookie season. While his completion percentage is up from last year, Ward's average depth of target is only 7.3 yards, which is the eighth worst of eligible passers, according to PFF .
The 24-year-old quaterback has a 73.8 passer rating, which is the third worst in the NFL. That number is worse than his 80.2 passer rating as a rookie. Ward's inability to move the ball down the field consistently is a major concern considering the Titans improved their offensive line from last year and are giving up fewer sacks.
Over the offseason, Tennessee added WR Carnell Tate with the fourth pick in the 2026 draft and WR Wan'Dale Robinson, who had 1,000-plus receiving yards last season with the New York Giants.
The Bengals' secondary is giving up an average of 230 pass years per game, which is the ninth most in the NFL. Ward's season-high is 222 pass yards against Baltimore, his only 200-plus passing yard performance of the year.
If Ward is held to under 200 yards passing and turns the ball over on Sunday against a medicore pass defense, I wouldn't be surprised if backup QB Mitchell Trubisky gets playing time soon. The former first overall pick has the opportunity to remind the league why he's a starting quarterback in the NFL with a major performance against Cincinnati.

title: Carnell Tate and Tyjae Spears Out for Titans in Week 8: Who Steps Up Without Them?
full_text:
The hits just keep coming for the 1-6 Tennessee Titans. Trading Jeffery Simmons may have primed the team for a better rebuild moving forward, but it does no favors for Tennessee's matchup with one of the best offenses in the league this Sunday. The Cincinnati Bengals await in Week 8.
On top of that, both WR Carnell Tate and RB Tyjae Spears have been listed as out for the road duel, with shoulder and knee issues respectively. Not only will Tennessee be freshly without their best defender, but two routine playmakers - including their fourth overall pick - will also now miss.
But we're about the optimism around here. In that spirit, here are two players primed for a breakout now that we know Tate and Spears can't go. When reserves need to step up, these two are likely to be called on.
We'll start with the less surefire of the two with backup RB Michael Carter. The veteran back spent most of this season on the practice squad until he was called up in Week 7 to cover for both Spears and rookie Nick Singleton being out.
Carter posted a fair seven yards on three carries, as well as another seven on his one target. Robert Saleh praised Carter's three-down capabilities, which seems to give him the edge over Singleton.
Pollard will one again be the workhorse in this offense, but down Spears and a receiver, Carter could be in line for more work. We're circling him as a breakout candidate, especially in the short passing game. The longer Spears sits, the more likely these chances are to come for Carter.
Ayomanor has a strong case to come away with the most targets in Tate's absence. Wan'Dale Robinson seems like the obvious pick, but the massive offseason acquisition has been largely ineffective as of late, especially downfield.
Robinson has just two games with 50+ yards this season; he's combined for only seven receptions for 29 yards through the last two weeks. Ayomanor, on the other hand, collected a whopping seven targets against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7.
He hauled in three of those balls for 44 yards. Robinson had six, and four catches, but only seven yards.
Cam Ward has had chemistry with Ayomanor since they shared a rookie campaign last season. That preference has swapped to Tate to some degree, but Ayomanor has outright succeeded Calvin Ridley and earned more time on the field.
Look for extended targets for Ayomanor this week, especially in the mid-to-deep capacities that Tate is often targeted.
